articleTitle: Drain near senior citizen’s home remains clogged despite complaints, he wins Rs 15,000
articleFeaturedImageAlt: PWD sewerage consumer drain puducherry
description: The consumer commission in Puducherry was hearing a complaint filed by a man seeking directions to the authorities to inspect and resolve the blockage in the sewer system linked to his residence.
body_raw: A Puducherry district consumer commission has awarded Rs 15,000 to a 60-year-old man after a sewerage block linked to his residence allegedly went unaddressed despite repeated complaints to public works authorities. The commission directed the authorities to inspect the drain system and carry out necessary desilting, noting that prolonged blockage could cause inconvenience, discomfort and mental distress to the occupants of residential premises. President S Mouttouvel, along with members A S Suvitha and G Arumugam, while hearing the mans complaint, held that the authorities failure to attend to the blockage, despite the matter having been repeatedly brought to their notice, amounted to deficiency in service. The opposite parties PWD have not produced any material to establish that the grievance was attended to or effectively rectified and that the sewerage problem resulted in inconvenience and unhygienic conditions in and around the residential premises, we are of the considered view that the Complainant is entitled to reasonable compensation, the August 28 order read. No solution despite complaints The man claimed that he had availed himself of the sewerage service of the Public Works Department PWD under the applicable policy and paid the charges as and when claimed by the authorities. He added that on December 6, 2025, there was a blockage of the drainage line to his house, causing severe inconvenience to him and his family members and also posing a health hazard. Aggrieved, he approached the PWD and submitted a written complaint to resolve the sewerage blockage, but allegedly no action was taken despite an assurance that immediate action would be taken. He also submitted that the stagnant sewage linked to his residence had been continuously emitting foul smell and attracting mosquitoes and insects, thereby posing extremely unhygienic living conditions and causing serious health hazards to him and his family members. The man was represented by advocates S Vimal and M Dhinagaran before the commission. Sewerage, drainage and public health The commission noted that the man has specifically pleaded that the blocked sewerage line resulted in stagnant sewage, foul smell, attraction of mosquitoes and insects, and unhygienic conditions around his residence. The failure of the opposite parties department to attend to and rectify the sewerage blockage caused not merely inconvenience but also mental agony and physical hardship to the complainant, it observed. It also pointed out that sewerage and drainage are essential civic services directly connected with sanitation, public health and the maintenance of hygienic living conditions. A service provider entrusted with the maintenance of a sewerage system cannot be expected merely to receive charges from consumers it is equally incumbent upon the concerned authority to maintain the system with reasonable care and to take appropriate and timely steps when a specific complaint regarding blockage or malfunction is brought to its notice, it added. It was also noted that the department did not appear before the commission and held that this did not dispense with the commissions duty to examine whether the complainant has established his case. Accordingly, the commission directed the authorities to do a thorough inspection of the drainage system connected to the mans residence. It added that if any blockage, defect or obstruction was found, the department should undertake all remedial measures, including desilting, repair and, wherever required, restoration or replacement of the affected portion of the sewer line. The commission directed the department to ensure proper, efficient and uninterrupted functioning of the sewerage system on payment of any charges lawfully payable by the complainant. It also directed the department to pay Rs 10,000 to the complainant for the deficiency in service and attendant mental agony, physical hardship and other suffering, along with litigation expenses of Rs 5,000. Takeaway This ruling shows that government authorities responsible for sewerage maintenance can be held liable for deficiency in service when they fail to act on repeated complaints about a drain blockage. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories Puducherry 180-0425-1082 or call the National Consumer Helpline on 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Nearly 1/3rd of electors in Delhi issued SIR notices now verified
articleFeaturedImageAlt: sir delhi
description: This is a sharp uptick in the number of notices disposed of compared to a week back. In the period from August 31 to September 29, only 4.01 lakh notices had been disposed.
body_raw: As the Special Intensive Revision SIR process continues in the Capital, nearly one-third of the electors around 31 who had to prove their eligibility to stay on the electoral rolls have been verified, data from the office of the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer CEO showed on Monday, with over 55 days left to dispose of the rest of notices and objections. This is a sharp uptick in the number of notices disposed of compared to a week back. In the period from August 31 to September 29, only 4.01 lakh notices had been disposed. Over the next one week, more than six lakh notices were disposed of, with the total figure reaching 10.28 lakh on Tuesday. Election officials have attributed this increase to exemptions from in-person hearings for voters who received notices, changes in the portal in which they had to upload documents, additional deployment of officials and special camps. Delhi had around 1.45 crore electors before the SIR process of voter rolls began in the Capital. Among them, 97.5 lakh were included in the draft electoral roll, while around 47.5 lakh electors were classified as uncollectible-after the Booth-level officers BLOs found them absent, shifted, dead or having duplicate entries, among other reasons-and were struck off the roll. Among the 97.5 lakh who did make it to the draft roll, one-third or around 33.1 lakh electors were issued notices to prove that they are eligible to be on the final roll. While 13.79 lakh electors got notices because they could not link themselves to the electoral roll of the last SIR, 19.33 lakh were flagged for logical discrepancies in their enumeration forms. On the new changes, an Electoral Registration Officer ERO said, Now, I dont need to call hundreds of people to my office everyday for hearings, right? BLOs are going house to house and where needed, electors can also forward their documents to the BLO on Whatsapp also. After its first meeting since The Indian Express reported on the rupture within the Election Commission, the poll panel had said last week that electors who were issued notices will not be required to attend hearings to prove their eligibility. BLOs will visit the homes of such persons for collection of documents and thereafter upload them on the ECINet, for decision by the ERO. Such persons need not be called for hearing to EROAERO office, a statement from the ECI said. Some BLOs, however, expressed disappointment with the deadline for disposal of notices, claims and objections getting extended to November 30. I am also working in the school for 5-6 hours, after which now I have to again go door-to-door to collect documents. The deadline has also been increased by another month. It was supposed to be a three month exercise, but now it will last five months. Should we leave school work and do this full time only? a BLO said. Another BLO said that in some areas it is easier to conduct hearings at a central location instead of going house to house due to often confusing and wrong addresses. The number of Assistant EROs, who are often school principals and can also dispose of notices like EROs, was also increased in Delhi. On September 24, the number of AEROs was increased from 297 to 902, an increase of 605. An official said that BLOs have been given a target of conducting at least 10 hearings every day. An ERO pointed out that the change in the ECINET portal which lets EROs dispose of notices without conducting a hearing is one reason behind the uptick in notices being disposed of. Especially for notices for very minor logical discrepancies, if a BLO has verified the elector and is satisfied, we dont need to trouble the electors for documents. I cleared hundreds of notices in one night after this became available, an ERO said.

articleTitle: ‘I have done my duty’: Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as India captain in all formats
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Harmanpreet Kaur of India during the 5th T20I match between India and Sri Lanka at Greenfield International Stadium, Thiruvananthapuram, India, on December 30, 2025. (CREIMAS for BCCI)
description: Harmanpreet Kaur, India's only Women's World Cup-winning captain, has stepped down from the role in all formats.
body_raw: Harmanpreet Kaur, the only Indian captain to have won the Womens World Cup, announced on Tuesday that she has stepped down from the role with immediate effect. Harmanpreet made the announcement in a lengthy post on her Instagram account. Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Womens Cricket Team across all formats. This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life, said Harmanpreet in her statement. Widely rated among Indias greatest cricketers of all time, Harmanpreet took over as Indias full-time captain across formats after Mithali Raj retired in 2022, having led the team periodically before that as Mithalis deputy. She has also been Indias T20I captain since 2016. Her last act as skipper of the side was leading the team to their second consecutive gold medal at the Asian Games last month. I leave the captaincy today with a heart full of emotions , but also with PEACE. Because I genuinely believe My team is in a good place. A team with talent, character, belief and a future that I am incredibly excited to watch and be a part of, Harmanpreet further said in her statement. I feel I have done my duty.   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Harmann imharmanpreetkaur Harmanpreet has confirmed that she will continue to be available for India in all formats. Captaincy may end today, but my love for Indian cricket never will. Thank you to every teammate, coach, support staff, management , BCCI , family members every single fan who stood by me through the highs and lows. Blood. Sweat. Sarifice. Pride. I gave it all Now, Im ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues, she concluded in her statement. She has led the Indian team in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is. The crowning achievement of her career came last year, when under her captaincy India won their maiden Womens World Cup title, beating South Africa in the final. Notably, they had defeated the runaway favourites and record winners Australia in the semifinal before that. Harmanpreet is overall just the third Indian captain to have won the 50-over World Cup after Kapil Dev and MS Dhoni and one of five Indians to have won any World Cup as skipper, with Rohit Sharma and Suryakumar Yadav leading the mens side to victory in the T20 World Cups of 2024 and 2026 respectively. She has captained the Indian team in 155 T20I matches, the most for any player across mens or womens cricket. She has played a total of 210 T20I matches, which is also the most for any player across genders. Harmanpreet made her international debut in March 2009 in an ODI against Pakistan in the Womens World Cup that year. Her T20I debut came a couple of months after that against England. She made her Test debut against England in August 2014.

articleTitle: CBSE mandates 30-minute session for school staff on October 7 to sensitise on special needs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: prashast portal cbse training module
description: CBSE has asked schools to ensure maximum participation. The 30-minute module on Inclusive Education for Children with Special Needs (CwSN) will be available through the PRASHAST portal at prashast.education.gov.in.
body_raw: The Central Board of Secondary Education CBSE has asked all its affiliated schools to organise a 30-minute sensitisation and orientation module on inclusive education for Children with Special Needs CwSN on October 7, 2026. The module has been developed in pursuance of directives from the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, with the aim of building sensitivity, empathy and an inclusive attitude among school staff. The module is intended for all teaching and non-teaching staff, including teachers, ayahs, drivers, clerical staff, receptionists, deans, wardens, heads of schools and other support personnel. Read Senior bureaucrat Mandeep Bhandari is new CBSE chairperson According to CBSE, the session will help staff understand the needs and challenges faced by children with special needs and encourage appropriate, respectful and inclusive practices in the school environment. Schools have been asked to ensure maximum participation and organise the screening in a manner that allows staff members to attend without disrupting essential school activities. The 30-minute module on Inclusive Education for Children with Special Needs CwSN will be available through the PRASHAST portal at prashast.education.gov.in. It can be accessed through the Video Tutorial option available under the Headmaster login on the portal. The initiative is part of the PRASHAST Screening Initiative being undertaken during the current academic year. The screening initiative aims to identify students with probable disabilities and facilitate timely intervention. CBSE said sensitising school staff to the needs and requirements of CwSN is an important component of the initiative, particularly to ensure that students receive appropriate support within the school environment. CBSE has asked principals and heads of affiliated schools to ensure maximum participation of their staff in the module. The Board will also track the number of schools that view the module at the national level. The initiative is intended to contribute to a more inclusive, accessible and supportive school environment for Children with Special Needs.

articleTitle: Veteran actor Sivakumar on Suriya-Jyotika’s 4-year wait to marry: ‘She was from Mumbai’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sivakumar on Suriya-Jyotika wedding
description: Sivakumar’s reflections on Suriya and Jyotika offer a closer look at patience, commitment and love
body_raw: Veteran Tamil actor Sivakumar recently recalled a core memory about his son Suriya and daughter-in-law Jyotika, who recently completed 20 years of marriage with a grand Christian wedding and celebration in Scotland. I sometimes wonder if they are our children laughs. Love doesnt come easy. She was from Mumbai. He was from Chennai. He had said that if he had to get married.it would be her. They waited four years, he recalled in a chat in Tamil with JFW. Rather than rushing the decision or walking away when approval was not immediate, the couple waited until the family eventually came around. Beyond the celebrity story, an interesting relationship question remains In a culture that increasingly celebrates instant decisions, what does the ability to wait tell us about commitment? DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. As a psychotherapist, Delnna Rrajesh, relationship breakthrough coach, said healthy waiting is not spending years hoping that an unavailable person will eventually choose you, tolerating disrespect or putting your entire life on hold. It is remaining committed to something meaningful while recognising that certain situations need time, conversations and emotional processing, expressed Delnna. Marriage in India is often not experienced purely as two individuals coming together. Families, cultures, languages, traditions and expectations may enter the relationship alongside the couple. While adults have the right to choose their partners, family resistance can create a painful psychological conflict between individual autonomy and family belonging. There is no single correct response to that conflict. Family approval should never become permission for coercion, control or indefinite interference in an adults choices. Equally, when concerns arise from unfamiliarity, fear or differences in background rather than abuse or prejudice, time and respectful dialogue can sometimes accomplish what confrontation cannot. This is where patience and conviction need to coexist, Delnna told indianexpress.com. Another relationship lesson deserves attention commitment is easier to declare than to demonstrate. It is relatively easy to say, I love you during the emotionally intense beginning of a relationship. Commitment becomes visible when circumstances are inconvenient - when there is uncertainty, disagreement, distance, career pressure, family complexity or delayed gratification. Waiting itself does not prove love. But the ability of two people to remain respectful, consistent and aligned while navigating difficulty can reveal something about the relationships foundations, shared Delnna. Four years can also change people considerably. This is why time, when used well, can provide information that chemistry cannot. You see how someone handles frustration. Whether promises and actions match. How they respond when they cannot immediately get what they want. Whether disagreements produce manipulation or conversation. Whether both people continue choosing the relationship after the initial intensity settles. Time does not automatically make a relationship stronger. It reveals what the relationship is made of, Delnna described. There is also a valuable distinction between fighting for a relationship and fighting inside a relationship. Couples facing external resistance sometimes become so consumed with proving everyone wrong that the opposition itself holds them together. Once that battle disappears, they discover they never sufficiently examined whether they were compatible. Therefore, waiting should also contain honest questions Do we share fundamental values? Can we communicate during conflict? What are our expectations around careers, finances, children, caregiving and extended families? Are we building a life together, or merely defending a love story? And perhaps this is where the story becomes particularly relevant to younger couples, said Delnna. articleTitle: After HC rap over depleting water table, Gurugram plans borewell phase-out
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gurugram
description: In parallel, the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) is also collaborating with IIT Gandhinagar to install water injection well systems.
body_raw: Following scrutiny from the Punjab and Haryana High Court over the rapid depletion of groundwater and unchecked extraction across the district, Gurugram authorities on Monday drew up an action plan directing government departments to gradually discontinue the use of borewells and push industrial units to switch to tertiary-treated wastewater for operational needs. At a high-level review meeting chaired by Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority GMDA Chief Executive Officer P C Meena on Monday, departments currently reliant on groundwater were instructed to identify alternative supply channels and phase-out tube wells, officials said. All concerned agencies have been given a deadline of October 6 to submit detailed roadmaps outlining measures to cut extraction and scale up rainwater recharge. The district administration was also tasked with framing a comprehensive enforcement strategy to identify and seal unauthorised borewells across the city GMDA spokesperson Neha Sharma said. Addressing the meeting, Meena highlighted the need to replace fresh groundwater usage with tertiary-treated wastewater from sewage treatment plants STPs. Currently, the GMDA supplies 10 million litres per day MLD of treated effluent to the textile industry. Now, authorities plan to bring other industrial clusters under the treated water distribution network. To ensure accountability at the local level, the Haryana State Pollution Control Board HSPCB was directed to monitor the functioning of captive STPs in group housing societies to ensure compliance with discharge standards. Directives were also issued to mandate separate electricity connections for these treatment plants and strictly enforce the zero-liquid discharge policy in residential complexes, Sharma added. The meeting saw authorities resolve to shift focus toward retaining rainwater within the urban catchment rather than allowing run-off to discharge into storm-water drains, officials said. This strategy includes reviving water bodies facing degradation, clearing encroachments, lowering green-belt levels to trap surface run-off, and converting designated neighborhood parks into bioswales. The HC in ongoing proceedings concerning the citys shrinking groundwater reserves had directed the Mondays meeting. It had said it expects the authorities to examine the issues and to suggest appropriate measures to tackle the worsening situation of ground water in Gurugram, noting that if the situation continues unabated then the future generation would have to face disastrous consequences. In an effort to refill underground water supplies, the GMDA, in partnership with Tata Consultancy Services TCS, is also carrying out a feasibility study to construct a large underground rainwater retention reservoir beneath the football ground at the Tau Devi Lal Stadium in the city, officials said. On the recharge front, the GMDA has rolled out five advanced scientific harvesting structures designed in collaboration with IIT Delhi. Three structures, at Sectors 31 and 39, and at AIT Park in Sector 55, have been commissioned, while work on a fourth at Rezangla Chowk is underway, Sharma explained. Prof Anshuman from The Energy and Resources Institute TERI, who attended the meeting, endorsed the system as an effective mechanism to halt aquifer depletion. In parallel, the Municipal Corporation of Gurugram MCG is also collaborating with IIT Gandhinagar to install water injection well systems. A water injection well system is a deep shaft that pushes treated water deep underground to maintain reservoir pressure, or safely dispose of wastewater. Meanwhile, according to the Haryana Water Resources Authority, rejuvenation work on 142 ponds has been planned across the district, of which 68 have been completed and 74 are in progress, alongside 21 ponds revived under rural employment schemes. Within municipal limits, 32 water bodies have been restored and work on 21 others is underway in the city, officials said.

articleTitle: Israel nearly shot down flydubai flight 1073 after cockpit attack on Indian pilot Smit Machchhar: Report
articleFeaturedImageAlt: FlyDubai
description: Israel was prepared to shoot down a FlyDubai plane after its captain was attacked in the cockpit.
body_raw: Israel was prepared to shoot down flydubai Flight 1073 with all passengers on board after Indian captain Smit Machchhar was attacked by his Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami in the cockpit, CBS News reported, citing two Israeli sources with direct knowledge of the matter. The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, with 182 people on board, most of them Israelis, was flying along the Saudi-Jordanian border when Captain Machchhar was stabbed by his co-pilot in an attempt to crash the aircraft. The report said that after the plane plunged 14,000 feet, the Israeli Air Force tried contacting the cockpit but got no response. It then activated its long-practised procedure for a potential 911-style incident, swiftly convened a pre-established emergency committee, set up a command centre, scrambled fighter jets and closed its airspace. Israel recalled fighter jets Israel, however, called back its fighter jets after authorities realised the aircraft was turning towards Saudi Arabia, which had also scrambled its own fighter jets, according to the report. The flight then made an emergency landing in Tabuk, after Captain Machchhar opened the cockpit door and passengers subdued the Omani co-pilot. The report, citing sources, further stated that Israel would have dispatched fighter jets into Jordanian airspace to investigate if the FlyDubai flight had moved closer to Israeli territory. The Israeli Air Force pilots would have then attempted to approach the aircraft closely enough to establish visual contact with the cockpit and assess the situation, before checking the cabin for signs of panic. After checking in on the aircraft, the IAF would have updated the emergency committee, which, according to the report, would in turn alert the defence minister and prime minister if a hijacking was confirmed and there was no response from terrorists. Ultimately, the final decision to shoot down the aircraft would have fallen to the prime minister, a course of action CBS News sources described as far preferable to letting the plane crash into Ben Gurion Airport, the Azrieli Center in Tel Aviv or another high-value target.

articleTitle: Karnataka plans AI training in government schools from Class 6
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka plans to introduce AI training in govt schools from Class 6
description: Shivakumar also directed officials to identify land for establishing an AI university in the state. Steps are being taken to recruit 956 teachers on an outsourcing basis, it said.
body_raw: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Monday directed officials to explore means to introduce Artificial Intelligence AI training in government schools from Class 6, with support from the Information Technology department and private partners. He issued these directions at a review meeting on the progress of his governments 100-day programmes, recruitments and priority schemes. AI training has already started for Class 9 students in government schools. The officials were asked to work toward extending it to students from Class 6, Shivakumar said. Also Read  Karnataka proposes rule to reserve 15 government seats in professional courses for rural students Google expressed interest in providing AI training in schools, and officials were asked to examine the companys initiatives in Telangana as part of this exercise, according to the CMO statement. Shivakumar also directed officials to identify land for establishing an AI university in the state. Steps are being taken to recruit 956 teachers on an outsourcing basis, it said. Reviewing the School Education Department, the chief minister directed officials to organise visits for Class 9 and 11 students from 941 urban schools to progressive farmers fields. The students should be provided facilities to stay overnight in villages, including community halls and hostels, and private schools should also mandatorily implement the programme, he said. The programme should be completed by December. Also Read  Karnataka SSLC Exam Fee 2027 revised check new fee details On the development of 1,000 Karnataka Public Schools KPS, Shivakumar directed officials to complete preparations for laying the foundation stones by November 14. The implementation process has been simplified by authorising deputy commissioners to approve detailed project reports and tenders for KPS, he said. The government also plans to develop 100 KPS schools through corporate social responsibility CSR funds, with companies having already shown interest in developing 60 schools. Reviewing the Agriculture Department, the chief minister said 25 lakh SMS messages had been sent to farmers under the CM Raitha Chaitanya Agritech Mission. He directed officials to also send video messages explaining the scheme in a simple manner.

articleTitle: ‘Focus on 403, not 3’: Akhilesh rules out Samajwadi Party’s third Rajya Sabha candidate
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has said the party will not field a third candidate for the upcoming Rajya Sabha polls (File photo).
description: The SP has already fielded party veteran Ram Gopal Yadav and Reliance Industries executive Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani, who filed their nominations in Lucknow last week.
body_raw: After a week of suspense, Samajwadi Party SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on Tuesday announced that the party is not fielding a third candidate for the upcoming Rajya Sabha polls, stating that the partys focus is not on three seats but on the 403 Assembly seats in Uttar Pradesh. The state goes to polls next year. Yadav had earlier stated that his party would field a third candidate once the required numbers are secured. However, in a post on X this morning, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister said, Now, our focus is not on three, but on 403. Tuesday is the last day for filing nominations for the biennial polls, followed by scrutiny of papers on October 7. Names can be withdrawn till October 9, while polling will be conducted on October 16. ALSO READ  Why Samajwadi Party fielded Reliance executive Dhanraj Nathwani in Rajya Sabha polls Rajya Sabha math The SP has already fielded party veteran Ram Gopal Yadav and Reliance Industries executive Dhanraj Nathwani for the Rajya Sabha polls, who filed their nominations in Lucknow last week. The BJP on Monday had announced eight candidates, including Dalits and Brahmins, leaving out Union Ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma, whose terms in the Upper House are set to end next month. They comprise state minister Dharampal Singh, Shruti Gangwar Prakash Pal, Vidya Sagar Sonkar, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Radhakant Ojha and Gopi Krishna Pandey and Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan. The SP and the Congress together effectively have 102 MLAs on their side, with the numbers enough to elect two MPs 37 first-preference votes are required. They are, however, nine first-preference votes short of getting a third candidate elected In the 403-member Assembly, the ruling NDA has 291 MLAs, including the BJPs 255. With support of Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, which has two MLAs, the alliances effective strength is 293. The main opposition, Samajwadi Party, has 101 MLAs, and its ally, Congress, has two.

articleTitle: Hanuman Ansh team performs aarti at Neem Karoli Baba’s Kainchi Dham, film earns Rs 424 cr
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shobhinaw Satyaa visits Kainchi Dham after the success of Hanuman Ansh.
description: As Hanuman Ansh earned over Rs 424 crore at the worldwide box office, its team including lead actor Shobhinaw Satyaa, visited Kainchi Dham, the spiritual site associated with Neem Karoli Baba.
body_raw: The team of Vishal Chaturvedis blockbuster devotional film Hanuman Ansh has paid a visit to Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand in order to offer their prayers to Neem Karoli Baba, the revered spiritual guru whose life their film is based on. However, their visit comes a day after the director urged devotees to exercise caution and avoid visiting the site amid reports of overcrowding over the long weekend. Vishal was not a part of the group visiting the holy site. Hanuman Ansh team visits Kainchi Dham The team of Hanuman Ansh - led by actor Shobhinaw Satyaa, who plays Neem Karoli Baba in the biopic - participated in the aarti and paid their respects to the spiritual gurus shrine at Kainchi Dham. Satyaa expressed his gratitude for the visit and also thanked the audience for making their film a super-duper hit, as per ANI. We are missing the rest of the team, especially our director Vishal Chaturvedi. It is because of his hard work that the film got made and reached this level of success. But he has a lot of responsibility at the moment and because of that, he couldnt make it, he told Uttarakhand News. ALSO READ  Salman Khan hosts BJP youth leader at Mumbai home Touched by your warmth, simplicity The team of Hanuman Ansh managed to make it to Kainchi Dham despite the swelling crowds reported in the past few days. So much so that Vishal Chaturvedi had to take to his Instagram handle on Sunday to urge devotees to check the situation before heading there. Kainchi Dham is overcrowded, and people have said that this is because of the influence of Hanuman Ansh. If that is the case, and if that is not the case, even then, people should visit there only after knowing the present conditions, he said. It is my humble request that if there is overcrowding, please consider visiting other places. Dont become part of a situation where women and children feel suffocated or get stuck in traffic jams, added the director. He also suggested that in case of overcrowding, the devotees could consider visiting other sites associated with Neem Karoli Baba, like Neem Karoli village and Vrindavan in the neighbouring state of Uttar Pradesh. Over the long weekend, which started with Gandhi Jayanti this past Friday on October 2, more than 35,000 devotees visited Kainchi Dham every day, as opposed to the 25,000 the administration is used to handling. The Nainital administration is now even considering opening an alternate route to ease the pressure, as reported by The Indian Express. Both the pilgrims and the locals use the same road to Kainchi, which also goes up to Mukteshwar, causing a traffic jam for hours, said Nainital District Magistrate Lalit Mohan. He attributed the rush to both the end of the monsoon season - enabling safer travel to the hills - and the release of Hanuman Ansh, which has amassed over Rs 420 crore at the worldwide box office so far. Hanuman Ansh box office collection After 60 days at the domestic box office, Hanuman Ansh has now earned Rs 384.44 crore gross and Rs 325.48 crore net at the domestic box office. Its just Rs 4 crore away from surpassing the domestic box office collection of Anurag Singhs period war drama Border 2, starring Sunny Deol and Varun Dhawan, post which itd become the second highest grossing Indian film of 2026 after Aditya Dhars spy thriller Dhurandhar 2 The Revenge, starring Ranveer Singh. Ever since its overseas release by Hombale Films on September 11, Hanuman Ansh has collected Rs 39.80 crore at the international box office. The films worldwide collection currently stands at Rs 424 crore. On October 9, Hanuman Anshs dubbed Telugu version will also release in cinemas across India, which is likely to increase the films box office collections. Made on a budget of less than Rs 2 crore, the film has already earned over 212 times globally.

articleTitle: Gujarat approves Rs 21,840 monthly stipend for foreign medical graduates
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gujarat to give Rs 21,840 monthly stipend to MBBS interns who studied abroad; 350 doctors to benefit
description: The decision was taken in a meeting held at Suvarna Sankul-2 state administrative building in Gandhinagar, where detailed discussions were conducted with the officials concerned, Pansheriya said.
body_raw: The Gujarat government has decided to pay a monthly stipend of Rs 21,840 to medical graduates who completed their MBBS abroad and are currently undergoing internships in the state, bringing them on par with interns who graduated from medical colleges in Gujarat. The decision, announced by Health Minister Pansheriya on Monday, is expected to benefit around 350 foreign medical graduates who were allotted internship postings in the state between June 1 and October 1, 2026. According to rules set by the National Medical Commission NMC, every medical student who has completed an MBBS degree abroad is required to acquire a mandatory one-year internship experience in India, he was quoted as saying in a release. Also Read  UP government increases MBBS, BDS interns stipend to Rs 25,000 Such MBBS doctors doing internships at government and medical colleges managed by the Gujarat Medical Education and Research Society GMERS will be paid a stipend, he added. The step was welcomed by the All India Medical Students Association AIMSA, calling it a result of collective representation, continuous follow-up, and unity and perseverance of FMG students over the years. Congratulations to all FMGs Today marks a historic and long-awaited milestone for Foreign Medical Graduates in Gujarat. articleTitle: FIR against 2 ‘BJP agents’ over Form 7s to delete 5,698 Bengaluru voters
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka SIR Form 7 mass voter deletion
description: As per Karnataka Pradesh Mahila Congress president Sowmya Reddy’s complaint, the Form 7 applications claimed that 5,698 voters had permanently shifted from Jayanagar constituency.
body_raw: An FIR was registered in Bengaluru against two alleged BJP booth level agents BLAs and others for submitting fraudulent Form 7 applications seeking the deletion of 5,698 voters from the electoral rolls in Jayanagar Assembly constituency. The FIR registered on October 5, based on a complaint by former Jayanagar MLA and Karnataka Pradesh Mahila Congress president Sowmya Reddy, names BLAs Ramakrishna and Yogesh as accused, alleging that they are affiliated with the BJP. The move comes amid a growing row over bulk Form 7 filings in Karnataka, with the Congress alleging a conspiracy to delete lakhs of eligible voters from the electoral rolls amid the Special Intensive Revision exercise, and the BJP and Janata Dal Secular seeking protection from what they term false or unwarranted cases against party workers. Form 7 allows an elector to object to the inclusion of a name or seek deletion of an existing entry from the electoral roll. 5,698 voters permanently shifted What the Form 7s said According to the October 5 complaint, the alleged irregularities took place between June 16 and October 5 during the electoral roll revision process. Form 7 applications were allegedly submitted claiming that 5,698 voters had permanently shifted from the constituency. As per the complaint, the applications sought deletion of 54 voters in Pattabhiramanagar Ward 165, 525 in Byrasandra Ward 169, 719 in Jayanagar East Ward 170, 4,327 in Gurappanapalya Ward 171, and 82 voters across J P Nagar, Sarakki and Shakambarinagar Wards 177, 178 and 179. Reddy alleged in her complaint that the applications disproportionately targeted voters from minority communities and other sections perceived to be politically opposed to the BJP and its allies. The complaint also alleged that the identity details and voter IDs of two citizens or voters identified as C Ramesh and his wife Roopa were used to file the Form 7 applications without their knowledge or consent. Some of the applications allegedly carried forged signatures and were submitted to Booth Level Officer Lokesh at the election office in Jayanagar 4th Block. The police are investigating the allegations. Similar complaints across Karnataka In Bengaluru, the Vyalikaval police on October 2 registered an FIR after Congress leader Anoop Iyengar alleged that 778 Form 7 applications had been filed seeking deletion of voters in eight polling parts of Ward 64 in the Malleswaram Assembly constituency. The complaint alleged that several voters were still residing at the addresses mentioned in the electoral rolls and that some applications contained false information or suspected forged signatures. G S Vasanthalakshmi, identified in the FIR as a BJP member, was named as an accused. The allegations are under investigation. Similar complaints have been reported from other parts of Karnataka. Police have registered cases in Bidar, Mysuru and Belagavi over Form 7 applications seeking deletion of voters, with the complaints alleging false information and forged documents.

articleTitle: After sexual harassment complaint, Delhi cop’s additional charge withheld
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Assistant Commissioner of Police Vivek Bhagat
description: Three women journalists have complained of alleged harassment during an October 3 protest near Jantar Mantar. One of them specifically named Delhi cop Vivek Bhagat
body_raw: The Delhi government has withheld a temporary posting given to Assistant Commissioner of Police Vivek Bhagat, who is accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during a protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The government said Bhagat had requested that he not be given the charge of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police until the allegations are fully investigated. The government said the proposal to confer the Additional Duty Charge ADC on 12 Selection Grade DANIPS officers, including Bhagat, was initiated on August 25, much before the present set of events, and the orders were issued after due approval on October 5. It clarified that this was a temporary arrangement with no financial benefit, and that officers assigned the charge could not exercise the statutory powers of the regular incumbents. Accordingly, the October 5 order is being modified in respect of Bhagat and will be reissued for the 11 remaining officers, the government said. Bhagat is currently posted as Sub-Divisional Police Officer, Connaught Place. The complaints The development came at a time when three women journalists had complained of alleged sexual harassment and manhandling during the October 3 protest near Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls. The women journalists had alleged that they were manhandled and subjected to inappropriate behaviour while covering the police action during the protest. One of the complainants specifically alleged that Bhagat touched her inappropriately while she was covering the police action. The complaints by the three women have been transferred to the Crime Branch for a fair and impartial inquiry. The government order said the arrangement had been made in the interest of government work. Besides Bhagat, the officers assigned the current duty charge include Dr Vikas Sheokand, A Venkatesh, Gursewak Singh, Renu Lata, Vidushi Kaushik, Manu Himanshu, Sakaria Mihir Pravinbhai, Garima Tiwari, Ashish Kumar, Manish Ladla and Rohit Gupta. The government said the arrangement would continue until the Ministry of Home Affairs fills the Addl DCP posts on a regular basis. It can also be discontinued at any time without assigning any reason.

articleTitle: Bombay High Court fines 2 lawyers Rs 52,000 each over ‘won’t spare you’ threat to judge
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bombay High Court threat judge lawyers fine
description: According to the court records, an advocate shouted in the courtroom, alleging that their cases were being treated differently and threatened to complain against the judge and take action through the Bar Association.
body_raw: The Bombay High Court has held two advocates guilty of contempt for threatening a judicial officer during court proceedings and telling him, We will not spare you, and imposed a fine of Rs 52,000 each while referring the matter to the Bar Council for disciplinary action. The court underlined that the legal profession cannot be equated with any other traditional profession, and lawyers have contributed to the countrys independence struggle, helped frame the Constitution and assisted courts in developing the law through research and hard work. Justices Urmila Joshi Phalke and Raj D Wakode were hearing a criminal contempt reference against two advocates arising from proceedings before a civil judge, junior division and judicial magistrate first class, at Arni in Yavatmal district. The legal profession cannot be equated with any other traditional professions. It is not commercial in nature and is stated as noble considering the nature of duties to be performed and its impact on the society.lawyers have contributed in the struggle for independence of the nation. They have helped in the framing of the Constitution of India and they have also assisted the Courts in evolving jurisprudence by doing hard labour and research work, the court said on October 5. It added that the nobility of the legal system is to be ensured at all costs so that the Constitution remains vibrant and to expand its interpretation so as to meet new challenges. Thus, the lawyers who bring the cause to the Court are supposed to protect the rights of individuals of equality and freedom. The lawyers are supposed to be fearless and independent in the protection of rights of litigants. Thus, their role is significant, the court said. Dispute over warrant The case was listed before the Arni court on November 26, 2021, to check the status of a bailable warrant issued against an accused. After the judge recorded that the accused had remained absent despite the warrant, a non-bailable warrant was issued against him, following which his lawyer stated that the accused was present but had not entered the courtroom. However, when the accused was called, he was found to be absent. His lawyer then sought cancellation of the warrant and later stated that the matter had been settled between the parties. He also insisted that the informants evidence be recorded. The judge declined, noting that other accused were also absent and their presence had to be secured. According to the judicial officers account, the advocate then shouted in the courtroom, alleging that the court was troubling them, treating their cases differently and imposing higher fines, and threatened to complain against the judge and take action through the Bar Association. Later, another advocate, who was the then president of the Arni Taluka Court Bar Association, entered the courtroom while the judge was dictating an order, and allegedly told him in Marathi,                    , which translates to If you take anything on record and act on it, we will not spare you. We will give evidence of corruption against you to senior officials. Conduct aimed to terrorise judge The high court held that the conduct of both advocates interfered with the administration of justice. It said that if they were aggrieved by the judicial order, they had an opportunity to challenge it. Instead, the threats had the effect of pressuring the judicial officer while he was performing his duties. The due administration of law is of greater importance than the success or failure of any individual, the bench said, holding that the conduct of the advocates was aimed to terrorise, pressurise the Judicial Officer. The court said giving threats, addressing a judicial officer in a loud voice and preventing him from passing orders were serious acts, particularly when committed by an advocate who is an officer of the court. The bench held that the statements were apparently made to pressurise and terrorise him from passing an order and described the conduct as scandalous and amounting to misconduct. The advocates denied the allegations and argued that the incident occurred during the heat of arguments. They also relied on unconditional apologies tendered by them later. The court noted that the apologies were not offered at the earliest stage. It also recorded that the respondents had initially failed to appear despite service of notice in the contempt proceedings, leading to bailable warrants being issued against them. Apology is not a weapon of defence to purge the guilty of their offence, nor is it intended to operate as universal panacea, but it is intended to be evidence of real contriteness, the court said. Referring to a Supreme Court verdict, it added, Apology is an act of contrition. Unless apology is offered at the earliest opportunity and in good grace, the apology is shorn of penitence and hence it is liable to be rejected. If the apology is offered at the time when the contemnor finds that the court is going to impose punishment it ceases to be an apology and becomes an act of a cringing coward. The bench also said that where an advocate has a serious grievance against a judicial officer, the grievance can be taken to the proper authority. However, an advocate is expected to act in a dignified manner and maintain respect towards the court. The court said such respect is essential and that contempt jurisdiction protects not only the concerned judges ability to administer justice fearlessly and fairly but also the fair name of the judiciary. Rs 52,000 fine, costs The court held both advocates guilty of contempt but decided against imprisonment. It noted that while the law permits imprisonment, fine or both, fine is ordinarily the rule and imprisonment an exception. Present respondents have committed the contempt of Court, the bench held, adding that considering they were practising lawyers and had subsequently tendered apologies, a fine and reference to the Bar Council would be adequate punishment. The high court directed each advocate to pay a fine of Rs 2,000 within two weeks and referred the proceedings to the Disciplinary Committee of the Bar Council of Maharashtra and Goa for appropriate action. Each advocate was also ordered to pay Rs 50,000 as costs to the Public Welfare Account. Their total financial liability under the order was therefore Rs 52,000 each.

articleTitle: Parents arrested for repeated rape, sexual abuse of minor daughter in Gujarat
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gujarat police
description: According to police, the girl told them her father had repeatedly abused her over a period of a fortnight in September. Police found pictures of the abuse in the girl’s mother’s phone
body_raw: A couple living in the Kutch district of Gujarat were arrested over the past weekend for the alleged repeated rape and sexual abuse of their minor daughter over a period of a fortnight in the second half of September. The horrific incident came to light only after the minor girl managed to get her hands on a phone and call police, which led to her rescue and the arrest of her parents, police officers said. However, even this happened only after the couple had succeeded in thwarting the complainants attempt to reach police once, and cutting off ways for her to reach for help by switching off the mobile phone that she had used, officers said. Senior officers of the Kutch East Police have claimed that they have found evidence to support the minors allegations in a phone that they seized from her mother. This evidence allegedly includes nude photos of the child, as well as photos of her with her father, the officers said. According to police officers, the complainant, who is in her early teens and the oldest among four siblings, was caught by her mother allegedly talking to a male friend in a North Indian state. The woman had allegedly complained about this incident to her husband. The minor told the police that the alleged abuse had begun the next day. She was not given food for a day, after which her father had allegedly raped her in front of her mother in the living room of their home. The entire sequence of abuse was repeated again and again during the latter half of last month, the complainant alleged-she was stripped and beaten before being raped, according to police officers. The complainant allegedly told the officers that on September 30, she had finally attempted to reach out to police from the home of a relative who lives in the same housing society. However, her parents had snatched away the phone and switched it off, she allegedly told police. This was followed by another day of abuse on October 1, and her mother allegedly took photos of the events, the complainant told police. But then she managed to escape again to her relatives home and to call the police helpline number 112. The minor gave the police her address, after which personnel from the jurisdictional police station reached her home and rescued her, police officers said. Mukesh Chaudhary, Deputy Superintendent of Police of the Kutch East Police, told The Indian Express that the father and mother of the complainant had been placed under arrest on the same day after the FIR was registered and evidence was found on the mothers phone that corroborated the account of the complainant. Further investigations were underway, Chaudhary said.

articleTitle: Eye on regulation of student housing, Delhi Govt holds meet with PG owners
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi
description: The law was proposed two days after a five-storey boys’ private PG building collapsed in Southwest Delhi's Satya Niketan on September 6, killing seven people including five Delhi University students.
body_raw: As the Delhi government works on a regulatory framework for students housing accommodation in the Capital, Education Minister Ashish Sood on Monday held consultations with PG owners, operators and managers. Regulating private PGs, addressing safety concerns and expanding student housing have emerged as key components of the Delhi governments proposed Paying Guest Accommodation Regulation and Safety Bill, 2026, officials said on Monday. The law was proposed two days after a five-storey boys private PG building collapsed in Southwest Delhis Satya Niketan on September 6, killing seven people including five Delhi University students. Mandatory registration, safety audits, standard rental agreements and mechanisms to check arbitrary charges are among the measures being considered as part of the proposed regulatory framework, officials said. In a statement issued Monday, the government said the consultation with PG operators was aimed at understanding operational perspectives and addressing key challenges while prioritising student security and basic living standards. Officials said that the need to address the challenges arises owing to the large outstation student population in Delhi, as at least six lakh students come to the Capital annually for higher education. Following the recent unfortunate incident in Delhi, the process of regulating PGs and formulating new laws for them is ongoing. Under this initiative, a few days ago, I had engaged to understand the concerns of the students and residents living in PGs. Today, I met with PG operators, owners, and managers to understand their perspectives and stakes, Sood said in the statement. Before drafting any new law, our government is engaging with everyone through stakeholder consultations. This is true participatory governance-the very model of participatory governance we are working on, he claimed. The consultation comes nearly three weeks after the first meeting of a 20-member High-Powered Committee on Student Accommodation and Safety, chaired by Sood. The committee was constituted to examine the shortage of student housing in Delhi, safety standards and regulation of student accommodation. It is responsible to draft new laws and regulations on PGs, officials said. At its September 15 meeting, the committee discussed mandatory registration and a central database for institutional and private PGs, regulation of lease agreements, curbing arbitrary electricity surcharges and introducing zone-wise rent bands. It also proposed mandatory structural and fire-safety audits, emergency evacuation protocols and regular mock drills for PG operators and students. A centralised digital grievance mechanism was also proposed, through which students would be able to report overcrowding, building safety hazards and lease violations for time-bound resolution. The committee had decided to develop, within 15 days, a portal for PG owners to register their facilities and provide details such as the age and size of the building and fire-safety measures, officials said. A separate portal was proposed to map student data across universities and educational institutions in Delhi. The committee, which has a 60-day deadline to submit its recommendations, also would examine the shortage of university hostels and the possibility of allowing higher floor area ratio for expansion of accommodation on campuses. The Delhi Development Authority DDA and Urban Development Department have been tasked with identifying suitable land parcels for new hostels, while under-utilised government and DDA properties are also to be examined for possible conversion into student housing. Sood said the governments aim was to ensure that students had access to safe and affordable accommodation. Our concern is to ensure that people have access to safe, secure, reliable, and reasonably priced PG accommodations in Delhi, he said. As part of that responsibility, todays Monday discussions were held with the PG operators during this stakeholder consultation, he said.

articleTitle: EC protesters take over central Delhi, Rahul Gandhi stands on barricade
articleFeaturedImageAlt: rahul gandhi
description: Police said paramilitary and local cops have been deployed along several routes in New Delhi district to ensure security during the protests.
body_raw: Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi, and others were detained on Tuesday as the INDIA bloc leaders marched to the Election Commission office, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. Security was stepped up across the New Delhi district, and the MPs were stopped on the way, following which they sat on a dharna. After a face-off with the cops, the MPs and leaders were removed from the spot and carried away in a bus. Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi was joined by Trinamool Congress leader Derek Obrien and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. As police moved in to detain the MPs, Rahul Gandhi climbed onto the barricades and began waving the Tricolour. Police personnel then brought him down and began escorting him towards a bus. Gandhi was seen adhering to Gen-Z lingo at the protest as he carried a poster that read Gyanesh, its done bro He posted the slogan on X,too, adding Its time to resign Gyanesh, its done, bro. Time to resign. IndiaAllianceMarch  - Rahul Gandhi RahulGandhi October 6, 2026 More than five companies of paramilitary personnel, along with local police, have been deployed along the route from Makar Dwar of Parliament to the Election Commission office. Around 140 Opposition MPs are expected to join the march, which is likely to begin between 10.30 am and 11 am. Multi-layered barricading has been put in place outside the main entrance of the Election Commission and around Jantar Mantar. Police said prohibitory orders under Section 163 remain in force in the district and gatherings are not allowed. Opposition steps up protests over electoral rolls The New Delhi district has been witnessing protests since October 2 by the Left and other opposition parties. On October 1, the INDIA bloc announced a joint action plan which included protests across the country, a march by the Opposition MPs to the EC headquarters, and a mega rally in Delhi on November 1. These decisions were taken at a three-and-a-half-hour meeting of the group in Delhi, which was attended by leaders of 19 parties and Independent MP Kapil Sibal. Among the Opposition faces who attended the meeting were Congress leaders Sonia Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi Trinamool Congress TMC chief Mamata Banerjee Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah RJDs Tejashwi Yadav NCP SP MP Supriya Sule PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti CPIM chief M A Baby CPIM-Ls Dipankar Bhattacharya and CPIs P Santosh Kumar. Earlier, around 25 MPs, including top Opposition leaders such as Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Trinamool Congress MPs Abhishek Banerjee and Derek OBrien, were detained and taken to different police stations in buses. Several party workers from the Congress and Samajwadi Party were also detained. 9 FIRs filed in connection with anti-EC protests In connection with protests over the last five days near Jantar Mantar, police have registered nine FIRs under various sections, including those related to violation of prohibitory orders, rioting, and attacking police personnel while they were discharging their duties. Eighteen people have also been arrested, while more than 300 people were detained and later released. Police are also bracing for another protest later this week. The Cockroach Janta Party CJP has given a call for a demonstration at Jantar Mantar, as part of a nation-wide stir, on October 10, demanding the resignation of CEC Kumar. This is the groups second round of protests in the national capital after its July agitation demanding the resignation of then Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-UG paper leak.

articleTitle: Noida mall theft video: Woman allegedly caught stealing ghee, refined oil
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Woman stealing Noida mall video
description: A store employee reportedly said staff had been monitoring the woman after noticing similar incidents over the past month.
body_raw: A video showing a woman being stopped by security at a Noida mall after she was allegedly caught with grocery items in her bag has gone viral on social media. According to multiple reports, the incident took place Sunday evening when the woman visited Le Marche at DLF Mall of India in Sector 18 with her husband. When a security guard allegedly stopped her for a routine bag check, the woman reportedly refused, leading to an argument with store staff. Additional security personnel were then called to the spot. Store staff reportedly reviewed CCTV footage and allegedly found the woman placing a 1-kg pack of ghee and a 1-kg bottle of refined oil into her bag. Caught on camera Videos of the incident, shared in three parts on X, have gone viral and show the woman being escorted back inside the mall by security guards while covering her face with her phone. description: The BJP rejected the allegations as Opposition candidates staged protests and sought repolling in the two Bengal constituencies.
body_raw: As polling continued in West Bengals Nandigram and Rejinagar Assembly bypolls Monday, Opposition candidates and leaders alleged vote-rigging, booth capture, and the removal of their polling agents, with Congress demanding repolling in both seats. While the Bharatiya Janata Party BJP rejected the allegations, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said polling in Nandigram was peaceful. West Bengal is voting in Nandigram and Rejinagar, with both seats having fallen vacant for different reasons. Democracy is being murdered Abdullahil Kafi, Congress candidate in Rejinagar, staged a sit-in protest near the police station alleging that booths had been captured by BJP agents and that the police and administration are biased towards the ruling party. They are not allowing valid voters to cast their votes. Only BJP agents are in the booths. Our agents are driven away. Multiple agents of BJP are inside the booths looting the votes. When I tried to visit some booths, the police shoved me away. Democracy is being murdered, and votes are being looted. We will plan further agitation, Kafi told reporters. Meanwhile, West Bengal state Congress president Subhankar Sarkar demanded a repoll in Nandigram. Through the help of the administration and the police, a system is in place where common voters are not being allowed to cast their votes. Outsiders were brought into Nandigram who are looting the votes in the booths, Sarkar said. In Rejinagar, the situation is the same. Our candidate in Rejinagar was heckled. I spoke with him over the phone. We have videos and other proofs which we have shared with the Election Commission. We demand a repoll in Nandigram, Sarkar added. Senior Congress leader and former Lok Sabha MP Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury protested outside the district magistrates office in Baharampur, alleging vote loot. They are allowing Hindus to vote but not Muslims. In many areas, they are trying to loot votes. Humayun Kabirs arrest is just an eyewash. They BJP want to keep him relevant so that Muslims vote division and polarisation continue, said Chowdhury speaking with media persons. He was referring to the arrest of Aam Janata Unnayan Party AJUP founder Humayun Kabir earlier in the day in Rejinagar. Opposition wants the old days The BJP rejected the Oppositions allegations of vote-rigging and booth capture, accusing the Congress of attempting to cast doubts on the polling process after demanding repolls in the two constituencies. Congress has demanded a repoll in the two seats. They should have done this yesterday. They know they are going to lose, so they are preparing the ground to question the polling process, BJP spokesperson Debjit Sarkar said. The Opposition wants the old days to return when bombs were hurled, men kicked candidates, and cars were vandalised. That is why the Opposition is trying to instigate. But we want violence-free, peaceful polls, which we are witnessing today. We will not allow hooliganism or violence in polls. If they allege that people are not allowed to vote, why are they not going to the election commission? he asked. Nandigram Congress candidate Milan Pradhan also alleged that BJP workers and agents were being threatened. Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, Mamata All India Trinamool Congress candidate in Rejinagar, wrote a letter to the state chief electoral officer, demanding a repoll. We are observing that in several booths, the police administration cast votes in the dead of night and did not allow agents to enter. Additionally, in many areas, the police administration is driving polling agents away from the booths, casting fake votes rigging, and turning voters away from the booths claiming their votes have already been cast, Chowdhury said in his letter, a copy of which is with The Indian Express. Therefore, Sir, it is my urgent request that you kindly take immediate measures to properly arrange for a re-vote, for which I shall be grateful, he added. Law is the same for all Speaking in Nandigram, Chief Minister Adhikari said polling in the seat has been peaceful. In by-polls, generally it is seen that voting percentage is less. But I think 85 per cent of voters will turn out. I will be happy if 90 per cent of voters turn out. In 2016, I won in Nandigram by 82,000 votes. I think this time we will cross the margin, Adhikari said. He also mentioned the arrest of AJUP leader Kabir. Law is the same for all. Even for me. I can cast my vote in my booth, and now I am in the rest house. I cannot visit other booths or campaign. If I break the law, I will be arrested. That is what happened, he added. The police arrested Kabir in Rejinagar after he accused them of interfering with voting at multiple polling stations. Bengal bypolls The Nandigram seat was left vacant after Adhikari, who won from two constituencies in the Assembly elections earlier this year, decided to retain his other seat. Rejinagar became vacant after Kabir resigned from the seat after winning from Naoda as well. Kabirs son, Gulam Nabi Azad, is an AUJP candidate from Rejinagar in Murshidabad district. CPIMs Md Sayeed, Congresss Kafi, and Safiuzzaman Sheikh of the rebel Trinamool faction, Democratic Trinamool Congress, are also contesting the Rejinagar bypolls. The BJP has pitted Hansirani Rath, the mother of Chandranath Rath, Suvendu Adhikaris aide who was murdered, as its candidate in Nandigram. Votes for all the bypolls will be counted on October 9.
