articleTitle: Darya Shipilova: Who was Russian anti-plague lab worker who died? Moscow accused of covering up leak
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Darya Shipilova, russia,
description: Darya Shipilova, 28, worked at Siberia’s Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute and died after developing pneumonia of unknown origin, triggering quarantines and fears of pneumonic plague.
body_raw: Darya Shipilova worked in a place devoted to studying one of the worlds most feared infectious diseases. The 28-year-old laboratory worker was employed at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East, a specialist facility in eastern Russia. She died on October 2 after developing severe pneumonia, according to reports. Russian health authorities have described the illness as pneumonia of unknown aetiology, meaning its cause has not been established, news agency Reuters reported. Her death has since become the centre of a public-health scare in Siberia, after reports circulated that she may have contracted pneumonic plague, the respiratory form of a disease caused by Yersinia pestis. But there is currently no confirmed evidence that Shipilova died from plague or that she contracted an infection through her work. What happened to Darya Shipilova? Shipilovas condition deteriorated rapidly before she was taken to a hospital in Shelekhov, a town near Irkutsk. She died there on October 2, according to Reuters. Unconfirmed reports circulating in Russian media have suggested that she may have been exposed to plague bacteria following an accident involving a test tube at the laboratory. But Russian authorities have not confirmed that account. The Guardian reported that another account linked the onset of her illness to a work trip to Buryatia. Neither explanation has been publicly confirmed by Russian health authorities. Rospotrebnadzor, Russias public-health watchdog, said extensive testing found no microorganisms associated with the patients professional activities. It also said investigators found no incidents at the institute involving pathogenic microorganisms. The institute where she worked The Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute is a specialist facility with a long history of studying dangerous infectious diseases.The Washington Post reported that the institute was established in the 1930s as an anti-plague organisation and later expanded its work to diseases including cholera, brucellosis, tularemia and anthrax. She was working at an institute dedicated to researching plague when she developed severe pneumonia and died. Yet authorities say there is no evidence so far linking her illness to the pathogens handled at her workplace. Did she die from pneumonic plague? It has not been confirmed as yet. Rospotrebnadzor said Shipilova was diagnosed with pneumonia of unknown aetiology and that extensive testing found no microorganisms associated with her professional activities. The Independent and local media have raised the possibility that she died from pneumonic plague, but those reports remain unconfirmed. Why were people quarantined? Authorities placed the hospital in Shelekhov, where Shipilova was treated under quarantine and began monitoring people who had been in contact with her. Anna Popova, head of Rospotrebnadzor, travelled to the Irkutsk region and met regional officials as authorities coordinated their response. Governor Igor Kobzev said identified contacts had been placed under medical observation and that they were showing no signs of illness, with laboratory tests returning negative results. News agency Associated Press reported that two contacts tested positive for a virus that causes a common cold and two others for Covid-19. Other people who were tested were negative, according to the agency. Why are there accusations of a cover-up? The Telegraph reported that local pro-Kremlin websites and some local officials deleted posts referring to the suspected plague case. One local authority reportedly advised residents against travelling to Shelekhov after unofficial information about a possible plague infection emerged, before the post was removed. The Guardian reported that Alexey Tsydenov, head of neighbouring Buryatia, initially wrote that Shipilova had died of plague before editing his post to say she had possibly died of the disease. Authorities in Baikalsk also briefly advised residents not to travel to Shelekhov, citing unofficial information about a possible plague infection, before deleting the post. Hamish de Bretton Gordon, a former commanding officer of the UKs Joint Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Regiment, told The Telegraph that Russian authorities had clammed up over the incident. We should be worried about whats happened in Russia because plague has a long history of causing mayhem, he said.For a lab technician working with plague to die from plague is extraordinary. She should have been vaccinated, there should have been medical countermeasures, he said. What do Russian authorities say? Russian authorities have repeatedly rejected speculation that there is a confirmed plague outbreak. Rospotrebnadzor said Shipilova died from pneumonia of unknown aetiology and that tests found no microorganisms linked to her professional work. The agency also said it had found no incidents involving pathogenic microorganisms at the institute, Reuters reported. Kobzev said there had been no new cases of anti-plague institute staff seeking medical attention and described the situation as stable, according to Reuters. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov urged the public and media to rely on Rospotrebnadzors official statements rather than rumours and speculation. Former Rospotrebnadzor chief Gennady Onishchenko also said the infection was most likely not the plague, CNN reported, while cautioning that even if plague were confirmed, he did not expect it to spread. What happened to people who came into contact with her? AP reported that two people who had been in contact with Shipilova tested positive for a virus that causes a common cold and two others tested positive for Covid-19. Other people tested were negative, according to the agency. Kobzev said those identified as contacts were under medical observation and had shown no symptoms, with laboratory testing returning negative results. What is pneumonic plague? Pneumonic plague is one of the three main forms of plague caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. It affects the lungs and can be transmitted from person to person through respiratory droplets. It is the most serious form of plague and can become fatal quickly if untreated, but it can be treated with antibiotics when detected early. The disease is associated with the same bacterium that caused historic outbreaks of bubonic plague, including the Black Death. Plague remains endemic in parts of Siberia and the Russian Far East, where Yersinia pestis occurs naturally among small wild mammals and their fleas. Human cases in Russia are rare. Why is the US monitoring the case? US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was monitoring the situation but did not believe there was cause for alarm.Were watching and monitoring it closely. I dont think its cause for alarm, Rubio said. He added that if an infection were to spread, it could spread quickly. The Financial Times reported that US officials were closely monitoring the suspected case, while The Guardian reported that the US was watching developments because of the potential for a respiratory infection to spread. articleTitle: Family member held for murder of two elderly women in Baramati, robbing gold jewellery
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police detained Vikas Ladkat after finding his movements suspicious.
description: Pune rural police Superintendent Sandeep Singh Gill formed eight teams to crack the murders.
body_raw: Pune rural police have arrested a family member in connection with the murder of two elderly women at their house in Baramati. Police identified the accused as Vikas alias Appa Rajendra Ladkat 25, a resident of Sherechiwadi village in Baramati taluka of Pune district. Indumati Maruti Ladkat 75 and Krushnabai Kundalik Ladkat 60 were found dead, with their throats slit, in an open space near their house in Sherechiwadi on September 29. About 50 grams of gold ornaments on their bodies were missing. Indumatis son Ganesh Ladkat 45 lodged the FIR at the Supa police station in Pune rural. Initial probe revealed that the two elderly women were murdered while they were sleeping, robbery being the motive. Pune rural police Superintendent Sandeep Singh Gill formed eight teams to crack the murders. Police teams checked about 200 history sheeters in Ahilyanagar, Solapur, Satara, Kolhapur, Pune and Beed districts in Maharashtra and Nipani in Karnataka. Police also checked CCTV cameras installed at various locations for leads. Simultaneously, the police also kept watch on the movements of people in Sherechiwadi village, especially those residing near the deceased women. Police detained Vikas Ladkat after finding his movements suspicious. During interrogation, Vikas admitted that he murdered the two women, who were his relatives, by attacking them with an axe and then looted their gold ornaments, a press release issued on Monday stated. Police arrested Vikas under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS sections 103 1 murder, 309 4, 332 c, on October 4. Police also recovered the robbed ornaments from his possession. Assistant police inspector Shashikant Shelke of Supa police station said, A court has remanded the accused in police custody for five days. He is a distant family member of the deceased woman. Probe so far has revealed that he was debt-ridden. So he killed the elderly women when they were alone and robbed their gold jewellery. In the past he was booked in a criminal case when he was a minor. Further investigation is on.

articleTitle: ‘If citizens being removed, what is purpose of SIR?’ Bombay High Court asks Election Commission
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bombay High Court questions purpose of Special Intensive Revision exercise if citizens face exclusion from voters list, flags voter Catch-22 over rejected address change forms
description: Hearing a petition where names of six members of a Goa family had been deleted from the electoral rolls after their Form 8 applications for a change of address were rejected, the High Court of Bombay at Goa said the voter is facing “a Catch-22 situation” in this matter
body_raw: Stating that the Election Commission has an obligation to ensure all citizens are on the electoral rolls, the High Court of Bombay at Goa on Monday asked what the purpose of this entire SIR process if citizens are being removed from the voters list. If citizens are excluded, what will we do with SIR? the HC asked. Hearing a petition where names of six members of a family had been deleted from the electoral rolls after their Form 8 applications for a change of address were rejected, the HC said the voter is facing a Catch-22 situation in this matter. A division bench of Justices Amit S Jamsandekar and Valmiki Menezes said, If a gentleman comes and says I have shifted, I am giving you ECI Form 8 for change of address. You cannot tell him I will not hear you.You cant do that. because the roll that is being referred to in Rule 21 Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 is the existing roll, not the draft roll. It said, Everything must be seen qua the existing roll, otherwise the voter has absolutely no way out of this. look at this complete Catch-22 situation before him. If he gives Form 6, it is a false declaration. He gives Form 8.you say I cannot accept it and you must give the enumeration. He says I dont want to give the enumeration. But Rule 21 says you have to hear him before removing his name. not from the draft, from the original roll. The bench said the ECI has an obligation to ensure all the citizens are on the list. If citizens are excluded, what will we do with SIR? If citizens are being removed from the list, then what is the purpose of this entire SIR process?, it asked. The petitioners-Paresh Salgaoncar and five members of his family-had moved to a new house in the same Santa Cruz Assembly constituency eight years ago and were instructed by the booth-level officer BLO to submit Form 8 for change of address. The petitioners submitted that the Assistant Electoral Registration Officer informed them that their EPICs Electors Photo Identity Cards had been deleted from the rolls and consequently, their Form 8 applications could not be processed. The only recourse available was to submit Form 6 which is for new voters since there was no option in ERONET for reviewing or restoring the deleted EPICs. No voter should sign a false declaration .in the enumeration form, the declarations are such that I have to declare in a pre-filled form for a ward, where I used to reside.I have to make a declaration that please include me in that same place, and I state that I am not there in any other place. How will a person make such a declaration when he knows he is in another place? The moment he makes such a declaration, he is open to prosecution, the court said. We are asking this. Why will he sign this? This is a false statement.Why should he give a false declaration? No voter should sign this, the bench said. The Election Commission of India ECI told the court that the guidelines clearly state that if someone has not submitted the enumeration form, their name is liable to be deleted from the roll. In case an elector is unable to submit their filled-in enumeration form within the specified time, they may fill Form 6 along with declaration for inclusion during the claims and objection period.Ordinarily, Form 8 is by a person whose name is there in the draft roll, but says I am no longer residing here and I have shifted. He submits his Form 8 because it refers to an existing residence on the roll. So, if you are not there on the draft roll only, what entry am I transferring under Form 8? I cant transfer a non-existent entry, the counsel for ECI said.

articleTitle: Suryakumar Yadav asked to confirm availability for Ranji Trophy, and then snubbed; Yashasvi Jaiswal picked
articleFeaturedImageAlt: FILE: Suryakumar Yadav in action. (CREIMAS for BCCI)
description: While Jaiswal found a place in the squad, Suryakumar was overlooked for the match scheduled from October 11 to 15.
body_raw: The Mumbai selectors have not picked former India T20 captain Suryakumar Yadav for their Ranji Trophy season opener despite the veteran confirming his availability for the same a week ago. The selection committee of the Mumbai Cricket Association MCA announced a 16-member squad on Monday. Both Suryakumar, under whose captaincy India had successfully defended their T20 World Cup crown earlier this year, and Yashasvi Jaiswal had informed the panel that they were available. But only the latter finds his name in the list. Chief selector Rajesh Pawar said Suryakumars lack of recent red-ball match practice was behind their decision. He is a very big player. But he hasnt played red-ball cricket in the last one and a half years. Should he play a few red-ball games, he can definitely come into the side, Pawar said. It was just last week that Suryakumar was asked about his availability and willingness to play Ranji Trophy, and he took a day before confirming it. However, MCA officials claim they tried to reach out to him many times but he didnt respond to their calls. Mumbai will take on Chandigarh in their season opener at the Wankhede Stadium from October 11-14. The selection committee has appointed Siddhesh Lad as skipper for the season with opener Ayush Mhatre as his vice-captain. Speaking on Jaiswals return, Pawar said, Its a good thing that Yashasvi is coming to play for Mumbai. He also needs match practice. When asked, he said he is available, so thats good for the team. There is a chance he might be in either the senior or the A team touring New Zealand so we only announced the squad for the first match. The squad features India batter Sarfaraz Khan, who recently played for the Rest of India side that beat Jammu and Kashmir in the Irani Cup. Also included is Shams Mulani, whose all-round performance against Australia A helped India A clinch their two-match unofficial Test series 1-0. Mhatre, who led India to the Under-19 World Cup title earlier this year, has been rewarded for his impressive leadership with the vice-captaincy. Mumbai will miss the services of pacer Shardul Thakur, who got injured a few weeks ago. Mumbai squad Siddhesh Lad capt, Ayush Mhatre vice-capt, Shams Mulani, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Tanush Kotian, Atharva Ankolekar, Divyaansh Saxena, Tushar Deshpande, Musheer Khan, Mohit Avasthi, Sarfaraz Khan, Sylvester DSouza, Suved Parkar, Onkar Tarmale, Aakash Anand wk, Hardik Tamore wk.

articleTitle: Keralam to install Rs 10 sanitary napkin vending machines at public places
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Women and Child Development, Labour, Animal Husbandry and Dairy Development Minister Bindu Krishna will inaugurate the project at the Thampanoor KSRTC Bus Terminal in Thiruvananthapuram at 5 pm on Tuesday.
description: As part of the pilot project, sanitary napkin vending machines and incinerators will be installed at 14 KSRTC terminals and depots across the state, the release said.
body_raw: Sanitary napkins will soon be available through vending machines at select public places in Keralam, with the Women and Child Development Department launching an initiative aimed at improving access to menstrual hygiene products for women and girls during travel. The initiative, called WOMN - Women on the Move  Menstrual Need-s, will begin on Tuesday as part of the state governments 100-day action programme, according to an official press release. As part of the pilot project, sanitary napkin vending machines and incinerators will be installed at 14 KSRTC terminals and depots across the state, the release said. Each packet will contain three sanitary napkins and will cost Rs 10. Incinerators will be provided at the locations to facilitate the disposal of used sanitary napkins, it said. The project will subsequently target major tourist destinations, KSRTC terminals and depots and other public places across the state, according to the department. Women and Child Development Minister Bindu Krishna will inaugurate the project at the Thampanoor KSRTC Bus Terminal in Thiruvananthapuram on Tuesday. With PTI inputs

articleTitle: Sharat Saxena starts work 27 days post spine surgery; expert explains recovery in the 70s
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sharat Saxena
description: The actor’s quick return to work after a major spine procedure has experts weighing in on what recovery really involves
body_raw: Veteran actor Sharat Saxena, 76, recently underwent a six-hour lumbar spine surgery and is back to work. What a wonderful feeling to be able to work again. Started working again, 27 days after spine surgery, he wrote in a post on Instagram. Dr Amogh Zawar, consultant, spine surgery, KIMS Hospitals Thane, told indianexpress.com that resuming work just over 25 days is possible in a few cases. Yes, in select cases, patients can return to work within a few weeks of spine surgery, particularly when the procedure is minimally invasive, and recovery is progressing well. However, there is no universal timeline for returning to work. It depends on the type of surgery, the spinal condition being treated, the patients age and health, and the physical demands of their work, said Dr Zawar. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. What factors determine how quickly someone can return to normal activities after spine surgery? According to Dr Zawar, pain control, mobility, muscle strength, neurological recovery, and the nature of the surgery are key factors. A patient with a less extensive procedure may regain mobility relatively quickly, while someone undergoing a more complex surgery may need several weeks or months. Rehabilitation and following post-operative precautions also play an important role, emphasised Dr Zawar.         View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Sharat Saxena sharatsaxena Does returning to work within 27 days mean the spine has completely healed? Not necessarily. Being fit to resume selected activities is different from complete healing. Patients may feel considerably better and become independent in their daily activities while the operated tissues continue to heal. Even after returning to work, they may need to avoid heavy lifting, prolonged sitting, excessive bending or other strenuous movements for some time, said Dr Zawar. The expert noted that the return must be assessed based on the specific demands of the job. An actor may need to deal with long hours, travel, prolonged standing or physical movements, depending on the role. A gradual return, with modifications wherever required, is generally safer than immediately resuming the full workload, asserted Dr Zawar. What to note? The focus should be on recovery rather than simply meeting a deadline. Patients should follow their surgeons advice, continue prescribed rehabilitation and increase activity gradually. New or worsening pain, weakness, numbness or difficulty walking should not be ignored. An early return can be possible for some patients, but 27 days should not be considered a standard recovery period for everyone, said Dr Zawar. articleTitle: Sentence tossed after AI video of victim ‘forgiving’ his killer is played
articleFeaturedImageAlt: stacey wales, ai
description: The three-judge panel reaffirmed the conviction of Gabriel Horcasitas, 55, who had been sentenced to 10 1/2 years in prison, but said that he must be resentenced in the 2021 road-rage shooting death of Christopher Pelkey, 37.
body_raw: An appeals court in Arizona on Wednesday threw out the prison sentence of a man convicted of manslaughter after a video created by artificial intelligence depicting the victim forgiving his killer was played in court. The three-judge panel reaffirmed the conviction of Gabriel Horcasitas, 55, who had been sentenced to 10 12 years in prison, but said that he must be resentenced in the 2021 road-rage shooting death of Christopher Pelkey, 37. The judges concluded that the sentencing judge committed a fundamental error by allowing and relying on an AI video that generated a likeness of Pelkeys voice and appearance. The appeals court found the video did not reflect actual events while presenting statements in the footage as if they were coming directly from the victim. The appeals court noted the use of the AI-generated video posed a novel legal issue and that no prior Arizona case had addressed the admissibility of such a depiction of a victim during sentencing. The video was used with victim-impact statements made by members of Pelkeys family and friends in the courtroom during the sentencing of Horcasitas last year. At the sentencing, Pelkeys older sister, Stacey Wales, presented the AI video depicting Pelkey addressing Horcasitas. I believe in forgiveness and in God who forgives, the video said. The video also portrayed Pelkey as addressing the court, saying, This here is a true representation of who I was. The sentencing judge, Todd F. Lang of Maricopa County Superior Court, praised the video, saying, I loved that AI. He called it genuine and noted that the victim was allowed to speak from his heart. He then imposed the maximum sentence, which was more than the nine years that prosecutors had sought. Critics have argued that the introduction of AI in legal proceedings can open the door to manipulation and deception, compounding the already emotional process of giving victim-impact statements. The appeals court held that a victims right to speak cannot trample a defendants right to be sentenced based on accurate and reliable information. The video erases the interpretive distance between the familys belief about what the victim would have said and the victims own voice and opinions, the judges wrote. They decided that the reliance on the video made the sentencing procedure fundamentally unfair. Lawyers for Pelkey and Horcasitas did not immediately respond to requests for comment Sunday. Wales was preparing her own victim-impact statement for two years, she told The New York Times last year, but believed that it was missing a critical element. I kept hearing what Chris would say, she told the Times. Wales said that her husband and the couples longtime business partner had used AI to help corporate clients with presentations, including one featuring the likeness of a companys CEO who had died years ago. With the help of her husband and business partner, she took Pelkeys voice from a YouTube video of him speaking after completing treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder at a facility for veterans, she said. For his face and torso, they used a poster of Pelkey from a funeral service, digitally trimming his thick beard, removing his glasses and editing out a logo from his cap, she said. Wales said that she had written the script that was read by her brothers AI likeness. I know that AI can be used nefariously, and its uncomfortable for some, Wales said last year. But this was just another tool to use to tell Chris story. Wales was not immediately available for comment Sunday. On Nov. 13, 2021, Pelkey was stopped at a red light in Chandler, a Phoenix suburb, when Horcasitas pulled up behind him and honked. That caused Pelkey to leave his vehicle and approach Horcasitas car and gesture with his arms as if to say, What the heck? according to a probable cause statement. Horcasitas then fatally shot Pelkey in the chest. The case will be returned to Maricopa County Superior Court for a new sentencing hearing, without the AI-generated video of Pelkey giving his statement.

articleTitle: When did India begin latest round of talks with Russia, Ukraine? Jaishankar reveals
articleFeaturedImageAlt: **EDS: THIRD PARTY IMAGE** In this image posted on Oct. 5, 2026, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar along with Institute of Economic Growth (IEG) President NK Singh, left, and former Singapore Foreign Minister George Yeo, right, during the concluding session of the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave (KEC 2026) on ‘India and the World: Adaptive by Design’, in New Delhi. (@DrSJaishankar/X via PTI Photo)
description: Jaishankar said New Delhi started the latest round of conversations with both sides in July this year, after commercial ships came under attack from both sides in the Black Sea.
body_raw: A day after stating that India is in touch with both Ukraine and Russia over the ongoing conflict, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Monday spelt out the kind of conversations India was having with the two sides amid evolving dynamics. However, he emphasised that while its not an easy situation, it would be a big positive even if Kyiv and Moscow were to agree on something of a limited nature. The minister said that from the very beginning, India has held that this conflict is unlikely to be resolved on the battlefield. Therefore, it was important to have negotiations between the parties. There were actually negotiations in the early stages of the conflict. Though we have been maintaining for some time that both parties should come to the table, and there were a number of conferences where countries gathered to express their support for peace, but often they would gather in the absence of Russia, he said, in reference to initiatives like the Swiss peace conference. However, he added that New Delhi has always believed that there was no point of having a gathering dealing with the Ukraine conflict where Russia is not there. He said New Delhi started the latest round of conversations with both sides in July this year, after commercial ships came under attack from both sides in the Black Sea. In fact, after losing Indian sailors in such attacks, New Delhi had strongly conveyed its condemnation to both sides and also summoned envoys to register protest. In July, there were attacks on civilian shipping by both Russia and Ukraine. And in the course of those attacks, some Indian sailors were killed, some were injured. We regard these attacks as completely unacceptable, whether it is in the Black Sea, the Red Sea, or the Gulf. So, we protested very strongly to the Russians, to the Ukrainians. I myself took it up with the foreign ministers of both countries. We started getting active initially to secure the maritime shipping and the mariners involved in that, he said. Jaishankar added that those conversations brought out the nature of the cargo which was being shipped. And there was the concern expressed about the grain exports which had come to a halt in the Black Sea. So the conversation developed into whether non-attack on shipping is good, but is there a possibility of facilitating the shipment of grain. it got linked to energy. So, it became a somewhat broader conversation, added the minister. The conversations started with Prime Minister Narendra Modis meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek in August. After that, Jaishankar went to Kyiv to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, which was followed by another discussion between Modi and Putin in New Delhi on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit. We still keep in touch with both sides. Its not obviously an easy situation. Its not something which anybody can say with a high degree of confidence that something is going to come out. But it seems definitely an effort worth making, he says, adding that resolving concerns about grain, fertiliser and fuel are in Indias as well as the Global Souths interest. We have the interests of the parties themselves that if they can even agree on something of a limited nature, we feel that in the given circumstance thats a big positive, he said. He also spoke about the need to fix the United Nations, not work around it, and how this was going to be an age of flux for the world, with conflicts and tariff volatility making it turbulent, underlining that responding to the challenges emerging out of the choppy waters is the task at hand. Im very confident that we will rise to the challenges, Jaishankar said during an interactive session at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi, where he shared the dais with former foreign minister of Singapore, George Yong Boon Yeo, during the closing session. The minister, however, said that as Indias record shows, we have been able to rise to the challenges, whether it was Covid, or the challenge of a double conflict today. The challenges of energy, food, fertilisers - we need to factor them into our thinking, plan and respond. That in a sense is the task before us. And Im very confident that we will rise to the challenge, he said. Jaishankar also spoke about championing the voice of the Global South. The Global South expects India to articulate on the world stage, he said. On reforms needed for the United Nations and other multilateral institutions, Jaishankar said, The UN is gridlocked, adding that a few countries were resisting its reforms. However, he said that the US is one of Indias principal strategic partners - our largest economic account, our biggest trade account, it is a very major critical defence partner.

articleTitle: A judge must be impartial, never indifferent: Justice Vikram Nath
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Justice Nath is also the executive chairman of the National Legal Services Authority. (Image Enhanced using AI)
description: Justice Nath also said courts must pay attention to how those who pass through the system experience justice.
body_raw: Judges are not appointed to be charitable, and compassion in adjudication is not favour and it is not leniency, Justice Vikram Nath said while delivering the second Prof. Dr N R Madhava Menon Memorial Lecture in New Delhi on Monday. He said, Impartiality and indifference are not the same thing. The blind fold on Lady Justice does not mean she cannot see. It means she does not look at who stands before her before deciding what is right. She still weighs and weighs with care. A judge must be impartial but never indifferent. Justice Nath, who is also the executive chairman of the National Legal Services Authority, delivered the annual lecture on the topic Judging with Compassion Human Understanding in the Practice of Law. Chief Justice of India CJI Surya Kant inaugurated the session. Justice Nath also said courts must pay attention to how those who pass through the system experience justice. For the survivor made to relive her trauma in the witness box, or the litigant who cannot follow the language of the proceedings, the process is what justice actually feels like, he said. We must ask whether, for too many, it has itself become a trauma, he said. The Supreme Court judge also highlighted that courts must see the gap between formal equality and experienced equality. He gave the example of undertrials granted bail on identical conditions, where one walks out and another stays in prison because he cannot furnish sureties. On paper the law treated them equally. In life, it did not. During his address, CJI Kant underlined the importance of legal scholarship saying that while courts hear individual disputes, research helps show how judicial decisions affect peoples lives long after a case is over. The scholar who follows the victim beyond the courtroom, asking whether the compensation is actually paid, whether a brief family receives the support it needs, and whether victims are truly hurt.it is scholarship that gathers those 10,000 orders into one picture. and shows us whom our well-meant judgments may have left behind, CJI Kant said. On cases involving survivors of sexual violence and child witnesses, Justice Nath said that a trauma-informed courtroom is not a softer courtroom. Compassion, he added, does not tell us who should win. It tells us how carefully we must understand what winning and losing mean.

articleTitle: ‘Sent 6.3 ft cake in tempo’: How Tips Music won over Subhash Ghai after Saudagar rejection
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ramesh Taurani, Subhash Ghai, Prakash Jha and Mahesh Thakur at an event
description: In a recent interview, Kumar Taurani and Ramesh Taurani recalled why Subhash Ghai did not give Tips the music rights to his 1991 film Saudagar. They also revealed how they convinced the filmmaker to rope in Nadeem-Shravan for Pardes.
body_raw: Tips Music, co-founded by brothers Kumar Taurani and Ramesh Taurani, has released several hit soundtracks from Subhash Ghais films, including Khal Nayak 1993, Pardes 1997, Taal 1999 and Yaadein 2001. In a recent interview, the Taurani brothers recalled why Ghai did not give Tips the music rights to his 1991 film Saudagar. They also revealed how they convinced the filmmaker to rope in composer duo Nadeem-Shravan for Pardes. When the Saudagar cassette was released, we sent Subhash ji a 6-foot-3-inch cake During a chat with Komal Nahta, Ramesh Taurani recalled approaching Subhash Ghai before he sold the music of his film Saudagar to HMV. Subhash jis film Saudagars music wasnt sold yet, but he told me that he had commited to HMV. I asked him to give the music to us, so he asked me to come next time. He gave the music to them. When the Saudagar cassette was released, we sent Subhash ji a 6-foot-3-inch cake, which said, Saudagar, Saudagar, TIPS ke saath Sauda kar, he shared. When the cake reached his house, the filmmaker was very happy and promised to sign Tips Music for his next film. My associate went to deliver the cake, but it wasnt fitting in a car, so it got delivered in a tempo. He Subhash Ghai went to his house, he was so happy, and he called all the distributors to his house at night. He praised me in front of them, saying that this man doesnt have my music or anything, but still sent such a beautiful letter to me with a cake, Ramesh said. Later, Ramesh Taurani reached out to Subhash Ghai for the music rights of Khalnayak. Then, I went to him for Khalnayak. Subhash ji told me that all the distributors had asked him to take Nadeem-Shravan instead of Laxmikant-Pyarelal for the film. Subhash ji called Nadeem, but he kept negotiating on the price. Subhash ji got angry that he was not talking about music but only money. He eventually went to Laxmikant ji and said that hes ready to pay double the amount. He signed him on by paying a token amount of Rs 5 lakh, he recalled. While Ramesh lied to his brother Kumar Taurani about the actual price demanded by Laxmikant, the success of the song Choli Ke Peeche Kya Hai made everything fruitful. Finally, Laxmi ji said that I will not take less than Rs 1 crore. I asked him to take Rs 70, 80 lakhs. Kumar had said that we wont pay more than Rs 75 lakhs. I gave him a nod for Rs 1 crore. When I came back, I told Kumar that the deal was done in Rs 81 lakhs. He complained why I paid Rs 6 lakhs over and above the decided amount. As soon as I left Subhash jis office, the news was everywhere in the media, Khalnayaks music has been sold at Rs 1 crore. I told Kumar that it is false news, he said. The producer continued, When Choli Ke Peeche Kya Hai was released, it was a superhit the same day without any promotions. We released the song in the morning and it was being played in a party at night. I told Kumar that we will have to pay Rs 10 lakhs more because the song is already a hit. Years later, Subhash Ghai considered Nadeem-Shravan for Pardes, but his previous experience with the duo made him wary of negotiating their fees. Later, when Trimurti and its music flopped, Subhash Ghai asked for my advice for his film Pardes. He took the names of 2-3 music directors and asked for my suggestion, I told him to take Nadeem-Shravan. He then told me the Saudagar story. I gave him the guarantee that Nadeem will not talk money with you he will just received whatever youll give, Ramesh Taurani shared. Ramesh further added, I spoke to Nadeem and told him to do Subhash jis film without talking about his fees, and he agreed. He said, You will give me the money, na. He had the perspective that if hes giving great music, he should get his due. Everyone used to complain that his music is repetitive, but still everyone went back to him because it used to work. The best part about Pardes music was that it had Subhash Ghais touch. The music of Pardes, Khalnayak and Saudagar, all directed by filmmaker Subhash Ghai, was hugely successful.

articleTitle: Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd line commissioned, train operations to improve on Pune-Daund rail route
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd line commissioned to improve train operations and ease congestion on the Pune-Daund rail route. (Image: Central Railway)
description: The Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd line has been commissioned on the Pune-Daund rail route, improving train operations, freight movement and railway capacity while helping ease congestion at Pune station.
body_raw: Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd railway line commissioned The Central Railway CR has commissioned Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd railway line in Pune. The move is expected to improve train operations and increase capacity on the Pune-Daund rail route. This new railway line is also likely to improve the movement of both passenger and freight trains and provide greater operational flexibility in the Pune railway network. It will also help in reducing congestion and enable smoother movement of freight rakes. Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd line to improve train movement The commissioning of the third Ghorpuri-Hadapsar line is expected to provide a dedicated transfer route between the rake maintenance depot and the proposed Hadapsar Satellite Terminal. This will allow such movements to take place without affecting operations on the UP and DOWN main lines. The arrangement is expected to facilitate the introduction of new train services from Hadapsar. New line to reduce congestion at Pune railway yard According to Dr Swapnil Nila, Chief Public Relations Officer CPRO of CR, the Ghorpuri-Hadapsar 3rd line will serve as an alternate shunting neck for rake formation, sorting, engine and brake-van reversal and other shunting activities.This will help reduce the detention of trains on the main line and improve punctuality. Overall, it will help in decongestion of Pune station by facilitating transfer and operational activities through the Hadapsar Satellite Terminal, the CPRO said in a statement. Major signalling and track works completed Several works were carried out as part of the project, including alterations to signalling and interlocking systems at Pune and Hadapsar. At Pune, 32 new or altered routes, six new or altered point machines, nine new or altered signals and 11 new or altered tracks were completed. At Hadapsar, the existing Kyosan K5D electronic interlocking was altered. The work also included 28 new or altered routes, one new or altered point machine and six new or altered signals. Other works included replacement of insulated overlaps and section insulators, installation of new portals, provision of AC brackets in turnout areas and four DC track circuits. 900 metres of contact wire replaced As part of the work, around 900 metres of damaged contact wire was replaced, restoring the speed potential on the affected section from 75 kmph to 130 kmph.Rail renewal, tamping, distressing, greasing, packing and welding works were also carried out. The works were completed over a span of 15 days using equipment including track relaying machines, Duomatic machines, Poclain machines, Hydra cranes, JCBs and gas-cutting equipment. A total of 745 personnel, including 485 contractual workers and 260 departmental staff, were deployed for the project.

articleTitle: ‘Won’t be able to step out of house’: Bengal CM warns Mamata Banerjee
articleFeaturedImageAlt: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari, former CM and TMC leader Mamata Banerjee. (PTI, ANI Photos)
description: Suvendu Adhikari's statement came after Banerjee sought that her 2021 leg injury medical records be made public
body_raw: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday warned his predecessor Mamata Banerjee against digging too deep into the disclosure of her 2021 leg injury medical records, stating that more such documents could be made public if required. The remarks came hours after Banerjee served a legal notice on SSKM Hospital and Bangur Institute of Neurosciences seeking an explanation over how her medical records relating to the 2021 Nandigram incident were disclosed publicly without permission. Addressing the media, Adhikari said, Do not poke around too much. If I start showing the X-ray plates and MRI reports, you will not be able to step out of your house. If necessary, I will say where I got the records from. The papers were not at SSKM. It was not supposed to be at SSKM. I will tell her lawyer not to dig too deep into this issue. She had thought she would become chief minister for a fourth term. So, she had left all the documents in her drawer in her chamber at the Chief Ministers Office at Nabanna, Adhikari said. He did not, however, specify whether the medical records had been obtained from Banerjees office or residence. This comes a few days after Adhikari claimed that Mamata had faked her leg injury during campaigning in Nandigram in 2021. At a press conference a few days ago, he had held up a document saying it was the March 11, 2021, report of the Department of Radio Diagnosis of Bangur Institute of Neurosciences, which showed no evidence of a fracture. The state government would launch a fresh inquiry into her false claims of leg injury during the 2021 assembly poll campaign, Adhikari had said. Following this, Banerjees lawyer Arka Nag sent the notice through email to the director and medical superintendent of SSKM and the head of the neurology department at Bangur Institute of Neurosciences, seeking an explanation on how his clients medical records reached Adhikari and were subsequently made public.

articleTitle: How skipping breakfast for a month affects men and women differently
articleFeaturedImageAlt: breakfast
description: A gastroenterologist explains the health effects of skipping breakfast every day, who should avoid it, and whether it really helps with weight loss
body_raw: Does skipping breakfast every day for a month affect men and women differently? Thats the question we asked Dr Saiprasad Lad, consultant gastroenterologist, Wockhardt Hospitals, Mumbai Central, who affirmed that it can but added that the effects will vary between individuals. Breakfast is the first chance to replenish energy after fasting overnight. Regularly skipping it may cause blood sugar fluctuations, increased hunger later in the day, overeating, fatigue, irritability, and trouble concentrating. Some people delay their first meal as part of intermittent fasting. However, doing this without planning the days nutrition can have unexpected consequences, said Dr Lad. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Dr Lad noted how women tend to be more sensitive to energy balance and hormonal changes. For some women, regularly skipping breakfast may lead to mood swings, irregular eating habits, and worsen blood sugar control, especially if they have conditions like PCOS or diabetes, said Dr Lad. Men might handle occasional breakfast skipping a bit better, he asserted. Still, if it leads to excessive hunger, large evening meals, or poor food choices, it can negatively impact metabolism, energy levels, and weight management. Ultimately, the overall quality of the diet is more important than whether breakfast is consumed, said Dr Lad. What happens if someone skips breakfast for an entire month? The effects over a month depend on the persons lifestyle and eating habits. Some might experience reduced energy, headaches, lower productivity, or increased cravings for sugary and high-calorie foods later in the day. Others may not notice obvious symptoms but could still be missing out on essential nutrients if breakfast is not replaced with balanced meals later. People with diabetes, acid reflux, or certain digestive issues may find that regularly skipping breakfast worsens their symptoms, said Dr Lad. Who should avoid skipping breakfast? Dr Lad stressed that children, adolescents, pregnant women, people with diabetes on medication, individuals with recurrent acidity, and those with physically demanding jobs should not regularly skip breakfast. These groups are more likely to face negative effects like low blood sugar, low energy, or worsening digestive symptoms if they go too long without eating, said Dr lad. If someone is trying to lose weight, is skipping breakfast a good strategy? Not necessarily, affirmed Dr Lad. Weight loss depends on maintaining a sustainable calorie deficit and following a nutritious eating pattern, rather than just missing one meal. Skipping breakfast can backfire if it leads to overeating later in the day or frequent snacking on high-calorie foods. A better approach is to choose a balanced breakfast with protein, fibre, and healthy fats, as this helps improve satiety and supports better appetite control throughout the day. If someone prefers intermittent fasting, they should plan it carefully to ensure their nutritional needs are met, said Dr Lad. articleTitle: Seven-year-old died in Andhra after anti-malaria dose. Now top court asks High Court to monitor probe
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court took cognizance of the matter and directed the Andhra Pradesh High Court to closely monitor the investigation into the girl's death.
description: The girl was among 70 people, including 15 children, from her village who were hospitalised early September. Taking suo motu cognizance of the death, CJI Surya Kant has asked the HC to monitor the probe ordered by the state government
body_raw: In the last week of August, a seven-year-old girl was handed out an anti-malaria tablet in Andhra Pradeshs Polavaram district during a drive against the mosquito-borne illness in her village. A few days later, along with 70 people in her village, she was hospitalised. While the rest of them recovered, the girl, Madivi Jamuna, died during treatment. A month later, the Supreme Court took cognizance of the matter and directed the Andhra Pradesh High Court to closely monitor the investigation into the girls death. Several villagers of Gollaguppa village in Yetapaka mandal in Polavaram fell ill after consuming chloroquine tablets during a drive that was carried out after reports of malaria cases. The girl, a Class 2 student, developed complications on August 31 and died on September 2. Taking suo motu cognisance of her death, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has asked the HC to monitor the probe ordered by the state government. Meanwhile, an investigation team is awaiting detailed reports from different laboratories, including the Andhra Pradesh Forensic Science Laboratory in Amaravati, to check if the batch of anti-malarial tablets was contaminated. On September 1 and 2, at least 70 people, including many children, were hospitalised at primary health centres in Polavaram. They were later moved to Bhadrachalam Area Hospital in neighbouring Telangana where all of them recovered and were discharged the next day. The girl, however, died at the hospital. The village is located on the Andhra Pradesh-Telangana border. CM ordered probe Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu had ordered a probe into the matter. District Collector K Dinesh Kumar said two villagers had tested positive for malaria, following which officials conducted the drive. As per the FIR, Jamuna fell ill and lost consciousness a day after taking the tablet. She was among the 15 children from the village who fell ill. Health officials said that the chloroquine tablets had been distributed in age-appropriate doses in accordance with medical and health department protocols and that quality-control tests conducted on the medication had given satisfactory results.
