articleTitle: Diego Forlan on Indian football: ‘Talented young players, need stronger academies & league’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uruguay coach Diego Forlan in action. (AP)
description: The 2010 FIFA World Cup Golden Ball winner said that playing international friendlies against stronger opposition like Brazil and Uruguay would benefit the Blue Tigers in the long run.
body_raw: After Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti caused quite a stir last month when he said India did not have a footballing culture, Uruguay coach Diego Forlan said that while the main sport in the country was cricket, India still had a lot of young talented football players. Your main sport is cricket, so its different. Football has been here for many years, of course, but its not the main sport. But you have a lot of young talented players, Forlan said, speaking on the eve of the India vs Uruguay match. The 2010 FIFA World Cup Golden Ball winner said that playing international friendlies against stronger opposition like Brazil and Uruguay would benefit the Blue Tigers in the long run. I think this kind of game, playing against Brazil, Uruguay, and also having a strong league, would improve the development of young players. In the near future, India could be playing important and crucial games, he said. ALSO READ  India vs Uruguay Can the Blue Tigers build on Brazil lessons? You need to build from the roots - academies, young players, kids to start playing a lot. If you build more academies, the league gets stronger and stronger, you will achieve getting more players and getting better players, thats for sure, added Forlan. Before the Uruguay fixture, India have played Panama against whom they drew 1-1 and then taken on Brazil, where they showed some spark in the beginning before getting trounced 4-0. Uruguay, meanwhile, landed in Kolkata on September 30 and have been taking time to acclimatise to the Indian conditions. We know its not going to be easy. Playing here, the weather is humid. You also need to adapt. Thats why all these days that we came here were good for us to adapt. The weather is different from Japan and Korea, so we know its going to be a difficult game, Forlan said. Before talking on India, Uruguay had toured Japan and Korea, losing to the former 1-3 and defeating the latter 4-1.

articleTitle: Beyond Mughal monuments & ghats: UP putting lesser-known sites on tourism map
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tulsidas birthplace, Chitrakoot
description: 97 such projects worth Rs 1,425 crore taken up in 35 districts of the state from 2021 to 2026, say officials
body_raw: Uttar Pradesh is increasingly expanding its tourism map beyond established destinations. From the temple town of Bateshwar in Agra district and Munshi Premchands birthplace, Lamhi near Varanasi to the Buddhist sites in Maharajganj and Gorakhgiri Parvat in Mahoba, the state government is turning its attention to lesser-known tourism sites - places with religious, historical, literary, cultural or natural significance but limited presence on the mainstream tourist itineraries. Between 2021 and 2026, at least 97 such projects worth around Rs 1,425 crore were taken up across 35 districts of the state, officials said. The focus is on developing these sites and linking them with existing tourist circuits, rather than concentrating the tourism activity around a handful of established destinations, in an attempt to encourage longer stays and greater local economic activity, they added. They maintained that since Agras tourism identity has long been dominated by its Mughal monuments, Bateshwar offers another aspect - a temple settlement along the Yamuna river which is also associated with the ancestral roots of former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The effort is aimed at giving the visitors to Agra another reason to travel beyond the established Mughal circuit and explore a part of the district with a distinct religious and cultural identity. For this, more than Rs 200 crore is being invested in nine projects there, covering the temple complex, heritage conservation, kunds, ghats, lighting and visitor facilities, it is learnt. Varanasi adds literary and Jain heritage In Varanasi, the tourism focus is being extended beyond the Ganga river and major temples. At Lamhi, the ancestral house of Munshi Premchand is being developed as a museum, bringing the citys literary heritage into its tourism circuit. At Chandravati, a project worth more than Rs 17 crore is being developed at the birthplace of the eighth Jain Tirthankar, Chandraprabhu. In Amethi, around Rs 35 crore is being spent to develop the sites associated with Jains, and Guru Gorakhnaths Taposthali and the literary legacy of Malik Mohammad Jayasi. In Chitrakoot, projects at Maharishi Valmiki Ashram in Lalapur, Tulsidass birthplace in Rajapur and Sri Ram Vatika Eco Park near Ganesh Bagh are intended to expand the tourism circuit beyond Ramghat and Kamadgiri. In Prayagraj, Nishadraj Park at Shringverpur is being developed around the traditional association of Lord Ram with Nishadraj. In Maharajganj district, development at Ramgram and Devdah is aimed at bringing attention to sites associated with Buddhism. Officials said such destinations require not only infrastructure but also better interpretation, connectivity and digital information to explain their significance and link them with established Buddhist circuits such as Sarnath, Kushinagar and Shravasti. Chyavan Rishi to Vedic traditions At Gugrapur in Kannauj district, Rs 81.35 lakh Chyavan Rishi Ashram project is being developed around the traditions associated with Sage Chyavan. At Naimisharanya in Sitapur, the Rs 14.09 crore Vedaranyam project will have zones inspired by the Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda, along with medicinal planting, yoga, contemplation, music and traditional learning. In Mahoba district, the Gorakhgiri Parvat is being developed around its association with Guru Gorakhnath, while the Sun Temple Interpretation Centre has been planned to bring together heritage, archaeology, yogic traditions and astronomy. A proposed planetarium is expected to add an educational component to the project. In Gorakhpur, two projects worth nearly Rs 47 crore have been taken up at the birthplace of Paramhansa Yogananda, whose writings helped popularise yoga and Indian spirituality internationally. Local suggestions drive development The state is also using local suggestions to identify sites for tourism development. Under the Chief Minister Tourism Development Partnership Scheme, MPs, MLAs, local bodies, trusts, institutions and other eligible participants can propose religious, historical, cultural and natural sites. Projects costing between Rs 25 lakh and Rs 5 crore can receive the Tourism Departments support for up to half of the eligible cost. Tourism and Culture Minister Jaiveer Singh said the states tourism identity should reflect the breadth of its history and traditions. Every district has places closely connected with its people, traditions and history, but many of them remained outside organised tourism because their stories were not presented and essential visitor facilities were missing, Singh said. The expansion of tourism to lesser-known destinations also brings a challenge infrastructure does not automatically create sustained visitor demand. Connectivity, accommodation, trained guides, local businesses, cleanliness, safety and credible interpretation would be important for these destinations to develop as sustainable tourism centres, the officials said. The government is also looking at digital tools to make such places easier to discover. Additional Chief Secretary, Tourism, Culture and Religious Affairs, Amrit Abhijat, said verified digital information, mapping, thematic itineraries, QR-based interpretation and multilingual content could help travellers discover lesser-known destinations. The larger test for the governments plan will be whether visitors coming to established destinations begin adding these lesser-known sites to their itineraries - turning them from individual development projects into functioning tourism circuits.

articleTitle: Indian Railways identifies 11 trains with journeys over 40 hours for special cleanliness monitoring
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Indian Railways will step up cleanliness monitoring on 11 long-distance trains that remain on the tracks for more than 40 hours. (Image: Southern Railway)
description: Indian Railways has identified 11 long-distance trains with journeys of more than 40 hours for enhanced cleanliness monitoring, including Vivek Express, Avadh Assam Express and Jhelum Express.
body_raw: Indian Railways has identified 11 long-distance trains with journey durations of more than 40 hours for enhanced cleanliness. The move is aimed at ensuring that passengers get better housekeeping, cleaner toilets and improved onboard services throughout the journey, rather than only at the originating station. According to a Railway Board letter dated October 3, the identified trains will receive special attention for cleanliness and serviceability during their journeys. Why are these trains being monitored? Long-distance trains remain on the tracks for several days. During such extended journeys, issues related to coach cleanliness, toilets, garbage disposal and minor repairs can affect the passenger experience if they are not addressed on time. The Railway Board RB has asked the concerned zones to closely monitor these trains while they are en route. The focus will be on maintaining cleanliness throughout the journey until the train reaches its destination. The list includes some of the countrys longest-running trains, including the Vivek Express, Avadh Assam Express, Amrapali Express and Jhelum Express. The Vivek Express has the longest journey among the identified trains, covering about 4,158 km, while its rake turnaround time is 170 hours. What will Indian Railways do? The Railway Board has directed the zones to take several measures to improve cleanliness and upkeep. The identified trains will be closely monitored by the owning depots during their journeys. Officers will also review cleanliness levels and passenger complaints on a regular basis. Special attention will be given to Clean Train Station CTS points, where cleaning teams will be expected to have adequate manpower, equipment and consumables. The RBhas also asked for small repairs to be attended to during the journey, while bio-toilets will be checked at maintenance depots and designated en-route locations. Garbage collection to be monitored Under the onboard housekeeping arrangements, garbage collection is carried out every two hours in coaches. The RB has directed that the collected waste should be handed over at designated disposal points instead of being thrown along the railway track. Photographic monitoring Time-stamped photographs of coaches and toilets will also be taken at selected inspection points, as well as at originating and destination stations, to help monitor the condition of the trains. Focus on passenger experience The Railway Board has stressed that the objective is not simply to improve cleanliness when a train starts its journey. In the new OBHS scheme emphasis has been given on the passenger awareness and regular training of OBHS staffs. This need to be emulated in all depots on OBHS trains. The OBHS staffs to be regularly trained for task assigned and proper etiquettes and behavior, the letter reads.

articleTitle: How a sports psychologist helped Pranavi Urs win Asian Games gold
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pranavi Urs became the first Indian women to win a gold in golf at Asian Games. (Reuters)
description: A session before the final round trained her brain for every scenario, including the triple bogey that came on the third hole
body_raw: If sports psychology looks like a luxury at the elite level, Pranavi Urs has an answer. It could be the difference between an Asian Games gold medal and nothing. The 23-year-old had little sleep the night before the final round at the Kasugai Country Club East Course, and her anxiety wasnt helped by a triple-bogey 7 on the third hole, which wiped out her three-shot lead going into the last day and handed the edge to World No. 6 Yin Ruoning of China. That is where her work with her sports psychologist paid off. Going into the final round of any big event, you are bound to be nervous because you care so much, Pranavi told The Indian Express on Monday. I had a session with my psychologist before the final round, where we trained my brain for all the possible scenarios and focused on having fun out on the golf course. Preparing for Murphys Law anything that can go wrong will go wrong worked to her benefit.It triple bogey was the worst thing that could have happened. I told myself that I had hit rock bottom and the only way from there was upwards. I just had to stick to the gameplan. The preparation did its job. Pranavi caught Yin with a birdie on the 10th, went ahead with another on the 13th, and did not give up the lead after that. Not that Pranavi suffered from a lack of confidence going into the competition. ALSO READ  How Pranavi Urs shrugged off a triple bogey to win golf gold Whenever you enter a tournament, you want to win, not just participate, she said. But to go ahead and actually do it was surreal. The psychologists contribution was vital to the biggest title of her career so far. She is in her third season on the Ladies European Tour LET and, despite contending several times, has not quite taken the final step. Whats more, her teammate Aditi Ashok had an unenviable history at big events. At the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games, she held a seven-shot lead going into the final round before a 5-over 77 relegated her to the silver medal. At the Tokyo Olympics in 2021, she was second going into the final 18 holes, but finished just outside the medal positions. No negative vibes Pranavi said the topic remained off-limits during team discussions. Ive known both Aditi and Diksha Dagar for a long time. Ive always looked up to Aditi. Ive played together with Diksha. All three of us are good friends and in good form. When we came together at the start of the week, we were confident that we will definitely win a medal, she said, preparing to board a flight out of Japan. I didnt ask for any advice from Aditi, and certainly didnt bring up those two final rounds in our chats. Were friends, why would I do that? We talked about everything other than that during our dinners together. Though Aditi 14th at two-over and Diksha tied 23rd at 12-over didnt do as well individually as they would have liked, the Indian womens team did clinch a silver medal behind China. Indias first womens individual golf gold at the Asian Games is likely to give the game a shot in the arm, and could help the golfer from Mysuru in her own development. Im in a better headspace now and feel more confident now. This gold medal is definitely a boost for me. The next step is to win on the LET, she said. That she beat some of the top players in the womens game augurs well for her growth. Apart from Yin World No. 6, bronze medallist Shannon Xuan Yin Tan of Singapore is the 2025 LET Order of Merit winner. Its great to win an event beating such players and a good sign that my career is going in the right direction. Now I have complete clarity that my game is in great shape and good enough to win big events, said Pranavi, who will play the Womens India Open at the DLF Golf  Country Club in Gurgaon later this month.

articleTitle: Flydubai Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami planned Tel Aviv crash before joining airline: Report
articleFeaturedImageAlt: flydubai copilot
description: Two Israeli officials told Reuters the co-pilot allegedly told UAE interrogators he had planned the attack before joining flydubai and had searched for airlines flying to Tel Aviv.
body_raw: The flydubai flight FZ1073s co-pilot, who allegedly stabbed Indian pilot Smit Machchhar in a suspected attempt to crash the plane in a midair cockpit brawl last week, has reportedly told the UAE authorities that he had planned the attack before he was hired by the Dubai state-owned airline, two Israeli officials said. The co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national, had planned to crash the flydubai flight into Tel Avivs Ben Gurion International Airport, news agency Reuters reported, citing Israeli officials. Israeli officials have said the co-pilot is from Oman but have not named him, while the UAE and flydubai have not publicly disclosed the co-pilots identity. Previous Israel-bound flight also allegedly targeted The plane took off from Dubai last Wednesday with 174 passengers and six crew members. The report added that Hamam had operated another Israel-bound plane earlier this year and had intended to hijack and crash it, but he chose not to. Little information is available as to why the Omani co-pilot changed his mind while operating the previous flight bound for Tel Aviv however, he is thought to have known someone on board, the Reuters report added. The Omani co-pilot attacked Machchhar with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said. The UAE official termed the midair violence a terrorist incident. Co-pilot allegedly sought flydubai job to target Tel Aviv The Omani co-pilot reportedly told the UAE authorities that he had applied for a job at flydubai after searching for several airline companies that fly to Tel Aviv, Israeli officials were quoted as saying. The major disaster on flydubai flight FZ1073 was averted after Captain Smit Machchhar, who has been hailed as a hero, was able to open the cockpit door, and passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot. Questions over airline vetting and Israeli security protocols The new details have raised concerns about how thoroughly flydubai vets potential employees, and how the Omani co-pilots presence on a flight filled with Israeli passengers leapfrogged Tel Avivs stringent security protocols. This comes as Israeli authorities have said that they have agreements with foreign airlines to keep pilots of nations without diplomatic ties from flying there. Israel and Oman do not have formal diplomatic relations.

articleTitle: ‘Must run to the bed’: Amitabh Bachchan opens up on sleep struggles ahead of 84th birthday
articleFeaturedImageAlt: amitabh bachchan on KBC 18
description: Acknowledging the importance of sleep, Amitabh Bachchan said he now wants to make an effort to go to bed early so that he can rest and be ready to wake up early for work.
body_raw: Just a week before turning 84, Amitabh Bachchan has revealed that he struggles to find time to sleep. With a packed work schedule and an extremely active mind, the veteran actor said it can be difficult for him to get enough rest. Taking to his blog, the actor wrote, They said the night sleep is the best repair mechanism of the human body. and I struggle to find the time to follow that. Acknowledging the importance of sleep, Amitabh Bachchan said he now wants to make an effort to go to bed early so that he can rest and be ready to wake up early for work. Sharing what keeps him from sleeping, the actor wrote, It is a different feel. a state of many thoughts and ideas. all filled with drive and a sense of conquering all that was once considered as a goal. He added that this excitement to achieve more gives him the power to keep moving towards his goals and reach his destination in time. He concluded, And I must run to the bed. Last week, Amitabh Bachchan revealed on the sets of Kaun Banega Crorepati that he had slipped and injured his knee during a shoot. ALSO READ  Yami Gautam-Aditya Dhar not moving to Himachal Pradesh, filmmakers team clarifies After making his grand entry on the show, Amitabh quickly chose to sit down. Explaining the reason, he said, Usually, I do my monologue standing at the centre, but today, I have a knee injury. Yesterday, during the shoot, I slipped and fell and injured my knee. The veteran star pointed towards his left knee while talking about the injury. After noticing the audiences worried expressions, he was quick to clarify that the injury was not serious. He explained that he chose to sit because he was having a little bit of difficulty standing up. Soon after the incident, however, Amitabh was seen attending a book launch event in Mumbai alongside his wife and actor Jaya Bachchan and legendary writer Gulzar. Even at 84, Amitabh Bachchan continues to remain active in the entertainment industry. From hosting the popular quiz show Kaun Banega Crorepati on Sony to appearing in films such as Vettaiyan and Uunchai, the actor continues to take on new projects. In 2024, he played the role of Ashwatthama in Nag Ashwins Kalki 2898 AD, performing several action sequences in the film. He is set to reprise the role in the second instalment of the franchise.

articleTitle: JSA, working group seek cap on hospital charges, medicine margins
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jan Swasthya Abhiyan and health rights groups urge government intervention to regulate private hospital rates amid soaring treatment and medicine costs
description: While the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 (CEA) provides a legal framework for regulating clinical establishments and envisages government-determined ranges of charges, it has not been implemented, they said.
body_raw: The Jan Swasthya Abhiyan JSA and the Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatment Working Group have called for urgent government intervention to regulate healthcare by private hospitals, warning that patients continue to face excessive and arbitrary charges for treatment, medicines and medical consumables with little effective protection or recourse. The demand comes amid renewed scrutiny of private hospital pricing. The Supreme Court recently questioned steep mark-ups on medicines sold through hospital pharmacies, including a case in which a cancer medicine supplied at around Rs 2,700 carried an MRP of around Rs 27,000. The SC also questioned practices that require patients to purchase medicines from hospital-linked pharmacies and has asked the government to examine regulation of trade margins. At a virtual media conference, Dr Abhay Shukla, co-convener, JSA, said private healthcare has expanded enormously in India, but regulation has simply not kept pace, adding there is no regulation of rates and the patient has virtually no bargaining power over what they are charged. Leading corporate hospital chains have been earning huge surpluses estimated in the range of Rs 22 lakh to Rs 55 lakh per year from each bed in the last few years, Dr Shukla observed. Experts said there is a need for an effective nationwide system to regulate what private hospitals can charge patients for procedures, services, medicines and consumables. Leading corporate hospital chains charge on average Rs 60,000 to Rs 78,000 per day of treatment. This is an unacceptably high level of profiteering that is paid for by ordinary patients through exorbitant hospital bills, Dr Shukla said. While the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 CEA provides a legal framework for regulating clinical establishments and envisages government-determined ranges of charges, it has not been implemented, they said. Regarding fixing margins on medicines and medical consumables, concerns have also been raised with Maharashtra FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe. Dr Shukla said at the state level, the FDA Commissioners office can issue orders requiring hospitals that supply medical consumables above a specified unit price to disclose their procurement price alongside the selling price. This will lead to a huge amount of transparency, so that patients are aware of the actual cost of what they are buying and the cost incurred by the hospital, Dr Shukla said. Maharashtra is in the process of drafting a Clinical Establishments Act CEA. Since pricing is a subject in the Concurrent List, there is a possibility that the state could introduce a provision in the CEA requiring hospitals to limit the markup on medicines and consumables they supply to no more than 30 per cent over the procurement price. Such a provision could potentially be introduced and implemented at the state level itself, the experts said. The CEA was passed more than a decade ago, but its non-implementation has produced zero results on the ground. It is high time the government starts to regulate the procedures in private hospitals. A patient should know how much they will they be charged before agreeing to a treatment, according to K M Gopakumar, co-convener, Working Group. The MRP cannot become a licence to charge patients many times the procurement price. The government must urgently fix the trade margins on all medical products and ensure that patients are free to purchase medicines and consumables from outside wherever clinically possible, said Jyotsna Singh, Co-Convenor, Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatments.

articleTitle: 150 Bangladeshi immigrants flown out of J&K on IAF aircraft for deportation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jammu and Kashmir: Police sources said a batch of people described as "illegal immigrants" was sent in an Indian Air Force plane to Bagdogra airport in West Bengal. (File Photo)
description: This comes two months after a high-level committee on demographic changes, set up by the Union Home Ministry in May this year, visited Jammu and Kashmir for its first field visit.
body_raw: As many as 150 Bangladeshi nationals who were allegedly living illegally in Jammu and Kashmir were airlifted on Monday to West Bengals Bagdogra, from where they will be deported. The 150 are among 500 people who were detained from different parts of the Union Territory during a survey to identify illegal immigrants and kept in a facility manned by the police. From Bagdogra, the 150 will be deported to Bangladesh, officials said. This comes two months after a high-level committee on demographic changes, set up by the Union Home Ministry in May this year, visited Jammu and Kashmir for its first field visit. Police sources said that the batch of 150 immigrants was sent in an Indian Air Force aircraft. They would be handed over to the Border Security Force BSF and deported on October 7, sources said. JK police have conducted a special exercise over the last few days to identify illegal immigrants in the Union Territory, sources said, adding that around 500 people-mostly from Bangladesh-were detained and shifted to the facility on the outskirts of Srinagar city. Most of these people have been settled in different parts of the Kashmir Valley for many years now, said a police officer. They were mostly doing menial jobs like ragpicking, etc. Sources said some of those detained are Rohingya from Myanmar. Others will also be sent out in batches in the coming days and deported, sources said. The high-level committee, during its visit to Jammu and Kashmir, was informed that there are 7,656 Rohingya and 504 Bangladeshi nationals in Jammu and Kashmir-6,737 Rohingya and 46 Bangladeshi immigrants in Jammu, and the rest in Kashmir. The committee was also informed that 117 cases are registered against them-101 in Jammu and 16 in Kashmir. The committees mandate is to study demographic changes arising from illegal immigration and other factors and to recommend measures to address them. It has been asked to submit its report within one year. It had sought details from states and Union Territories regarding visible changes in religious demography across districts, industrial clusters and border districts over the last 15 years. In a letter dispatched to states and UTs over the last two months, the Committee sought time-series data indicating changes over the years, alongside other administrative datasets, an assessment by state governments of major trends in demographics, and data on the religious composition of tribal populations since 2011. -With PTI

articleTitle: Odds back Can Xue, pattern a woman: All about 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nobel Prize in Literature 2026: Composite portrait of three women writers on a dark background: a woman with grey hair in a topknot and dark-rimmed glasses resting her chin on her hand; an older woman with curly grey hair, a pink beaded necklace and a headset microphone; and a woman with shoulder-length dark hair, glasses and a maroon scarf over a white top.
description: Nobel Prize in Literature 2026 will be announced on October 8 at 4.30 pm IST. Can Xue leads the odds; Rushdie at 25/1. Prize money, process and more.
body_raw: Will it be Can Xue, the Chinese writer known for her experimental fiction, perennial favourite Haruki Murakami, or a writer of Indian or South Asian descent? The question, which has occupied literary circles for months, will be answered on October 8, when the Swedish Academy announces the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature. When and where to watch The Swedish Academy will announce the prize on Thursday, October 8, at 4.30 pm IST 1 pm in Stockholm at the earliest. The announcement will be streamed live on the Nobel Prizes official website and social media channels. Who are the frontrunners According to the British betting site Ladbrokes, Can Xue is the favourite at 101, followed by Haruki Murakami Japan at 141, Gerald Murnane Australia and Thomas Pynchon US at 161, and Cristina Rivera Garza Mexico, Enrique Vila-Matas Spain, Lidia Jorge Portugal, Ludmila Ulitskaya Russia, Margaret Atwood Canada and Michel Houellebecq France at 20 Bookmakers have no inside information, but they are not always wrong. Last years winner, Lszlo Krasznahorkai, fluctuated between 61 and 101 across various betting markets. Who is Can Xue? Deng Xiaohua, who goes by the pen name Can Xue, has appeared on bookmakers lists for years. She was tied with Lszlo Krasznahorkai, who won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature, at 101 on Ladbrokes. The 73-year-old author is known for experimental fiction, including dreamlike, stream-of-consciousness prose that defies conventional plot. Her writing has been likened to Franz Kafka and Jorge Luis Borges. Her best-known books in English areThe Last Lover, which won the US Best Translated Book Award in 2015 Love in the New Millennium, which was longlisted for the International Booker in 2019 and I Live in the Slums,which was longlisted in 2021. Is this her year? Since 2018, the prize has alternated between women and men, ending with Krasznahorkai. If that pattern holds, which the Academy is under no obligation to keep, the 2026 winner would be a woman. Patterns over the last decade Over the past decade four of the 10 laureates were women  six wrote in a language other than English six were European  one was from Asia South Koreas Han Kang, in 2024  none from South Asia Is there an Indian or South Asian contender? This year, the best-placed writers of South Asian origin are Salman Rushdie, 251 One of the worlds most famous writers, Rushdie was the target of a fatwa issued by Irans Ayatollah Khomeini in 1989 over his book, The Satanic Verses. Thirty-three years later, in August 2022, he was stabbed during a speaking engagement in New York. He won the 1981 Booker for Midnights Children, and is credited with bringing magic realism into Indian writing in English. His latest book is The Eleventh Hour 2025, and a documentary on the attack, which left him blind in one eye, was released this year. Michael Ondaatje, 251 With the same odds as Rushdie, Ondaatje was born in Colombo in 1943 and shared the 1992 Booker for The English Patient. He is known for lyrical, fragmented narratives that blend poetry with history. His latest book is a poetry anthology, The Distance of a Shout 2026. Ananda Devi, 401 A Mauritian writer of Indian descent who writes in French. Devi is known for her unsparing portraits of women confined within tradition and her depiction of fractured identities. She won the 2024 Neustadt Prize her latest book is Chronicle of a Lost Kingdom 2026. Amitav Ghosh, 501 Of late, the Kolkata-born author is known for his writings on climate change. He is the author of the Ibis trilogy, beginning with Sea of Poppies, and The Great Derangement. His latest book is Ghost-Eye 2026. Has an Indian ever won? Only once. Rabindranath Tagore won in 1913 and was the first Asian laureate. Two other winners have Indian links Rudyard Kipling, born in Bombay, won in 1907, and V S Naipaul, a Trinidad-born British writer of Indian descent, won in 2001. Does a Booker help? While the Nobel Prize honours a writers whole body of work, the Booker rewards a single novel written in English, and the International Booker rewards a single book translated into English. Even so, the two lists overlap. Five authors-V S Naipaul, Nadine Gordimer, William Golding, J M Coetzee, and Kazuo Ishiguro - who won the Booker Prize, and four who won the International Booker Prize-Alice Munro, Lszlo Krasznahorkai, Han Kang, and Olga Tokarczuk- have won the Nobel Prize. Abdulrazak Gurnah, the 2021 laureate, was shortlisted for the Booker in 1994 for Paradise. Interestingly, Rushdies Midnights Children won the prize in 1981. It was later named the Booker of Bookers in 1993 and the Best of the Booker in 2008 Ondaatjes The English Patient shared the 1992 prize and won the Golden Man Booker in 2018. A Booker is not a guarantee. For instance, Doris Lessing was shortlisted several times without winning, and won the Nobel in 2007. The favourite, Can Xue, was longlisted for the International Booker in 2019 and 2021, while Amitav Ghosh was shortlisted in 2008 for Sea of Poppies. How is the winner chosen? Each September, the Academy invites qualified people to nominate. They include members of the Swedish Academy and similar academies professors of literature and linguistics former laureates heads of national writers organisations Writers cannot nominate themselves. In April, the Nobel Committee picks 1520 preliminary candidates, then narrows them to five in May. The Academys 18 members vote, and whoever gets more than half the votes wins. Will we ever know who was nominated? The Academy publishes no longlist or shortlist, and it doesnt tell nominees they are under consideration. Nomination records are sealed for 50 years, so this years nominations will only open in 2076. Several Indians have been nominated, according to the Nobel archive, including  philosopher Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, repeatedly from 1933 to 1962 Sri Aurobindo, in 1943 Bengali novelist Tarashankar Bandyopadhyay, from 1971 to 1973  R K Narayan, from 1974 How much does the winner get? This year, the winner will receive SEK 12 million, about 12 crore, up from SEK 11 million in 2025. The prize will be presented in Stockholm on December 10.

articleTitle: Inside Adnan Sami’s luxurious Mumbai penthouse: Vintage vinyls, rare memorabilia, and awards
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Adnan Sami home tour video
description: Adnan Sami’s Mumbai penthouse features rare vinyl records, gold records, a private theatre, music studio and memorabilia from music and cinema legends.
body_raw: Singer and musician Adnan Samis luxurious Mumbai penthouse is more than just an extravagant home. In a recent vlog, filmmaker Farah Khan, accompanied by her cook Dilip, visited the Padma Shri awardees residence and noted that the sprawling space is also a celebration of music, cinema, art, and Adnans family history. The tour offered a glimpse into the Lift Karadeysingers extensive collection of rare musical memorabilia, prestigious awards and artefacts collected from across the world. The expansive residence features several distinct spaces, including a grand living hall, music gallery, formal dining area, private home theatre, executive office, music studio, and more. A music gallery with vintage records One of the biggest highlights of Adnans home is his collection of vintage vinyl records and memorabilia. A polished black grand piano takes centre stage in the open-plan music hall, while the surrounding walls are covered with framed vinyl records and album artwork. The singer has also displayed first-press vinyl records and vintage photographs from some of the most iconic films in Indian cinema, including Baiju Bawra, Amar Akbar Anthony, Mughal-E-Azam, Sholay, and Alam Ara. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. The space also features glass shelves displaying classical bust sculptures, along with a sunlit seating nook furnished with beige wingback chairs and an antique globe. Rare memorabilia from music legends Adnans collection extends beyond Indian cinema. His home features original gold record awards associated with international music legends, including The Beatles, Michael Jackson and Elvis Presley, which he acquired through auctions. He also owns a print of the original manuscript of Beethovens Moonlight Sonata. Another striking display includes silver tea sets, pitchers and animal sculptures placed on a wooden credenza with gold detailing. The house also has a framed piece of sacred cloth associated with the Kaaba in Mecca. Grand living spaces and a dramatic foyer The main open living hall connects several areas of the home under a continuous white recessed ceiling and glossy flooring. The space includes the grand piano and music gallery on one side, a formal dining area on the other and a central lounge decorated with a large metallic wall sculpture. The foyer features a wooden spiral staircase with a curved railing. Damask-patterned wallpaper lines the hallway, which also functions as a gallery for framed gold record awards. The formal living room features cream sofas and plush armchairs arranged around low wooden tables. A sage-green accent wall carries a metallic wave sculpture and framed oil paintings, while another section of the room is dedicated to family photographs. Floor-to-ceiling windows, heavy olive-grey curtains, and a large Persian rug add to the rooms traditional aesthetic. A private home theatre The space features beige leather media recliners, movie-themed cushions, and additional floor seating arranged around a central rug. Dark wood panelling covers the walls and is paired with deep red damask-patterned acoustic panels. The theatre also pays tribute to some of the singers favourite classic films, with framed 35mm film strips and posters from movies including Fiddler on the Roof, Lawrence of Arabia, Deewaar, Oceans 11, The Sound of Music and The Godfather. Music studio The singers office and music studio combine luxury with functionality. Designed with classic Chesterfield seating, soundproofing and custom architectural details, the space is equipped for professional music production, including Dolby Atmos sound. The office features a large desk with a built-in pull-out keyboard, while the acoustically treated space has been designed to preserve views of the Mumbai skyline. A dedicated singing and microphone booth forms another part of the studio. Its walls feature pictures of musicians and icons who have inspired Adnans musical journey. The office space follows a darker, more traditional design language, with extensive wood panelling and a geometric coffered wooden ceiling. A large desk with green leather detailing sits alongside matching green leather chairs, while a green Chesterfield sofa occupies another section of the room. Built-in illuminated glass bookcases display books and memorabilia, complemented by brass wall sconces and table lamps. Dining space, crystal chandelier The formal dining room features a rectangular dining table surrounded by eight cream upholstered chairs. A crystal chandelier hangs above the table, while one wall is decorated with grids of framed vinyl records. The home also has a private leather lounge or cigar-den-inspired space, designed in deep maroon and dark wood tones. Brown tufted Chesterfield sofas and armchairs surround a trunk-style coffee table. Parquet-style flooring, warm table lamps and full-length glass doors opening onto a balcony complete the space. Difference between curating and decorating a house Rubeena Singh, Founder of The Verve Collective, interior stylist  home decorator, shared her insights on how homeowners can make sentimental objects look intentional rather than cluttered. The expert shared her one rule that she follows while designing a home curation, not collection. You dont have to display everything you own simply because it is sentimental. Choose the pieces that mean the most to you and give them enough space to be noticed. I also like grouping objects into stories, she explained. Highlighting the difference between decorating and curating, Rubeena shared that for one of her clients, she turned her mothers sari into an artwork for a wall behind the sofa. For another, we displayed her late husbands camera collection on a console rather than treating it as something that needed to be stored away. Weve displayed art created by a clients 12-year-old daughter in the foyer, created a used maps of places the homeowners have lived in and used a Japanese scroll in the living room of a client who was raised in Japan, Rubeena explained. articleTitle: By Election 2026: Bypolls on 6 seats in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam; Results On Oct 9
articleFeaturedImageAlt: West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam By Election 2026
description: West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam By Election 2026 Polling - Date, Time, Streaming: The by-elections hold much significance following the BJP's victory in West Bengal ending TMC's 15 year rule, Vijay's TVK's victorious electoral debut in Tamil Nadu and it remains to be seen how the new leaders have factored in the electorate.
body_raw: West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Assam By Election 2026 The by-elections to five Assembly constituencies across West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, and one Lok Sabha constituency in Assam, will be held on Tuesday, with voting beginning at 7 am. Counting of votes will be held on October 9. The by-elections hold significance following the BJPs victory in West Bengal, ending TMCs 15-year rule, and Vijays TVKs victorious electoral debut in Tamil Nadu, and it remains to be seen how the new leaders have factored in with the electorate. By Election 2026 Live Updates Follow Here West Bengal In West Bengal, the Suvendu Adhikari-led BJP government faces its first electoral test after assuming power in the Assembly polls earlier this year. With Nandigram and Rejinagar going to polls, the Opposition faces a tough battle amid candidate withdrawals, arrests and allegations of police pressure on its workers. Nandigram The Nandigram seat paved the way for the TMCs rise in 2011 following Mamata Banerjees anti-land acquisition movement, and its where Adhikari defeated the TMC supremo in 2021. Adhikari, now chief minister, won Nandigram again in the 2026 Assembly election but retained Bhabanipur, necessitating the bypoll. The BJP has fielded Hasirani Rath, mother of Chandranath Rath, a former aide of Adhikari. Chandranath was shot dead on May 6, two days after the BJP won the Assembly elections. The Mamata Banerjee-led TMC factions nominee Sanchita Pradhan Dey withdrew her name after meeting Adhikari, following which Banerjee, left without a candidate, backed Congress candidate Milan Pradhan and described the move as an effort to strengthen the INDIA bloc. Pradhan was arrested in old cases linked to the 2007 Nandigram land-acquisition agitation but later secured interim bail and returned to campaign. The rival TMC faction led by Ritabrata Banerjee has fielded Mohammad Eteshamul Haque under the envelope symbol and a separate temporary party identity. The CPI has nominated Santigopal Giri. Rejinagar The by-election in Rejinagar was necessitated after Humayun Kabir, who won both Rejinagar and Nowda in the 2026 Assembly election, retained Nowda. His Aam Janata Unnayan Party has fielded his son Golam Nabi Azad. Kabir had won Rejinagar by nearly 59,000 votes. The contest includes BJP nominee Sakharav Sarkar, former Murshidabad district president Mamata-led TMC candidate Rabiul Alam Chowdhury rival TMC candidate Safiuzzaman Sheikh Congress nominee Mohammad Abdullahil Kafi and CPIMs Syed Asad Ali. Tamil Nadu The two seats in Tamil Nadu, Madurantakam and Dharapuram, saw four-day aggressive campaigning by TVK chief and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, as the electoral contest would be crucial for his party. It is a four-cornered contest, with the TVK, DMK, AIADMK and CPI fielding their candidates. Both constituencies were vacated by AIADMK legislators who resigned within weeks of being elected and crossed over to Vijay. The same two leaders-Maragatham Kumaravel in Madurantakam and P Sathyabama in Dharapuram-are now contesting as TVK candidates. The DMK enters these by-elections without the broad alliance that accompanied it into the Assembly election. The Congress, VCK, MDMK and IUML have moved into Vijays political orbit, while the CPI and CPIM are contesting separately. A total of 27 contestants are in the fray for the bypoll at Madurantakam, and a total of 30 contestants are in the fray in the Dharapuram Assembly constituency. In Madurantakam, a total of 2,12, 639 voters will exercise their franchise in 268 polling stations. In Dharapuram, 2,22, 406 electors will exercise their franchise in 282 polling stations. Thattanchavady in Puducherry The poll scenario is different in neighbouring Puducherry, where its a test of popularity for the four-month-old NDA government led by veteran N Rangasamy. Although a total of 11 candidates are in the fray, the battle is being seen as a three-cornered one between the ruling AINRC-led NDA, the Congress and its former ally DMK. While AINRC founder and CM Rangasamy has nominated Ashok Anand on behalf of the ruling party and the coalition it leads, the Congress has fielded E Vinayagam, who has the backing of the Tamizhaga Vetri Kazhagam TVK, which is part of the ruling alliance in neighbouring Tamil Nadu. The DMK nominee is K Sedhu Selvam. CPIs M A Saleem and S Karthikumari of actor-politician Seemans Naam Tamilar Katchi are also fighting the poll battle. Nagaon Lok Sabha seat in Assam The Nagaon Lok Sabha seat in Assam would witness a triangular contest, with the ruling BJP seeking to expand its base in this Muslim-majority constituency, and the Congress going all out to retain the seat by keeping its minority support base intact. The AIUDF, the third prominent party in the fray, is fighting to maintain its influence after it was reduced to two MLAs from 16 in the April Assembly election. A total of 15 candidates, including nine Independents, are contesting the bypoll. Among the key candidates are ex-MLA Sibamoni Bora of the Congress, former IAS officer Devasish Sharma of the BJP and sitting MLA Badruddin Ajmal of the AIUDF. The bypoll was necessitated after sitting MP Pradyut Bordoloi quit the Congress to join the BJP ahead of the Assembly elections earlier this year. Out of the eight Assembly segments under the Nagaon Lok Sabha seat, the BJP won four, the Congress three and Raijor Dal one in this years state elections. For the Congress, which won three out of 14 Lok Sabha seats in the 2024 election, retaining Nagaon is crucial to prevent further erosion of its support base. The BJP, which has been aiming to spread its base among the Muslims, has viewed the Nagaon bypoll as an attempt to establish its presence across all sections of people and further strengthen its hold in the state.

articleTitle: Blue economy: How to make maritime expansion a lasting source of prosperity
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India, blue economy, finance
description: While India seeks to harness its vast maritime wealth, it remains committed to making the blue economy inclusive and sustainable. How can it effectively connect economic growth, finance, livelihoods, and conservation? And how can it attract the long-term capital needed to support the sector’s expansion? See infographics.
body_raw: - Pushpendra Singh and Archana Singh What might a richer coastline look like? It could mean more ports, bigger ships, and higher seafood exports. It could also mean higher income for fishing families, clean waters, and better protection for coastal villages from storms. An integrated approach that balances these objectives will be crucial to making Indias Blue Economy inclusive and sustainable. As the Blue Revolution is set to be another success story, lets understand how India seeks to harness its marine wealth. Ocean as the engine of growth For decades, Indias infrastructure story was written largely on land. Roads connected markets, railways moved freight, and industrial corridors attracted investment. The sea entered this story mainly through ports and trade. Now, India is looking at the ocean as a wider economic space for fisheries, tourism, energy, research, and new industries. Indias blue economy ambitions are complemented by its 11,098 km of coastline. The blue economy refers to the sustainable use of ocean and coastal resources to support economic growth, jobs and livelihoods, while protecting marine ecosystems. Its scope extends beyond fishing and shipping to emerging fields like marine biotechnology and ocean energy. Indias maritime activity is already growing. The countrys major ports handled 915.17 million tonnes MT of cargo during FY 202526, marking a year-on-year growth of 7.06. This underscores the growing efficiency of Indias maritime sector. Building Indias blue economy Alongside its extensive coastline, Indias maritime infrastructure supports around 95 of the countrys trade by volume. As the government aims to increase the maritime sectors contribution to GDP significantly by expanding maritime infrastructure, Sagarmala has played a crucial role in this. The ambitious port-led infrastructure development programme, launched in 2015, has supported port-led development through various initiatives. Around 845 projects, estimated at Rs 6.06 lakh crore, have been taken up under the Sagarmala programme, according to an assessment by the government. As of March 24, 2026, around 315 projects worth Rs 1.57 lakh crore have been completed, while 210 projects are currently under implementation, and 320 projects are in the planning stage. Better links between waterways, ports, roads and railways can improve freight movement, reduce transport costs and strengthen the competitiveness of Indian businesses. But the blue economy is not merely about transport. It also encompasses food security, energy, livelihoods and the scientific knowledge needed to manage ocean resources sustainably. Fisheries, economy, and livelihoods Fisheries show how closely economic opportunity is linked with everyday life. The sector supports nearly 30 million livelihoods through inland fisheries and aquaculture, not just marine fishing. This distinction matters when discussing coastal development. The fisheries sector has evolved into a commercially significant sector over the past decade. India is now the second largest fish-producing country and accounts for about 8 of global fish production. Its seafood exports span a wide and diversified basket, with over 350 varieties of products shipped to nearly 130 global markets. Seafood export earnings registered a strong growth, rising from Rs 62,408 crore in 2024-25 to Rs 73,890 crore in FY 2025-26 an increase of about 18.4. While the growth underscores the sectors economic potential, translating this into returns for producers and workers remains important. For fishing families, this requires safe landing facilities, ice plants, cold storage, affordable credit and access to markets. Better processing can reduce losses and raise earnings without putting additional pressure on fish stocks. Cooperatives can improve bargaining power, while women in processing and marketing may also need stronger support. Investing in new ocean opportunities Further offshore, India is exploring new possibilities. A 7,453-crore government scheme supports the development of one gigawatt of offshore wind capacity - 500 MW each off the coast of Gujarat and Tamil Nadu - along with port upgrades. These are planned investments, rather than operating capacity. The 4,077-crore Deep Ocean Mission covers underwater technologies, biodiversity, ocean observation and deep-sea exploration. The research into seabed resources may widen future opportunities, but exploration does not establish that commercial extraction is ready or environmentally sound. However, these activities show why maritime development needs different kinds of finance. Ports require large investments with long repayment periods. Fishing enterprises need smaller loans and insurance. The research and conservation often require public funding, as their benefits far outweigh commercial returns. Blue bonds and the maritime financing gap How can India bring long-term capital into this expanding economy? Blue bonds offer a route. A blue bond is a borrowing instrument whose proceeds are reserved for sustainable water and ocean-related projects. Like a conventional bond, it must be repaid with interest. Its distinguishing feature is the specified use of funds and environmental reporting. Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India SEBI recognises the potential of blue bonds for the countrys blue economy. Its 2023 framework introduced blue bonds within debt securities. Their scope includes clean water, recycling, sustainable shipping and fishing, traceable seafood, ocean energy and ocean mapping. However, a projects location beside the sea does not automatically make it eligible for blue financing. For maritime infrastructure, long-term bonds can help match borrowing periods with the years projects need to generate income. They can also attract institutional investors seeking long-duration investment opportunities. But a blue bond remains a debt instrument and needs a credible repayment plan. Indias first proposed blue bond, under the Sagarmala programme, offers a case in point. Sagarmala Finance Corporation planned to raise Rs 600 crores through 10-year bonds but withdrew the issue on September 28 after investors sought higher interest rates than it was willing to offer. Bids totaled 525 crores. However, the setback does not remove the case for blue finance. It shows that a sustainability label alone cannot guarantee lower borrowing costs. Affordable borrowing requires sound projects, reliable income and a financial structure that addresses risk. Environmental objectives, therefore, need to be backed by financial credibility. What global experiences show Other countries offer useful lessons. Seychelles issued the worlds first sovereign blue bond in 2018, raising USD 15 million. A USD 5 million World Bank guarantee and USD 5 million in concessional financing from the Global Environment Facility helped support the transaction. However, Belize followed a different approach. Its USD 364 million debt conversion in 2021 refinanced sovereign debt while creating funding for marine conservation and supporting a commitment to protect 30 per cent of its ocean. This was a debt-for-conservation arrangement, rather than simply a bond financing new infrastructure. Indias scale and financing needs are different, but these examples offer useful insights blue finance works better when financial support is clearly linked to environmental results. Guarantees or concessional funding should serve measurable public benefits, with their costs disclosed. Growth without bluewashing Finance alone cannot make maritime growth sustainable. A port can increase trade while damaging mangroves. Tourism can create jobs while adding waste. Bigger fishing fleets can raise catches in the short-term but can reduce stocks over time. India needs clear standards to prevent bluewashing - attaching a blue label to projects without convincing environmental benefits. Independent review, transparent use of funds, and regular reporting can help establish what investments have achieved. This could include measures such as reductions in pollution, protection of marine habitats, and improvements in the livelihoods of coastal communities. Indias blue economy will, therefore, need to effectively connect growth, finance, livelihoods, and conservation from the outset. Coastal communities need a meaningful voice. The goal is to make the ocean more productive without undermining the ecosystems. That balance will determine whether maritime expansion becomes a lasting source of prosperity. Post read questions 1. Indias Blue Economy represents a shift from a port-centric maritime strategy towards a broader economic engagement with ocean resources. Discuss the opportunities and challenges associated with this transition. 2. The success of Indias Blue Economy will depend not merely on expanding maritime infrastructure, but on balancing economic growth with ecological sustainability and coastal livelihoods. Discuss. 3. Fisheries illustrate the dual character of Indias Blue Economy-as a source of economic growth and as a foundation for millions of livelihoods. Discuss the measures required to make fisheries growth more inclusive and sustainable. 4. Sagarmala reflects Indias attempt to leverage its coastline for port-led development. Assess its potential to reduce logistics costs and improve competitiveness while examining the limitations of a predominantly infrastructure-led approach to the Blue Economy. 5. What are blue bonds? How can they help finance Indias maritime and ocean-related development? Discuss the challenges involved in making blue finance both affordable and environmentally credible. articleTitle: Himachal High Court halts operation of anti-hail guns in Himachal apple belt: ‘affects rain pattern’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Anti-hail guns are shock-wave generating machines used by some horticulturists with the objective of preventing crop damage by disrupting the formation of hailstones in clouds.
description: Directs state to examine if anti-hail system pushes out cloud from apple orchards leading to excessive rainfall in adjoining areas.
body_raw: The Himachal Pradesh High Court on Monday directed the state government put an immediate halt on the operation of anti-hail guns across the state for at least one year, while observing that concerns raised by orchardists over excessive rainfall and damage to adjoining apple-growing areas appear to stand substantiated. A Division Bench of Chief Justice G S Sandhawalia and Justice Bipin Chander Negi issued the directions while hearing a Public Interest Litigation PIL, initiated suo motu by the court, following representations from apple growers who have complained that anti-hail guns were impacting the rainfall and hail patterns. Anti-hail guns are shock-wave generating machines used by some horticulturists with the objective of preventing crop damage by disrupting the formation of hailstones in clouds. The Court took note of an affidavit filed by the Director of Horticulture, which stated that heavy and prolonged rainfall was observed when the hail-control system was operational for more than an hour. It is apparent.the concerns raised in the representation, that operation of anti-hail guns could push clouds towards adjoining orchard areas, resulting in excessive rainfall and hail in neighbouring locations, stand substantiated in the circumstances, the bench observed. It directed that two anti-hail guns installed by the government at Deorighat and Bareonghat in the Jubbal-Kotkhai area of Shimla district is not operated till further orders. It also directed the government to issue instructions prohibiting the operation of privately owned anti-hail guns anywhere in the state. The system should remain non-operational for at least one year, the Bench said, while directing the authorities to examine whether surrounding areas benefit after the guns are stopped. Earlier, appearing for the State, Additional Advocate General Gobind Korla, submitted in the court that Dr Y S Parmar University of Horticulture and Forestry, Nauni, Solan, was conducting a study to assess the efficacy and impact of anti-hail guns. It was submitted that the study would require at least another four years before reaching a definitive conclusion. In view of the duration required for the study, the Court impleaded the university through its Registrar as a respondent and issued notice to it, returnable within four weeks. The Bench further directed the State to file a response specifically addressing whether stopping the operation of the anti-hail guns results in any benefit to areas in the neighbourhood or vicinity of Deorighat and Bareonghat. The Court also noted that the representation before it referred to alleged adverse effects associated with anti-hail guns in Mexico, Romania and other countries. It directed the Himachal Pradesh government to file a comprehensive response dealing with the available global studies as well as the impact of anti-hail guns in the state. The matter has been listed for further hearing on December 8, 2026.

articleTitle: ‘No one is to blame’: Kalaranjini lost her voice after consuming fake blood containing acid
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kalaranjini lost her voice on a movie set after purportedly consuming fake blood that had mistakenly been prepared using acid instead of coconut oil.
description: Decades ago, Kalaranjini shockingly lost much of her voice on a movie set after purportedly consuming fake blood that had been mistakenly prepared using acid instead of coconut oil.
body_raw: Although Kalaranjini never had a career as illustrious as those of her younger sisters, Kalpana and Urvashi, she has repeatedly demonstrated impressive acting skills, shining brightest in comedic roles, with the most recent examples being director Krishnadas Muralis Bharathanatyam 2024 and its sequel Mohiniyattam 2026. Apart from Malayalam, she has also acted in Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada languages, as well as in television serials, leaving a lasting impression wherever she set foot. However, while she was slowly soaring high, an unexpected incident turned Kalaranjinis life upside down, affecting both her career and emotional well-being. Must Read  My father married around 20 people Sreelakshmi Arackal reveals traumatic childhood Decades ago, Kalaranjini shockingly lost much of her voice on a movie set after purportedly consuming fake blood that had been mistakenly prepared using acid instead of coconut oil. Despite the incident significantly affecting her film career, she recently said she has no complaints against anyone, as she believes it was an honest mistake on the part of the makeup artist. The shocking on-set accident that changed everything At that time, he was terribly upset. Everyone avoided him on all sets. Then, in his final days, I was the one who helped him. Their children also still have a very good relationship with us. It was a small mistake. He must have been very sad that it happened that way. He wouldnt do such a thing to his profession on purpose. KV Bhaskar who prepared the fake blood was one of the biggest makeup artists in Malayalam cinema. He would have never done it on purpose it was a slip of the hand. He wouldnt have thought that it would make my life like this either, she shared during a conversation with Can Channel Media. Also Read  He asked if I had AIDS Gayathri Suresh on her past toxic situationship Kalaranjini continued, Therefore, I dont have any major sorrows. I have been acting since that day, thanks to my co-workers and fellow artistes. Whenever I say my lines, people go completely silent because those acting with me need to react to what I am saying. This her acting career has moved forward because of everyones cooperation. Ambili used to dub everything for me. She is no longer with us. Later, Rosshan Andrrews director asked me to use my own voice. Even then, I didnt have the confidence. When I saw it, I felt it was not necessary. Then I did it in Chirakodinja Kinavukal. In Bharathanatyam, director Krishnadas insisted that I dub for myself. Thats how he helped bring my voice back, she added. Dont Miss  Sanjay Dutt says he cant feel peace in India anymore, comments on PM Modi as Munna Bhai What happened on the fateful day According to Mathrubhumi, the aforementioned tragic incident happened while Kalaranjini was working with Malayalam superstar Prem Nazir. In one scene, she was supposed to die by vomiting blood. Back then, fake blood was made by mixing coconut oil with red colour. Since Kalaranjini was wearing a white saree, it was certain the dress would be stained if the red liquid splattered on her body. Hence, right before the shoot, Prem Nazir told her, I will feed it to you when the moment arrives. Kalaranjini agreed. However, she only remembers him pouring the red liquid into her mouth. Suddenly, Kalaranjini felt like her mouth and throat were burning and swelling up. But she couldnt do anything her windpipe contracted. Even after extensive treatment, there was no result. She mostly lost her voice and never fully regained it. She was in the hospital for about three months. ICYMI  Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr Kalaranjini only learned what had actually happened to her later. The makeup artist had prepared the liquid by adding acid instead of coconut oil. Disclaimer This article is a personal narrative detailing a set injury and its long-term impact. It is provided for informational and editorial purposes only and does not constitute medical advice or professional safety guidance.

articleTitle: Bihar labourer arrested for sexually assaulting minor daughter in Bengaluru
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru child sexual assault case
description: CCTV footage from around the rented house where the family was staying raised suspicion about the girl's father, the police said.
body_raw: The police in Bengaluru South district arrested a 30-year-old labourer from Bihar for allegedly sexually assaulting his minor daughter, who has a hearing impairment, officers said on Monday. According to the police, the incident came to light after the girl developed severe abdominal pain about a week ago. Her stepmother took her to a nearby private hospital, where doctors suspected sexual assault and alerted the District Child Protection Unit. Officials who visited the hospital subsequently confirmed that the girl had been sexually assaulted. As the girl has a hearing impairment and could not communicate verbally, a sign-language interpreter was brought in to speak to her, the police said. However, she could not provide clear information about the person responsible for the assault. The police initially registered a case against an unidentified person under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Pocso Act. During the investigation, the police questioned the girls father, who allegedly behaved as though he was unaware of the incident. However, CCTV footage from around the rented house where the family was staying raised suspicion about him, the police said. During questioning, he confessed to the crime. He was subsequently arrested and produced before a court, which remanded him to judicial custody, a police officer said. According to the police, the girl was born to the mans first wife, who died following an illness. The man and his second wife have three children, taking the total number of children in the household to four. The police said further investigations are underway.

articleTitle: Karnataka SIR: Over 43.5 lakh notices delivered, 91,278 form 7 applications received
articleFeaturedImageAlt: According to data released by the CEO’s office, 43,82,313 notices have been generated across Karnataka. Of these, 43,55,818 have been delivered, while 26,495 are yet to be delivered, taking the delivery rate to 99.40 per cent.
description: The notices have been issued to electors whose names fall under the “No Mapping” and “Anomalies” categories during the electoral roll revision exercise.
body_raw: More than 43.5 lakh notices have been delivered to electors in Karnataka as part of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls, with 91,278 Form 7 applications received between June 16 and October 4, Chief Electoral Officer V Anbukkumar said on Monday. Form 7 is used to file an objection to the proposed inclusion or seek deletion of a name from the existing electoral roll. The notices have been issued to electors whose names fall under the No Mapping and Anomalies categories during the electoral roll revision exercise. Anbukkumar said no voter has been deleted from the electoral roll so far, and clarified that the filing of an objection does not automatically result in deletion. Just because objections have been filed, no name has been deleted so far from the electoral roll, he said at a press conference. He said objections would be examined by the concerned Electoral Registration Officers EROs, who would take necessary action according to law. On applications seeking deletion of names through Form 7, Anbukkumar said the ERO is required to issue a notice and conduct a hearing before taking any decision. The officer has to call both the objector and the voter for the hearing. The officer has to verify the documents. Only after that, once the officer is convinced, a decision can be taken whether to delete or not to delete, he said, referring to the procedure under Sections 16 to 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The CEO said no case had been registered by his office so far. According to data released by the CEOs office, 43,82,313 notices have been generated across Karnataka. Of these, 43,55,818 have been delivered, while 26,495 are yet to be delivered, taking the delivery rate to 99.40 per cent. Of the notices delivered, hearings have been completed in 36,89,063 cases, or 84.69 per cent. Hearings in 6,66,755 cases remain pending. The CEOs office said that of the 91,278 Form 7 applications received between June 16 and October 4, none related to objections to proposed inclusion. During the same period, the state received 9,10,732 Form 6 applications, 4,677 Form 6A applications and 11,98,484 Form 8 applications. The total number of applications received across these categories stood at 22,05,171. Bidar recorded the highest number of Form 7 applications at 5,953, followed by Shivamogga with 5,936 and Dakshina Kannada with 5,534. The CEOs office said the last hearing would be conducted on October 12, while October 22 is the last date for disposal of claims and objections and the notice phase. As on October 5, Karnataka had 4,50,29,916 electors on its electoral roll, comprising 2.23 crore male, 2.26 crore female and 2,863 transgender electors. The CEOs office said that, following requests from registered and recognised political parties, lists of persons who have been issued notices under the No Mapping and Anomalies categories have been published on the CEOs website. It also said EROs had been directed to take action according to law against applicants who knowingly make false statements or declarations in Form 6, Form 6A, Form 7 or Form 8. Such action would follow an inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and would be in accordance with Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950. The CEOs office also clarified that some electors may find that their Part Number and Serial Number have changed in the draft electoral roll because of the rationalisation of polling stations and re-serialisation of electors. Electors unable to locate their names in the same part where they were previously registered have been advised to search using their EPIC number on the Election Commissions voter portal or through the ECINET mobile application. -With PTI Inputs

articleFeaturedImageAlt: AICWA claims Pati Patni Aur Panga 2 set affected in Goregaon Film City fire
description: The blaze erupted in the structure behind Prime Focus Studio around 4 pm, following which Mumbai Fire Brigade and other agencies were immediately mobilised.
