articleTitle: Do we really need affidavits?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: affidavit
description: If identity can be authenticated, false statements can be punished and facts can be verified, what does the act of swearing actually add?
body_raw: By Preeti Kumari The Act XIV of 1848 empowered the Supreme Court at Fort William to commission persons to take affidavits and solemn affirmations. An affidavit so taken was deemed to have been taken in Court. The purpose was practical It let a sworn statement be treated as made in court without the maker appearing in person. Nearly two centuries later, we must ask whether a device intended to save a journey has itself become the reason for another journey? Affidavits are routinely used for caste, income declaration, residence, and eligibility for benefits, etc. But this does not answer a fundamental question Why must the statement be sworn at all? Suppose an applicant states in an affidavit that her annual family income is below Rs 2 lakh. The notary neither verifies ITRs, employment records or bank accounts nor bears responsibility if the statement later proves false. The affidavit establishes the makers belief in its truth under oath, not the truth of the assertion. The government may still require documentary evidence or administrative enquiry before deciding the claim. We are dealing with four separate questions Who made the statement? Can the authority or court legally receive it? What happens if the maker deliberately lies? Is the underlying fact true? If identity, admissibility and consequences for deliberate falsehood can all be provided by law, why must I go before another person and swear that I am telling the truth? The line Affidavit to be enclosed creates an entire journey. She finds the format, gets it drafted, procures stamp paper, locates a notary or magistrate, pays, and returns to the government office or court carrying substantially the same statement she could have made directly. A few thousand rupees fee, and a days lost work mean something very different to a poor person seeking a caste certificate or welfare benefit than they do to the system imposing the requirement. But the argument cannot stop at the government counter. There is another citizen whom affidavit reform often forgets The person caught in a legal proceeding - a witness, an accident victim, a maintenance claimant, a spouse in a matrimonial dispute or a person defending her home in a property case too is a citizen. Some inconvenience is unavoidable in administering justice but inconvenience should serve a clear purpose. If the statement needs to be challenged, challenge it. If the maker needs to be cross-examined, summon her. If records contradict her, examine the records. If the underlying fact needs verification, verify it. If she deliberately lies, punish her. Which of those protections disappear merely because she did not submit a sworn affidavit? To dispense with affidavit is not an untested idea. In the United States, 28 U.S.C. 1746, Unsworn declarations under penalty of perjury, separates truthfulness and legal liability from the necessity of swearing. Irelands Civil Law and Criminal Law Act 2020 has removed the need for making statements through sworn affidavits with electronically signed self-declarations - Statement of truth. Crucially, it has replaced, in the proceedings covered by the reform, the sworn form with a statement carrying direct legal responsibility. Affidavit reform in India has generally asked In which cases can we dispense with the affidavit and accept a self-declaration?. That is, it starts with the affidavit as the default and the declaration as an exception. Perhaps the presumption should now be reversed. The reform can begin with the principle Preserve the legal consequence, dispense with the ritual. For government services, an authenticated self-declaration carrying clear legal consequences for deliberate falsehood should suffice. The courts could recognise an electronically authenticated statement of truth, with Aadhaar-based authentication as one possible means of establishing identity, give it the evidentiary status by law, preserve the ability to challenge it and cross-examine its maker, and attach serious consequences to deliberate falsehood. In Swear Not At All 1817, Jeremy Bentham asks If these safeguards can be built into the process, and falsehood punished, what does swearing add? Perhaps it is time the affidavit itself proved its necessity. The writer is IAS officer of 2020 batch, Assam-Meghalaya cadre

articleTitle: Ex-Bengaluru jail chief held for releasing lifer on fake Supreme Court order
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru prison official fake Supreme Court order
description: Shankar A Aradhya, who was serving a life sentence in a kidnapping case, was released from Bengaluru Central Prisons on November, 13, 2018.
body_raw: The police have arrested a former chief superintendent of Bengaluru Central Prisons for allegedly assisting in the release of a life convict by forging a Supreme Court order. M Narayana, Deputy Commissioner of Police Electronic City, announced the arrest of M Somashekar, who is now Deputy Inspector General Prisons, North Zone, Gulbarga, on Monday. In May, the current superintendent in-charge of the prison discovered that the release order submitted for the convict Shankar A Aradhya was fake and filed a police complaint. The police later found that Srikanth S, who was then a second-division assistant and is now a first-division assistant in the prisons Convict Prisoner Section, had forged a Supreme Court order dated November 2, 2018, to release Shankar. Based on the order, Shankar was released from the prison on November, 13, 2018. During the investigation, Shankars wife stated that Somashekar had also assisted in securing her husbands release. The police arrested both Srikanth and Shankars wife and they were remanded to judicial custody. However, Somashekar allegedly failed to cooperate with the investigation. He was produced before court and sent to police custody for further investigation till October 9. Who is Shankar A Aradhya? Shankar had been serving a life sentence in a 2001 kidnapping case registered by the Chickpet police. His appeals before the Karnataka High Court and later the Supreme Court were unsuccessful, with the sentence being upheld. Shankars wife, who had come in contact with Srikanth, allegedly managed to strike a deal to get her husband out. While Srikanth had sought Rs 12 lakh, she paid Rs 6 lakh and then Shankar came out of the prison using the forged Supreme Court order, a police officer said. Shankar was engaged in construction contracting, a business his father had also been involved in.

articleTitle: Suvendu Adhikari signs UDAN airport pact, blames delay on TMC ‘attitude’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UDAN scheme West Bengal Suvendu Adhikari
description: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari said land had become the main obstacle for aviation infrastructure development under Trinamool Congress rule.
body_raw: The West Bengal government has finally joined the Union civil aviation ministrys UDAN scheme by signing a memorandum of understanding to set up four new airports in the state-at Chharra in Purulia, Balurghat, Hasimara, and Kalaikunda. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, Union Civil Aviation Minister Kinjarapu Rammohan Naidu, and senior officials from both the state and the Centre attended the event at Nabanna where the agreement under the Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik UDAN scheme was signed on Monday. At a press conference held afterwards, Adhikari sharply criticised the previous Trinamool Congress government, accusing it of delaying the states airport and infrastructure development. Even though the central government asked for land, the previous government did not provide it. The signing of the agreement was stalled for so long because of this negative attitude. The previous government had refused to provide land for a second airport in Kolkata. Not only the airport, but due to the failure to provide land, several important national highway and railway projects remained stuck for years, the chief minister said. Adhikari further said, Land had become the main obstacle in the path of development. Once the new airports are built, trade and economic activity in the state will surge. As per the MoU, the state government will provide required land and basic infrastructure, while the Centre and the Airports Authority of India will oversee the airport development. The chief minister said the government planned to set up a modern pilot training centre at Behala in southwestern Kolkata. The four new airports are expected not only to reduce pressure on Kolkata airport but also to create direct air connectivity between the states districts and other parts of the country.

articleTitle: CJI says Supreme Court did not approve Form 6 changes: What the form is, why it matters
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Form 6 mess: People served SIR (Special Intensive Revision) notices arrive at Appasaheb Kulkarni Primary School in Gokhalenagar on Monday with their documents. (Express Photo - Arul Horizon)
description: The voter enrolment form was changed to include questions linked to the special intensive revision, prompting objections over the legal process followed.
body_raw: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday October 5 said that the Supreme Court had not approved any of the modifications to Form 6 in response to an argument on the unlawful modifications made to Form 6. While hearing petitions against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, a three-judge bench headed by the CJI said the Supreme Court will examine who modified the form after receiving a report from the Election Commission. The latest development comes two weeks after The Indian Express investigation on September 23 that revealed that two Election Commissioners had flagged the illegal and unauthorised changes to Form 6. One petition accused the Chief Election Commissioner of deliberately manipulating the electoral roll bears no reasonable nexus or legal connection to his official duties. Such an act falls squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constitutes distinct, personal criminal liability, it added. What is Form 6? Form 6 is the statutory form for applicants who have newly become eligible voters after turning 18 years of age or acquiring Indian citizenship or deleted voters who want to apply afresh. The existing Form 6, which is published in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, asks the applicant to provide the name and EPIC number of those family members with whom they currently reside. The Indian Express reported on July 12 that the online version of the form on ECINET had a new declaration inserted between the above two sections. The change introduced questions related to the Special Intensive Revision SIR into Form 6. It asked applicants to choose one of three statements whether their name appeared in the electoral roll during the last SIR held in the early 2000s, whether a parents or grandparents name appeared in that roll, or whether neither their name nor that of their parents appeared in it. If their name appeared in the 2000s SIR, applicants were asked to provide the Assembly constituency number, the polling booth number known as part number and the serial number at which their father or mother was registered in the last SIR. Interestingly, the Form 6 available for download on the EC portal did not have this declaration. Why was the change disputed? The Indian Express investigation revealed that Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi had formally objected to decisions taken and orders issued without their knowledge at least 14 times over 10 months. The changes under scrutiny concerned the national rollout of the SIR. After The Indian Express reported on the updated Form 6 on ECINET in July, Sandhu put on record on August 13 that it was unauthorised and illegal and must be removed immediately. Since the move was without amendment, the two Election Commissioners had objected to the same. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, only the central government can amend the voter enrolment, deletion and correction forms. On September 26, the Election Commission announced it had removed the SIR declaration in Form 6 on the ECINET application portal in states where the SIR has concluded. However, the declaration was still there for those states where the SIR is still ongoing. The EC said, For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used. Interestingly, the ECs press note did not mention the online form, or the question, or say whether it has been removed. However, it said that the Supreme Court upheld the declaration, which the courts May 27 order on the SIR does not appear to do in terms. And it does not say who put the question there in July, or why it stayed after Sandhu called it unauthorisedillegal on August 13. What does the law say? Article 326 of the Constitution guarantees the right to enrol as an elector to all adult citizens who are ordinarily resident in a particular Assembly constituency, unless otherwise disqualified by law. The Representation of the People Act, 1950 empowers the Union government to make rules for the conduct of elections and the registration of electors. Section 28 of the Act, titled Power to make rules, says The Central Government may, after consulting the Election Commission by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. It also says that every rule made under the Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament. Form 6 is a part of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, which emerges from the Act. Therefore, any change to the form would require an amendment and gazette notification by the Law and Justice Ministry. However, the ministry did not notify any change to Form 6, as seen in the notifications available on the e-Gazette website from June 24, 2025 - when the EC first announced the SIR - to date.

articleTitle: Minimum 10% water cut in Maharashtra from October 16 amid drought, El Nino concerns
articleFeaturedImageAlt: maharashtra drought water cut
description: Amid drought-like conditions, the Maharashtra government has ordered a minimum of 10 percent water cut.
body_raw: The Maharashtra government has directed all municipal corporations, municipalities, and gram panchayats to impose a minimum 10 percent water cut from October 16, citing water storage, drought-like conditions, and the possibility of El Nino-related water stress extending into next year. Local bodies have also been asked to undertake special drives to identify and stop water leakage. Besides, sewage treatment plants have to be operated at full capacity. The government has local bodies to ensure that instead of fresh water, treated wastewater should be used for gardening, construction and washing. Water Resources Minister Girish Mahajan said the department had prepared a reservoir-wise and use-wise water management plan up to August 31, 2027, with drinking water given the highest priority. The government has asked all agencies to use water carefully and take measures to conserve available supplies. Under the plan, water needed for drinking purposes will first be reserved in dams and reservoirs up to August 31 next year. The department said it would take into account evaporation, siltation and unauthorised water extraction while calculating the available supply. A 10 percent emergency buffer stock will be maintained in every reservoir to deal with uncertain rainfall and water situation. In an extreme situation, water from the dead storage of a reservoir may also be used after a technical assessment, the government said. Irrigation only after drinking water, livestock needs The department has also laid down a priority order for agricultural use. Water will be released for agriculture only after meeting the drinking water, livestock and fodder requirements. For irrigation, the priority will be rabi foodgrain and fodder crops, followed by other rabi crops. Water will be made available to perennial crops only if supplies remain after meeting these requirements. The government has also said it will encourage water-saving irrigation methods. Industries must reuse 30 of water For the industrial sector, the government has made reuse or recycling of at least 30 per cent of the consumed water mandatory. The move is part of the departments efforts to reduce freshwater demand as reservoir levels remain limited, according to the government. Illegal extraction under scanner As two-thirds of Maharashtra is reeling under drought-like conditions, the government will form joint squads to patrol dams, rivers and canals and prevent unauthorised water extraction. The squads will take action against those drawing water illegally. The water availability will be reviewed regularly through guardian ministers and canal advisory committees, Girish Mahajan said. Every department and citizen must use every drop of water carefully to avoid a water crisis in the coming year, Mahajan said. The government also referred to 265 talukas where drought had been declared, saying that the possibility of El Nino conditions continuing into the following year had prompted the detailed planning.

articleTitle: Supreme Court gets 3 new judges, including its second woman Justice

description: High Court Chief Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh elevated to Supreme Court
body_raw: President Droupadi Murmu has appointed three High Court chief justices - Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh as judges of the Supreme Court. The appointments were made in exercise of the powers conferred on the President by the Constitution of India, Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said in a post on X on Monday. In exercise of the powers conferred by the Constitution of India, the President of India is pleased to appoint the following Chief Justices of High Courts as Judges of the Supreme Court of India  - Arjun Ram Meghwal arjunrammeghwal October 5, 2026 Justice Sunita Agarwal is the Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court, while Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya is the Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court. Both have the Allahabad High Court as their parent High Court. Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh is the Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court and has the Jharkhand High Court as his parent High Court. The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended the names on September 28. articleTitle: Woman loses 13 kg after completing 75 Hard challenge; what daily workouts do to your joints
articleFeaturedImageAlt: weight loss
description: Consistency works better when it includes recovery
body_raw: At a time when many people struggle to stay consistent, digital creator Yashmine Kaur recently shared a glimpse of completing the 75 Hard challenge. Sharing glimpses of her diet and fitness journey, she wrote, Day 7575 Hard Challenge. Fat to Fit Journey. Forever grateful for the support I got. This was one of the reasons I never stopped showing up. She also shared that she started at 75 kgs and lost more than 13 kgs, down to 62.5 kgs. For context, 75 Hard consists of a structured discipline program for 75 days that includes strict daily rules like indoor and outdoor workouts, hydration, reading, and diet adherence. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Dr Mrinal Prakash, consultant orthopaedics joint replacement and sports injury specialist at KIMS Hospitals, Thane, said a structured fitness routine can improve muscle strength, mobility, endurance, and overall physical conditioning. However, when exercise is done consistently for several weeks, recovery becomes just as important as the workout itself. Muscles may adapt relatively quickly, but tendons, ligaments and joints can take longer to adjust to repeated loading. The key is to increase exercise progressively rather than suddenly pushing the body beyond what it is accustomed to, said Dr Mrinal. Can exercising every day increase the risk of joint or muscle injuries? Daily movement is not inherently harmful, but the type and intensity of activity matter. Repeating high-impact exercises or heavy resistance training without adequate recovery can contribute to overuse injuries. Common problems can include tendon irritation, muscle strains, knee pain, shin pain or lower-back discomfort. Risk also increases when someone ignores persistent pain and continues training at the same intensity. Exercise should challenge the body, but it should not consistently leave it struggling to recover, said Dr Mrinal. What is the difference between normal post-workout soreness and an injury? Mild muscle soreness after a new or demanding workout is common and generally settles as the body adapts. Injury-related pain tends to be more localised, persistent or progressively worsening. Swelling, instability, restricted movement, a sudden sharp pain or discomfort that changes the way a person walks or performs an exercise should not simply be pushed through. These are signals to reduce activity and, if they persist, seek an appropriate medical assessment, said Dr Mrinal. How can someone continue a demanding fitness routine while protecting their joints? Consistency works better when it includes recovery. Warm-ups, proper exercise technique, suitable footwear and adequate rest can reduce unnecessary stress on the musculoskeletal system. It is also useful to vary the type and intensity of workouts instead of repeatedly loading the same joints and muscle groups, said Dr Mrinal.   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Yashmine Kaur yashminek24 Strength, mobility and low-impact activities can complement more demanding sessions. Most importantly, progress should be gradual. Completing a fitness challenge is not just about showing up every day it is also about giving the body enough time to adapt, repair and become stronger, said Dr Mrinal. articleTitle: The Cornell case made me ask my sons — what would you have done?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Cornell fraternity case, Cornell sexual assault case, Cornell Chi Phi fraternity, Cornell 2024 allegations,
description: As a mother of two boys studying at American universities, I have talked to them about consent, sex, drugs and equality. But I had never asked them what they would do if another man crossed the line
body_raw: By Nalini Sorensen As details surfaced about the reopening of the alleged 2024 gang-rape case at Cornell University, I felt physically ill. I read every horrific detail, and then my thoughts turned to my sons. I have two sons, aged 18 and 21, both studying at universities in America, including an Ivy League one. That made this feel very real for me. I share a close relationship with both of them, and over the years, we have spoken openly and honestly about pretty much everything - relationships, sex, consent, equality, LGBTQ issues, alcohol, drugs, cigarettes and vaping, but I had never asked them what they would do if another man crossed the line. I wondered if Id done enough. What is enough in this world where the rules change daily? Is a mothers work ever truly done with her children? Here I was, thousands of miles away in Mumbai, my head swirling with thoughts, while both my sons were living in university dorms where frat parties happen regularly. There was something I needed to ask my sons. I called my older son first. He didnt pick up. My younger one didnt answer my call either. So, I did the next best thing. I sent each of them a text message This Cornell incident has made me feel sick to my stomach, and it has made me ponder. We have never had this kind of a talk, and so I have to ask. if you were in a text thread with 50 other young men, and they sent violent and explicit messages about a passed-out young woman, what would you do? Because, to me, its not just about those seven boys. Its also very much about the 50 others who were on that chat. Thats what I was calling about. Both my sons called me back. The conversations went very differently, but on reflection, very similarly. I told each of them that it was the silence of those other boys that bothered me. Only a thin line separates silence from complicity. I asked questions When is it okay to keep quiet? When must you call for help? When do you take yourself out of a setting? What kind of situations demand what kind of action? Is consent from someone drunk or high valid? It was interesting to hear their responses and see the difference in their personalities coming through. My younger son was outraged. He could not believe I thought he would keep quiet. It upset him that I had to even ask him what hed do that I didnt just know. Young, brash, fiery, principled. My older son was fuming over what he had read about the case. He wanted consequences that fit the allegations. He hated that Jane Doe had to go through this, that she had had to keep living with it. He wanted justice for her. And yes, he sure as hell wouldnt look the other way. Compassionate, just, action-driven. Both touched on the fact that the other boys on the chat might not have thought this was really happening. That they might have regarded it as someone typing nonsense while high or drunk, or both. It gave all three of us some pause. That led us to discuss which messages we should question, particularly when someones safety is at stake. Who should we believe? Who should we give the benefit of doubt to? They werent easy conversations to have, but I definitely slept better that night. The truth is, as parents, we are never really done. Our children may grow up and leave home, but the conversations dont have to end. We keep asking the difficult, uncomfortable questions. We keep reminding our sons that masculinity doesnt require hardness. We keep teaching them not just how to avoid doing the wrong thing, but how to recognise when something is wrong, and find the courage to do something about it. We keep hoping that we have raised boys who will know when to speak up, when to step in, when to ask for help, and when to understand that silence is a choice too. We owe that to our sons. And we owe it to every girl in the world. Sorensen is a Mumbai-based childrens author

articleTitle: Delhi waste dumped in Gurugram: 10 arrested, interstate syndicate under scanner
articleFeaturedImageAlt: waste pickup
description: The action comes as the city grapples with 1,200 tonnes of municipal waste a day and millions of tonnes of legacy waste. Police said so far, no link with any Delhi civic body has been found.
body_raw: A waste trail from Delhi to Gurugram has led to 10 arrests and the seizure of seven vehicles, with police alleging that an interstate network was bringing in municipal and plastic waste to dump, segregate and sell in the state. As of now, we have found that the dumping work was operating like a syndicate, where they would also segregate useful items theyd find and sell those, a senior police officer said. Senior officers said the enforcement drive on Sunday evening was launched following a Friday review meeting chaired by Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, who directed authorities to ensure the city is not turned into a dumping ground and ordered strict action against vehicles bringing in garbage from outside. Following the directives, police initiated suo motu action rather than waiting for formal complaints, officials said. Four FIRs have been registered across three border-adjacent police stations two at Bajghera, and one each at Udyog Vihar and Rajendra Park. This is the first of its kind police operation earlier we would only get complaints of it happening on a small scale, said an officer. Inside the op Gurugram Police spokesperson, Assistant Sub-Inspector ASI Sandeep Kumar, said the drive was carried out under the directions of the Commissioner of Police and the supervision of the Deputy Commissioner of Police West. Police teams conducted checking and naka-bandi at several locations. Vehicles bringing garbage and plastic waste from Delhi were intercepted, leading to the arrest of 10 accused and the recovery of seven vehicles, including canters and tractor-trolleys, Kumar said. Questioning revealed that the waste was being transported into Gurugram through a coordinated network linked to Delhi, ASI Kumar. Once brought across the border, the plastic waste was separated from the general refuse and segregated before being dispatched to buyers elsewhere, he added. ASI Kumar said that investigators are scrutinising ownership records of the seized fleet. Police teams are gathering information regarding the arrested accused and vehicle owners. If the involvement or role of any vehicle owner is established during the probe, strict legal action will be taken against them as per law. Strict action for environmental protection will continue, he said. A senior police officer said notices have been sent to truck owners to join the investigation. We will check if the vehicles belong or are under any government or private body from Delhi, he said. So far, no prima facie link with any Delhi civic body has been found, officers said. Police said further investigation is underway to track the waste supply chain back to its collection points in the national capital and identify all intermediaries involved in the transport and recycling network. Gurugrams waste problem The operation assumes importance given the scale of the citys garbage problem. Millennium City generates roughly 1,200 tonnes of municipal solid waste daily, as per civic body data, while struggling to fully clear millions of tonnes of legacy trash at the oversaturated Bandhwari landfill. The landfill site is under persistent National Green Tribunal NGT scrutiny over alleged groundwater contamination, toxic leachate, and frequent fires. Garbage is currently not segregated at the time of collection from most residents. The citys garbage collection and processing has been addressed only through stopgap arrangements and short-term tenders for over two years, when the work order of the previous contractor was scrapped due to poor performance.

articleTitle: Ola, Uber, bike taxis in Maharashtra get 9 months to switch to 100% EV fleets
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ola uber 100 percent EV fleets maharashtra
description: The 100 percent EV fleets directive comes amid concerns raised by bike taxi associations and riders over the mandatory transition to electric vehicles.
body_raw: The Maharashtra government has set July 2027 as the deadline for bike taxi aggregators, including Ola, Uber, Rapido and other bike taxis to transition to a 100 per cent electric fleet. In October, the State Transport Department wrote to ride-hailing aggregators and Regional Transport Offices RTOs across Maharashtra, granting a nine-month phased transition period to operators to switch to 100 percent EV fleets, following directions from Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis. Under the 100 percent EV transition plan, aggregators currently operating petrol-powered bike taxis will be given six months in the first phase to comply with the EV mandate. Operators that have applied for provisional or temporary licences under the Maharashtra Bike Taxi Rules, 2025, will receive an additional three months to meet the requirement. The directive comes amid concerns raised by bike taxi associations and riders over the mandatory transition to electric vehicles. What did the bike taxi aggregators seek? In September, the Maharashtra Bike Taxi Welfare Association had written to CM Fadnavis and other officials, including the State Transport Minister and Transport Commissioner, requesting one-and-a-half years to fully switch to EVs given several considerations. Most bike taxi riders hail from middle or lower-middle-class backgrounds, making it difficult for them to undertake a significant investment to purchase an EV bike at once. The lack of EV charging infrastructure and the smaller life of an electric vehicle also makes this decision more difficult, Amit Gawde, President of the Maharashtra Bike Taxi Welfare Association, said. Aggregators had also sought an extension until 2030, citing the Maharashtra Electric Vehicle Policy and the need for more time to transition their fleets, according to a state government official. The government has, however, granted them only nine months to switch to 100 percent EV fleets. Aggregators had also sought an extension until 2030, citing the Maharashtra Electric Vehicle Policy and the need for more time to transition their fleets, according to a state government official. The government, however, has granted only a nine-month transition period. The move comes as the state has stepped up enforcement against unauthorised and non-compliant bike taxi operations. State Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik had earlier told The Indian Express that the government had initially considered allowing a 5050 mix of petrol and electric motorcycles. However, the Cabinet rejected the proposal amid concerns that companies could choose not to procure electric vehicles despite having the capacity to do so, as they are more expensive.

articleTitle: 10,107 women candidates clear JEE Advanced, highest in 6 years
articleFeaturedImageAlt: women in IIT
description: While the qualification rates for most categories improved, the figures for general and OBC candidates dropped.
body_raw: For the first time in six years, the number of women candidates qualifying the JEE Advanced crossed the 10,000 mark in 2026, shows the Joint Implementation Committee JIC report by IIT Roorkee, which conducted the JEE Advanced this year. According to the JIC report, a total of 43,112 female candidates registered for JEE Advanced. Of these, 40,562 appeared in both papers and 10,107 qualified. The success rate among registered women candidates rose from 21.7 in 2025 to 23.4 this year. One in four registered women candidates qualified this year, compared with roughly one in five last year. The top female candidate scored 280 marks mathematics 101, physics 86, chemistry 93, securing All India Rank 77. Among the 3,814 female students who got admission, 37 secured seats through the gender-neutral pool, the report said. Read  IITs, IIMs see more women joining than ever as placements and salary packages rise The qualification rate for Scheduled Caste SC and Scheduled Tribe ST candidates also saw a sharp jump of 9.8 and 8.1 percentage points, respectively, from last year. In 2026, a total of 15,856 SC candidates and 6,379 ST candidates qualified in JEE Advanced, whereas last year it was 12,499 and 5,008, respectively. The number of Economically Weaker Section EWS candidates qualifying the entrance exam also went up from 6,291 to 6,377. The report also shows a decline in the number of general category candidates qualifying for the entrance exam this year. Last year, a total of 16,154 students from the general category qualified the exam. The number dropped to 15,883 this year, with the qualification rate declining from 43 to 39.8. articleTitle: DMK gets court permission to sue TVK ministers over Veeramani case remarks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Granite baron R Veeramani faces multiple child sexual abuse cases as Madras High Court clears DMK to sue ministers and TVK IT wing over shielding claims (File Photo)
description: The DMK, which was in power when the allegations first came to light, is seeking Rs 1.01 crore in damages from Ministers Aadhav Arjuna and CTR Nirmal Kumar, and the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s IT wing
body_raw: The Madras High Court on Monday granted the DMK permission to pursue a defamation suit against two Tamil Nadu ministers and the ruling TVKs information technology wing over statements allegedly accusing the party of shielding granite businessman R Veeramani, who is facing multiple child sexual abuse cases. The DMK, which was in power when the allegations first came to light, is seeking Rs 1.01 crore in damages from Ministers Aadhav Arjuna and CTR Nirmal Kumar, and the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagams IT wing. It has also sought an order restraining the ministers from making statements it describes as defamatory. Justice K Govindarajan Thilakavadi allowed the partys application for leave to institute the suit. Mondays order concerns permission to bring the proceedings, and it does not decide whether the disputed statements were defamatory or establish the merits of either sides account. The application, argued by senior counsel J Ravindran, sought the courts permission because the TVK IT wings office and the headquarters of social media companies named in the proceedings-X Corp, Meta Platforms and YouTube-were outside the HCs territorial jurisdiction. Filed on behalf of the DMK by its general secretary, Duraimurugan, the suit places the timing of the original police response at the centre of the partys defence. According to the petition, police registered a First Information Report FIR under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act on October 7, 2025, a day after a child rights activist submitted a video clip showing the alleged sexual assault of a minor girl. The DMK argues that this sequence demonstrates that the police acted promptly under its government. The police had in February this year sought to file a closure report in the case, but a POCSO court intervened and ordered a fresh probe. The CMK maintains that the subsequent investigation proceeded according to law and the evidence available, and that it neither interfered in the inquiry nor had any connection or connivance with the accused. Those assertions form part of its case before the court. The DMK also alleges that the ministers remarks were intended to secure political advantage ahead of the Madurantakam and Dharapuram by-elections and to divert attention from what it calls the current governments failures. The ministers opposed the application on procedural grounds. They argued that, because they had been sued in their official capacities as Cabinet members, the DMK should have served notice under Section 801 of the Code of Civil Procedure or obtained permission under Section 802 to dispense with that requirement. At an earlier hearing two weeks ago, the judge had directed the defendants to file a counter-affidavit and listed the matter for Monday.

articleTitle: Woman goes under knife for ‘pointed’ nose, left with ‘crooked’ one, wins Rs 65,000 payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: cosmetic surgery nose job delhi woman hospital refund medical negligence consumer news
description: The doctor claimed that the complainant approached him with problem of bulbous nose and wanted refinement of her tip. It was stated that she specifically wanted cosmetic rhinoplasty for a well-defined and sharper nose.
body_raw: A Delhi District Consumer Commission has directed a doctor to pay Rs 65,000 to a woman who underwent cosmetic nose surgery, observing that while aesthetic dissatisfaction and medical negligence are distinct, the cosmetic outcome cannot be ignored, as the primary objective of cosmetic surgery is to make individuals appear beautiful. A bench of president Monika Aggarwal Srivastava and members Rajender Dhar and Ritu Garodia said the procedures purpose is to improve appearance and found shortcomings in service. The primary objective of cosmetic surgery is to make individuals appear beautiful. Aesthetics is frequently the focal point of the procedure. However, dissatisfaction with the aesthetic outcome and proof of medical negligence are two distinct matters and cannot be treated as synonymous, the bench observed on September 25. At the same time, it held that the aesthetic outcome cannot be completely disregarded in a cosmetic-surgery case because the very purpose of such a procedure is to improve the patients appearance. The ruling noted that the complainant has filed photographs which indicate that the tip of the nose has been turned a little up and the nose appears to be a little crooked. It added that the complainant also underwent a revision surgery by another doctor. Woman challenged nose job outcome The matter concerned a woman who approached the consumer commission alleging deficiency in service against a doctor and the hospital over the outcome of a cosmetic rhinoplasty surgery. Rhinoplasty surgery, commonly called a nose job, is a plastic surgery procedure that changes the size, shape, or proportions of the nose. The complainant had approached the doctor with concerns relating to the shape of her nose. A CT scan showed deviation of the nasal septum towards the right, following which she was advised open rhinoplasty with functional tip plasty and septoplasty. Septoplasty is a surgical procedure to straighten a deviated nasal septum, the wall of bone and cartilage that divides your nostrils. She underwent the surgery in January 2023, after paying Rs 1.30 lakh. After the surgery, she alleged that the nose tip had been positioned upwards, that the nose remained crooked, and that she continued to face breathing problems. She also alleged that the nasal packs were not properly fixed and that she had to undergo a revision procedure. The complainant later underwent a revision rhinoplasty with septal reconstruction by another doctor, incurring an expense of Rs 4.60 lakh. She wanted sharper nose Doctor The doctor, on the other hand, maintained that the complainant had been informed about the risks, had given informed consent, and had been told that the shape of the nose could change during the healing process. It was stated that the complainant approached him with a problem of a bulbous nose tip and wanted refinement of her nose tip. It was stated that she specifically wanted cosmetic rhinoplasty for a well-defined and sharper nose. Nose appeared crooked Order The commission noted that the complainant had undergone rhinoplasty after paying Rs 1.30 lakh, and the medical records confirmed that she had a deviated nasal septum and was advised open rhinoplasty with functional tip plasty and septoplasty. It was found from the photographs that the tip of the complainants nose had turned slightly upwards and appeared somewhat crooked, forcing her to undergo a revision surgery by another doctor. Considering the shortcomings in the service, the commission directed the doctor to pay 50 per cent of the Rs 1.30 lakh paid for the surgery. Takeaway The judgment clarified that while aesthetic dissatisfaction alone does not establish medical negligence, cosmetic outcomes remain relevant. It recognises shortcomings in cosmetic surgery as deficient service and provides consumers a remedy where the intended aesthetic outcome is not achieved. Consumers facing similar grievances may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Delhi helpline 011-23379146 or dial the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance.
