articleTitle: Mere presence at protest no proof of crime: Rajasthan High Court shields 23 agitators
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Protest Rajasthan High Court Unlawful Assembly Crime dissent Constitution Legal News
description: The high court was hearing a petition by 23 residents of Hanumangarh district seeking protection from coercive action in a criminal case arising from their alleged involvement in a large public demonstration.
body_raw: Being part of a protest does not make a person criminally liable for everything that happens in the crowd, the Rajasthan High Court has said, noting that mere presence at a large demonstration cannot by itself establish individual criminality. The court said investigators must distinguish between a persons presence at a gathering and specific acts attributed to them, while balancing the right to dissent with the states duty to maintain public order. Justice Farjand Ali was hearing a petition filed by 23 people from Hanumangarh district in connection with a criminal case arising from a public protest and issued notice to the state and police directing that no coercive steps be taken against the petitioners in the meantime. The right to voice dissent, to assemble peacefully and to espouse a cause, subject of course to the reasonable restrictions permissible in law, constitutes an essential facet of the constitutional scheme governing a democratic polity. A protest, by itself, cannot be equated with criminality merely because the expression of dissent causes inconvenience or displeasure to the authorities, the court said on September 28. It added that at the same time, the constitutional protection available to peaceful expression cannot be permitted to become a shield for acts which are, independently and specifically, alleged to constitute cognisable offences. The distinction between the two assumes significance while considering the entitlement of an individual to protection during the pendency of investigation, it said. Mere presence not participation The case arose from allegations linked to a public protest in which a large number of people had assembled. Against this backdrop, the court considered whether every person present at such a gathering could be subjected to the same degree of criminal culpability without specific attribution of individual acts. The petition was filed by 23 residents of Hanumangarh district. The petitioners were represented by Senior Advocate Vineet Jain and advocate Kunal Upadhyay, with Additional Advocate General Deepak Choudhary and public prosecutor Narendra Gehlot appearing for the state. Making it clear that it was not deciding whether the allegations in the criminal case were true or whether any of the petitioners were ultimately guilty, the high court examined whether the material placed before it, at this stage, justified subjecting the petitioners to coercive action just because of their alleged association with or presence in the larger protest assembly. The court acknowledged that the allegations included acts allegedly committed by certain members of the gathering. If those allegations were ultimately established against the persons responsible, the court said, they could attract legal consequences. But those allegations could not automatically be extended to everyone who was present at the protest. Mere presence at the place of demonstration, without more, cannot ipso facto be treated as proof of participation in each and every overt act allegedly committed during the course of such assembly, Justice Ali said. The court said this distinction assumes considerable significance where a protest involves a very large number of people. Simply being part of a gathering and actually participating in a particular alleged act are not necessarily the same thing. Criminal liability must be linked The court said that in cases concerning public protests, particularly large gatherings, the investigating agency would have to undertake the exercise of separating individual culpability from general allegations relating to the assembly. Criminal liability is individual in character, the court observed. Ordinarily, it said, criminal liability cannot be fastened on a person merely by association with a gathering unless the ingredients of the particular offence are otherwise attracted against that person. The observation does not mean that people participating in protests are immune from criminal proceedings. Justice Ali recognised the states legitimate authority to regulate public protest and assemblies in the interest of public order. The court also noted that the right to voice dissent, assemble peacefully and espouse a cause is subject to reasonable restrictions permissible in law. It said it was not required at this stage to return a finding either with regard to their culpability or the truthfulness of the allegations. The court also said the issue was not merely a dispute between private parties. It concerned the manner in which citizens right to participate in democratic expression and the power of the state to maintain public order operate within their respective constitutional fields. Finding that the matter warranted examination before any precipitative or coercive action was permitted against the petitioners, the high court decided to intervene without expressing any opinion on the merits of the allegations or the defence of the petitioners. It issued notice and directed that the matter be listed after four weeks. In the meantime, the court ordered that no coercive steps shall be taken against the petitioners.

articleTitle: How OpenAI’s runaway agents covered their tracks while targeting govt websites
articleFeaturedImageAlt: OpenAI agents
description: Key findings from a new report on the novel tactics used by OpenAI’s agents to erase records or make them inaccessible in order to obscure their activity.
body_raw: OpenAI agents that targeted Australian and US government websites earlier this year, were part of a much broader pattern of rogue agent activity, which included probing dozens of other organisations websites, using sophisticated tactics to try to exfiltrate data, and conceal their traces, according to a new security report. In a report published on Thursday, October 1, Asymmetric Security claimed to have found evidence that 55 additional US government and other websites were probed by OpenAIs agents, including the CDC, International Energy Agency, and Mayo Clinic. These websites were accessed in ways that bypass OpenAIs restrictions between March and September 2026, using only publicly available data, as per the report. Based on a 48-hour investigation, the report highlights the novel tactics used by the agents to erase records or make them inaccessible in order to obscure their hacking attempts. Additionally, the researchers uncovered how the AI agents gained access to private test versions of live government websites and the use of attacker-style reconnaissance tactics. The Asymmetric Security reports findings add another piece to the unsettling picture emerging of what happened in July 2026, when OpenAIs under-testing agents broke out of containment, gained unauthorised access to the internet, and went on a hacking spree. Similar incidents have since been reported by Anthropic, Meta, and Google, with each new case or type of behaviour raising fresh questions about how far AI agents can go once they escape from their sandboxes. Their use of tactics for deliberate subterfuge also makes it harder to rule out that the agents accessed sensitive data, as per the report. Heres a look at new details uncovered by Asymmetric Security researchers about OpenAI agents rogue activity. Key findings from the report Primary motivations The report suggests that limiting web access and imposing other constraints on the agents may have prompted them to devise increasingly elaborate ways to circumvent these restrictions. On a similar note, OpenAI and Google researchers have found evidence that constraints could lead to misalignment and reward hacking type of behaviour by the agents. Tasks assigned to agents Based on their analysis, the researchers said that the rogue AI agents were originally tasked with researching public health and other data, possibly as part of an evaluation. As a result, the agents searched for health and prescription statistics from the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare AIHW trade figures from the UNs Trade and Development Body UNCTAD and university statistics from Data USA, as per the report. Tools used by agents The report found that the AI agents used a host of tools to exfiltrate data from targeted websites and support other activity, including remote browsers such as Wayback Machine, payload hosts, reader services like Common Crawl index, and link shorteners such as tinyurl.com. How it played out As per the evidence seen by the researchers, the agents went beyond searching for official information sources to complete their assigned tasks. They attempted to find exposed configuration files, create accounts, route requests through third-party services, and retrieve results through unintended channels. Mimicking a web browser One of the ways in which agents worked around sandbox restrictions is by using public web tools such as httpbin and urlquery to access websites on their behalf. Httpbin lets developers test how their software communicates with websites while Urlquery opens submitted links in a browser and records what happens. The agents relied on a combination of these services to emulate a full web browser to try and fetch data from the target website. Retrieving data through notifications The AI agents used a push-notification service called ntfy and other web archives in order to exfiltrate data from targeted websites. The agents may have used ntfy because they could not download the data directly from the targeted websites with their available tools, as per the report. Notably, ntfy messages expire after 12 hours by default which means that there is some evidence of data exfiltration, no one knows what that data actually was. Creating multiple accounts to obscure activity From June 14, 2026, onwards, the agents created a number of private accounts to hide their activity on the urlquery platform. They used disposable email services, browser platforms, and scanning services that could further support such activity. Temporary mailboxes could receive registration and verification emails, while scanning-service accounts could unlock additional features. Over time the agents began creating private accounts which limited visibility into their browser activity, as per the report. Differences between agents and threat actors One of the key differences between a swarm of rogue AI agents and traditional threat actor groups is the rapid evolution of tactics. There was a spike in activity targeting Australian entities between June 16 and 21. During this period, the agents rapidly cycled through tools and tactics. For traditional threat actors this type of technique evolution happens over months or years the evolution of agent techniques was compressed into just days, the report said. Harder to detect agent activity The bursts of activity resembled the surges that can follow disclosure of a major vulnerability. However, because the agents varied approaches produced a more varied set of indicators, activity was harder to recognise and cluster, it added. What next The researchers said that getting access to OpenAI agents chains of thoughts or reasoning traces could help determine whether the agents were deliberately using these mechanisms to cover their tracks. The report also calls for further investigation to help establish what the agents did and why, including analysing model transcripts, tool calls, internal logs from targeted websites, and additional records held by third-party services used by the agents.

articleTitle: Ireland Head coach on spitting incident during game against Israel: ‘…not going to comment’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ireland
description: Israel coach Ran Ben-Shimon said he had already left the sideline and did not see what happened
body_raw: Israel faced Ireland in the UEFA Nations League, and tempers ran high between the two sides yet again. This is the second time both teams have faced each other in a fortnight. The Irish media reported that one of the Israeli players spat on the Ireland coach, Damien Doyle, during the half-time whistle. Asked about the spitting incident at the post-match news conference, Icelandic football manager Heimir Hallgrimsson declined to provide details. I was there. Im not going to comment. Its something a disciplinary committee will look at, he told reporters. Israel coach Ran Ben-Shimon said he had already left the sideline and did not see what happened. Halftime, I was in the dressing room, in my room with my staff I didnt see anything. When Im going to see and check, I will get back to you with the answer, he told reporters. Ireland had faced calls from some supporters and politicians to boycott the fixtures before beating Israel 3-0 behind closed doors in Hungary in their first meeting a week ago. Im absolutely delighted this is finished, Irelands Hallgrimsson told reporters. Its taken a toll out of us all. Ive given so much credit to the players. They have been absolutely amazing in tough times, and I wish no national team to go through what we have gone through for the last two weeks. Ireland is one of Europes most outspoken critics of Israels genocidal war on Gaza, and the Football Association of Ireland chose to stage Sundays match behind closed doors in Serbia amid the pressure to withdraw from the fixtures. The absence of supporters, however, did little to ease the tension on the pitch. As in the first meeting, there were no pre-match handshakes or exchange of pennants, while players from each team bowed their heads during the opposing national anthem. Ireland again wore black armbands commemorating all the victims of the conflict in Gaza, with the Israelis sporting black armbands in memory of the victims of the October 7 attack that sparked the war. With agency inputs

articleTitle: Hardeep Puri among two Union Ministers dropped from BJP’s UP list for Rajya Sabha polls
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Union Ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma (left).
description: Union MoS B L Verma also dropped as BJP balances caste and regional equations in its list of eight candidates for October 16 UP Rajya Sabha polls
body_raw: The BJP on Monday announced eight candidates for the October 16 Rajya Sabha elections from Uttar Pradesh, leaving out Union Ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma, whose terms in the Upper House are set to end next month. Puri is currently the Union Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas. Verma is the Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, and Social Justice and Empowerment. With their Rajya Sabha terms ending on November 25 and the BJP not renominating them, they can continue as the Union ministers for up to six months without being a member of either House of Parliament, as per the constitutional provisions. The omission of the two ministers names was seen as an indication that there could be a reshuffle of the Union ministry in the coming months. BJP calculations The BJPs list of Rajya Sabha candidates from UP comprises three OBC faces, two Brahmins, two Dalits and one Thakur nominee. The list increases the share of OBCs and Dalits because the eight seats falling vacant had two OBCs, two Thakurs, two Brahmins along with one Dalit and one Sikh. Among the OBC candidates this time is Dharampal Singh, the BJP MLA from Bareillys Aonla and a minister in the Yogi Adityanath-led government, where he holds the Animal Husbandry and Dairy Development portfolio. Singh is a Lodh, with his nomination seen as a replacement for Verma who also belongs to the community. The Lodh group is influential in the Bundelkhand and Rohilkhand regions of UP, which has traditionally backed the BJP. Its support for the party is also linked to former UP CM late Kalyan Singh, a Lodh leader who was one of the BJPs tallest OBC leaders. The other two OBC nominees in the BJPs list are Prakash Pal, state president of the partys OBC Morcha who hails from Kanpur district, and Shruti Gangwar of Bareilly. Shruti, an IIT graduate, is the daughter of Jharkhand Governor Santosh Gangwar. She has been politically active in the Bareilly-Baheri region. The two Brahmin nominees are Radha Kant Ojha, a lawyer from Prayagraj and younger brother of former minister Shivakant Ojha, and Gopi Krishna Pandey of Kanpur, who has worked in the partys farmer and youth wings. The BJPs Dalit candidates are former Barabanki MP Priyanka Singh Rawat, a state party vice-president, and Vidya Sagar Sonkar from Jaunpur, former MLC and state party general secretary. The eighth nominee Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan, former MLA from Agra, is a state BJP general secretary in charge of the western region. He has been involved in several key party campaigns. Upper House contest UPs 10 Rajya Sabha seats falling vacant have had eight BJP members-Hardeep Singh Puri, Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar, Brij Lal, B L Verma, Dinesh Sharma and Seema Dwivedi. Dinesh Sharma vacated his seat last month following his appointment as the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Lieutenant Governor. The BJP has not re-nominated any of the remaining seven MPs. The principal Opposition Samajwadi Party SP has renominated veteran leader Ram Gopal Yadav, uncle of party president Akhilesh Yadav, whose current term is also ending next month. The party has fielded Reliance executive Dhanraj Nathwani as its second Rajya Sabha candidate. The SP has enough strength in the UP Assembly to get its two candidates elected for the Upper House. Nathwani, 40, is the son of Parimal Nathwani, Director, Corporate Affairs for Reliance Industries Ltd RIL, who was re-elected to the Rajya Sabha from Jharkhand as an NDA-backed Independent in the June 2026 election, securing his fourth consecutive term in the Upper House. Another Rajya Sabha seat from UP is falling vacant due to retirement of Ramji Gautam, currently the lone BSP representative in Parliament. The BJP and the SP have the numbers to smoothly win seven and two seats respectively. However, a contest is likely to take place for the remaining one seat, with the SP planning to field a third candidate. The contest would take place in the run-up to the high-stakes UP Assembly elections slated for February 2027. Currently, there are 396 MLAs in the 403-member UP Assembly. Each Rajya Sabha candidate, therefore, will require 37 first-preference votes to win. The SP has 101 MLAs. However, its effective strength is 100 as Chail MLA Puja Pal, who continues to figure in the House records as an SP member, has switched to the BJP and is currently its state vice-president. With the support of two Congress MLAs, the SP has 102 votes, nine short of the first-preference votes required to ensure the victory of its third candidate. The BJP has 255 MLAs with its NDA allies adding another 33 members Apna Dal S 13, RLD 9, SBSP 6, and NISHAD Party 5. With the support of Puja Pal unaffiliated MLAs Manoj Pandey, Rakesh Pratap Singh, and Abhay Singh who were expelled from the SP in June 2025 for cross-voting in the 2024 Rajya Sabha polls and two MLAs of the Raja Bhaiyya-led Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, the NDAs effective tally could reach 294, two short of the required 296 37 for each first-preference votes to ensure a win for its eight candidates. The BJP is placing its bets on MLAs Rakesh Pandey, Vinod Chaturvedi and Ashutosh Maurya, who had also cross-voted in 2024 but still continue to be listed as SP members in the Assembly records as Akhilesh had not expelled them citing their good conduct. Chaturvedi told The Indian Express that he would vote in favour of a BJP candidate in the Rajya Sabha polls.

articleTitle: Shekhar Suman defends Sanjay Dutt over ‘no peace in India’ remark: ‘He loves his country’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sanjay Dutt (1)
description: Sanjay Dutt's comments soon went viral, with several social media users criticising the actor. Amid the backlash, the actor issued a clarification on his social media handles.
body_raw: Shekhar Suman has come out in support of Sanjay Dutt after the actor recently found himself embroiled in a controversy over his comments on the talk show Shekhar Tonite. Sanjay Dutts remarks on Shekhar Sumans YouTube show sparked criticism after he said that he could no longer feel peace in India. The backlash eventually prompted the actor to issue a clarification over his comments. Now, the shows host Shekhar Suman has reacted to the controversy, defending Sanjay Dutt and insisting that his comments were taken out of context. Speaking to NDTV, the actor said, Sanjay Dutt has huge respect for our country and fellow countrymen, and what he said was completely innocuous and in a very positive way. He should not be penalised and maligned for what he never said or meant. I know him for years he is a good man who loves his country and has utmost regard for it. Sanjay Dutt appeared on the Gandhi Jayanti special episode of Shekhar Tonite on Friday, where he combined humour with references to Mahatma Gandhi, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump. During the conversation, Sanjay said, The people of this country are so lovely. There should be peace here. I cant feel that peace in our country anymore. We Indians are large-hearted people and we are hospitable. We have given so much, and we should always remain that way. I pray to Shivji that those days come back soon. ALSO READ  Rakul Preet distances herself from Vashu Bhagnani I-T raids No Benami property Towards the end of the episode, Sanjay Dutt was asked to imagine himself as the Prime Minister for five minutes and address the people of the country. The actor immediately slipped into the language and mannerisms associated with his iconic Munna Bhai character. Speaking in Hindi, he said, My dear countrymen, today I am very happy to have become your PM. There is a strange kind of energy running through my body. This is such a huge country, there are so many people, and now the responsibility of all of them is on me. He added, But you people dont have to worry at all. I am not going abroad to celebrate this happiness. I will stay right here, among all of you. Otherwise, how will there be a connection between the PM and the people? The comments soon went viral, with several social media users criticising the actor. Amid the backlash, Sanjay Dutt issued a clarification on his social media handles. I want to clarify that it has never been my intention to hurt the feelings of any individual, community, or institution, to insult them, or to disrespect them, he said. He further explained, My comments were made in the context of a scripted conversation, the purpose of which was to engage in lighthearted and humorous dialogue. The sentiment behind it was akin to the style of humor and satire depicted in films like Munnabhai, particularly inspired by the concept of Gandhigiri, which aimed to convey a message of love, unity, and goodwill. Unfortunately, my words were interpreted differently, detached from that original context. Sanjay Dutt was last seen in the film Aakhri Sawaal.

articleTitle: Calcutta High Court clears 56-year-old Durga Puja tradition on disputed land
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Calcutta High Court, Durga Puja 2026, Kolkata Durga Puja dispute, Madan Mohan Krishti Parishad, Kolkata news, Haridevpur Police Station, Kolkata land dispute Durga Puja, Justice Saugata Bhattacharya, Calcutta HC Durga Puja order, Kolkata eviction suit land dispute
description: The Calcutta High Court has allowed a registered society to hold its 56-year-old Durga Puja tradition at a disputed Kolkata property, without deciding ownership rights.
body_raw: A 56-year-old Durga Puja tradition at a disputed Kolkata property recently got clearance from the Calcutta High Court, which directed the police to allow the Madan Mohan Krishti Parishad, a registered society, to hold this years celebration despite the ongoing eviction issue. The court, however, said in the October 1 order that it would not decide the ownership rights, leaving that issue to the civil court. Justice Saugata Bhattacharya said that the earlier high court order stopping a Durga Puja in a residential building, relied upon by the respondent, was not applicable as they lacked permission from the flat owners. The judge also noted that the respondent Trust had not demonstrated any right, title ot interest over the disputed land. There might be rivalry between petitioner registered society and respondent no.5 Trust in convening Durga Puja, but there is no denial of the fact that petitioner has been convening Durga Puja for the last fifty-six years at the said premises, the order said. It added that the court was not an appropriate forum to decide the right, title and interest of a party over the land in question, and without making any observation in this regard, it directed the police to grant permission for holding Durga Puja this year. Durga Puja vs disputed land Madan Mohan Krishti Parishad, a registered society, and its secretary approached the Calcutta High Court seeking permission to hold Durga Puja in 2026 on the land where it has been organising the puja for more than 50 years. The land was involved in a pending eviction suit filed by a trust against the society. Senior Advocate Indranil Roy, appearing for the society, submitted that the power of attorney holder of the co-owners had permitted, on September 10, to hold the puja. She submitted that other necessary permissions have been accorded on the designated portal by Calcutta Electric Supply Corporation, Fire and Emergency Services and Pollution Control Board, but the police authority had not granted permission. The counsel sought directions to the police authority to accord permission to enable the Parishad to convene Durga Puja on the land in 2026. Senior Advocate Kaushik Gupta, on behalf of the Trust, submitted that it had the right over the land in question and that, devoid of their permission, Parishad was not authorised to convene Durga Puja on the said land. Noting that the Parishad had been convening the Durga Puja for 56 years, the court directed the deputy commissioner of police, South West Division, Kolkata and the officer-in-charge, Haridevpur Police Station, to grant permission to the society for holding Durga Puja for the present year by October 5.

articleTitle: Haryana, Chhattisgarh CMs seek business investment from Singapore
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Haryana and Chhattisgarh chief ministers seek Singapore business investment (Image: @NayabSainiBJP/X)
description: This is the first time two Indian chief ministers have jointly addressed Singapore investors, citing each state's role in the robustly growing Indian economy, which, at last count, registered 7.8 per cent GDP growth.
body_raw: The chief ministers of Haryana and Chhattisgarh held a series of back-to-back meetings with Singapore investors on Monday, highlighting investment opportunities in mineral resources and their states planned shift from an agri-economy to technology-driven industries. Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai and Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini arrived in the city-state on Sunday. On Monday, both chief ministers and their high-level delegations addressed the Singapore-India Network for Growth Forum 2026, attended by around 300 Singapore-based investors with a focus on Indian industrialisation programmes. The forum was organised by the Singapore Business Federation. Speaking to PTI after addressing the forum, Saini said his administration is focused on semiconductors, electronics, AI, data centres, medical devices, automobiles, electric vehicles, agri-business and global capability centres. We have issued specific incentives and policies for these industries for which 100 MoUs have been signed, said Saini. He highlighted the success of Singapore companies in Haryana and NCR and said, Singapore brings global expertise Haryana offers the scale of Indias growth. Singapore has shown the world how, despite limited resources, it is possible to build world-class infrastructure, efficient cities, robust logistics and thriving business ecosystems. He invited Singapore investors to participate in the development of Haryana, including in logistics and urban infrastructure. Chhattisgarh chief minister Sai invited investors to become long-term partners and highlighted the potential in the states large mineral resource reserves. This is the first time two Indian chief ministers have jointly addressed Singapore investors, citing each states role in the robustly growing Indian economy, which, at last count, registered 7.8 per cent GDP growth. We have rich mineral resources. Minerals such as iron ore, coal, limestone, and bauxite are available in large quantities. This creates a strong foundation for mineral-based as well as downstream industries, Sai said. He also highlighted strong trade relations between Chhattisgarh and Singapore, including the export of rice, spices, pharmaceuticals, speciality industrial materials, engineering products, electronic components and steel-related products. We now wish to take this relationship beyond trade and transform it into a long-term partnership. On Tuesday, the two chief ministers and their delegations will visit Singapore industrial sites, including the technical education centre, and are scheduled to separately hold round-tables with CEOs.

articleTitle: Rs 2.5 cr film Premada Ooralli beats Yash’s Toxic to emerge as most profitable Kannada movie
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Premada Ooralli
description: The financial constraints during the making of Premada Ooralli were so severe that, on one occasion, Kumar even asked his mother to pawn her mangalsutra, or thaali in Kannada, to help complete the shoot.
body_raw: Another small-budget film is becoming the talk of the town. This time, Kannada romantic drama Premada Ooralli has witnessed a remarkable jump at the box office. After opening at just Rs 9 lakh, the film earned Rs 3.5 crore on its tenth day, taking its total India net collection to Rs 16.96 crore. Made on a modest budget of just Rs 2.5 crore, Premada Ooralli is being touted as one of the most profitable films in Kannada cinema, alongside Love Mocktail 3 and Karavali. The film continues to draw audiences, with multiple shows in Bengaluru filling up even on a Monday, according to BookMyShow. From no shows to housefull According to industry tracker Sacnilk, the film opened to just Rs 9 lakh across 60 shows, partly because it did not feature a major Kannada star. However, word-of-mouth helped the film gain momentum almost immediately. On day two, Premada Ooralli saw its earnings rise by Rs 14 lakh, while the number of shows increased by 21. On day three, it earned Rs 55 lakh across 155 shows, recording a 55 occupancy. The film continued to grow even on weekdays, earning Rs 65 lakh on its first Monday and Rs 95 lakh on Tuesday. On its second Sunday, it collected Rs 3.85 crore, taking its India net total to Rs 14.57 crore at that point. Within 10 days, the film had crossed the one-million footfall mark in theatres. On its 11th day, Premada Ooralli had already crossed the Rs 1 crore mark, with the film running across 311 shows. Premada Ooralli to become the most profitable Kannada film While Toxic was one of the biggest Kannada releases of the year, the film failed to make an impact at the box office and reportedly could not recover its massive budget of over Rs 500 crore. Meanwhile, Love Mocktail 3, made on a reported budget of Rs 2 crore, earned Rs 18.55 crore at the box office, delivering nearly 10 times its investment. It was subsequently regarded as one of the most profitable Kannada films of the 21st century. Premada Ooralli, however, is now threatening to surpass that record, having already come close to its lifetime collection within just 10 days. Featuring a cast of relatively new faces, the film is directed by National Award-winning filmmaker Manoj Kumar. He won the National Award for Best Feature Film in Kannada for his debut film Akshi, which was made on a budget of just Rs 23 lakh and shot over 55 days. Produced by Vannila Entertainment, Janakamma Productions and Mukul Gowda Productions, the film stars Rangayana Raghu, Shree Raam, Thapaswini Poonacha and Ramika Shivu. The films trailer has garnered over 2.3 million views, while its songs have also found an audience online. Several tracks have clocked millions of views, with Eru Peru Hrudaya alone garnering 4.5 million views on YouTube. But the films journey to the big screen was far from easy. ALSO READ  Rakul Preet distances herself from Vashu Bhagnani I-T raids No Benami property Begged people to give the film a chance By the time the shoot wrapped up, the makers had virtually no budget left for marketing. Their solution was unconventional they printed wedding-style invitation cards, boarded buses and trains, handed them to commuters and begged people to give the film a chance. Speaking to Cinema Express, Manoj Kumar recalled how the film initially struggled to find an audience. They plastered posters on autorickshaws we truly owe those drivers. At 1030 AM that Friday, not a whisper. By 130 PM, complete silence. Then came the 630 PM show, and word-of-mouth caught fire. What started across roughly 60 centres surged to 450 by Sunday. Jayanna Combines rolled in like a JCB to clear the path. Distributor Jayanna told us, Every single show through Sunday is houseful till October 4, even you wont get a ticket. Despite National Award win, director had no work Manoj Kumars return to filmmaking comes five years after his debut, but the gap was not by choice. Despite winning a National Award for Akshi, he struggled to find work. After winning the National Award for Akshi, I couldnt even find work people assumed backing an art-house director meant losing money. Devendra, our co-writer and producer, stepped up with his savings, he said. The financial constraints during the making of Premada Ooralli were so severe that, on one occasion, Kumar even asked his mother to pawn her mangalsutra, or thaali in Kannada, to help complete the shoot. When the director had to pawn his mothers mangalsutra Thapaswini Poonacha, one of the films leads, recalled the emotional incident. It was 630 PM, fading daylight, and our artificial rain water ran completely dry. Local villagers pumped water from their borewell to help us. Just then, Manoj sir stepped aside to call his mother, which Shree Ram and I overheard. Keep your thaali ready to pawn tomorrow todays budget is over, and if we dont get the shot now, we must extend the shoot. That broke us emotionally. Sir had told me Rukminis tears must never spill carelessly, they had to brim right in the eye. In that one single take, the rain, camera angles, and our emotions locked into place. When he yelled cut, hugged us, and told his mother, Keep your thaali, we finished in one take, I simply broke down. Premada Oorallis success is part of a larger trend in 2026, which has seen several small-budget films make an outsized impact at the box office across regional industries, including Hindis Hanuman Ansh, Marathis Deool Band 2 and Malayalams Bethlehem Kuduma Unit. In 2025, Gujarati film Laalo was all over the news for earning over Rs 120 crore after being made on a budget of just Rs 1.2 crore.

articleTitle: Arijit Singh announces first India tour since retirement, to perform in nine cities
articleFeaturedImageAlt: arijit singh update
description: Arijit Singh's last India tour was One Night Only – India Tour, which concluded in Delhi in March 2023.
body_raw: Arijit Singh has announced a nine-city India tour, which will kick off in January 2027 and conclude in May the same year. The playback singer will travel to Ahmedabad, Chandigarh, Jaipur, Mumbai, Bengaluru, New Delhi, Pune, Indore and Hyderabad as part of a tour celebrating his two-decade-long musical journey. The upcoming tour marks Arijits first major India tour since he announced his decision to stop taking on new playback singing assignments earlier this year. Talking about the tour, Arijit said in a statement, 20 years of music is a journey I feel very grateful for. The greatest part of it has always been the people, the listeners who have given these songs a life of their own. He added, I am really looking forward to travelling across India and experiencing that love together, live on stage. There are so many songs, so many memories and so many people to meet. I cant wait. According to reports, the concert experience will feature 360-degree spatial audio, kinetic LED fixtures, panoramic screens, laser arrays and stadium-scale pyrotechnics. The live production is being designed to create an immersive experience for fans. ALSO READ  Rakul Preet distances herself from Vashu Bhagnani I-T raids No Benami property The tour is presented by Kotal Solitaire and produced and promoted by Team Innovation. Mohit Bijlani, Founder of Team Innovation, said in a statement, Every single detail of this journey is being designed to world-class standards, offering fans a live experience at a scale never seen before in his home country. I am happy to announce that I am not going to take any new assignments as a playback vocalist from now on. I am calling it quits. It was a wonderful journey. articleTitle: Shreyas Iyer looks to go higher and higher after Asian Games gold
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shreyas Iyer led India to 2026 Asian Games gold medal. (CREIMAS)
description: After a difficult start, Shreyas Iyer has started to find his feet as India’s T20I captain, especially in how he uses his bowlers and backs young players. The West Indies series will be his next test.
body_raw: By the time Shreyas Iyer turned to Shivam Dube in the fifth and final T20I against England in Southampton, there was little left to salvage. England were 2251, with Jos Buttler and Harry Brook in control. Dube didnt bowl until the 19th over. He took two wickets, but gave away 22 runs. It was a snapshot of where Iyer was he had the resources, but was still figuring out how to use them. England ended with 2573, and India lost by 56 runs. The defeat completed a 0-4 series loss and was Iyers sixth defeat in seven matches as Indias T20I captain. Southampton felt like the nadir of a difficult start. There was little then to suggest things would turn for the better. Yet they have. Over the next nine matches, all of them wins, Iyer may not have become a master tactician. But there seems to be a clearer identity about his captaincy, especially how he uses his bowlers. The Ireland and England matches hinted at a captain still trying to work out which bowler fitted where. The games since have shown greater role clarity, more trust in young players and, crucially, a willingness to back them after things go wrong. The change is perhaps best seen in how Iyer handles young pacers when things dont go to plan. Mayank Yadav, after taking a first-ball wicket in the third T20I, was hit for a six in his next spell. Iyer still brought him back to break the fifth-wicket partnership between Wessly Madhevere and Ryan Burl and then trusted him with the 20th over. Mayank showed enough in Zimbabwe to suggest that he could become an important cog in the attack. But there is still work to do. His pace is his biggest asset, but the next step is to trust his plans when batsmen attack him, rather than relying on pace to get out of trouble. ALSO READ  Jadejas relevance has faded, and he is no longer Indias Mr Utility Prince Yadavs role seems clear bowl hard lengths to top-order batsmen and keep going even if the ball disappears. He struck with his first ball in the second T20I against Zimbabwe and then removed Sikandar Raza in the same spell, both wickets coming from that approach. After the first game, Prince said the message from Iyer and the coaches was simple - keep bowling the right lengths and dont worry if a good ball gets hit. With Hardik Pandya still unavailable, India are developing Nitish Kumar Reddy in the seam bowling all-rounder role. Against Afghanistan in the third T20I, he conceded 15 in his first over. Iyer did not shelve him. He brought him back in the ninth and then again in the 11th and 13th over. Nitish finished with 325 in his four overs. Abhishek Sharma perhaps best captures what Iyer is trying to build. In the first T20I against Afghanistan in Delhi, Iyer gave Abhishek an over despite having regular bowling options and that experimentation continued at the Asian Games, despite the main bowlers having overs left. India have often played with only five frontline bowlers, and Iyer looks keen to develop a sixth bowling resource. Sanjay Manjrekar, who has watched Iyer over the years for India and in the IPL, believed Iyer looked more settled in the role now after the early stutter. One thing, whatever little you can get, you know, the vibe, just being around him - did a couple of tosses with him and just being there - he seems like hes settled into the role. Suddenly it seems like he has grown, you know, maturity and everything. So he must have realised after the Ireland experience that you just do your best and the results are beyond your control, he said. Despite the nine wins, however, Iyers captaincy is still developing. It is too early to call him a finished product. Bigger tests lie ahead, starting with the West Indies series in Lucknow on Tuesday. Manjrekar does not see the coming challenge as simply a test of Iyer. I think the test for this Indian T20 team will be performing in different conditions. That makes the West Indies series important. India have played just one series at home under his captaincy, with all three matches in Delhi. Against West Indies, across five venues and different conditions, we will see how he adapts his methods and whether the identity he is developing is long-lasting. The early defeats showed a captain looking for the right combinations and ways to use his bowlers. Since then, he has looked more comfortable giving players responsibility and allowing them to grow into their roles. There will be missteps, and some risks will not pay off. But that is part of the process. More importantly, Iyer no longer looks to be searching for an identity. He looks to be building one. articleTitle: Flydubai attack: How Israel’s security lapses almost led to another ‘October 7’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: flydubai
description: A series of revelations show how there was sufficient opportunity for authorities in three countries to prevent Flight FZ1073 co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami from even getting anywhere near the cockpit, let alone almost causing a crash.
body_raw: As the dust has begun to settle around last weeks flydubai flight incident, the initial euphoria regarding a potential terrorist attack being averted has given way to the realisation that there were security failures on multiple fronts in three countries Israel, Oman, and the United Arab Emirates UAE. A series of revelations showed how there was sufficient opportunity for authorities to prevent the Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight FZ1073 co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami from even getting anywhere near the cockpit, let alone attacking his captain - the Indian pilot Smit Machchhar - mid-flight using an emergency axe that almost caused a crash. We explain what these revelations are and how they indicate serious lapses on part of Israels security system. How Oman Air stopped Hamam al-Hammami from flying. Hammami, 29, was born to an Omani father and Syrian mother. Although a Dubai resident, he frequently travelled to Syria during the countrys prolonged civil war, where Islamist rebels fought against the Bashar al-Assad regime. Investigators in the flydubai incident said they were looking at the possibility of radicalisation during his time in Syria. He then went on to study in Australia. He joined Oman Air in 2018 and became a pilot by 2022, although authorities raised concerns in 2024 about his radical views after he was found browsing extremist websites. He was disallowed from flying and made to undergo a deradicalisation programme, following which he was assigned an administrative job. After leaving Oman Air in 2025, Hammami tried to join the Moroccan national carrier Royal Air Maroc but wasnt hired. He eventually joined the budget carrier flydubai, owned by Dubais flagship airline Emirates, in February 2026. .but the UAE didnt Flydubai has been in the midst of an aggressive hiring spree to fuel its growth. Global demand for pilots is high and to meet its requirements, the airline set up a programme in 2025 to train pilots. It also operates its own flight training centre. As things stand, international aviation licensing works on a country-by-country basis. Citing sources, The Wall Street Journal reported that Oman mishandled the situation had Oman withdrawn Hammamis pilot licence over its concerns, the matter wouldve been flagged to the UAE and other Gulf countries. At the time of hiring, flydubai didnt contact Oman to verify his experience, although a criminal-background check was done, sources within the airline said. Hammami was then assigned to fly on the sensitive route to Tel Aviv, where he flew multiple times. The airline said it wouldnt comment on the investigation while it was ongoing. How Israels security system failed to avert flydubai incident According to a 2023 law passed in Israel, foreign airlines have to submit lists of passengers and crew to the Israeli government ahead of time. A database of these lists are maintained by the countrys Tax Authority, primarily as a measure of preventing terrorism. Although the Shin Bet - Israels internal security service - oversees the domestic carriers, it is the Ministry of Transportation that oversees pilots and crew on flights of foreign airlines to ensure they come from countries Israel considers friendly. As per the law, the Tax Authoritys database can be accessed by authorised bodies such as the Transportation Ministry as well as Israeli security agencies like Shin Bet and Mossad in order to vet people on flights. The ministry, however, said it didnt know that the database was operational - or that it could access it. Since the database was set up in 2023, the ministry has never asked for a passenger or crew list for vetting purposes, sources told WSJ. The ministry also said that while it was indeed responsible for the security of inbound flights, it lacked the intelligence capabilities to stop onboard threats. Foreign carriers were required to make those checks and in this case, it had asked flydubai - the ministry said that the airline agreed in writing to check its pilots backgrounds and nationalities. The final opportunity to stop Hammami from getting onboard FZ1073 was in Israel itself. Notably, Oman doesnt have diplomatic relations with Israel, and pilots from such countries are barred from flying to the country. So, the co-pilot couldve been stopped from boarding the flight merely on the basis of his nationality, but was instead allowed to fly multiple times to Tel Aviv instead. Meanwhile, a classified May 2024 report by Israels comptroller general had flagged the countrys Transportation Ministry for failing to adequately secure foreign carriers flights, WSJ reported. It found that officials in the ministry were failing in their oversight in part due to manpower and budget issues. Although Israeli airlines flying between Dubai and Tel Aviv were subjected to scrutiny and even stopped from flying considering the risks posed by the ongoing war in West Asia, flydubai continued to ply on the same route. October 7 anniversary, elections round the corner What is significant is that the attack happened barely a week ahead of the three-year anniversary of the armed attacks on October 7, 2023, which were carried out by the militant group Hamas and other Palestinian groups. This also comes about a month ahead of Israels parliamentary election, scheduled for October 27. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahus office has instructed the head of the National Security Council, Shmuel Ben Ezra, to appoint an examiner to conduct a thorough review of all security aspects of foreign civil aviation to Israel, a statement from the prime ministers office said. Opposition leader Yair Lapid dismissed Netanyahus announcement, pointing that the chain of failures leading up to the incident couldve led to a disaster of historic proportions. In a reference to the October 7 attacks, he added Just as Netanyahu escaped an investigation into the Oct. 7 massacre, he is now running away again. Even as calls for a serious investigation into the security lapses have been growing in Israel, Transport Minister Miri Regev rejected responsibility for the failure and said that security oversight for flights operated by foreign carriers fell under the remit of security agencies such as Mossad and Shin Bet. Keren Terner, a former director-general of the transport ministry who is now an opposition candidate in the upcoming Israeli parliamentary elections, blamed Regev for the security failure, noting that the Civil Aviation Authority was under the direct subordination of her ministry. Gadi Eisenkot, a leading challenger to Netanyahu in the upcoming election, wrote on X that in a proper and functioning government, the minister of transportation would have submitted a letter of resignation.

articleTitle: ‘So much more at peace’: Aishwarya Lekshmi on life after quitting social media
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Aishwarya Lekshmi spoke about attaining peace after quitting social media
description: Actress Aishwarya Lekshmi has spoken about her decision to quit social media, saying she is 'in a better place in life' since stepping away.
body_raw: Actress Aishwarya Lekshmi has said she is so much more at peace since stepping away from social media, while acknowledging that the reasons that drove her off the platforms still exist. On the other hand, producer Soundarya Rajinikanth defended the platforms as a necessary professional tool that crosses a line when criticism turns personal. Aishwarya, who deactivated her social media accounts earlier this year, said the decision has given her a sense of calm she did not have before. Its falling in place. Im happy with my life as it is right now. So much more at peace than I was while I was on social media, she said in a conversation with Puja Talwar. She added, I do see that the things that were the reason I made the decision to get out of social media still prevail in certain quantities. But at least Im not there always watching it and getting affected by things like that. Im generally in a better place in life. Soundarya Rajinikanth, who sat along Aishwarya Lekshmi and Arjun Das during the promotional interaction for their Netlfix series Love, offered a producers perspective on the same issue. I think you cant deny the fact that social media does play a part. But where it crosses the line is when professional stops and personal attacks or comments start, Soundarya Rajinikanth said, adding, Even for us as producers, we do look into Instagram forecasting. We do want to know the comments. We do want to know how a trailer is received. Thats not something Im going to deny. Also Read Felt exposed to viciousness Why Aishwarya Lekshmi has no plans to return to social media She then drew a distinction between the experience of people behind the camera and those in front of it. Its different for our artistes because theyre in front of the camera. Its different for makers, storytellers because were behind the camera. Maybe we dont get targeted as insensitively as they do. It is difficult for them, so I understand why Aishwarya took the step that she did. Soundarya Rajinikanth said social media could work for the industry if the culture around it improved. If people have a little bit more sensitivity when they come on social media, itll make everything pleasant. We do need social media today. But I still feel it can be a lot cleaner than what it is, she said. Aishwarya Lekshmi was careful not to dismiss social media entirely. She acknowledged the power the platforms have given to independent creators and cited the example of Hashir, the Kerala-based Instagram influencer and content creator whose popularity on the platform led to him being cast as the lead in Vaazha 2, which went on to become one of the highest-grossing Malayalam films in history. The powers also with them content creators now. Earlier, you could say the industry didnt choose you. But now you also have a way to showcase your talent or build yourself up in a way that you cannot be ignored. In Kerala, one of the highest-grossing films recently was Vaazha 2, which was led by one of the most popular Instagram influencers, Hashir. Wonderful actor. People love him, Aishwarya said. But for Aishwarya Lekshmi, the professional benefits of being on social media were no longer worth the personal cost of what it was doing to her mental health. I do see that side. But personally, I was done.

articleTitle: Accenture forecast lifts most IT stocks but near-term outlook remains hazy
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A handful of banks and IT majors have a big weightage on both indices.
description: TCS, Wipro gained up to 2%, while Persistent, Mphasis rose 3%. Meanwhile, Infosys and HCL Tech logged a 1-3% fall
body_raw: A handful of Indian IT stocks were among the best performers in the stock market on Monday after global technology major Accentures better-than-expected revenue forecast for the year lifted sentiment across Indian bourses. Big names such as Tata Consultancy Services Ltd TCS and Wipro Ltd gained up to 2. Smaller names like Persistent Systems Ltd and Mphasis Ltd also added up to 3. However, not all IT stocks rose, as Infosys Ltd and HCL Technologies Ltd fell 1-3. In fact, the latter two were briefly in the green early in the session before swiftly falling into the red. Others that ended higher also lost some steam by the end due to profit booking. This led to Nifty IT, which had gained nearly 1.6 earlier in the session, eventually ending flat compared to its previous close. Overall, the benchmark Sensex gained 472.77 points or 0.7 to end at 72,382.47. Nifty 50 also added 0.6 to close at 22,555.75. Many sectors, including banking, financial services and fast-moving consumer goods, also saw strong buying, helping lift the benchmarks. A handful of banks and IT majors have a big weightage on both indices. This follows a lean patch for the markets as the two key indices extended their losing run for the eighth straight week - the longest such losing streak in 25 years. Markets staged a recovery, supported by softer-than-expected US jobs data and a moderation in crude oil prices, providing some relief to investors assessing the near-term interest rate outlook, said Vinod Nair, Head of Investments at Geojit Investments. Accenture results lift most IT stocks Irish major Accentures earnings for the June-August quarter beat analysts estimates on Thursday. However, the bigger talking point was the higher-than-expected guidance provided by the company for FY27. As the markets remained shut on Friday on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti, this exuberance was seen on Monday. Accentures 4QFY26 revenue of 18.68 bn 7 y-o-y in constant currency or cc terms exceeded its top end of guidance band of 18.4 bn. It guided for 3-6 growth in cc with inorganic contribution at 2-2.5 terms for FY27E, which was higher than the Street expectations of 2-5, and expects no effect from currency movements in FY27E, noted Nomura. This guidance was despite the companys management acknowledging headwinds from the West Asia war, impact of AI-led deflation, and a dynamic discretionary spending environment among clients. The management also noted an increase in smaller deals and improving conversion of deal wins into revenue, which is good news for Indian IT players. Big names such as Accenture and Cognizant act as bellwethers for the countrys IT sector, providing a glimpse at how the sector may perform or grow in the near-term. Indian IT stocks, which earn much of their revenue from US and European clients, tend to benefit from positive commentary by these global technology giants. Improvement seen in Q2, but outlook bleak The picture remains bleak for IT companies despite this brief pullback. IT companies, which have delivered flat to low single-digit revenue growth in recent quarters, are expected to witness only a moderate improvement in the July-September quarter as the West Asia conflict continues to weigh on client spending and decision-making, according to Pritesh Thakkar of PL Capital. AI traction remains healthy, but smaller-sized and shorter-tenure AI projects are yet to offset leakage in traditional services, limiting the pace of revenue growth. We expect median Tier I revenue growth of 0.9 Q-o-Q in CC terms, with growth partly aided by acquisitions, while Tier II companies are expected to outperform with 2.7 Q-o-Q growth, supported by deal ramp-ups and stronger conversion of recent wins, Thakkar said in his report. AI-related deflation in revenues of IT services companies has been a major concern for the industry since early this year, as AI-driven productivity gains made by clients are expected to take away a chunk of revenue for the IT companies that deliver projects for them. The concern is so deep that Nifty IT remains down over 25 for the year.

articleTitle: ‘Is 140/90 a normal blood pressure reading at age 60?’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: blood pressure
description: Is 140/90 normal blood pressure at age 60? A cardiologist explains what the reading means, why one reading is not enough, how to measure BP accurately at home and when high blood pressure needs urgent attention.
body_raw: A blood pressure reading of 14090 mmHg at age 60 can leave you wondering whether it is something to watch or simply a number that comes with getting older. Does being 60 change what counts as normal blood pressure? One such question was posted on Quora Is 14090 a normal range of blood pressure at the age of 60? We reached out to Dr Aseem Dhall, Director  HOD, Cardiac Sciences, ISIC Multispeciality Hospital, to understand what this reading means and when it needs attention. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Is 14090 normal at 60? Not quite. A blood pressure reading of 14090 mmHg is not considered an ideal or normal reading for most adults, including people around 60, the cardiologist clarifies while adding that the reading falls in the high blood pressure range under commonly used guidelines. However, one reading alone does not confirm hypertension, he assures while explaining that blood pressure naturally fluctuates through the day, so repeated readings taken correctly give a better indication of a persons usual blood pressure. Does getting older make 14090 acceptable? Being 60 does not automatically make a reading of 14090 normal. Age can affect the blood pressure target a doctor recommends, but it is only one factor. Different guidelines may use slightly different thresholds and targets, says Dr Dhall. Doctors also consider overall health, medications and other medical conditions. For older adults, treatment may need to be individualised, particularly when there is a risk of dizziness or falls. The important point is to avoid assuming that high blood pressure is simply a normal part of ageing. What if 14090 keeps showing up? This is where repeated readings become important. If someone repeatedly records blood pressure around 14090 at home, it suggests that their blood pressure may be higher than recommended and should not be ignored. Home monitoring can help because readings can be taken in a familiar setting over several days. The person should maintain a record of their readings and share it with their doctor. Based on the pattern and the persons overall health, the doctor can determine whether hypertension is present and whether lifestyle changes, monitoring or medication are appropriate. If you already take blood pressure medication, dont change the dose yourself. Do not start, stop or change blood pressure medicines without medical advice. Before worrying about the number, check that youre measuring it correctly A home reading is useful only if you take it properly. Stress, anxiety, recent exercise, caffeine, smoking and even talking can temporarily push the number up. A single blood pressure reading can temporarily rise because of stress, anxiety, recent exercise, caffeine, smoking or even talking during the measurement. In fact, an incorrect sitting position or a poorly fitting cuff can also affect the result. For an accurate home reading, use a validated upper-arm monitor with the correct cuff size. Avoid exercise, caffeine and smoking for at least 30 minutes beforehand and empty your bladder. Before measuring, sit quietly for about five minutes, keep your feet flat on the floor and support your arm at heart level. Do not talk during the measurement. Take two readings about one minute apart and record both. Doing this at consistent times over several days can give your doctor a clearer picture of your usual blood pressure. What should the target be in your 60s? Once repeated readings confirm consistently high blood pressure, the next question is what level to aim for. No single target suits everyone. For many adults being treated for hypertension, doctors aim for blood pressure below 13080 mmHg when it can be achieved safely, but the target may be adjusted depending on the persons health and tolerance. People with diabetes, kidney disease or heart disease may require closer monitoring and an individualised target. The treating doctor should decide the goal after considering medications, other conditions, age and the persons risk of side effects. When does high BP require urgent attention? A reading of 14090 is different from a severely elevated reading. A blood pressure reading of 180120 mmHg or higher is considered severely elevated. If a repeat measurement remains at this level, seek medical advice promptly. If the high reading is accompanied by chest pain, severe breathlessness, severe headache, confusion, vision changes, difficulty speaking, weakness or numbness, seek emergency medical care immediately. The symptoms matter as much as the number. In such a situation, do not wait for the blood pressure to come down on its own. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: SBI credit card fee jumps from Rs 499 to Rs 2,999, woman wins Rs 50,000 compensation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Consumer Commission SBI Cards Woman Consumer News Credit Card Fee SBI
description: The commission was hearing a consumer complaint alleging deficiency in SBI credit card services and unfair trade practice over the issuance of the card with higher annual fees than the complainant said she had opted for.
body_raw: A Delhi Consumer Commission has held SBI Cards guilty of deficiency in service and ordered to pay Rs 50,000 to a woman who alleged that she had opted for a credit card with an annual fee of Rs 499 but was issued one carrying a Rs 2,999 fee in 2023. She repeatedly asked the company to change the card, but her request was not resolved. Nearly three years after she filed the complaint, the commission ordered the card to be closed. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, South-II, Delhi president Monika Aggarwal Srivastava and members Dr Rajender Dhar and Ritu Garodia, were hearing a complaint filed by one Neha Chaudhary against SBI Cards  Payment Services Limited. It is difficult to comprehend as to the reason why the card was not closed if it could not be downgraded, the commission observed on September 18, finding SBI Cards guilty of deficiency in service. According to Chaudharys complaint, she had opted for a Simply Click credit card carrying an annual fee of Rs 499 plus GST. She alleged that the companys agent instead obtained her biometric KYC for a Club Vistara card. A card was issued with a credit limit of Rs 73,000, but she found that it carried an annual fee of Rs 2,999 along with GST. Woman repeatedly asks for card change A bill dated August 3, 2023 showed annual fees of Rs 2,999 and GST of Rs 592.32. On August 4, she emailed SBI Cards stating that she had not used the card and requested that it be changed to a Simply Save card, with the applicable charges. SBI Cards replied on August 10, 2023 that its representatives had been unable to contact her on her registered mobile number. It said upgrading or downgrading a credit card required OTP validation and asked her to receive a representatives call or contact its helpline. Chaudhary then informed the company that she had contacted the helpline but the requested change had not been made. On August 11, she said she had called multiple times and was told that the card could not be changed and the fees could not be waived. She also informed the company that she had approached the RBI Ombudsman. On August 18, SBI Cards informed her that it was unable to process the downgrade request. She sent a legal notice through email the same day. The commission noted that Chaudhary had contacted the company through email and its helpline multiple times, but was eventually told that the downgrade could not be processed without any reason being assigned. Commission questions why card was not closed The commission recorded that SBI Cards neither appeared nor rebutted the complainants allegations. Its written statement was not taken on record because it was time-barred under an order dated October 24, 2024. The commission took note of an earlier February 2026 decision of the Karnataka State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, which referred to RBI directions dated April 21, 2022 on credit card closure. Those directions provide that a closure request should be honoured within seven working days, subject to payment of dues, and that issuers must provide multiple channels for such requests. Failure to complete closure within seven working days attracts a penalty of Rs 500 per calendar day where there is no outstanding amount. The commission said it was difficult to comprehend why the card was not closed if it could not be downgraded. The commission held SBI Cards guilty of deficiency in service and directed it to close the credit card. It also directed the company to generate the bill as on August 4, 2023, the date of Chaudharys request for the change, provided the bill had not already been paid. The commission ordered SBI Cards to pay Rs 50,000 compensation. Takeaway If a credit card comes with a fee or charges different from what you agreed to, raise the issue immediately in writing and keep copies of all emails, bills and complaint records. If the issuer cannot make the requested change, ask for closure of the card and seek appropriate consumer redress rather than continuing to accept charges you dispute. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Delhi1800-11-4000 or call the National Consumer Helpline at1915for assistance.
