articleTitle: Why Harish Rawat’s defiance of AICC deals a blow to Uttarakhand Congress on poll eve
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress veteran and ex-Uttarakhand chief minister Harish Rawat
description: AICC leadership issues a stern warning to Rawat for his bid to continue with his statewide yatra, making it clear that “individual campaigns will not be tolerated”.
body_raw: Congress veteran and ex-Uttarakhand chief minister Harish Rawats decision to continue with his Dhanyawad evam Jansamvad Yatra despite a directive from the party high command to call it off has deepened rifts within the state party unit, with the All India Congress Committee AICC leadership warning that his independent outreach could undermine efforts to present a united front ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. The Congress leadership issued a stern warning to Rawat Monday evening, making it clear to him that individual campaigns would not be tolerated. AICC general secretary in charge of organisation K C Venugopal, in an X post, said Met with Uttarakhand Ex-CM Harish Rawat ji, to discuss on the ongoing campaigns in the election-going state. It was made clear that our campaigns will be taken forward jointly along with all Uttarakhand leaders, solely under the Congress banner under Mallikarjun Kharge ji and LOP Rahul Gandhi jis leadership, with the singular aim of ensuring the partys victory. Venugopal also said Individual campaigns will not be tolerated by the party, and there must only be collective programmes as planned by the party organisation. The party is confident that with the energy and hard work of the entire state unit, we will emerge victorious in Uttarakhand Earlier in the day, Rawat pressed ahead with the Jaspur-Haldwani leg of the yatra, days after AICC general secretary and Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja wrote to him on October 1, asking him not to proceed with the programme. The confrontation has brought into sharper focus differences within the state Congress over Rawats political role and his efforts to remain at the centre of the partys activities in Uttarakhand. In her letter to Rawat, Selja said the party had learnt that he was undertaking the yatra without discussing it with either the state Congress president Ganesh Godiyal or the Uttarakhand in-charge. She also referred to what she called his controversial statements during his recent programmes. The state elections are to be held in the next few months and the party must put up a united front. You will appreciate that any such parallel programme at this juncture will not be in the interest of the party. You may therefore not go ahead with these programmes, the letter read. Rawat, however, made clear that he had no intention of backing down. Hours before beginning Mondays leg of the yatra, he posted on social media There is no stopping now, while calling on his supporters to work to bring the Congress back to power in Uttarakhand and said the resolve was firm for the pride of Uttarakhand. Uttarakhand is due for the Assembly elections in February 2027. On Monday, Rawats yatra began at 11.30 am at Heera Garden in Jaspur in Udham Singh Nagar district en route to Haldwani. Rawat has described the exercise as a public dialogue and thanksgiving campaign, rather than a parallel political programme. A senior Uttarakhand Congress office-bearer close to Rawat said the former CM was continuing with the yatra to strengthen the party ahead of the elections. The yatra is continuing because Rawat ji wants to bring the Congress back to power in the state. Whatever he is doing is in the interest of the Congress and Uttarakhand. Local Congress workers are participating in the yatra and he is getting an overwhelming response from the public, the leader said. The Congress leadership, however, remains concerned about the political message of Rawats independent programme. An AICC leader said the party was already running programmes in the state ahead of the polls and that a separate initiative by Rawat risked reinforcing the perception that it was divided. When there are other party programmes being run ahead of the polls, any such parallel programme by Rawat sends a message to the public that the Congress is a divided house in Uttarakhand. That is not in the interest of the party, the AICC leader said. The leader added that since Rawat had announced Mondays programmes much earlier, the party was keeping a watch on his upcoming programmes and that the matter would be conveyed to the high command. The latest disagreement comes at a difficult time for Rawat within the Congress. Last month, he appeared before the Enforcement Directorate ED in connection with its money-laundering investigation into alleged irregularities in the 2016 Gram Panchayat Vikas Adhikari recruitment examination conducted by the Uttarakhand Subordinate Service Selection Commission. The EDs probe followed searches at multiple locations, including the premises of Chandan Singh Jeena, Rawats former Officer on Special Duty OSD and his current personal assistant. The agency has said it seized or froze assets worth around Rs 1.28 crore, including Rs 32 lakh in cash, around 200 grams of gold and 12 luxury watches. Rawat returned to Uttarakhand last month after spending a prolonged period in Delhi for medical reasons and subsequently led a roadshow in Dehradun. During his yatra in Haridwar last week, a vehicle in his cavalcade carried his photograph alongside the slogan Tiger is back. He is the tallest leader of the Congress in the state. Through such programmes, he is keeping himself in the leading position among the contenders for the CM face, said another party leader.

articleTitle: Pune Crime Files | Attacks on gay dating app users rise; reported cases ‘tip of iceberg’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pune gay dating app crimes
description: A 19-year-old man and two others attacked a man having sex with another man he met through the Grindr app.
body_raw: Over the last couple of years, there have been several attacks in Pune on men looking for same-sex relationships through apps used by LGBTQIA people, the police and activists said. On September 29, three youngsters allegedly attacked a 22-year-old man having sex with another man he met through the Grindr app. The victim, who hails from Bhosari, and his gay date were attacked by the assailants at a dilapidated building near the Mental Asylum in the Yerwada area around 6 pm, according to the FIR. The other man allegedly ran away to escape from the assailants. The assailants also forcibly transferred Rs 20,000 using the victims PhonePe account, threatened to kill him, and tried to have sex with him, according to the FIR. When he resisted, the assailants dropped him at Vishrantwadi Chowk on a two-wheeler and left, it added. The man approached the police two days later after receiving counselling from YUTAK Trust, which works among LGBTQIA people. Assistant Police Inspector Chandrakant Lohkare said, We probed the bank account into which the accused had forcibly transferred the victims money. This led to the arrest of 19-year-old Devendra alias Karan on the same day. A court remanded him to police custody until October 7 for further investigation. Attempts are underway to arrest the remaining two accused. The police booked the three men on charges including voluntarily causing hurt, robbery, and criminal intimidation. Minor boy lures 25-year-old man In a previous incident, a minor boy lured a 25-year-old man from Warje Malwadi through a gay dating app and called him for a meeting near a shopping mall in Karve Nagar on the night of April 29. The minor then took the man for a long drive. They reached a secluded spot, where the minors aides allegedly attacked the man, stoned his face, snatched his cell phone, and transferred Rs 8,600 from his account. Within an hour after he complained, the police apprehended the minor accused on May 8. His three aides were arrested later. History-sheeter among 5 arrested Earlier this year, the police arrested a gang of five who allegedly robbed three users of a gay dating app between December 28, 2025, and January 11, 2026. According to an FIR registered in these cases, a 27-year-old man received a message on a gay dating app from an ID named ImTop, used by a person identifying himself as Rahil. They decided to meet in Kondhwa around 9 pm on January 11 for a hook-up. But when the man reached the spot, Rahil and his friends allegedly took the victim to an isolated spot and robbed him of his gold ornaments. The police arrested Rahil and four others, including a history-sheeter charged under the stringent Maharashtra Control of Organised Crimes Act MCOCA in the past. The police said the gang members had similarly robbed at least two more men. They targeted men looking for same-sex dating, believing that victims would not file police complaints. Extortion over nude videos In July 2025, when a 22-year-old man went to meet another man he met through a gay dating app, two others forced him to take his clothes off and recorded his videos in a car. Threatening to publicise the videos, they allegedly forced the victim into making online transfers of Rs 8,000. A 24-year-old man was allegedly blackmailed into paying Rs 1.09 lakh between August 2024 and January 2025 by people who befriended him on a gay dating app. The FIR in the case was lodged after YUTAK Trust members met top Pune police officials. Later, in April 2025, the police arrested a gang of four youngsters for allegedly robbing several men from Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad after luring them through a gay dating app. Many are not willing to approach police LGBTQIA rights activist Bindumadhav Khire said the cases registered represented the tip of the iceberg. Also, gay victims are not targeted only in urban centres, but also in rural parts, for easy money. We have received calls on our helpline from several rural victims. Many are not willing to approach the police due to social pressures, said Khire. Anil Ukarande of Yutak Trust said the police should be prompt in registering the crimes against the LGBTQIA community. These crimes will increase if they go unreported. Efforts like posting reels on such crimes on official social media handles of police establishments should be made to raise public awareness. It will encourage the victims to ignore social taboo and lodge police complaints, he said.

articleTitle: Woman’s Rs 20 lakh caught between two banks’ ‘ping-pong’, gets refund, payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Himachal Pradesh Consumer Commission, deficiency in service, wrongly transferred money to closed account, bank transfer to closed loan account reversal, Consumer Protection Act 2019 45 days reply rule, refund of wrong bank transfer, National Consumer Helpline 1915, bank ping pong blame game consumer case, principle of non-traverse consumer court, Hemanshu Mishra consumer commission order, private bank transfer error refund rules
description: A woman mistakenly transferred Rs 20 lakh to her husband’s already-closed loan account and was caught between the two banks' blame game for over two months.
body_raw: A Himachal Pradesh Consumer Commission has held two banks guilty of deficiency in service after a womans Rs 20 lakh remained blocked in an administrative loop for over two months after she mistakenly transferred it to her husbands already closed loan account, involving two banks blaming each other over who should reverse the transaction. Calling it a ping-pong blame game, the commission directed the banks to refund the amount and pay Rs 30,000 payout to the woman. President Hemanshu Mishra, members Arti Sood and Narayan Thakur observed that the institutional apathy of both banks subjected the woman and her family to avoidable financial distress, severe mental agony, and forced litigation. The ping-pong blame game trapped the consumer in an administrative loop. Holding funds in a closed loan account despite clear, immediate written notices from both the remitter and the account holder constitutes a gross operational default and a clear deficiency in service, the September 11 order said. The order added that instead of executing a prompt reversal, standard protocol when funds were credited to a defunct or closed account, the bank engaged in bureaucratic delay, issuing automated responses before ultimately advising the wife to approach the remitting bank. 20 lakh transferred to a closed account The wife initiated a transaction of Rs. 20 lakh from her savings account held with a private bank, intending to transfer funds to her husband, and due to a clerical error, the funds were mistakenly directed to her husbands closed personal loan account maintained with another private bank. The loan account was fully settled and closed before the transaction date. Realising the error, the wife immediately notified her husbands bank on April 2, requesting reversal. The bank advised her on April 5 to approach her home branch from which the transaction was initiated. She then routed her complaint through her home branch on April 14. Subsequently, her bank put the blame back on the husbands bank, stating that reversal depends on the beneficiary bank. Caught in a cycle of blame-shifting between both banks, her funds remained blocked, forcing her husband to take an alternative loan by pledging shares on April 24 to manage liquidity. Alleging deficiency in service on the part of both the banks, she filed the present complaint, seeking refund along with compensation and litigation costs. Upon notice, both the banks appeared before the commission, but failed to file their reply within 45 days from the date of service. Hence, their right to reply was struck off and not legally recorded. Complaint allowed The commission observed that the documents adduced by the woman remain entirely unrebutted, unchallenged, and unimpeached, leaving no cogent reason to disbelieve the reliable and convincing evidence presented on record. The commission directed the two banks to pay Rs. 12,500 to the woman along with interest and also directed the husbands bank to pay Rs. 7,500 to her along with interest. It further added that both the banks jointly and severally pay Rs. 10,000 to the woman for litigation expenses. Takeaway The ruling highlights that if the banks fail to file their written versions within 45 days of notice, as mandated under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the principle of non-traverse would apply, and the complainants avermentswould stand legally admitted. Aggrieved consumers may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Himachal Pradesh 1800-180-8087 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. That struggle led me here. Im open about everything because there was no patriarchy in my home. Thats why I can speak freely. I am a basrd. And I salute that man for that, she added. articleTitle: Surat Police arrests ‘influencer’ for objectionable content on Mahatma Gandhi
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bharatiya Gauraksha Manch president Dharmesh Gami of Surat filed the complaint at Umra police station after seeing the video stating that the content would hurt the sentiments of several people.
description: Bharatiya Gauraksha Manch president Dharmesh Gami of Surat filed the complaint at Umra police station after seeing the video, stating that the content would hurt the sentiments of several people.
body_raw: The Surat Cyber Crime Branch arrested a social media influencer for allegedly insulting Mahatma Gandhi in an Instagram reel she uploaded on the eve of Gandhi Jayanti on October 1. Simran Patel, 47, whose account describes her as a digital creator, has one million followers. She uploaded the video featuring a woman showing the picture of Gandhiji on the 500-rupee note in an obscene manner and placing it in a gender context with insulting and objectionable remarks. By the time the complaint was filed, she had deleted the viral video. Patel, who lives in the Adajan area of Surat, was arrested under sections of the Information Technology Act after police investigated the account following a complaint. Her husband has been identified as Amit Patel. Bharatiya Gauraksha Manch president Dharmesh Gami of Surat filed the complaint at Umra police station after seeing the video, stating that the content would hurt the sentiments of several people. Gami told the paper, Our sentiments and respect for the father of the nation, Mahatma Gandhi, were hurt by such an objectionable video. We wanted a criminal case lodged against her so that in the future, nobody dares to commit such an act. Surat police has warned against posting such objectionable content.

articleTitle: Pneumonic plague in Russia? What we know about Siberian lab tech’s death
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sterile laboratory bench showing biohazard containment protocols (AI generated image). Russian health authority Rospotrebnadzor initiated plague quarantine procedures in Shelekhov near Irkutsk following the fatal laboratory-acquired infection of technician Daria Shipilova.
description: Plague outbreak in Russia: A lab technician at an Irkutsk anti-plague institute in Siberia died, and 197 contacts have been isolated amid reports of a pneumonic plague exposure but Rospotrebnadzor has not confirmed either a plague or a laboratory accident.
body_raw: It always begins with a broken test tube and a pathogen released, in every good or bad movie about plagues and epidemics. And one version of recent events in Russia sounds uncomfortably familiar. At least 197 people who may have had contact with a lab technician in Russias Irkutsk region have been placed under medical isolation. This was after reports the technician - Daria Shipilova - broke a test tube containing pneumonic plague bacteria while working at the anti-plague institute in Shelekhov, a small town roughly 20km from Irkutsk city. Shipilova was admitted to hospital with severe pneumonia on September 29. She died on October 2. Rospotrebnadzor, Russias federal public health body, diagnosed a pneumonia of unknown etiology but said it found no microorganisms associated with her work. It also said the sanitary and epidemiological situation in the region remains stable. But Alexei Tsydenov - the leader of Buryatia, a neighbouring republic Shipilova reportedly visited on work - first said she died of the plague. Hethen altered his post to add possibly. So is there really a plague in Russia? Not confirmed. Rospotrebnadzor has not confirmed a plague or that a laboratory accident occurred. Russian media has said 197 contacts have been identified and 189 are under observation. On October 2 Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said none of them are showing symptoms and their laboratory tests are negative. However, since then two have tested positive for COVID-19 and two others for rhinovirus, a viral infection behind the common cold. Gennady Onishchenko, a former head of Rospotrebnadzor, told state news agency TASS the onset of cold weather would likely prevent transmission. But that is one officials view and not a guarantee. How did Daria Shipilova fall ill? That is unclear, and there are two competing accounts. The first is the broken test tube. According to The New York Post, after that incident she was at places on Russias eastern border - near Mongolia - and fell ill on September 25. But Rospotrebnadzor contradicts this story. Its biosafety commission found no emergency involving pathogenic microorganisms at the institute. The second is that she fell ill after the work trip to Buryatia. But Tsydenov says she never visited the republic and that there is no outbreak there. What is pneumonic plague? It is a disease caused by the Yersinia pestis bacterium, the same one behind bubonic plague that ravaged Europe from 1346 to 1353 and was one of the most fatal pandemics in human history as much as 60 per cent of the European population of the time were killed. According to the US Centers for Disease Control, the pneumonic form spreads through infectious droplets when an infected person or animal coughs or sneezes. It can also develop when bubonic or septicaemic plague spreads to the lungs. Health officials consider it the most serious form. Symptoms usually appear between one and four days after exposure and can include fever, headache, weakness and a bloody or watery cough. The pneumonia rapidly worsens without treatment and can be fatal. But common antibiotics work, and recovery rates are high when treatment starts within 24 hours of the first symptoms. That is why close contacts are monitored. So what now? Three things to watch a laboratory report confirming the cause of Shipilovas death, a clearer account of how she was exposed, and the health of those under observation.

articleTitle: Knowledge Nugget | CAFE-III norms: What are the new rules and how will they work?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Knowledge Nugget | CAFE-III norms: What are the new rules and how will they work?
description: The final Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE)-III norms are notified. What are new norms and how will they make passenger vehicles more fuel-efficient? Here’s what you need to know. Also, go "Beyond the Nugget" to know about the Bharat Stage norms.
body_raw: Take a look at the essential events, concepts, terms, quotes, or phenomena every day and brush up your knowledge. Heres your UPSC Current Affairs knowledge nugget for today on new Corporate Average Fuel Economy CAFE norms. Knowledge Nugget New Corporate Average Fuel Economy CAFE Norms Subject Environment and Economy Why in the news? Recently, the new Corporate Average Fuel Economy CAFE Norms for passenger vehicles were notified by the Ministry of Power. It will come into effect from 1 April 2027 and remain applicable up to 31 March 2032. The new norms will apply to new passenger vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in India. In this context, lets know what CAFE norms are and key highlights of CAFE-III norms. Key Takeaways 1. CAFE-III is a set of fleet-level fuel-efficiency standards for passenger vehicles. They were first introduced in 2017 under the Energy Conservation Act. 2. CAFE norms require manufacturers to keep the average fuel consumption - and therefore CO2 emissions - of all eligible passenger vehicles they sell within a prescribed limit, rather than requiring every individual model to meet the same number. Key Highlights of CAFE-III Norms 3. The CAFE norms will apply from April 1, 2027, to March 31, 2032. They cover M1 category passenger vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in India. 4. The CAFE-III framework will drive progressive improvements in fuel economy through year-on-year tightening of targets across all five years. 5. At the heart of the system is a fleet-wide calculation a manufacturers permitted fuel consumption is determined by the weighted average unladen weight of the vehicles it sells. 6. The government has set an annual formula for calculating each manufacturers target Annual average fuel consumption  a A- W a b  c Here, W is the weighted average unladen mass of the manufacturers eligible vehicles. The reference weight, or b, has been fixed at 1,229 kg. The figure a determines how much the fuel-consumption target changes for every kilogram that a manufacturers average fleet weight is above or below the reference weight, and c is the baseline fuel-consumption target, expressed in litres per 100 kilometres. 7. The new norms provide flexibility to manufacturers to adopt cleaner technologies, alternative fuels and other innovative solutions. It promotes technological innovation in new technologies such as high efficiency air-conditioning for improved fuel efficiency and Solar reflective paints. 8. Through the introduction of the Carbon Neutrality Factor CNF, the CAFE-III framework recognises the contribution of renewable and low-carbon fuels, including ethanol-blended petrol, biofuels and CBG. 9. The list of recognised fuel-conservation technologies has been significantly expanded from four to twelve technologies. 10. Battery Electric Vehicles BEVs, Range-Extended Electric Vehicles REEVs, Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles PHEVs, Strong Hybrid Electric Vehicles SHEVs, and Flex-Fuel Vehicles will receive super credits that are volume derogation factors in fleet-average calculations. 11. CAFE-III does not require manufacturers to balance their books completely every year. Manufacturers may opt to meet their obligations over specified two-yearthree-year compliance blocks.A This allows manufacturers greater flexibility in managing their technology transition and product portfolios over the compliance period. 12. Manufacturers that perform better than their prescribed targets will generate credits, which may be carried forward within the specified compliance blocks. 13. Manufacturers with a compliance gap may utilise eligible carry-forward provisions, enter into exchangetrade of credits with other manufacturers, or purchase credits through the buyout mechanism administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency. 14. Reporting will be done under both the Modified Indian Driving Cycle MIDC and the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure WLTP. What is WLTP ? The Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicles Test Procedure WLTP, which the European Union adopted in 2018, ensures that emissions of carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxides NOx, and particulate matter from vehicles on the road more closely reflect results recorded in laboratory conditions. BEYOND THE NUGGET Bharat Stage norms 1. Bharat Stage emission norms are Indias standards for regulating pollution from motor vehicles. They set legal limits on exhaust emissions of pollutants such as carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter. Each successive BS tightens these limits, pushing manufacturers to adopt cleaner engine technologies, better exhaust treatment systems and cleaner fuel. 2. India introduced emission norms first in 1991, and tightened them in 1996, when most vehicle manufacturers had to incorporate technology upgrades like catalytic converters to cut exhaust emissions. Fuel specifications based on environmental considerations were notified first in April 1996 - to be implemented by 2000, and incorporated in BIS 2000 standards. 3. Following the landmark Supreme Court order of April 1999, the Centre notified Bharat Stage-I BIS 2000 and Bharat Stage-II norms, broadly equivalent to Euro I and Euro II, respectively. BS-II was for the National Capital Region and other metros BS-I for the rest of India. 4. From April 2005, in line with the Auto Fuel Policy of 2003, BS-III and BS-II fuel quality norms came into existence for 13 major cities, and for the rest of the country, respectively. From April 2010, BS-IV and BS-III norms were put in place in 13 major cities and the rest of India, respectively. 5. The BS IV norms had been enforced across the country since April 2017. In 2016, the Centre had announced that the country would skip the BS-V norms altogether and adopt BS-VI norms by 2020. 6. Major emissions governed under these norms are carbon monoxide emissions, hydrocarbon emission limits. Nitrogen Oxides and particulate matter are also significant metrics. Furthermore, for every step up in standards, an improved standard of fuel is required. For BS-IV compliant vehicles, BS-IV standard fuel is required. CAFE-III is a set of fleet-level fuel-efficiency standards for passenger vehicles. 2. The CAFE norms will apply from October 1, 2026, to September 30, 2035. 3. The CAFE norms were first introduced in 2017 under the Energy Conservation Act. articleTitle: Create fear in miscreants: Supreme Court on crime against women
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court Delhi Police women's safety
description: Hearing a suo motu case on recent rape crimes in Delhi-NCR, the Supreme Court asked the Delhi Police to implement 24-hour monitoring cells and enhance security in vulnerable parks and public areas.
body_raw: Underlining the need to prevent crimes against women and not just arrest the accused after an offence is committed, to ensure that the National Capital Territory remains safe even during late hours, the Supreme Court Monday asked the Delhi Police to put in place a 24-hour monitoring cell for continued surveillance in vulnerable areas. Justice J B Pardiwala, presiding over a two-judge bench, said, . create fear in the minds of all these criminals. Something goes wrong, you are doomed. You need to prevent this at any cost. What is happening today is you catch hold of the culprit. Undoubtedly, you have that skill, you have that promptness, expertise you will apprehend him, he will be arrested, put behind bars. That is not the solution. What is important is to prevent the crime and not just obey the orders. He said that these goons, these miscreants, these anti-social elements will be at high during the upcoming festivals. On September 28, the bench, also comprising Justice K Vinod Chandran - taking suo motu cognisance of incidents of alleged rape of a minor in August on a sleeper bus that travelled nearly 47 km from Greater Noida to Old Delhis Kashmere Gate, the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old at Astha Kunj Park in South Delhi by three men posing as policemen on September 21, and an alleged gangrape and murder in Northwest Delhi earlier last month - had issued a series of directions for examining the broader institutional failures that may have led to the crimes. On Monday, the bench said there appears to be a feeling that women are not safe in the national capital, especially in vulnerable pockets. Lets try our best to ensure that these types of crimes are not committed repeatedly . there appears to be a feeling that women are not safe in the city, more particularly some vulnerable pockets of the city . So, we need to deliberate a little . the only concern is that the deficiencies, if any, should not lead to, should not facilitate the commission of a crime, said Justice Pardiwala. What is important is to prevent the crime, not what you do after the crime is committed. We have to work together. We must ensure that every young girl, every woman in the NCT of Delhi . should feel safe even at 10 oclock, 11 oclock in the night, whether she is travelling by Metro, whether she is walking on the streets, he added. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, who appeared for the Centre said, We are doing this for our daughters ., adding Mere system being there is not enough. We will have to show that its functioning and it is giving results. The court Monday also sought information on the working status of CCTV cameras installed at vulnerable locations. Referring to the incident at Astha Kunj Park, it sought the status of CCTV cameras and lights installed there and whether security personnel had been deployed. It has been said people warned you about these people criminals even in this unfortunate case, the court noted. Addressing the Delhi Police, Justice Pardiwala said, People should not run away from you. People should come forward to meet you, to talk to you and your response should be such that would repose confidence in a common man. Referring to the September 28 order, Justice Pardiwala said, We impress upon them Delhi Police to take steps as fast as possible so far as these measures which we have suggested. Our immediate concern is to prevent crimes relating to women. Dont let us down. Rise to the occasion, please. Every woman, every girl molested is our sister, our mother. So, it is a huge challenge for the police department of the NCT. Take it up as a challenge, the judge also told the police. Justice Pardiwala added, It is not just installation of CCTV cameras that is going to help you. There has to be a cell. A 24-hour cell, which keeps monitoring what is happening. The bench said it would pass a detailed order in the matter and that the authorities would be given 4 weeks to act on its directions. The top court posted the matter for hearing next on November 16.

articleTitle: ‘We were in love for 1.5 years’: Jason Sanjay on how his only relationship before Sigma ended

description: Director Jason Sanjay has revealed details about his only romantic relationship, a year-and-a-half-long college romance that ended in a mutual breakup while he was studying overseas.
body_raw: Jason Sanjay, director of Sigma and the son of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay, has spoken publicly for the first time about his personal life, revealing that he has had only one romantic relationship, a college romance that lasted about a year and a half before ending in a mutual breakup. The period following the breakup was when he fully committed himself to making Sigma. There was only one love. It was a long time ago, when we were in college. We were in love for about a year and a half, Jason Sanjay said in a conversation with VJ Siddhu. It was a mutual breakup. We both talked to each other and broke up. Jason Sanjay, who studied filmmaking, said the breakup happened while he was overseas. The distance, he said, made the experience both isolating and clarifying. Also Read Sigma movie review Jason Sanjays debut has the vision but not the script to match Asked how he coped, Jason Sanjay answered, During the breakup, I used to listen to all the love songs of Yuvan Shankar Raja. The director later revealed that he deliberately stayed away from social media during and after the breakup.I didnt have any plans to post stories on Instagram. If we post stories after the breakup and then reconnect, we cant get out of it. So we kept a distance between us. I always control myself to not do things that I dont want to do, Jason Sanjay said. Jason Sanjay said he is at peace with the relationship and its ending. Im okay now. It was good at the time. We move on with our lives, he said. And then came the line that connects his personal life to his professional one After that, I got down to Sigmas business. About Sigma Sigma, an action-adventure heist comedy, stars Sundeep Kishan in the lead alongside Faria Abdullah, Raju Sundaram, Sampath Raj, Shiv Panditt, Anbu Thasan and Yog Japee. articleTitle: 47-year-old surgeon shoots himself dead in UP’s Kanpur
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police said Singh and his wife had an argument before the incident and that marital differences appeared to be the main reason, though the investigation is underway.
description: Police said the victim's wife heard a loud sound and rushed to the puja room at their home to find the doctor with an injury to his chest
body_raw: A 47-year-old doctor allegedly shot himself dead with his licensed revolver inside the puja room of his three-bedroom flat at Bloosom Apartment in Kanpur, in the early hours of Monday. Police said Sandeep Singh was working as a general surgeon at a government hospital in Kanpur Dehat. No suicide note has been found so far. The incident occurred around 2.30 am, but police received the information only around 6 am from the hospital, following some confusion over jurisdiction. The matter came to light when the victims wife, Kanchan, heard a loud sound from the prayer room. She rushed in and found Sandeep lying on the floor in a pool of blood with injury on chest. She rushed him to hospital and, in the meantime, informed his family members, who live in another part of the district, in the Chakeri area. Doctors declared Sandeep dead on arrival. Police said, the motive behind the drastic step is yet to be ascertained. The post-mortem report is pending. Assistant Commissioner of Police, Kanpur, Virendra Vikram, said the victims family had indicated that the incident may have followed a family dispute. He added that the preliminary inquiry also hinted at this. At the time of incident, Kanchan and their two children - a four-year-old daughter and a two-month-old son - were present at home, said senior sub-inspector, Neeraj Dwivedi. Police said the deceaseds family told them that Sandeep had separated from his first wife, who is also a doctor. The couple had a love-cum-arranged marriage but mutually separated in 2019. Over a year later, Sandeep married Kanchan, who is from Kasganj, in an arranged marriage. Sandeep has a son from his first marriage who lives with his ex-wife.

articleTitle: India’s HPV vaccine Cervavac gets WHO’s safety nod
articleFeaturedImageAlt: hpv
description: Previously approved for its use in India by the drug controller, Cervavac is administered for the prevention of diseases caused by the four HPV types
body_raw: Cervavac, Indias first indigenously developed gender-neutral quadrivalent Human Papillomavirus vaccine qHPV developed by Serum Institute of India has got the prequalification status by the World Health Organization WHO. This regulatory milestone marks the 32nd WHO prequalification for productsbiologicals received by Serum Institute of India. Inclusion on the WHO List of Prequalified Vaccines allows Cervavac to be procured by United Nations UN agencies. The vaccine targets HPV types 6, 11, 16 and 18. It is indicated for girls and boys aged nine through 26 years. Adar Poonawalla, Chief Executive Officer, Serum Institute of India, said, WHO prequalification of CERVAVAC is an important step in strengthening the global response to HPV. This milestone reflects the effectiveness of the vaccine and creates the opportunity for countries to prevent HPV-related risks. We are pleased to see this indigenously developed vaccine reach this achievement, and look forward to contributing to immunisation coverage, advancing global healthcare Previously approved for its use in India by the Drugs Controller General of India DCGI, Cervavac is administered for the prevention of diseases caused by the four HPV types. This includes the prevention of anal cancer in boys and young men, and cervical, vulvar, vaginal, and anal cancers in girls and young women. It is also indicated in preventing genital warts, as applicable to the indicated population. Cervavac is indicated in girls and women between 9 through 26 years of age for the prevention of cervical, vulvar, vaginal and anal cancer caused by HPV types 16 and 18, and genital warts caused by HPV types 6 and 11. Cervavac is indicated in boys and men 9 through 26 years of age for the prevention of anal cancer caused by HPV types 16 and 18, and genital warts caused by HPV types 6 and 11. Those between 9 and 14 years of age receive Cervavac according to a two-dose schedule 0.5 mL at 0, 6 months, while individuals 15 to 26 years of age receive a three -dose 0.5 mL at 0, 2, 6 months schedule. The vaccine is administered intramuscularly. Cervavac is available in 1-dose vials of 0.5 ml and 2-dose vials of 1.0 ml presentations.

articleTitle: CJI Surya Kant: Any modified Form 6 not approved by Supreme Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court Election Commission of India SIR Form 6 Gyanesh Kumar
description: Referring to The Indian Express report, Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy argued that the Election Commission had made an 'unlawful alteration' to Form 6, targeting first-time voters.
body_raw: In response to an argument on the unlawful modifications made to Form 6, which new voters have to fill, Chief Justice of India CJI Surya Kant on Monday said that the Supreme Court hadnt approved any of the modifications to Form 6 and indicated that the court will examine who had modified it upon receiving a report from the Election Commission. The statement came when a three-judge bench headed by the CJI was hearing the petitions filed against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. For the first time, the Election Commissions online version of the electors registration form, known as Form 6, included a new section that seeks the status of the applicants parents vis-a-vis the last Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls, even though the statutory form itself has not been amended. The Election Commission, however, removed the SIR declaration added to Form 6 from its ECINET application portal in states where the SIR has concluded. The poll body had on September 26 announced that for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used. Referring to The Indian Express report, Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy argued, Let me give you an illustration.since it pertains to most recently, for instance, Delhi. Let us see how the SIR was conducted in Delhi. Form 6 has two new conditions added. Those Forms 6 were circulated. Neither the petitioner is now allowed to be on the roll. I got a notice also.based on this new Form 6, which cannot, under the schedule, be modified. Responding to Guruswamy, the CJI said, Lets be very clear. Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let us also be clear that when the report will be produced, we will like to see who has modified what. Form 6 coverage The Indian Express had reported on the Election Commissions September 26 press note on Form 6. The ECI had then said the form prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules will apply outside the SIR period. The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used, it read. Guruswamy was arguing a petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, which stated, Defying this binding majority, respondent number 3 Gyanesh Kumar, acting in concert with respondent number 6 DG-IT, altered Form 6 digitally on the ECINet portal in July 2026. On August 13, 2026, Commissioner Sandhu formally recorded that this alteration was unauthorised and illegal and was causing arbitrary harassment to young, eligible first-time electors, ordering its immediate withdrawal. Despite this, the unauthorised form was kept live on the portal. The plea argues there was a unilateral and illegal alteration of statutory Form 6 for first-time young voters without legislative authority or amendment of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 which could be termed unauthorised and illegal by a majority of the Commission. The petition further alleged that the act of the Chief Election Commissioner of deliberately manipulating the electoral roll bears no reasonable nexus or legal connection to his official duties. Such an act falls squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constitutes distinct, personal criminal liability, it added.

articleTitle: Does RAC guarantee a seat in Indian Railways? What Reservation Against Cancellation means for your train ticket
articleFeaturedImageAlt: An RAC ticket allows passengers to travel with reserved seating accommodation. (Image generated using AI)
description: Does an RAC ticket guarantee a seat on Indian Railways? Know what Reservation Against Cancellation means, whether you can board the train and when an RAC ticket can become confirmed.
body_raw: Indian Railways RAC rules seat guaranteeWhen booking a train ticket, passengers often come across the term RAC and wonder what it means for their journey. Does an RAC ticket allow them to board the train? Will they get a seat, or will they have to wait for a berth to become available?In Indian Railways, RAC stands for Reservation Against Cancellation. Here is how the RAC system works and what passengers can expect when travelling with an RAC ticket. What Reservation Against Cancellation means Speaking to Indianexpress.com, a senior railway official said that RAC is a reservation status used by Indian Railways when confirmed berths in a particular class have already been allotted but limited accommodation is still available for passengers. The official explained that a RAC passenger is permitted to board the train and is provided reserved seating accommodation. In classes with sleeping berths, two RAC passengers may initially be allotted seating on a berth designated for RAC passengers. This means that while the passengers journey is assured, a full sleeping berth is not necessarily assured at that stage, the official stated. Can RAC ticket become confirmed? According to the railway official, an RAC ticket can move to confirmed status if a berth becomes available.For example, if passengers holding confirmed reservations cancel their tickets before chart preparation, the available berths can be allotted to RAC passengers according to the applicable reservation system. So, a passenger whose status was RAC 25 at the time of booking may see it improve to RAC 10, RAC 2 or eventually CNF before the journey. Once the ticket becomes confirmed, the passenger is allotted a full berth, the official said. What happens if the ticket remains RAC after chart preparation? When asked about whether a passenger can travel with RAC ticket after chart preparation, the official replied that the passenger can still travel. If the ticket remains RAC after the final reservation chart is prepared, reserved seating accommodation remains available, but a full berth may have to be shared as per the RAC arrangement, the official added. The official further said that there is also a possibility of getting a full berth during the journey. If a confirmed passenger does not turn up, cancels at a stage permitted under the rules, or a berth otherwise becomes available, the vacant accommodation may be allotted to an RAC passenger by the travelling ticket checking staff as per applicable rules and priority. Why does Indian Railways have RAC system? As per the official, the RAC system helps Indian Railways make better use of available accommodation while giving more passengers certainty about their journey. Instead of keeping passengers entirely on the waiting list, RAC allows a limited number of passengers to travel with seating accommodation while keeping them in line for full berths that may become vacant due to cancellations, the official added.

articleTitle: Rakul Preet distances herself from Vashu Bhagnani I-T raids: ‘No Benami property’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rakul Preet Singh distances herself from IT raids. (Photo: Rakul Preet Singh/Instagram)
description: Rakul Preet Singh also urged publications and individuals who had carried what she described as “false, malicious and speculative reports” to retract them and clarify the facts.
body_raw: Nearly a week after the Income Tax Department conducted searches at several locations reportedly linked to Bollywood actor Rakul Preet Singh and her father-in-law, producer Vashu Bhagnani, the actress has issued a statement to set the record straight. Taking to her official Instagram handle, Rakul distanced herself from claims that she was involved in foreign remittances or held any benami properties. Have been paying taxes since the age of 20 The actress wrote, Its heartbreaking to see that theres a growing trend amongst the self styled online reporters  some main stream media journalists to sensationalise the news without verifying facts. Lets therefore set the record straight once for all. In her statement, the actress claimed that the searches were not related to her, contrary to several reports that linked her to the investigation. Let it be known that I am from the Armed Forces background  had no Godfather in the Industry. I have come up through sheer hardwork  as a responsible law abiding citizen have been paying my due taxes since the age of 20 years, she wrote. Not involved in any foreign remittances on behalf of any production house Rakul further clarified that she is not involved in any foreign remittances, either in her personal capacity or on behalf of any production house. However, she did not specifically mention Pooja Entertainment, the production company associated with her father-in-law. The actor also denied holding any benami properties on behalf of anyone in India or abroad. I would also add here that I do not hold any Benami property on behalf of anyone anywhere in the country or abroad. Neither ANYONE has EVER gifted me any property at anytime nor do I accept such expensive gifts as a principle, she added. ALSO READ  Ajay Devgns Drishyam 3 writer says wrote 100 versions of film Friends tried to bribe me for ending Rakul also urged publications and individuals who had carried what she described as false, malicious and speculative reports to retract them and clarify the facts. I understand that everyone running a media business however big has their own commercial pressures. But it cannot come at the cost of facts. And certainly not at the cost of someones reputation and livelihood, she said. What prompted Rakul Preet Singh to put out this statement? On September 28, the Mumbai Income Tax Department reportedly conducted searches at 12 locations over suspected financial irregularities. According to reports, investigators suspect that funds may have been routed abroad under the guise of financing film projects. Soon after reports of the Income Tax searches surfaced online, it was also reported that Vashu Bhagnani had been hospitalised in London. However, the reason for his hospitalisation has not been disclosed. According to NDTV, when the publication reached out to the Bhagnani family for a statement, they requested the media to leave them alone. While Rakul has distanced herself from the controversy, she has not mentioned her father-in-law or Pooja Entertainment by name in her statement. Her husband and actor-producer Jackky Bhagnani, meanwhile, has also remained silent amid the controversy. On the work front, the actress is gearing up for the release of Ramayana, in which she will play the role of Shurpanakha.

articleTitle: In Maharashtra, everybody is protesting – From ‘cockroaches’ to tribals to women
articleFeaturedImageAlt: abhijeet dipke, cjp, mumbai protests
description: The triggers are many – farm loan waiver, student hostel facilities, better roads, noise pollution, irregularities in government recruitment exams, functioning of the Election Commission, among others.
body_raw: Protests in Maharashtra have reached a crescendo. In the past few weeks, different parts of Maharashtra have witnessed a string of agitations-from Gen-Z to tribal students to women, though only a few made the headlines. On Friday, October 2, the Cockroach Janata Party CJP held a protest in Mumbai, demanding the ouster of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, followed by a similar protest by the Thackeray cousins. As this was happening, another one walked into Mumbai from Nashik over the weekend-the tribal students. The triggers are many-farm loan waiver, student hostel facilities, better roads, noise pollution, irregularities in government recruitment exams, functioning of the Election Commission, among others. The Indian Express has listed what has kept the state government and the Maharashtra Police on their toes over the past few months. Farmers Farmers protested in June and July 2026, demanding eligibility relaxations in the Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar farm loan waiver scheme. In September 2026, the All India Kisan Sabha launched protests, demanding regular crop loan payees be given a Rs 2 lakh incentive In June 2026, onion farmers staged Rasta Roko on the Pune-Nashik national highway, demanding MSP for their produce. For the past year, farmers from western Maharashtra and Marathwada have protested against the Shaktipeeth road project, refusing to part ways with their lands. Students For over 2 years, students preparing for Maharashtra Public Service Commission MPSC examinations have protested against exam fees, online exams, delayed results and irregularities. The protests intensified after Vivek Bhimanwar was appointed the MPSC chairman. Students in Pune protested over hostel rules. What worked as a catalyst was the deaths of tribal students in Gadchiroli due to snake bites. In September 2026, resident doctors and interns across Maharashtras government medical colleges protested against allowing homoeopathy practitioners to be registered with the Maharashtra Medical Council MMC. Students have been protesting at IIT Bombay since the death of Sahil Wakode on September 18. CJP protests in Mumbai and surrounding areas in support of the Jantar Mantar agitation. Women Women excluded from Majhi Ladki Bahin scheme are protesting, alleging bias. Pune, Nagpur, and Mumbai witnessed citizens protesting in solidarity with the survivors of sexual assault across India. Social activist Manoj Jarange-Patil held a 20-day hunger strike, demanding Maratha quota To counter Jarange, OBC organisations held protests, alleging the government was diluting OBC reservation. Maharashtra is witnessing protests from Dhangar and Banjara communities, demanding Scheduled Tribe ST status. Mischellaneous A road blockade was held in August 2026 across Pune, Nashik and Ahilyanagar districts to demand restoration of the original direct railway alignment between Pune and Nashik. Citizens and environmentalists from across the state are protesting against the felling of trees in Nashik to make arrangements for the upcoming Sinhastha Kumbh Mela. Days before the Ganesh festival, Pune residents took to the streets, demanding a blanket ban on the use of DJs during festivals and religious events. Thanes Balkum, Majiwada and Dhokali saw protests against a hyperscale data centre, expected to consume 422 MW of power, 125 kilolitres of treated water daily and have 193 diesel generators on standby.
