articleTitle: Raju Kher recalls bad phase when brother Anupam Kher refused help: ‘Took him for granted’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Raju Kher recalls bad phase when brother Anupam Kher refused help
description: Veteran actor Raju Kher, recently recalled a bad phase of his career when he lost everything and expected his brother Anupam Kher to help. However, Anupam was going through challenges in his own life.
body_raw: In the year 2000, both brothers, veteran actors Anupam Kher and Raju Kher were going through a tough career phase. In a new interview, Raju recalled asking Anupam for financial help but later realised how his elder brother was dealing with his own issues, and learnt not to expect anything from him anymore. During a podcast with Siddharth Kannan, Raju Kher revealed shifting to a rented flat after investing his money in a programme on an upcoming new channel. There was a time when I was going through a bad phase. I had sold my house because a new channel was coming, so I had bought a flat elsewhere. A new channel was going to launch and many people were making pilots, agreements were already signed. I also made a programme Life Ke Liye Kuch Bhi Karega, he shared. The veteran actor-director continued, Suddenly, I got to know that the channel has disappeared. I had invested the money that I got from selling the flat in that programme. I thought that I had a first-class life, a 4-BHK house, everything set for the family. And then, the channel disappeared and no one knew what happened.. there was just a lock on their door. During the career setback, Raju Kher reached out to his elder brother, Anupam Kher, for help. He said, I also felt the pressure to pay the rent. I had no one else, I could only talk to my brother, and I thought he will help me. But at that time, he had also stopped working. The reason was that he didnt want to do any of those weird films, he wanted substantial roles. So, I felt that my brother did not help me out. He could have done so, that was my thought at that time. ALSO READ  It ended in one day Raju Kher recalls brother Anupam Khers first marriage to Madhumalti However, his perspective towards his brother changed completely after reading a single headline in an article. Then, I was reading a magazine on the toilet. In the interview, Anupam Kher had said, I wish I had my own child. Although, he considers Sikander his own child. But then I never thought about my brother in that light. We took him for granted, thinking he doesnt have any problems because he was doing well financially. We never thought that what was going on in his life. He added, That was the thing that changed the whole concept of my life. Have expectations but dont do it like that. Try to find out what is going in the other persons life as well. I am talking about the year 2000, the year that changed my whole life, my thinking. On that day, I stopped expecting anything from anyone, no matter who it is. When asked about rebuilding his life and career, Raju recalled signing a TV serial after a long phase of no work. When your time is bad, your expenses tend to increase. Some suggested wearing certain rings, doing rituals, prayers, I got those done too. Work had also stopped coming. After a few months, I told my wife that we should trust in God, lets see what happens, and I removed all the rings. The next day, I got a call for work. I got an offer for a TV serial. I instantly agreed and told them to pay whatever they want. Life started again, he concluded. When Anupam revealed taking care of Rajus expenses Earlier this year, during an interaction with Zindagi with Richa Youtube channel, Anupam Kher had revealed that he has been taking care of his brothers finances for years. If every brother remembers what they were like when they were young, there would be no fight. I look at my life like its a film. How can I forget that we grew up together? I must also compliment Kirron Kher, wife, because she never, ever asked me, Why do you do so much for your brother? Thats how problems begin. I would sign cheques for Raju, the household, and other things. I told my manager long ago, Remember one thing in life, never ask me how much money Im giving to my brother.

articleTitle: ‘Mere paternity dispute not enough’: Kerala High Court refuses to order child’s DNA test
articleFeaturedImageAlt: paternity DNA test father child domestic violence case kerala high court
description: The court held that DNA test cannot be sought simply because the child's paternity is disputed. Before directing such a test, there must be initial material establishing non-access between spouses during the period under consideration.
body_raw: The Kerala High Court has refused to order the DNA test of a minor child to determine paternity, holding that such testing cannot be sought routinely without preliminary proof that the spouses had no access to each other during the relevant period. Justice Jobin Sebastian was dealing with a plea in connection with a domestic violence proceeding in which the husband sought a direction for the couples minor child to undergo a DNA test to ascertain paternity. In the absence of specific pleadings and prima facie material demonstrating non-access between the spouses during the relevant period, a direction for DNA profiling cannot be sought as a matter of course merely on the basis of an allegation disputing paternity, the court said on September 26. The ruling held that a DNA test is not to be directed routinely and may be ordered only in appropriate and deserving cases where the court finds such examination necessary for the proper adjudication of the dispute. Unless non-access between the spouses during the relevant period is prima facie established, evidence cannot be permitted for the purpose of disproving the paternity of a child born during the subsistence of the marriage, it observed. Husband disputes childs paternity The case arose from proceedings under the provisions of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, initiated by a woman and her minor child before the trial court. They sought maintenance and return of the womans gold ornaments. During the pendency of those proceedings, the husbandrespondent disputed that he was the minor childs biological father. He filed an application seeking a direction for the child to undergo a DNA test, claiming that it would establish that he was not the childs biological father. He also contended that the woman had agreed to undergo the DNA test during mediation. The trial court, however, dismissed the application. Aggrieved, the husband approached the high court challenging the order. Marriage raises presumption of childs legitimacy The court observed that proceedings under the Domestic Violence Act are meant to adjudicate allegations of domestic violence and provide legal reliefs, and not to determine the biological parentage of a child. It noted that the marital relationship between the parties was undisputed. Since there was no material showing that the husband had no access to the wife during the relevant period, the presumption under the Indian Evidence Act operates in favour of the childs legitimacy. The court explained that Section 112 of the Indian Evidence Act embodies a rule of public policy intended to protect the legitimacy of children born during a valid marriage. The ruling said that such legitimacy is conclusive unless it is shown that the spouses had no access to each other when the child could have been conceived. It further observed, A consensual understanding reached during mediation cannot, by itself, compel a court to order a DNA examination unless the court independently finds that such an examination is legally permissible, necessary, and justified in the facts and circumstances of the case. Parties cannot, by consent, require a court to pass an order contrary to law or public policy. Since there was no material establishing non-access, the presumption of legitimacy remained operative. The high court, hence, found that the magistrate was justified in refusing to direct the DNA examination and dismissed the petition.

articleTitle: Dead drops in Punjab to godowns in MP, how drug kingpin’s syndicate operated
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh, alias Navab Virk, sits inside an aircraft following his deportation from Turkiye to India. (Handout via PTI Photo)
description: A Delhi court has remanded the ‘drug kingpin’, who was deported from Turkey, to 10 days’ police custody.
body_raw: Narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh, accused of running an international heroin syndicate, allegedly told investigators that drugs were delivered through dead drops - buried at multiple locations in Punjab and stored in godowns in Madhya Pradesh - according to the prosecution. A Delhi court on Saturday remanded the 34-year-old to 10 days custody of the Delhi Police Special Cell, which told the court it needed to recover the drugs, trace the syndicates supply chain, and identify other people involved in the alleged trafficking network. Navpreet, 34, was deported from Turkiye and arrested at Delhi airport on Saturday. Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced his deportation in a post on X, saying Singh had obtained Turkish citizenship using the false identity of Navab Virk. The 2021 heroin case Navpreet was produced before Special Judge, Narcotic Drugs And Psychotropic Substances NDPS, Anuradha Shukla, at Rouse Avenue court on October 3 in a case dating back to July 2021. The Special Cell had then arrested a man in South Delhi and followed the trail to Faridabad, where a total of 358.08 kg of heroin was seized. During submissions, Special Public Prosecutor SPP Akhand Pratap Singh told the court, There is ample evidence against this accused Navpreet in form of his connection with co-accused Gurpreet and Gurjyot Singh, from whom huge quantity of heroin in total 358.08 kilogram was recovered. He also submitted that the co-accused had made disclosure statements against Navpreet. A cheque book recovered from the premises of co-accused Ramandeep belonged to the accused, the court order recorded. The court noted that Navpreet was declared a proclaimed offender on February 16, 2022. According to the prosecution, he had avoided investigation and court proceedings for more than four years. The court order also recorded the prosecutions submission that Navpreet had inflicted injuries on his hand and stomach when he was being handed over to the Special Cell. He was taken to Medanta Hospital at the Delhi Airport for medical treatment. Police seek to trace supply chain, identify associates According to the Special Cells remand papers, it sought Navpreets custody to question him about the alleged syndicates operations, his movements and the preparation of his passport in Delhi, as well as to confront him with statements made by other accused. It also sought to identify and apprehend other alleged suppliers, financiers, carriers and facilitators. The disclosure of the accused is on record wherein he has stated that he used to deliver drugs through dead drop, SPP Singh told the court. In a dead drop, a consignment is left at an agreed location for someone else to collect later. SPP Singh said Navpreet had told investigators that drugs had been buried at several places in Punjab and that he could identify the locations and help recover them. . the accused, in his disclosure, also stated that his associates, Labba and Manna, had taken godowns in MP where drugs were kept and there is a house in Punjab also which can be identified, the order reads. Judge Shukla said, The investigation necessitates police custody of the accused to recover the buried drugs which were dead dropped and other drugs which accused has stated that he has kept hidden to unearth the supply chain, source and transportation route for identification of other persons involved in procurement, transportation, storage and distribution and to establish complete financial trail connected with the illegal drug trade. The accused has to be taken to Punjab and MP for investigation purposes. For the needful to be done, 10 days police custody is being sought, which seems reasonable, the NDPS Judge said in the order. Navpreet is also an accused in a 2022 terror case lodged by the Special Cell. The case pertains to using funds allegedly obtained from selling narcotics to finance terror activities. A trail in Punjab Navpreet is from Wazir Bhulla village in the Beas area of Amritsar. He was first arrested in Punjab in a drug smuggling case in 2013 and was acquitted in 2017. Navpreets name re-surfaced in October 2024, when the Punjab Police counter-intelligence wing seized 105 kg of heroin at Baba Bakala. The two men arrested at that time were allegedly his associates. The India-based operations of the alleged drug syndicate were run by his cousin, Prabhdeep Singh alias Harry. Prabhdeep was extradited from Azerbaijan on May 13 by the Central Bureau of Investigation in coordination with the Special Cell.

articleTitle: Why more Indian students are choosing Ireland over UK, Europe for education
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ireland Trinity college Dublin
description: Latest data shows Indian students now form the largest international cohort in Irish universities, driven by lower total costs, a thriving tech sector, and favourable post-study work norms.
body_raw: Written by Sameer Anasingaraju Ireland is increasingly emerging as a preferred destination for Indian students pursuing higher education abroad, with its English-speaking environment, shorter postgraduate courses and post-study work opportunities drawing students away from traditional destinations like the United Kingdom UK and other European countries. According to the Ireland Higher Education Authority HEA, 44,535 non-Irish-domiciled enrolments were recorded in higher education in 2024-25, a 10.2 per cent increase from the previous year. Indian students formed the largest international cohort, accounting for 20.6 per cent of these enrolments, around 9,175 students. While the numbers may be modest compared with the number of students who go abroad every year for studies, the uptick is unmistakable. From just over 2,000 students in 2017-18, the numbers rose steadily before the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted international student mobility. The recovery after the pandemic, however, was followed by a much sharper rise. Enrolments crossed 4,000 in 2021-22, then jumped to 7,070 in 2023-24. By 2024-25, the figure had climbed to 9,175, meaning Ireland was receiving more than four times as many Indian students as it did seven years earlier. The particularly steep increase in the last two years suggests that Irelands appeal is no longer limited to a small group of students, but is becoming a mainstream alternative for Indians considering education in the UK, US and other European countries. The English factor For many, Irelands use of English as the primary language of instruction is one of its biggest advantages over countries like Germany and the Netherlands, alongside shorter masters programmes, particularly when comparing overall costs. Tanishka Prabhu, 22, from Pune, studied at Griffith College Dublin from 2023-2025 and now works in Ireland. I came here for my bachelors. Mostly Indians come for masters here. When I came in January 2023, there were very few Indian students. But now they are here in huge numbers, Prabhu said. I chose Ireland because my elder sister also did her masters here, and while researching, we found out that expenses are lower than in Europe. It is an English-speaking country, and the weather is extremely nice too. Saanvi Gambhir, pursuing a masters in finance at University College Cork, had initially considered Germany. I chose Ireland as the post-study norms are much better than the UK. I was planning for Germany, but there is also the language barrier there. Here, theres no such issue. Aman Nanda, also pursuing finance at University College Cork, compared Ireland with the UK. I was initially planning for the UK, but I chose Ireland because the quality of life, education, and economy are much better than there, he said. My experience has been really amazing. Everyone is extremely nice and helpful here, with absolutely zero racism towards Indians. The course quality is excellent, and so are the teachers teaching it. Sadaf Sheikh, 28, is pursuing an LLM at Trinity College Dublin and initially considered the Netherlands. I wanted to go to the Netherlands, but it is much more costly than Ireland. Here the masters is only for one year, and we can work for two years after it is over. Sustainable career at affordable cost For Akheel Sisal, going abroad was a childhood dream, but the real question was where education could lead to a sustainable career without overwhelming costs. After his MBA in Pune and experience as a data analyst, he explored European colleges, but consultancies flagged his undergraduate record as a hurdle - until Ireland emerged unexpectedly. I started checking with friends studying in Ireland, and they told me the IT market was growing, there were job opportunities, and the process was relatively easy, Sisal recalls. Compared to the uncertainty of the United States - high tuition, heavy loans, visa concerns - Ireland seemed more manageable. The US was never an option because of the uncertainty, he says. Some of my friends had hefty loans and were still struggling to pay them back. Despite being warned his profile might not secure admission, Sisal received three acceptance letters and chose National College of Irelands one-year Masters in Data Analytics, with a E4,000 scholarship on a E15,000 fee. I asked if I would have to study from huge notebooks and prepare for written examinations. They told me the programme was much more practical and lab-focused. I knew then that this was where I wanted to go. Before graduating, he secured a full-time role and now works as a data and AI manager. Consultants see a pattern Education consultants in Pune also report rising interest. Digvijay Sawant of Imperial Overseas Educational Consultants said Ireland particularly attracts students in technology, pharma, and management. There is a rise in recent years of people going to Ireland. Ireland is known for three things IT, pharma, and management, noting the country is often called the Silicon Valley of Europe. In other European countries or the US, the masters programme is for two years. In Ireland, it is only for one year. After that, you can stay back for two years. Also, there is no language barrier. Costs are also down because youre only paying for 1 year of education instead of two, Sawant said. The seats for Ireland are getting filled very fast. Last year, we sent around 20-25 students to Ireland. We are currently on track to beat that number this year, he said. With inputs from Kalyani Lad. Sameer Anasingaraju is an intern with The Indian Express.

articleTitle: 3 women, 3 hotel rooms, 3 murders, and 1 police warning about couples
articleFeaturedImageAlt: On Friday, police broke open the door of a room in a small hotel in Miyapur and made a grisly discovery: the decomposing body of a 27-year-old medical student.
description: Police ask hotels to be on alert about couples checking in, but only one partner leaving
body_raw: The murder of three young women in separate incidents in hotel rooms over the past 10 days in Hyderabad has put the police on edge and the spotlight on small hotels renting out rooms for cheap. Police are now asking hotels and lodges to be alert, especially if a couple hires a room and one of them leaves and does not return. A particular focus is on customers using fake IDs to book rooms. Police on Monday warned hotels that if they do not verify whether Aadhaar or other IDs are authentic, they will face legal action. The Telangana Hotels Association has also urged hotels to exercise caution and thoroughly verify documents. Murder 1 On Friday, police broke open the door of a room in a small hotel in Miyapur and made a grisly discovery the decomposing body of a 27-year-old medical student. According to the police, the woman became acquainted with a man named Ravi Kumar on social media, and they entered into a relationship. Ravi borrowed heavily from her, including a gold chain, citing family emergencies but promising to return everything soon. When she pressed him, he asked her to come to Hyderabad, where he would return the jewellery. They checked into the hotel on September 30, and at some point Ravi left alone. Police said that when the womans father called her, her phone was switched off. When she did not return to the hostel on Saturday, her friends also alerted her father, who then lodged a police complaint. Cops traced her last mobile phone location to the hotel, where they discovered her decomposing body. Police say she was smothered with a pillow and Ravi is absconding. Murder 2 On September 29, a 34-year-old bank customer care executive was found dead inside a hotel room in SR Nagar. The woman had checked into the hotel with her partner, A Srinivas, who used a fake identity card. Both of them hail from Vikarabad but work and live in Hyderabad, police said. When Srinivas was leaving the hotel alone with his bag on Tuesday at 330 am, a staff member did ask him if the woman was also leaving, but he claimed that she would check out in the morning after having breakfast, the police said. It was not until late afternoon that the staff called police, after she did not answer the door for several hours. Deputy Commissioner of Police DCP A Ramana Reddy said that the woman was hit on the head with a blunt instrument, probably a curtain rod, causing her death. They may have had a quarrel late in the night, and he allegedly attacked her while she was eating. There were multiple injuries on her body. A plate of unfinished meal was found beside her on the bed, an official said. Police found that the accused does odd jobs in the Telugu film industry and is currently on the run. Teams have been sent to search in his native village. Murder 3 On September 22, a 29-year-old woman was taken to a hospital at Kothaguda by her male friend, with whom she was staying at a nearby hotel. Police said that the woman, who hailed from Jharkhand, and her friend, S Ravi Teja, who hails from Anakapalli in Andhra Pradesh, were working in the hospitality sector and had checked in a day earlier. On the morning of September 22, Ravi told hotel staff that the woman was unconscious, and they rushed her to a hospital, where she was declared dead on arrival. Ravi allegedly fled the spot, police said. Officials of Madhapur Police Station said there were injuries on the back of her head and face. Police traced the man to Visakhapatnam, where he attempted suicide and was admitted to King George Hospital. He was arrested on his release and brought to Hyderabad. According to the police, he confessed that he hit her with a blunt object as she was pressuring him to marry her. He was in an inebriated condition when he allegedly assaulted her, police said, and later fell asleep and woke up to find her dead.

articleTitle: Gym trainer found dead in Bengaluru flat ‘after party’; 4 friends detained
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru gym trainer found dead
description: The 25-year-old man’s mother said she initially got information that her son was in critical condition in a hospital.
body_raw: A gym trainer was allegedly found dead in a North Bengaluru flat on Sunday, and the police have detained four men in connection with the incident. The police identified the man as Nandan, 25, a resident of Hebbal who worked at the Masiv Gym, located at Sahakaranagar. Nandans family members were informed around 3 pm on Sunday. His mother Manjula said, We reached the hospital after I received a call stating Nandan was in serious condition. But by the time we reached there, we came to know that he had already died. There were injury marks on his dead body. Nandan was Manjulas only son. The police have detained gym trainers Vishwanath, Sharath, and Nishanth and Anush Shetty, owner of the Smocky Docky restaurant. Mithun Kumar G K, Deputy Commissioner of Police Northeast, said on Monday, On Saturday evening, all four celebrated the first anniversary of the Masiv Gym and visited the Prestige Misty Water apartment located in Kempapura. Anush Shetty stays there. We came to know about the death around 7.30 am on Sunday. The body was shifted to Manipal Hospital for a postmortem. Later, Nandans family members filed a complaint with the Amruthahalli police. His mother said the family suspects that the four detained men killed him. We are waiting for the postmortem report. It appears that some personal rivalry could have led to the incident. But the prima facie information suggests that all four were thick friends and knew each other for nearly one year, Mithun added. A police officer said that Nandan might have been hacked to death that night. They may have consumed alcohol, and it appears that there was a fight among them, leading to his death, the officer added.

articleTitle: How a drug drop in Rohini led Delhi Police to heroin worth Rs 50 crores in Lucknow
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lucknow raid
description: Delhi Police crack an inter-state drug network and seize 6.25 kg of heroin from a drug manufacturing unit in Lucknow
body_raw: Heroin worth around Rs 50 crore was seized on Sunday from a drug manufacturing unit in Lucknow, which the supply chain led Delhi Police to after it intercepted a drug delivery in Delhis Rohini on September 16. On the night of September 16, a team of police from Rohinis Special Staff division had stopped a white SUV in Sector 32 of the Begumpur area. In the car was 58-year-old Laxman Hooda who was carrying 300 grams of heroin to deliver to a client, said police. Officers said that they had received a tip-off about this delivery and were waiting there for Hooda. 300 grams of Heroin and 3 lakh cash were recovered from his Grand Vitara car, which was also seized, said DCP Shashank Jaiswal. According to police, Hooda told them about his supplier, a resident of Delhis Raghubir Nagar named Anil, alias Bhola, who was on the run. Police traced him to Haryanas Sonipat and arrested him there, seizing yet another 500 gram package of heroin from him. Then, police said, Anil told them that he was getting his supply from a man he identified as Bablu from Lucknow. It took police another 15 days to zero in on the identity and location of this supplier. When they found him, they also found over 6 kg of heroin. On the basis of technical surveillance and human intelligence, on 04.10.2026, a raid was conducted at a heroin manufacturing facility in Sita Colony, Jankipuram, Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, and Bablu, was apprehended. During the raid, 6.275 Kg of freshly manufactured heroin was recovered, said DCP Jaiswal. This quantity of heroin, police said, is valued at about Rs. 50 crores in the international market. Inside the Sita Colony house, a whole cache of drug mixing supplies was found 2.504 kg Sodium, 787 grams Acetic Anhydride, one tub, gas cylinder, mixer grinder, utensils, polythene, an electronic weighing machine, and a wooden basket. Police said that Bablu told them during interrogation that all the supplies had come from Bareilly, from a man he identified as Ruksar Ali. Ruksar Ali  Raju, the main source supplierowner of the manufacturing facility, was traced and apprehended from Bareilly, UP after a prolonged and intensive pursuit of 120 km, said DCP Jaiswal. This was the second big heroin bust in Rohini this year. In April, the cops apprehended a family-run heroin operation in Rohini, which led them, again, to Bareilly and other parts of UP, leading to the recovery of a batch worth Rs. 16 crores. The source of this was traced to Manipur, where two men were allegedly procuring opium poppy-from which heroin is extracted-from a woman in the Indo-Myanmar border.

articleTitle: Supreme Court refuses to intervene in pleas challenging Great Nicobar Project
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Great Nicobar Project, Great Nicobar Project case, Supreme Court Great Nicobar Project, Calcutta High Court Great Nicobar Project PIL, Forest Rights Act violations, Great Nicobar PIL, Great Nicobar tribal rights, Great Nicobar environmental case, Meena Gupta Great Nicobar Project PIL, Great Nicobar infrastructure project, Supreme Court news, Calcutta High Court, Indian express news
description: The Centre had challenged the Calcutta High Court order rejecting its objection to petitions filed by retired IAS officer Meena Gupta against the Great Nicobar project.
body_raw: The Supreme Court Monday refused to intervene in a Calcutta High Court order, that allowed PILs challenging alleged Forest Rights Act violations in the Great Nicobar Project to proceed, saying the matter was already pending before the high court. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also pointed out that the main case is pending for final arguments and is listed for hearing on November 25 and 26. The Centre argued that the project was of great national importance and the maintainability of such Public Interest Litigations goes to the root of the matter. If I am able to place something more regarding maintainability, please allow us to place that submission. Do not close the door on maintainability because something very important turns on that, Attorney General of India R Venkataramani, appearing for the Centre, submitted before the court. Justice Bagchi observed that the high court had already ruled on maintainability and that the question now was on how far public interest survives, which would be considered there. Do they become integrated completely with the mainstream, or do we keep them with their unique identity and the identity of their culture? Preservation of culture is a constitutionally protected fundamental right, Justice Bagchi said, referring to the projects impact on indigenous communities. Let the high court take necessary steps to complete pleadings in the other matters and make an endeavour to hear the cases on the date fixed, the bench noted. What Calcutta High Court said The Centre had approached the top court challenging the Calcutta High Courts May 6 judgement, which rejected its objection to PILs filed by retired IAS officer Meena Gupta. Guptas petitions challenge decisions linked to the Great Nicobar Project, including alleged violations of the Forest Rights Act in obtaining consent from tribal communities and notifications reducing eco-sensitive buffer zones around Galathea and Campbell Bay National Parks. The Centre had argued that Gupta, a resident of Hyderabad, lacked legal standing and that a project involving a proposed port, airport, power plant, and defence infrastructure could not be challenged through a PIL. Rejecting the objection, the Calcutta High Court held, There is no thumb rule regarding the aspect of locus standi. It would not be expedient to lay down any general rule which would govern all cases under all circumstances. The high court also said that merely because a project involves substantial public expenditure, it is not insulated from judicial review, observing that a project involving huge expenditure must proceed in accordance with governing laws holding the field. What is the Great Nicobar Project The Great Nicobar Project is a proposed large-scale development programme that involves building a major transhipment port, airport, power plant, and other infrastructure, along with associated roads and development, at an estimated cost of around Rs 72,000 crore. The project has faced criticism over its potential impact on tribal communities and their rights alleged violations of the Forest Rights Act and environmental clearance norms changes to protections around ecologically sensitive areas such as Galathea Bay and Campbell Bay and the large-scale diversion of forest land and its impact on wildlife and biodiversity. The Centres position is that the project is of major strategic and national importance, including because of Great Nicobars location near major international shipping routes.

articleTitle: Fahadh Faasil says ‘won’t get half of Rs 300 cr’ as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Fahadh Faasil has responded to the worldwide box office collection of Bethlehem Kudumba Unit.
description: Fahadh Faasil, who has co-produced Nivin Pauly-starrer blockbuster romantic comedy Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, has clarified that he would get only a small fraction of the film's Rs 300 crore plus worldwide gross box office collection.
body_raw: Filmmaker Girish ADs romantic comedy Bethlehem Kudumba Unit has amassed over Rs 300 crore at the worldwide box office, emerging as the highest grossing Malayalam film ever globally. The Nivin Pauly and Mamitha Baiju-starrer has begun receding from cinemas after 40 days, and following its OTT premiere on JioHotstar this past Friday on October 2. Fahadh Faasils clarification on Bethlehem Kudumba Unit global gross Malayalam superstar Fahadh Faasil, who serves as one of the producers on Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, reacted to the unprecedented Rs 332 crore gross earned by the film, claiming that he or any of the other co-producers would end up receiving only a fraction of that figure. None of us will get even half of this Rs 300 crore that they are talking about. That is the gross collection, he argued in a chat with Cue Studio. Even though Bethlehem Kadamba Unit has earned a worldwide gross of Rs 326 crore, there are a lot of variables at pay. Out of this amount, around half of the chunk usually goes to the international agents, exhibitors, and distributors. Only after deducting the Goods  Services Tax GST does the producers get the remainder of the amount. In the case of Bethlehem Kadamba Unit, its produced by Bhavana Studios, which is owned by the three producers of the film - Fahadh Faasil, actor-filmmaker Dileesh Pothan, and screenwriter Syam Pushkaran. Its distributed by Bhavana Release, Future RunUp Films, and Mythri Movie Makers, best known for backing Allu Arjuns blockbuster Telugu action thriller franchise Pushpa. The fact that Bethlehem has been a success is something that makes me very happy and proud. It is not just me. There is Girish, Shyam, and Dileesh. I see this as a collective success of all of us. I dont see it as my success alone, added Fahadh. Its co-written by Girish AD and Kiran Josey, and also features an ensemble cast including Suresh Krishna, Vinay Forrt, and Shyam Mohan among others. Bethlehem Kudumba Unit box office collection Bethlehem Kudumba Unit released in cinemas on August 21. It scored an opening day of 4.90 crore from 1507 screens at the domestic box office. It earned over Rs 20 crore during its opening weekend, and over Rs 50 crore in its opening week. It slipped down marginally to Rs 49.85 crore in its second week, and Rs 33.30 crore in the third week, as per Sacnilk. By the end of the second week, Bethlehem Kudumba Unit had crossed the Rs 100 crore mark at the domestic box office. Its fourth week earnings dropped by almost half to Rs 16.79 crore, and by another half to Rs 8.80 crore in week 5. By the end of its sixth week, the film has earned over Rs 190 crore gross and over Rs 160 crore net in India. Majority of these figures stem from the native Malayalam version, followed by the dubbed Tamil and Telugu versions in equal capacity. But Bethlehem Kudumba Unit has garnered most of its worldwide box office gross earnings from overseas, where it amassed around Rs 140 crore, only around Rs 25 crore short of its domestic net earnings. The Kalyani Priyadarshan-starrer, produced by Dulquer Salmaans Wayfarer Films, earned around Rs 304 crore globally.

articleTitle: Michael Bracewell 6th to opt out of central contract with New Zealand this season

description: Michael Bracewell is the sixth player to have opted for a "casual contract" with New Zealand for the 2026/27 season.
body_raw: All-rounder Michael Bracewell has become the latest New Zealand player to opt for a casual contract with the national team for the 202627 season to play in the Big Bash League in Australia, New Zealand Cricket said in a statement on Monday. The 35-year-old will be replaced on the central contract list by Northern Districts batter and former Wellington Firebirds captain Nick Kelly, who earns his first national contract eleven years after making his First Class debut, said NZC. The development comes after a month after Mark Chapman made a similar move. Other star names to have opted out of a central contract for the 202627 season are Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson, Adam Milne and Tim Seifert. NZC further said that Bracewell remains available for selection for New Zealands upcoming five-match T20I series at home against India. The big-ticket series, part of Indias full tour of New Zealand that will also include a three-match ODI series and two Test matches, starts on October 22. The backing from New Zealand Cricket for me to take this opportunity at this stage of my career means a lot, Bracewell is quoted as saying in NZCs statement. As a white-ball only player, this felt like too good of an opportunity to pass up. Im still very much committed to the BLACKCAPS and cant wait to be involved in the upcoming India tour and future white-ball series. Ive also got my eyes firmly fixed on the opportunity to be involved in the inaugural NZ20 which is set to be introduced from next summer. New Zealand head coach Rob Walter said that he was happy that Kelly has got a central contract. The 33-year-old has played eight ODIs and seven T20Is for New Zealand. Nick stuck his hand up with his performances against Bangladesh and the West Indies in what was at times challenging batting conditions, said Walter. He has more than 300 professional matches under his belt and is one of the best fielders in the country, so he adds a lot to our contracted group.

articleTitle: Can’t save ‘eroded’ marriage just by legally preserving it: Orissa High Court backs divorce
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Orissa High Court Marriage Divorce Cruelty
description: The Orissa High Court held that compelling a wife to resume a marriage marked by sustained mental anguish and eroded trust would be unrealistic.
body_raw: The Orissa High Court recently refused to reverse a divorce granted by a family court, observing that the sanctity of a marriage cant be saved by preserving only the legal form of the relationship when its foundation has been substantially eroded. Chief Justice Harish Tandon and Justice Chittaranjan Dash were hearing an appeal filed by a husband against a family court order by which a divorce was granted to his wife on the ground of cruelty. Marriage undoubtedly carries a sanctity which the court must ordinarily endeavour to preserve. But the sanctity of marriage is not served by preserving only the legal form of the relationship when the substantive foundation of that relationship has been substantially eroded. Mutual respect, trust, companionship and a willingness to make reasonable adjustments are not peripheral attributes of matrimonial life they constitute its very foundation, the October 1 order read. The high court added, Where those attributes have been progressively lost and the relationship has become a source of sustained mental pain and anguish, the court cannot shut its eyes to the reality of the relationship merely because its deterioration cannot be fitted into one isolated or neatly defined category of conduct. According to the husband, the couple got married on October 20, 2021, following which they initially resided at Visakhapatnam before shifting to Hyderabad, where they worked in the Information Technology sector. The husband alleged that the couple later developed differences and the wife left the matrimonial home in June 2023 and went to Rayagada along with her parents, after which she filed a case for divorce on the basis of cruelty before the family court. On January 27, 2024, the family court dissolved the marriage. The husband then moved the high court with the current appeal. Wrongly dissolved marriage Advocate S K Dwivedy, appearing for the husband, argued that the family court had wrongly dissolved the marriage on the basis of cruelty, as the allegations of the wife were neither proved by evidence and nor were they enough to be called cruelty under the Hindu Marriage Act. He further stated that the husband had also instituted a case for resuming the marriage, which reflected his intention to continue the relationship. Advocate T K Mishra, representing the wife, submitted that she had specifically named acts of physical and mental cruelty meted out to her during the marriage, along with evidence. He added that the husbands conduct had caused mental agony to the wife and rendered continuation of the matrimonial relationship impossible. Continuing discord The high court stated that ordinary wear and tear of married life, trivial irritations, occasional quarrels or differences arising in the course of matrimonial life cannot, by themselves, furnish a ground for dissolution of marriage. The conduct complained of must be of such a nature and degree as to cause a reasonable apprehension that it would not be possible for the parties to continue living together. According to the bench, Mental cruelty, by its very nature, may not always be capable of direct proof, and the effect of the conduct upon the mind of the spouse has to be assessed having regard to the circumstances, the status and background of the parties and the nature of the relationship. The high court observed that the evidence given by the wife could not be reduced to a case of a stray quarrel or an isolated matrimonial disagreement. As per the court, the allegations of physical assault and the specific incidents stated by the wife when seen as a whole, present a continuing course of discord. The court noted that the final separation of the couple was not an event occurring in isolation but the culmination of an already deteriorated matrimonial relationship and that according to the evidence there was not merely a difference in perception between two spouses, but a relationship in which the essential element of mutual confidence had substantially eroded. It further noticed that even when the parties were brought face to face before this court on March 20, the relationship could not be restored rather, both expressed their desire to bring the marital tie to an end. While granting divorce to the couple, the high court said that it did not grant a decree of divorce just because they were separated or wanted to end the marriage, but the foundation of the decree remains the cruelty established from the evidence. Accordingly, it refused to interfere with the family courts order and held that the matrimonial relationship has lost its essential character and that compelling the Respondent-Wife to resume such a relationship would be unrealistic.

That is my motivation and like, you know, to leave everything out there. And of course, the goal is absolutely to win the World Cup and whatever it takes, Im absolutely ready, Kohli told broadcaster JioStar on Saturday. articleTitle: Brazil election heads to runoff as Flavio Bolsonaro leads against Lula, second round of voting on Oct 25
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Brazil’s presidential election will go to a runoff on October 25 between Senator Flavio Bolsonaro (left) and incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva (right) after neither won a majority in the first round. (AP Photo)
description: Brazil’s presidential election is headed for a runoff on October 25 after Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva failed to secure a majority in the first round.
body_raw: Millions of Brazilians voted in the first round of voting for the Presidential elections on Sunday, with right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro facing the incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. A second round of voting will be held later this month after Bolsonaros stronger-than-expected performance. Bolsonaro narrowly led the winning margin by 47 while Lula da Silva had 45 of the vote share. Bolsonaro lacked the outright majority needed to win the election. The runoff election will be held on October 25. Brazil wants change and I am very happy with the results, Bolsonaro told reporters in Brasilia after almost all votes were counted. He declared the result marked the end of the era of Lulas Workers Party. The election was focused on the cost of living, corruption and insecurity. Brazils currency and stock market have also risen. Flavio Bolsonaro is the son of right-wing former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence after being convicted over a plot to overturn the 2022 election result. Lula da Silva, while speaking to supporters at a hotel in Sao Paulo, said he had expected to win in the first round. He said he would restart his campaign the next day and promised to highlight his record in office. Pre-election private surveys had projected Lula to lead by around three percentage points. Bolsonaro told Reuters before voting that he was counting on a protest vote from people opposed to Lula, even if they had initially planned to support other candidates. A voter and lawyer by profession, Thaise Lima, 41, said her priority was ending the Workers Partys rule, while a voter Fernando Tempel, 49, said he switched to Bolsonaro after initially backing former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema, belonging to the New Party. As per a report by Reuters, economic concerns dominated the election, with Lula struggling to win over voters facing high living costs, household debt and rising gang activity despite falling inequality and unemployment. Flavio Bolsonaro sought to capitalise on cost-of-living pressures, while Lula moved to ban online gambling, expand welfare measures and propose debt relief for families. Rising spending and public debt above 82 of GDP have also raised fiscal concerns, with the government cutting its growth forecasts to 2 this year and 2.3 next year. The Banco Master case, involving an alleged multibillion-dollar fraud, drew in political figures including Bolsonaro, who is being investigated over suspected money laundering and has denied wrongdoing. Campaign debate was overshadowed by scandals and allegations of foreign interference in the elections. On the other hand, Lulas allies also warned that the Trump administration could refuse to recognise the election result if he wins. US President Donald Trump has not endorsed a candidate but hosted right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly. Brazilian intelligence officials also briefed French and German officials on alleged US and Russian interference in the elections. The United States has rejected these allegations.

articleTitle: A Dean’s dilemma in India’s AI Economy
articleFeaturedImageAlt: dean, ai
description: The problem is not that India has too many educated young people. It is that the relationship between qualification, competence and employment is becoming increasingly uncertain
body_raw: By Shama Rana A certain university dean recently told me, with some disappointment, that his daughter had decided to join an AI startup immediately after completing her undergraduate degree instead of pursuing a Masters to attain skills. His reaction was understandable. For generations of Indian academics and middle class families, education has followed a reassuring hierarchy. A Bachelors degree was good, a Masters was better, and a doctorate represented the highest form of intellectual accomplishment. More years spent studying generally meant better prospects and greater professional security. As someone currently navigating a doctoral programme myself, I found myself looking at the daughters decision differently. Perhaps she was not walking away from education at all. Perhaps she had simply recognised something our universities have been slower to acknowledge - in parts of the emerging economy, another degree is no longer automatically the most valuable next step. India has spent decades trying, rightly, to expand access to higher education. The Gross Enrolment Ratio for the 18 to 23 age group reached 29.5 in 2022-23, compared with 23.7 in 2014-15. That is an achievement. But expanding access raises another question what exactly are students gaining access to? The problem is not that India has too many educated young people. It is that the relationship between qualification, competence and employment is becoming increasingly uncertain. The Economic Survey 2024-25 offers a revealing picture. Among workers with graduate degrees, 38.23 per cent were in occupations requiring specialised skills, while 50.3 per cent were in semi-skilled occupations. Possessing a degree and finding work that actually uses the level of skill associated with it are not necessarily the same thing. Artificial intelligence makes this mismatch more urgent. Generative AI can already perform some routine cognitive work around which white-collar employment has traditionally been organised, from summarising documents and producing standard reports to elementary coding and procedural analysis. The Economic Survey 2025-26 acknowledges this shift and argues that education will increasingly need to cultivate reasoning, problem solving, communication and adaptability. Yet much of our educational culture continues to follow an older sequence accumulate knowledge, reproduce it in an examination, acquire the qualification and enter the labour market. AI unsettles that sequence because access to information is no longer scarce. The ability to reproduce information becomes less valuable when compared with the ability to interrogate it, connect it to a problem, recognise when it is wrong and use it intelligently. This does not make the university obsolete. The qualities universities can cultivate at their best, including critical thinking, disciplinary depth, intellectual curiosity and ethical reasoning, become more important when machines can generate plausible answers within seconds. Turning universities into coding academies would be a poor response to AI. But pretending disciplinary knowledge alone will be sufficient would be an equally serious mistake. An economics student should understand economic theory while knowing how contemporary tools can interrogate a dataset. A journalism student should understand reporting and ethics, but also how algorithms shape information and synthetic media complicates verification. A literature student need not become a programmer, but should understand how generative systems are changing authorship, publishing and intellectual property. These need not remain extracurricular skills acquired through separate online courses. India already has some architecture for this flexibility. The Academic Bank of Credits facilitates credit accumulation and transfer, while UGC provisions allow credits earned through platforms such as SWAYAM and NPTEL to be considered for accumulation and transfer. The principle is already established learning need not remain confined within a single classroom or rigid disciplinary pathway. Universities can now make that flexibility meaningful by allowing students to combine core disciplines with rigorously assessed modules responsive to technological and professional change. A mass communication student, for instance, could study media theory alongside data visualisation, computational research or AI-assisted verification. The aim is not to replace degrees with certificates, but to ensure that degrees remain connected to the world into which students graduate. The harder reform concerns institutional culture. Academic safeguards are necessary because curricula cannot be rewritten whenever a new technology becomes fashionable. But academic rigour cannot become an excuse for inertia. Departments need room to introduce electives, short modules and practitioner collaborations while preserving the intellectual foundations of their disciplines. There is also a cultural question. Indian families have long imagined educational progression as a ladder on which stopping can feel like falling behind. Bachelors, Masters, doctorate each additional qualification appears to promise greater security. Advanced study will remain indispensable for many professions, but it need not be the automatic next step for every graduate. The Economic Survey 2025-26 itself argues for a more fluid relationship between education and employment, including earn-and-learn pathways, recognition of short-form credentials and movement between education and work. This may prove particularly important when skills can change faster than conventional educational cycles. The Deans daughter may therefore represent something larger than one familys disagreement over a Masters degree. She belongs to a generation for whom education may cease to mean the uninterrupted accumulation of qualifications. A young person might graduate, work, return for specialised study, acquire another skill and later return to education again. India should not respond by diminishing the university or declaring the degree irrelevant. It should do something harder make the degree valuable enough that students seek higher education for what a university can uniquely give them, rather than because another qualification has become the price of entering the employment queue. In the AI economy, the question will no longer be simply how many degrees a young Indian possesses. It will be what, after acquiring them, she can actually understand, question and do. Rana is a Gurgaon-based writer and research scholar at MDU, Rohtak

articleTitle: JEE Advanced 2026: SC qualification rate tops 50% for the first time; women reach 6-year high
articleFeaturedImageAlt: JEE Advanced 2026 exam
description: In 2018, the IITs created 800 supernumerary seats for women. That year, women made up about 15.34% of admitted candidates, above the 14% target. In last year's JEE Advanced, 3,633 female-only seats were allotted and 31 women got in through the gender-neutral pool, taking women's share to 20.15% of 18,188 seats.
body_raw: The latest JEE Advanced results show a noticeable shift in who is making it through the exam. The number of SC candidates qualifying rose from 12,499 last year to 15,856 in 2026, while the number of ST qualifiers increased from 5,008 to 6,379 - a rise of about 27 per cent in both categories. Women, too, recorded a 23.4 per cent qualification rate, the highest in the six years covered by the Joint Implementation Committee JIC report released by IIT Roorkee. The overall pool, meanwhile, grew only marginally, from 54,378 qualifiers to 56,880. The sharper change, therefore, was not in the size of the qualifying pool, but in who made it into it. Read  IITs, IIMs see more women joining than before as placements, salary rises A total of 1,87,389 candidates registered this year in JEE Advanced, against 1,87,223 in last year. Of them, 1,79,694 appeared for both papers, compared with 1,80,422 last year. Qualifiers rose about 4.6 per cent, lifting the share of those who appeared and qualified from 30.1 per cent to 31.7 per cent. Qualification rate by category Category 2025 2026 Change  SC 40.41 50.16 9.8 ST 33.99 42.14 8.1 General 43.0 39.8 3.2 OBC-NCL 18.2 17.5 0.7 Women-23.4 Six-year high Source JIC reports 2025, 2026 Half of SC candidates made the cut The SC qualification rate rose 9.8 percentage points to 50.16 per cent, from 40.41 per cent in the previous session. For ST candidates, it climbed 8.1 points to 42.14 per cent from 33.99 per cent. Put simply, about one in every two registered SC candidates qualified this year, compared with roughly two in five last year. Among ST candidates, more than two in five qualified, up from one in three. The headcount tells the same story. SC qualifiers grew by 3,357 and ST qualifiers by 1,371. That is nearly six times faster than the overall rise. Together, they make up 22,235 of the 56,880 qualifiers, nearly 39 per cent of the total. A year ago, that share was about 32 per cent. AlsoRead What global teacher shortage, and Indias numbers tells us Not every group moved up. The general category rate fell 3.2 points to 39.8 per cent, and OBC-NCL candidates slipped 0.7 points to 17.5 per cent. This means both SC and ST rates now sit above the general category figure, which is a notable change. Women enrolment reaches new high In 2026, 43,112 women registered for JEE Advanced. Of them, 40,562 appeared in both papers and 10,107 qualified. That works out to 23.4 per cent of registered women, the best rate in six years, and about 24.9 per cent of those who appeared. Women now make up nearly 18 per cent of all qualifiers. At the very top, the leading woman candidate scored 280 marks, with 101 in Mathematics, 86 in Physics and 93 in Chemistry, to secure All India Rank 77. articleTitle: Tom Cruise calls Digger an ‘honour’ as it bombs with $20 mn opening, set to lose $150 mn
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Digger worldwide box office collection: Tom Cruise's film opens at $20 million.
description: Alejandro Inarritu's satire Digger has opened at $8 million at the North America box office, which is Tom Cruise's lowest opening weekend in nearly 20 years.
body_raw: Alejandro Inarritus satire Digger, which stars Tom Cruise in the unrecognizable titular role of a greedy oil tycoon, has bombed at the worldwide box office after an underwhelming opening weekend. Irrespective of the trade estimates, Cruise has hailed the film as an honour and a truly unforgettable experience. Digger has earned 20 million at the worldwide box office, 8 million in North America, and Rs 1.55 crore in India. Digger worldwide box office collection Diggers opening weekend of 8 million at the North America box office is far lower than the trade predictions between 12 million and 15 million. After adding 12 million it collected overseas, the total worldwide earnings of the film stand at 20 million after three days. This makes Digger Cruises lowest opening weekend in nearly two decades. As per The Hollywood Reporter, it was 19 years ago that a Tom Cruise film opened lower than 8 million in North America. Robert Redfords 2007 war drama Lions for Lambs, which starred Cruise, Redford, and Meryl Streep, opened at 6.7 million. However, its budget was merely 35 million, almost one-fourth of that of Digger - 125 million. Another 100 million were spent on promotions. As per Guardian, the film is set to lose almost 150 million. For the past 30 years, Cruise has consistently struck gold at the worldwide box office, mostly owing to his popular spy franchise Mission Impossible. Its final instalment which released last year, Christopher McQuarries Mission Impossible - The Final Reckoning, opened at 24.8 million in North America, and 64 million more than three times of Digger in North America. Made on a budget of almost 400 million, it eventually amassed almost 600 million at the worldwide box office. DIGGER is officially in theaters and I am so honored to have had the opportunity to create this film alongside such talented artists. Thank you to the entire cast and crew for your dedication, hard work, and joy. The experience was truly unforgettable and Im so proud of what we created. 13 - Tom Cruise TomCruise October 3, 2026 Despite Cruises superstardom, Digger couldnt even emerge as the box office favourite in North America this weekend. It lost that spot to Michael Showalters erotic psychological thriller Verity. The Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson-starrer received even more negative reviews than Inarritus satire, but ended up earning 32.8 million during its opening weekend, likely to recover its modest budget of 40 million this week. The trajectory of Digger was no different at the India box office. On its first Sunday day 3, the Cruise-starrer earned only Rs 45 lakh, as much as it did on its first Saturday day 2 from 400 plus screens. It hasnt even crossed the daily mark of Rs 1 crore yet, opening at Rs 78 lakh this past Friday on October 2, despite it being a holiday on the occasion of Gandhi Jayanti. The box office performance of Digger has also been impacted by the homegrown juggernaut that is Abhishek Pathaks crime thriller Drishyam 3. The Ajay Devgn-starrer amassed Rs 176.50 crore from 17,000 plus screens at the domestic box office during its opening weekend, whereas Digger could only pull off Rs 1.80 crore gross and Rs 1.55 crore net in the same period. Tom Cruise hails Digger as an honour Despite Diggers underwhelming opening at the North America box office on Friday, and trade estimates of the opening weekend landing around 8 million, Cruise took to social media on Saturday morning to celebrate his new release. He shared pictures from the set - of him in the unrecognizable avatar as Digger Rockwell, alongside John Goodman, who plays the US President, Riz Ahmed scientist Ganesh, Sandra Huller Emma Rockwell, Michael Showalter US Vice President, Jesse Plemons Kenny, and director Inarritu among others. DIGGER is officially in theaters and I am so honored to have had the opportunity to create this film alongside such talented artists. Thank you to the entire cast and crew for your dedication, hard work, and joy. The experience was truly unforgettable and Im so proud of what we created, wrote the actor as the caption on his X handle. Impressive on so many levels. Great twists..Outstanding performance, Tom. Your work in Digger has to be seen, thought about and discussed to be fully appreciated. Its one of those rare ones. Full of surprises and great choices. Bravo, he wrote.

articleTitle: Tribal student protesters arrested from Maharashtra Congress headquarters? What cops say
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress earlier alleged that Mumbai Police arrested tribal student protesters from its headquarters. (Express Photo by Soham Shah)
description: The protesters had called for a march to Lok Bhavan, and only those who attempted to proceed towards the Lok Bhavan were detained, police said
body_raw: The Mumbai Police has denied allegations that they entered the Congress headquarters at Tilak Bhavan and arrested tribal student protesters staying there. In a statement, the police said they detained Lok Bhavan march protesters from different locations and that legal action was being taken against them. Lok Bhavan is the official residence of the Governor of Maharashtra at Malabar Hill, Mumbai. The protesters had called for a march to Lok Bhavan, and only those who attempted to proceed towards the Lok Bhavan were detained, police said, without giving details on those arrested. Congress leaders, including Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal and senior leader Balasaheb Thorat, had earlier alleged that police entered the partys Tilak Bhavan headquarters during the night and detained tribal students, including women, who had arrived in Mumbai from Nashik after a foot march. Sapkal had alleged that police entered the office premises and threatened the students, while demanding their immediate release. He had also claimed that NSUI office-bearers were among those detained. Shame on the so-called double engine government in Maharashtra which is clearly Adivasi-virodhi, senior Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said. Balasaheb Thorat also criticised the alleged police action and asked, Is it a crime for tribal people to protest for their legitimate rights? Congress spokesperson Atul Londhe said, Women cannot be arrested at night. Who gave them this right? The party has meanwhile warned that party workers will gherao Varsha, the chief ministers residence, if the students arent released. Tribal students protest The students have been protesting over a range of demands concerning facilities in tribal schools and hostels, and an independent inquiry into deaths at tribal ashram schools. They have also submitted a 26-point demand charter to the Maharashtra government, also seeking the resignation of Tribal Development Minister Ashok Uike. After their month-long agitation in Nashik, the students began marching towards Mumbai last week. A delegation had also sought a meeting with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.

articleTitle: Amid low detection, specialised stations to probe all cybercrimes in Karnataka
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka cybercrime detection rate
description: Although cybercrimes make up 32 per cent of total crimes in Karnataka, the detection rate is 18%.
body_raw: The Karnataka Police have decided that the 43 specialised cybercrime police stations, rather than jurisdictional police stations, will investigate all cybercrime cases in the state. This follows a high court order and a dispute within police ranks over the poor detection rate for cybercrimes in Karnataka, which ranks 30th in the country-a fact reportedly highlighted in a recent review by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, according to sources. Although cybercrimes make up 32 per cent of total crimes in Karnataka, the detection rate is 18 per cent, according to 2023 National Crime Records Bureau data, which places the state among the worst-performing ones for cybercrime detection. Jurisdictionallocal Police Stations shall continue to register complaints relating to Cyber Crime IT Act cases. However, after registration of FIR, the cases shall be immediately transferred to the concerned Cyber Crime Police Station in the District  The concerned Cyber Crime Police Station shall immediately take up the case for investigation, says an order issued by the state police chief, Dr M A Saleem, on September 11. Cybercrime cases need timely preservation and analysis of digital evidence, technical examination of devices and electronic records, coordination with bankspayment intermediaries, telecom service providers, social media platforms and other agencies, besides prompt action for freezingholding suspected fraudulent transactions, it states. The supervision of cybercrime cases will vest with the superintendents of police in the districts and commissioners of police in cities, the order states. Cybercrimes have surpassed other crimes such as dacoity, robbery, and thefts in the state, where 52,000 cybercrime cases were reported in 2024, the highest in the country. Cyber Command Centre and court order The government created a Cyber Command Centre CCC last year under the leadership of a DGP-rank officer, Pranab Mohanty, to handle burgeoning cybercrime cases. The governments September 2, 2025 order said that cases under the Information Technology Act, the Aadhaar Act, and cases of fraud and cheating exceeding Rs 50 lakh must be mandatorily registered in cyber crime police stations. The Karnataka High Court later called for all cybercrime cases in the state to be handled by 43 cyber police stations. It also noted that jurisdictional police stations are overburdened with traditional policing work. The court then called for integrating the jurisdictional police stations with the CCC so that all cybercrimes would be brought under a single umbrella. If all of what is aforesaid is not complied with, in todays world, where crimes are faceless, investigations would become baseless, the court added. The number of cybercrimes reported in 2021 was 8,396 but grew to over 50,000 in 2025, the court pointed out. The graph has climbed steeply, a chilling reminder of the exponential growth of cybercrime. Thus, the CCC is not an option, but an imperative born of necessity, it stated. CCC responsible for cybercrime detection The new order also comes in the wake of a dispute over responsibility for the low cybercrime detection rate. The new order makes the CCC responsible for cybercrime detection. However, it is likely to cause hardship to victims of cybercrimes on account of the low count of cyber police stations in the state, a police source said.

articleTitle: Need to instil fear in minds of goons committing crimes against women: Supreme Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SUPREME COURT, DELHI RAPES
description: Supreme Court said that there is a feeling that women are not safe in Delhi, especially in certain vulnerable pockets.
body_raw: The Supreme Court Monday said there was a need to instil fear in the minds of miscreants committing crimes against women, while stating that there is a feeling that women are not safe in Delhi, especially in certain vulnerable pockets. While hearing a suo motu case over the recent incidents of rape in Delhi-NCR, the apex court said What is important is to prevent a crime, not what you do after a crime is committed, the bench said, adding that the police need to create fear in the minds of goons and anti-social elements who are prone to committing such crimes. The bench, comprising Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran, said it must be ensured that every woman should feel safe, anywhere in the city at any time of the day. We have to work together. We must ensure that every woman in Delhi-NCR should feel safe even at 11 pm whether travelling on the roads or the metro, they observed, adding rape is something which is not at all acceptable to any society. On September 28, the Supreme Court took suo motu cognisance of various news reports on recent crimes against women and minor girls across Delhi-NCR and stated that such incidents highlight a systematic failure of the law enforcement agencies.

articleTitle: How military dogs are trained to brave Ladakh’s 14,000-ft heights
articleFeaturedImageAlt: dogs
description: From detecting explosives to tracking and patrolling, military dogs undergo specialised training and gradual acclimatisation to operate in Ladakh’s thin air and extreme cold.
body_raw: The Indian Army and the Indo-Tibetan Border Police Force ITBP have reportedly deployed trained Himalayan canines, including indigenous breeds such as the Bakharwal and Tibetan Mastiff, for surveillance and security operations along the Ladakh frontier. According to a report by The Telegraph online, the dogs are being used at sensitive posts, some at an altitude of up to 14,000 feet, along the Line of Actual Control LAC. But operating at such elevations requires more than a dog being physically strong or accustomed to cold weather. Military dogs undergo specialised training and acclimatisation to prepare them for the combination of thin air, extreme temperatures and demanding terrain. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. What makes military dog training different? Military working dogs are trained to remain focused on a task despite environmental and physical challenges. At high altitude, that capability has to be supported by appropriate acclimatisation, nutrition, rest, monitoring and protective measures, says Dr Vinod Sharma, Director and Head of Veterinary Services, DCC Animal Hospital, Gurugram. He explains, Their training at specialised centres such as those associated with the Remount and Veterinary Corps is adapted before they are deployed to high-altitude areas. High-altitude training is different because the dog has to perform its usual detection, tracking or patrol duties while simultaneously adapting to reduced oxygen availability and extreme cold. The dogs are therefore not immediately expected to perform strenuous drills after reaching a high-altitude environment. Acclimatisation is gradual and can take weeks, allowing their bodies to adjust to the thinner air. Initially, the intensity and duration of exercise are reduced. The workload is then increased progressively as the dog develops better tolerance to the altitude, Sharma explains. How do dogs cope with thin air? At around 14,000 feet, the amount of oxygen available in the air is considerably lower than at sea level. This can affect a dogs exercise tolerance, resulting in faster fatigue, heavier breathing and slower recovery. For a military dog, however, simply being able to walk or run at altitude is not enough. It may have to identify a scent, follow a trail or search an area while maintaining concentration. Detection and tracking skills themselves do not fundamentally change at altitude. What changes is the physical cost of performing those tasks. Pacing, adequate rest and recovery become much more important, says Sharma. This is why handlers closely observe the dogs during training and deployment and adjust their work-rest cycles accordingly. Training dogs to work in extreme cold Dr Sharma says the paws require particular attention because prolonged exposure to snow, ice and rough terrain can result in paw-pad cracking and other injuries. Protective equipment may be used where necessary, along with regular inspection of the paws and body. The dogs also need protection from more serious cold-related problems such as frostbite and hypothermia, particularly during prolonged exposure. What are the biggest health challenges? Hypoxia and reduced exercise tolerance are important challenges at high altitude. A dog that is breathing heavily, tiring unusually quickly or taking longer than normal to recover needs to be assessed and its workload adjusted, Sharma says. The rugged terrain adds another layer of difficulty. Uneven surfaces and long patrols can put additional stress on the joints, muscles and paws, increasing the possibility of musculoskeletal injuries. Unlike controlled training surfaces, mountainous terrain is uneven and unpredictable. Repeated movement over such ground can contribute to muscle, joint and paw strain, he adds. Why nutrition and hydration matter Nutrition has to be tailored to the workload and environmental conditions. Dogs working in severe cold and at high altitude may require greater energy intake to maintain body condition and performance, says Sharma. Hydration is equally important. Dry air, exertion and limited access to water can increase the risk of dehydration. Gastrointestinal problems can also affect a dogs ability to eat, drink and perform effectively, he adds. articleTitle: Accident death insurance rejected over ‘false information’, Andhra man secures Rs 50 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: consumer commission insurance post-mortem report death
description: The Kurnool District Consumer Commission was hearing a complaint filed by the deceased man’s brother and nominee challenging the rejection of his Rs 50 lakh insurance claim following the man’s fatal road accident.
body_raw: An Andhra Pradesh consumer commission has directed a private insurance company to pay Rs 50 lakh to the nominee of a man who died in a road accident, after the insurer rejected the claim citing alleged misrepresentation of facts. The commission also directed the insurer to pay Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental agony and Rs 5,000 towards costs after finding that the insurers own investigator had called the accident genuine. Kurnool District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission president Karanam Kishore Kumar and members N Narayana Reddy and S Nazima Kausar were hearing a complaint filed by Yellala Jagadeeshawara Reddy, brother and nominee of Divakar Reddy Yellala, who died in the accident in April 2025. The insurance policy had a sum assured of Rs 50 lakh and was in force when the accident occurred. The rejectionnon-settlement of the claim by the Opposite Party the insurer, without establishing a valid and substantiated ground under the policy terms and conditions, amounts to deficiency in service. The complainant, being the nominee under the policy, is therefore entitled to receive the Sum Assured of Rs 50 lakh. Having regard to the prolonged non-settlement of the legitimate claim and the hardship and mental agony caused to the complainant, he is also entitled compensation, the commission said on October 1. The accident occurred when an unknown vehicle allegedly hit Divakars motorcycle at about 11.30 pm on April 14, 2025, on NH-40 near Ganesh Godown in Govindapalle village, Sirivella. Divakar suffered bleeding head injuries and died on the spot. His post-mortem report recorded Head Injury as the cause of death. Insurer rejects claim The insurance policy commenced on December 19, 2024, and was valid until December 18, 2025. The premium was Rs 4,767, and Jagadeeshawara Reddy was the nominee. The insurance nominee submitted the claim form on May 8, 2025. The insurer later sought additional documents and rejected the claim. In an email dated June 28, 2025, it said scrutiny and verification had revealed misrepresentation of facts to obtain the insurance benefit and that the claim fell outside the policy terms. The insurance company told the commission that the nominee had failed to provide documents despite repeated reminders. It said letters dated May 17, May 19, May 21 and May 25 had sought documents required to process the claim, including the final police report. But the commission found that the insurer had not produced evidence that these communications reached the complainant. No proof that notices reached nominee The commission noted that there were no postal receipts, acknowledgements, tracking reports, courier records, email delivery reports or other documentary evidence establishing that the alleged communications had been dispatched and served. It said that simply mentioning the dates of the communications was not enough to establish that they had been sent to or received by the complainant. The burden was upon the insurance company to establish that the complainant had been called upon to furnish the documents and given a reasonable opportunity to do so, the commission said. It also relied on the insurance companys own field verification report. The investigator found the incident to be genuine and the cause of death consistent with the post-mortem report. The commission said the investigation verified the complainants account of the accident and death. The commission found that the insurer had not identified the particular fact allegedly misrepresented by the deceased. It said the company had not established what declaration was false, when the alleged misrepresentation was made or how it was material to acceptance of the insurance risk. It said the insurance company had not shown that the absence of the final police report extinguished or suspended its liability under the policy. No evidence was produced to show that the report contained any finding adverse to the claim. Holding that the rejection of the claim was not supported by a valid ground under the policy terms, the commission held that it amounted to deficiency in service. The insurer was given 45 days from receipt of the order to comply. If it fails to pay within that period, the Rs 50 lakh sum assured will carry interest at 9 per cent per annum from October 6, 2025, the date of the complaint, until realisation. Takeaway If an insurer rejects a claim citing misrepresentation or missing documents, it should be able to clearly establish the specific violation and show that the claimant was properly asked to provide the required documents. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Andhra Pradesh helpline0866-2551431 or call the National Consumer Helpline at1915for assistance.
