articleTitle: Election Commissioners’ SIR objections trigger court pleas: What they are seeking
articleFeaturedImageAlt: election commission of India EC commissioners ECI supreme court gyanesh kumar bombay high court
description: In response to 'growing concerns by citizens', the Lawyers Association for Constitution recently formed a panel of former apex court and high court judges, headed by retired Supreme Court Justice Madan B Lokur, to examine the SIR process.
body_raw: Following The Indian Expresss reports on objections raised by two Election Commissioners over decisions taken in connection with the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls, multiple petitions have been filed in the Supreme Court and the Bombay High Court questioning the functioning of Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar and seeking an SIT investigation into the matter, besides his removal from office. As decisions are awaited, heres a closer look at what has happened in these matters so far Before Supreme Court One of the petitions by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh referred to the alleged differences between CEC Kumar and ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi and the objections raised by the latter. Article 3241 of the Constitution does not vest the superintendence, direction and control of elections in an individual Chief Election Commissioner. It vests those powers in a Commission, said the plea. The petitioner urged the court to declare SIR, and all actions, decisions, directions, and measures taken under it, invalid from the very beginning and without legal authority. The petitioner argued that the SIR was undertaken without the necessary statutory or constitutional authority and without following the procedure required by law. The other petition by Delhi-based lawyer Shailendra Mani Tripathi has sought a probe by an independent, high-powered judicial inquiry commission or an SIT headed by a retired judge of the top court. The petition refers to unprecedented constitutional fractures and illegalities committed within the ECI under the CEC as exposed by documentary records published on September 23, 2026. The plea said the alleged act of.CEC Kumar.falls squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constitutes distinct, personal criminal liability. The petitions were filed days after The Indian Express reported that ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR of electoral rolls. The two commissioners said some of the decisions were taken without their knowledge or recommendation. They separately wrote to the countrys top bureaucrat, Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan, flagging concerns over the integrity of voter software. The ECI, however, said the letters sent by Sandhu and Joshi to the Cabinet Secretary concerned an officer on deputation and were not related to policy or IT division matters. At Bombay High Court Two pleas were also filed in the Bombay High Court seeking several directions to the Election Commission of India ECI, including placing on record 14 decisions concerning the SIR, criteria for polling station rationalisation and ECINET specifications. ECINET is the ECIs comprehensive digital platform to facilitate citizen participation in the electoral process. The pleas also seek the restoration of every voter deleted during the SIR process in Maharashtra, or quashing of the SIR directions for the state and a stay on forthcoming Assembly elections until the electoral rolls are made legally compliant. One of the pleas seek the appointment of an independent judicial committee to investigate the data deletions and software blockages implemented during the current SIR process. A writ petition filed by four Maharashtra residents and registered voters through advocate Asim Sarode before the Kolhapur circuit bench cited The Indian Express investigation and claimed they were aggrieved by the systematic erosion of constitutional norms governing the management of electoral rolls, which they said directly affected their fundamental rights. The matter is likely to come up on October 22. At the High Courts Goa bench, a matter was heard relating to the deletion of names of six members of a family in Goa from the electoral rolls after their Form 8 applications for address change were rejected. It remarked that the ECI must endeavour to have as many voters who are eligible on the electoral rolls. The court said the poll body has to achieve the objective of not missing out on a voter, even when they come forward with a wrong form. We are asking the principle. The Election Commission must endeavour, and we see that is the endeavour.to have as many voters who are eligible on the rolls. Why should it reject the Form-8 if it comes during that enumeration period of SIR? Independent panel of former SC, HC judges In a related development, former Supreme Court and high court judges have formed a panel to examine the SIR exercise. In a press release dated October 2, the Lawyers Association for Constitution LAFC said that the constitution of the independent inquiry commission was in response to growing concerns raised by citizens regarding the design, implementation, and consequences of the SIR of electoral rolls by the ECI. The panel is stated to function with complete autonomy to examine the constitutional and statutory validity, methodology, and overall impact of the SIR exercise on eligible voters. It will be chaired by former Supreme Court judge Justice Madan B Lokur and will comprise former Supreme Court judge Justice A K Patnaik, former Jammu and Kashmir High Court Chief Justice Badar Durrez Ahmad,former Delhi High Court judge Justice Rekha Sharma and former Patna High Court judge Justice Anjana Prakash. Senior legal practitioners, including Kapil Sibal, Prashant Bhushan, Chander Uday Singh, Prashanto Chandra Sen, Raju Ramachandran, Rebecca Mammen John, Warisha Farasat, Vrinda Grover, etc, will provide strategic legal advice, the release said. The panel seeks to travel across the country to hear testimony directly from affected citizens, civil society groups, and experts. At the same time, a dedicated research wing would collate and analyse the data regarding voter roll additionsdeletions across the country and present it before the panel. A legal support team will review relevant legislation, notifications, and verification processes to assess compliance with constitutional safeguards, the release added.

articleTitle: Bengaluru techie drowns in abandoned quarry during Instagram trekking group’s outing
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru trekker drowning
description: Following an exhaustive two-day search, rescuers retrieved the body of techie Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay from a vast, waterlogged quarry pit near Yellammanadoddi.
body_raw: What began as a promising long-weekend getaway for a group of trekkers connected through Instagram ended in heartbreak near Jigani on the outskirts of Bengaluru. Ganesh Anjaneya Vinay, 30, an IIT Delhi postgraduate and associate user experience UX designer living in Halasuru, drowned after taking a dip in an abandoned, water-filled stone quarry. Originally from Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh, Vinay built his career in Bengaluru over the past four years. On October 2, he set out for a holiday trek with eight companions met through an Instagram trekking circle, including his fiance, a veterinary doctor. Midway through their journey, the group paused at a massive stone quarry near Yellammanadoddi. Decommissioned nearly 15 years ago, the pit had gradually become a deep rainwater reservoir, tempting the trekkers to step in for a swim. The group spent nearly an hour and a half playing in the water before the outing took a sudden, fatal turn around 5.30 pm, when his friends realised Vinay was missing. For some time, I think the group might not have noticed Vinay. It appeared that he knew swimming and are investigating under what circumstances he drowned, a police officer said. Challenging search operation His friends attempts to find him were unsuccessful, leading to an urgent distress call to the Jigani police. Local residents also joined in to help, though the vast quarry presented a significant challenge. It is an abandoned quarry. Not many go to that place. We got to know around 6 pm on the day of the incident, and it was a very vast place to search, said Kalappa, a local resident. A desparate search operation unfolded over the next two days. Initial efforts by local Fire and Emergency Services expanded to include teams from the State Disaster Response Force SDRF, the National Disaster Response Force NDRF, and local divers. Authorities also called renowned expert scuba diver Eshwar Malpe and his team from coastal Karnataka to join the rescue efforts. Following a non-stop effort, rescue crews retrieved Vinays body at around 9 am on Sunday. The Jigani police registered a case of unnatural death based on a complaint filed by his brother.

articleTitle: Anti-CEC stir: Journalist detained 2 days after she alleged sexual harassment by cops
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police personnel detain All India Students' Association (AISA) National President Neha Bora during the ‘Citizens’ March’ from India Gate to Jantar Mantar, in New Delhi on Sunday. (ANI Photo)
description: The protesters had camped outside Parliament Street police station overnight, demanding against officers who allegedly sexually assaulted three women journalists
body_raw: The protest against the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the alleged irregularities in Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls entered its fourth consecutive day on Monday, with the Delhi Police registering six FIRs and arresting 18 people in connection with the alleged instances of violence that broke out during a NSUI demonstration and for circulating AI generated poster of policemen, officers said on Monday. Among the six FIRs, four were related to violence, vandalism and rioting during the NSUI demonstration, one tied to an alleged attack on a CISF personnel and another related to circulating a fake poster that showed an officer allegedly sexually harassing a woman. Meanwhile, one of the three women journalists who had alleged sexual harassment by Delhi Police personnel while covering the anti-CEC protest has been detained along with 16 others on Monday, for camping overnight outside Parliament Street police station, demanding action against the officers. The same day also saw a CISF constable allegedly getting attacked with a knife by a protester amid an NSUI demonstration at Jantar Mantar. The developments came amid continued demonstrations near Jantar Mantar and growing demands for a probe into the allegations made by three female journalists, who have accused police personnel of sexually assaulting them while they were reporting on the stir on October 3. A senior police officer said restrictions under prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS had been imposed across the New Delhi district. According to the officer, gatherings were not permitted at Parliament Street because it is not an authorised protest location. On Monday morning, around 17 people who had spent the night outside the Parliament Street police station were detained. The group, comprising freelance journalists, YouTubers and one of the alleged victims of sexual assault, had gathered to demand registration of an FIR and action against the officers accused in the alleged sexual harassment case. The protesters were detained individually and taken by bus to Delhi Cantonment Police Station, officers said. The woman who has alleged harassment told reporters that the group wanted to enter the police station and meet senior officers to find out the status of her complaint. The detainees were subsequently released in the evening. The police had on Sunday confirmed receiving three separate complaints from female journalists alleging sexual harassment by police personnel during the October 3 demonstration near Jantar Mantar. The complaints have been handed over to the Crime Branch. Meanwhile, a separate incident involving a CISF constable was reported during an NSUI demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Monday afternoon. The constable deployed for law-and-order duties was allegedly attacked with a knife by a protester, officers said. The constable, identified as Vikram Kumar, was reportedly moving a young man away from the barricades towards the designated protest area when the man allegedly pulled out a knife and attempted to strike him in the neck, police said. Kumar allegedly raised his hand to protect himself, suffering a cut and scratches on his right elbow, officers said. Kumar was taken to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital and was later discharged. Security personnel at the site detained the alleged attacker and handed him over to the police, officers said. In a purported video recorded after the incident, Kumar said he immediately informed his senior officers after the alleged attack. Police are questioning the accused to determine how he obtained the knife and what prompted the alleged assault. Around 50 NSUI protesters were also detained during the demonstration and later released. Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janta Party CJP expressed support for the women who have alleged sexual harassment and demanded action against the police personnel named in the complaints. CJP legal team head Ratna Singh alleged on X that the woman complainant and others demanding registration of an FIR were detained and claimed that some detainees were assaulted. Police, however, denied the allegation of manhandling, saying the protesters resisted detention while male and female personnel were escorting them to the bus.

articleTitle: Elon Musk’s SpaceXAI to be ‘SpaceXSI’: Where does ‘super intelligence’ term come from?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence tool Grok was used to launch strikes against Iran
description: Musk is joining US President Trump’s push to replace ‘AI’ with ‘SI’. But what does super intelligence mean, what are its origins, and why is it a contested term?
body_raw: Elon Musk has said that he will rename SpaceXs AI unit to closely reflect the term US President Donald Trump has been pushing, super intelligence or SI, instead of artificial intelligence. The tech billionaire in a post on X on Sunday, October 4, said that the name of SpaceXAI will be changed to SpaceXSI. However, he did not provide any further details regarding the Grok-makers rebrand. Yes, we will make that change, Musk said in a reply to a user on X asking him about the possibility of renaming SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI. The SpaceX CEO is one of the first bold-faced names in Big Tech looking to embrace Trumps preferred term for AI. Earlier, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang also said that data centres should now be referred to as superintelligence factories. These proposed name changes come days after tech CEOs and AI industry leaders met with Trump at the White House, and signed onto an agreement of voluntary safety standards that Trump said was morally binding. The voluntary pact primarily involves AI frontier companies teaming up with an independent external auditor to assess that models are operating as intended and implement internal controls to ensure that their AI agents do not hack systems. However, several critics have argued that AI is facing a crisis of public trust and a name change is unlikely to resolve mounting concerns over safety risks posed by the rapidly evolving technology. A look at Trumps super intelligence push Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Trump said, From this point forward, all of United States documents, and hopefully the worlds will be changed to use the much more accurate term super as opposed to artificial. So its super intelligence. The US president has even signed an executive order renaming artificial intelligence to super intelligence in order to better capture the fact that the technology does much more than imitate or automate discrete aspects of human intelligence. The executive order further requires US government agencies at the federal level to use the new term, or SI, when referring to the technology in public communications, websites, reports and policy documents. Michael Kratsios, director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy, has reportedly been tasked with figuring out whether an official definition of the new term should be modified or expanded, as per the order. On one hand, AI industry leaders such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman have called for a deliberate slowdown of frontier AI progress and urged the government to implement federal guardrails on frontier AI models, Trump has so far opposed regulation. He has also repeatedly dismissed whistleblowers warnings of AI security risks as overblown and a hoax. The Trump administration has also set up a task force or Super Intelligence Force, which will be tasked with producing a report on the risks and opportunities of AI within 120. The group will be led by Trumps newly appointed AI czar, Jay Clayton, who also serves as the director of national intelligence. Meanwhile, California Governor Gavin Newsom has looked to counter Trumps super intelligence push by issuing an executive order of his own, requiring state agencies to refer to the technology only as artificial intelligence or AI. Super intelligence is clearly not coming from the White House - thats why California continues to lead, Newsom said in a statement. What does SI mean in the AI space? So far, super intelligence has been used by AI industry executives and researchers to refer to an AI system with cognitive capabilities that essentially outperform humans in all aspects of thinking. Currently, such an AI system is hypothetical and does not exist. The term is also a severely contested one. Proponents of AI often use it to describe systems that surpass human abilities and bring major benefits. On the other hand, AI safety advocates have warned that such systems could outpace human control and may lead to the extinction of human beings. There are several other terms in AI discourse that are closely related to super intelligence, but slightly vary in meaning. For instance, artificial super intelligence ASI, has its roots in a 2014 book titled Superintelligence Paths, Dangers, Strategies written by controversial philosopher Nick Bostrom. OpenAI has been pursuing artificial general intelligence AGI, which is an umbrella term used to refer to technology that outperforms humans in several tasks without specifically being trained to do so. However, in September 2024, Sam Altman outlined a heady vision of ASI and what it would be like to live in a world with such technology. It is possible that we will have superintelligence in a few thousand days  it may take longer, but Im confident well get there, Altman wrote in his 2024 blog post titled The Intelligence Age. Another term popularised by a tech CEO is personal superintelligence. In August 2025, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg published a letter outlining his vision for personal superintelligence, which is rooted in the idea that people should use AI to achieve their personal goals. Metas vision is to bring personal superintelligence to everyone. We believe in putting this power in peoples hands to direct it toward what they value in their own lives. This is distinct from others in the industry who believe superintelligence should be directed centrally towards automating all valuable work, and then humanity will live on a dole of its output, he said.

articleTitle: Top 20 UPSC Current Affairs Pointers of the past week | September 28 to October 4, 2026
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Top 20 UPSC Current Affairs Pointers of the past week | September 28 to October 4, 2026
description: What were the most important current affairs for UPSC this week? From the 2026 Asian Games and Poompuhar excavation to 100 years of UPSC, red rot fungal disease, the UN sea level declaration, ECINET portal and other key developments for your Prelims and Mains preparation.
body_raw: Every Monday, we bring you UPSC Current Affairs Pointers-a concise, exam-focused guide to help you stay ahead in your Prelims and Mains preparation. If you missed the UPSC Current Affairs Pointers of the past week  September 21 to 27, 2026 , read it here. Art  Culture  New heritage sites added to Indias UNESCO Tentative List - Recently, five new sites and transnational proposals have been included in Indias UNESCO Tentative List and it increases Indias count to 78. - According to the World Heritage Conventions operational guidelines, a tentative list is an inventory of properties a country believes deserves to be a World Heritage Site. - The newly added sites include the Buddhist murals of Bagh Cave Paintings, Group of Temples of the Chambal Valley, the Gupta-era Udaigiri Caves, the tribal legacy of Ginnorgarh, and Sites of Satyagrah. - Group of Temples of the Chambal Valley It is unique cluster of early medieval temples built between the 8th and 11th centuries CE, representing an important phase in the evolution of regional Nagara-style temple architecture. - Udaigiri Caves It is a rock-cut sacred ensemble developed under Gupta patronage in the 4th and 5th centuries CE. The site includes 20 caves, sculptures and inscriptions, including the Varaha form of Vishnu in Cave 5 and Anantasayana Vishnu in Cave 13. - The Sites of Satyagraha It is a serial transnational proposal connecting India and South Africa. It includes nine properties across South Africa and India, including Sabarmati Ashram, Mani Bhavan Complex, Harijan Sevak Sangh Complex, Sevagram Ashram, Aga Khan Palace and Gandhi Smriti Residence in India, along with Pietermaritzburg Railway Station and Phoenix Settlement in South Africa. - Ginnorgarh Fort It was a major political and administrative centre of the Gond kingdom from the early 16th to early 18th century. The fort includes palace buildings, stepwells, reservoirs, wall paintings and an ingenious water management system. - Bagh Cave Paintings It is a group of nine rock-cut Buddhist caves, mainly in use from the 4th to 6th century CE. Their murals, particularly those in Cave 4, are significant examples of post-Ajanta Buddhist cave paintings.  Poompuhar excavation - Fresh underwater excavations off Poompuhar, the ancient Chola port city in Tamil Nadu, have yielded new evidence of the settlements maritime connections. - The 18-day exploration, conducted by the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology TNSDA in collaboration with the Indian Maritime University, recovered a fragment of a West Asian torpedo jar, four terracotta ring wells, and more than 250 ceramic fragments, among other finds. - Poompuhar, located in present-day Mayiladuthurai district, features prominently in Sangam and post-Sangam literature. Archaeological investigations over the decades have uncovered evidence of its links with wider Indian Ocean trade, while much of the ancient settlement is believed to now lie beneath the sea. - Located at the mouth of the 800-km-long Cauvery river, where it empties into the Bay of Bengal, Poompuhar - also known as Kaveripoompattinam - is believed to have been the capital of the early Cholas. - The port is described as having been very busy and crowded during the Chola period. Merchandise exported from the city was stamped with a tiger symbol, indicating that it came from Chola country. It is believed that catastrophic floods lashed the coast and swallowed major portions of the city around the 4th or 5th century CE. - Among other prominent findings were brick structures, terracotta ring wells, storage jars and clay patches that appear to have belonged to the Sangam period. Polity  UPSC turns 100 - Prime Minister Narendra Modi Thursday hailed the Union Public Service Commission UPSC on its centenary, calling it a proud milestone and a celebration not just of its legacy of serving the people but also of the aspirations of lakhs of youths year after year. - PM Modi marked the occasion by releasing a commemorative postage stamp, a special coin, and a compilation of 100 significant case laws. - Notably, based on the recommendations of the Lee Commission 1924, a Public Service Commission was established on October 1, 1926. Later on, the Government of India Act of 1935 formally established the Federal Public Service Commission FPSC in 1937. The FPSC became the Union Public Service Commission with the adoption of the Indian Constitution in 1950. - The UPSC is Indias central recruiting agency and an independent constitutional body, as it derives its authority directly from the Constitution. Articles 315 to 323 in Part XIV contain detailed provisions relating to the Commissions composition, appointment and removal of members, as well as its independence, powers and functions. - The UPSC consists of a Chairman and other members appointed by the President of India. The Constitution does not prescribe the strength of the Commission. Instead, it leaves the matter to the discretion of the President, who determines its composition.  Third-longest sine die adjournment - At 46 days and counting, the Eighth Session of the 18th Lok Sabha has acquired the distinction of witnessing the third-longest sine die adjournment in history, Parliament records show. - The Monsoon Session of Parliament began on July 20 and was adjourned sine die on August 13. Unlike prorogation, which formally ends a session, an adjournment sine die ends the sitting without fixing a date for the House to meet again. - An adjournment postpones the sitting of the House to another time. When a House is adjourned sine die, no date is fixed for its next sitting. The sitting has ended, but the session itself has not necessarily been terminated. - Prorogation is different. Under Article 852 of the Constitution, a session of Parliament is formally terminated by an order of the President. Ordinarily, prorogation follows an adjournment sine die, although the two are legally distinct. - The President exercises the power to prorogue Parliament on the advice of the Prime Minister. Prorogation may technically take place at any time, including while the House is sitting, though the usual sequence is for the House to be adjourned sine die before it is prorogued. - The Speaker can call a sitting of the Lok Sabha before the date to which it has been adjourned, or at any time after the House has been adjourned sine die. This means that an adjournment sine die does not, by itself, prevent the House from being reconvened. - The two longest sine die adjournments in Lok Sabha history occurred during the Eighth Lok Sabha.  ERONET and ECINET portal - The Election Commission has removed an additional SIR declaration from Form 6 on its ECINET portal in states where the revision exercise has concluded, days after questions were raised over whether the online form had been altered beyond what the law permits. - The Election Commission describes ERONET as a centralized form processing system for handling voter registration, migration and deletion. It replaced 36 separate systems and databases used by states to manage their electoral rolls. - ERONET is intended to aid the Electoral Registration Officer ERO in the capacity of a decision support system, in preparing and revising the electoral roll of an assembly constituency. - ECINET is a newer, broader platform that brings together electoral applications and services that were previously spread across multiple platforms. Officially launched in January 2026, it rationalised over 40 applications and websites used by voters, candidates, political parties and election officials. - Major services for voters range from registration and searching electoral rolls to tracking applications, downloading electronic voter identity cards and finding information about polling stations and candidates.  Conference on PRAHAAR-CT Policy and Strategy - Calling for a stronger, institutionalised counter-terrorism framework with a whole-of-society approach, Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated a conference on PRAHAAR-CT Policy and Strategy in New Delhi on Monday. - He stressed the need to strengthen the PRAHAAR strategy through continuous analysis of terror incidents and by establishing a concrete mechanism for the next 10 years. - PRAHAAR stands for the seven pillars of-Prevention, Response, Aggregating Internal Capacities, Human Rights, Attenuating Conditions for Terrorism, Aligning International Efforts, and Recovery and Resilience. - PRAHAAR, Indias first comprehensive counter-terrorism policy and strategy was announced by the Ministry of Home Affairs MHA in February, 2026. - The framework is built on zero tolerance, intelligence-led prevention and coordinated response to extremist violence. It also states that India does not associate terrorism with any religion, ethnicity or civilisation, even while observing that a few countries in the region have sometimes used terrorism as an instrument of state policy. - PRAHAAR seeks to deny terrorists, their financiers and supporters access to funds, weapons and safe havens, both within India and abroad, while adapting the countrys counter-terror response to emerging technological and transnational threats. What is Perimeter Fallacy? - On September 24, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh cautioned against viewing national security solely from the view of safeguarding geographical boundaries, stating that it would amount to perimeter fallacy. - He made this argument while pointing to the evolving nature of modern-day challenges - drones, cyberattacks, lone wolf attacks, and disinformation campaigns, in addition to the use of arms and artillery, by adversaries. - A perimeter in a security context is the physical boundary of the State in question. Traditionally, national security has placed emphasis on the prevention of the violation of such boundaries by adversaries. - This has largely been dependent upon fortifications at the border and troop deployments. While territorial borders remain geographically fixed, modern threats are highly fluid.  Post-facto environmental clearance EC - The Union Environment Ministry has directed its central and state-level expert bodies to resume processing post-facto environmental clearance EC proposals, two months after the Supreme Court permitted it to take such pending, rejected or returned proposals to their logical conclusion in accordance with law. - Post-facto environmental clearances refer to dispensation provided by the Centre for those projects which had begun work, expanded, or modernised them without seeking prior approval as mandated by law.  Pricing of medicines in India - The Supreme Court described the markup between the price at which medicines reach retailers and the price printed on the pack as carnage, calling the difference akin to broad daylight dacoity with patients. - Hearing petitions on medicine pricing, a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta asked the Centre why the 16 retailer margin under the Drugs Prices Control Order DPCO, 2013, should not apply to all essential medicines. - The Essential Commodities Act, 1955, gives the Centre power over essential goods, including medicines. Section 31 allows it to regulate production, supply, and distribution for maintaining or increasing supplies of any essential commodity or for securing their equitable distribution and availability at fair price. Section 32c allows for issuing orders controlling commodity prices. - The DPCO is such an order. It is the primary framework governing medicine prices in India. It authorises the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority NPPA, set up in 1997 under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, to fix and revise ceiling prices of scheduled formulations, set retail prices for new drugs, monitor overcharging and implement the DPCO. - The DPCO divides medicines into two broad categories - scheduled and non-scheduled formulations. A formulation refers to a medicine in a particular strength and dosage form. - Scheduled formulations are medicines included in Schedule I of the DPCO. Schedule I is based on the National List of Essential Medicines NLEM, a list prepared by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, identifying medicines considered essential for meeting the countrys healthcare needs. Non-scheduled formulations are medicines that are not listed.   Economy  Red rot fungal disease - Uttar Pradesh, Indias top cane growing state, has seen its sugar output plummet from 126.4 lakh tonnes lt to 89.5 lt between 2019-20 and 2025-26 October-September production years. - The primary reason has been the susceptibility of the widely-cultivated sugarcane variety, Co-0238 also called Karan 4, to red rot fungal disease. - Also known as the cancer of sugarcane due to its lethal and fast-spreading nature, the red rot fungus basically attacks the vascular system of sugarcane, through which the transport of water and nutrients from the roots to the stems, leaves and the rest of the plant takes place. Once infected, this system gets clogged, disrupting the plants ability to access these essential growth elements, leading to wilting, and eventually, shrivelled and hollow canes. - The industry is now pinning hopes on a new variety developed by the Indian Council of Agricultural Researchs Sugarcane Breeding Institute ICAR-SBI at Coimbatore. This variety, Co-20016 Karan 20, has already been picked as a potential replacement for Co-0238 by a Varietal Identification Committee under the All-India Coordinated Research Project AICRP on Sugarcane, which met on May 27. - The Co-20016 variety has shown itself to be resistant to red rot-specifically the highly virulent CF13 pathotype of the Colletotrichum falcatum fungal pathogen. When Co-0238 was developed by ICAR-SBI and released in 2009, it was evaluated as moderately resistant to the prevalent CF07 and CF08 pathotypes of the red rot-causing fungus.  Minimum Support Prices MSPs for rabi crops - The Centre announced MSPs for six rabi crops for the 2027-28 season, with wheat - Indias second-largest crop by acreage - receiving a 17-year-low hike of just Rs 25 per quintal, a marginal 0.97 increase. -Wheat is one of the six officially mandated rabi crops in India under the governments MSP system. The others are safflower, rapeseed and mustard, lentil, barley, and gram. Among the six, safflower saw the biggest hike in absolute and percentage terms. What is MSP? -MSP is the price at which the government is supposed to procurebuy that crop from farmers if the market price falls below it. MSPs provide a floor for market prices and ensure that farmers receive a certain minimum remuneration so that their costs of cultivation and some profit can be recovered. - The MSPs are announced by the Union government on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices CACP. CACP is an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare. It is an advisory body whose recommendations are not binding on the Government. -The CACP recommends MSPs for 22 mandated crops and fair and remunerative price FRP for sugarcane -Crops covered under MSP are  14 Kharif crops Paddy, Jowar, Bajra, Maize, Ragi, Tur arhar, Moong, Urad, Groundnut, Soyabean, Sunflower, Sesamum, Nigerseed, and Cotton.  6 Rabi crops Wheat, Barley, Gram, Masur lentil, Rapeseed and mustard, and Safflower  2 Commercial crops Jute and Copra Science and Technology  Indias first LNG-powered train - After launching the countrys first hydrogen train on July 17, 2026, Indian Railways has now introduced another alternative-fuel train based on Liquefied Natural Gas LNG. The LNG-powered train was launched from Sabarmati in Gujarat on September 27. - Developed by Chennai-based Integral Coach Factory ICF, the new train uses a LNG-diesel dual-fuel system, allowing its engine to run on both LNG and diesel. The move is aimed at reducing diesel consumption, fuel costs and emissions while encouraging the use of alternative fuels in railway operations. - During its inaugural run, the first LNG-diesel dual-fuel DEMU train operates between Sabarmati and Mahesana Junction. The train is an 8-coach, non-AC chair car train. Its regular route has not yet been finalised and will be announced after the route is confirmed. - Each DPC has been fitted with an LNG tank with a capacity of around 2,200 litres. The tank can hold approximately 9501,000 kg of usable LNG. - According to the approved design, a fully loaded LNG tank in one DPC can provide enough fuel for around 444 km of daily operation. This can reduce the need for frequent refuelling.  ISRO to get newest facility in Guwahati - The Indian Space Research Organisation ISRO will get a boost to its radar and satellite tracking capabilities with a new facility coming up in Chandrapur near Guwahati. - Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma laid the foundation stone of this facility in presence of V Narayanan, ISRO chairman, and other senior space scientists on September 21. Important Facilities of ISRO - Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre LPSC-Thiruvananthapuram Keralam and Bengaluru Karnataka - Space Applications Centre SAC-Ahmedabad Gujarat - Satish Dhawan Space Centre SDSC SHAR-Nellore Andhra Pradesh - ISRO Telemetry, Tracking and Command Network ISTRAC-Bengaluru Karnataka Health  Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection SCAD - The Spontaneous Coronary Artery Dissection is a hidden, sudden type of heart attack caused by a spontaneous tear or bruise inside a cardiac artery. In a normal heart attack, a cholesterol-rich plaque in a heart artery usually ruptures or erodes, causing a blood clot that obstructs blood flow. - The American Heart Associations 2026 scientific statement on acute coronary syndromes in premenopausal women highlights SCAD as an under-recognised problem. - Young women account for approximately 8090 of SCAD cases. Among women under 50 who have a heart attack, SCAD may account for as many as one-third of cases, says Dr Ambuj Roy, Professor of Cardiology, AIIMS, Delhi.   Environment  UN sea level declaration - On 24 September, the UN General Assembly adopted its first ever declaration on rising sea levels, which pose an existential threat to populations around the world. - The rise in sea levels has been accelerating to quote the declaration for some time now. The rate of global rise more than doubled from 2.1 mm a year in 1993-2002 to 4.7 mm a year in 2015-2024, according to the World Meteorological Organization. In 2024 alone the sea rose 6 mm, the largest annual increase on record. - The declaration addresses the issue of loss of territory faced by low-lying countries that are particularly vulnerable to rising sea levels and persistent coastal erosion. - Importantly, it also asks nations to build sea-level rise projections into the planning and design of their coastal infrastructure. Can a country retain its statehood even if it loses its territory? Under the 1933 Montevideo Convention, a State is defined using four main criteria a permanent population, a defined territory, a government and the capacity to enter into relations with other states. But if rising sea levels swallow a States defined territory, or render it uninhabitable for a permanent population, does it still remain a state? This is the question the UN declaration attempts to settle. Indeed, it affirms that a country stays a country when the sea takes its land. - The declaration calls adaptation and mitigation action essential, but leaves the negotiation of emission cuts to the UN climate convention and the Paris Agreement.  Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme - The Union Cabinet on September 30 approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III GEC-III scheme. With a total outlay of Rs 1,86,405 crore, the scheme is targeted for completion by FY33. The scheme aimed at enabling the evacuation of up to 135 gigawatts GW of renewable energy across states. -The scheme also, for the first time under the Green Energy Corridor programme, includes a dedicated battery energy storage component, with provisions for deploying 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems BESS at renewable energy developergenerator sites or other locations of importance to the grid. - The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy MNRE is implementing the Green Energy Corridorin two phases to augment transmission lines and transformation capacity through intra-state transmission InSTS and inter-state transmission ISTS networks. - Of the total outlay, Rs 1,36,378 crore has been earmarked for developing intra-state transmission systems, while Rs 50,000 crore has been allocated for 50 GWh of BESS. The scheme will involve total Central Financial Support of Rs 54,082 crore. - Under GEC Phase-II, which is being implemented in seven states - Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh - the target is to add 7,863 ckm of transmission lines and 24,388 MVA of substation capacity.The scheme is expected to help in achieving the target of 900 GW installed Non-Fossil capacity by 2035. Click here to read more on Green Energy Corridor Phase-III  Uttarakhands first glacial lake early-warning system - Weeks after the Nepal disaster, the Himalayan state of Uttarakhand is moving from mapping its vulnerable glacial lakes to monitoring them in real time, with the states first early-warning system for a glacial lake being installed at Vasundhara Tal in Chamoli from September 29. - The National Disaster Management Authority NDMA had identified 13 high-risk glacial lakes in Uttarakhand, of which five were classified as Category A, the highest-risk category. Vasundhara Tal was among them. - The system being installed at Vasundhara will track water level, weather, snow conditions, water flow and movement around the lake. - A water-level sensor will monitor fluctuations and abnormal changes. An automatic weather station will record temperature, humidity, rainfall, wind speed and direction, atmospheric pressure and light intensity. Snow-depth and sub-surface temperature sensors will monitor changes in snow conditions. - A data logger and monitoring dashboard will record the readings and generate alerts when predetermined thresholds are crossed.  Corporate Average Fuel Economy CAFE-III framework - The final Corporate Average Fuel Economy CAFE-III framework are notified on September 29. It has introduced a new formula to relax norms for smaller cars, while doing away with an earlier proposed special concession for the category, and gives electric vehicles the biggest compliance benefit among the different powertrains. - The CAFE norms will apply from April 1, 2027, to March 31, 2032. They cover M1 category passenger vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in India. At the heart of the system is a fleet-wide calculation a manufacturers permitted fuel consumption is determined by the weighted average unladen weight of the vehicles it sells. - CAFE-III does not require manufacturers to balance their books completely every year. A manufacturer whose fleet performs better than its target earns credits, while one performing worse accumulates debits. These are recorded in a manufacturer-level passbook. - Credits can be carried forward within a compliance block and traded between manufacturers. A manufacturer with an outstanding deficit can also buy credits from the Bureau of Energy Efficiency. - Notably, CAFE-III is a set of fleet-level fuel-efficiency standards for passenger vehicles. First introduced in 2017 under the Energy Conservation Act, they require manufacturers to keep the average fuel consumption - and therefore CO2 emissions - of all eligible passenger vehicles they sell within a prescribed limit, rather than requiring every individual model to meet the same number. - The first CAFE-III proposal dates back to 2024, with the rules subsequently going through several revisions covering the weight formula, treatment of powertrains and compliance mechanisms. Sports  Asian Games 2026 - India concluded their 2026 Asian Games campaign in Aichi-Nagoya with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze for a haul of 85 medals, which helped them finish fourth, ahead of the likes of Uzbekistan, Iran and Thailand. - Many historic medals came Indias way across the fortnight. Kumkum Anil Mohod became the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve gold. Neeru Dhandas trap gold ended a 48-year wait, and the mixed trap pair of Neeru and Kynan Chenai set a new Asian record. - Pranavi Urs won countrys first-ever golf gold. The boxing ring produced three golds, with Lovlina Borgohain becoming only the second Indian woman after Mary Kom to win an Asiad boxing gold. - The Indian mens hockey team thrashed Malaysia 5-1 in the final at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya , winning the gold medal and successfully defending their Asian title for the first time in history. The victory also secured Indias qualification for the Los Angeles Olympics 2028. - India edged out Pakistan in a final by 19 runs to claim the Asian Games mens cricket gold medal at the Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin. Click here to see the full list of Asian Games 2026 Indian medal winners  Exchangeable Pitch System EPS - With an eye on keeping cricket pitches fresh for the 2027 Mens ODI World Cup, co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, pitch curators in the Rainbow Nation have come up with a unique Exchangeable Pitch System EPS. - Of the eight South African venues scheduled to host World Cup matches, five are preparing to install the system, allowing ground staff to exchange pitches to prevent deterioration from excess usage. - For starters, this sounds like a drop-in pitch, commonly used at Australias Melbourne Cricket Ground, in Adelaide, and in the US during the 2024 T20 World Cup. As the name suggests, a drop-in pitch is prepared externally and then dropped into a stadium before a cricket match is played. - This is because many stadiums are used for playing multiple sports, such as rugby and football, and hosting other events that require very different ground conditions. Places in News Just FYI The location of the place is important, considering that UPSC has asked several questions about places that were in the news, such as Aleppo and Kirkuk, in the 2018 UPSC Prelims. The best way to remember them is to plot them on a world map. articleTitle: ‘16 years apart’: Telangana High Court grants man divorce over false criminal case, cruelty
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Telangana High Court divorce false case cruelty The bench also noted that the wife’s allegations of dowry harassment and possession of her jewellery were “vague or unsupported”.
description: The wife had approached the women’s protection cell and lodged a criminal complaint over cruelty and dowry demands, following which the husband filed the divorce petition.
body_raw: The Telangana High Court has granted divorce to a couple after 16 years of separation, holding that a false criminal complaint against the husband and his family, coupled with prolonged separation, amounted to mental cruelty. The court set aside the family courts earlier dismissal of his petition. Dealing with a plea of husband, a bench of Justices K Lakshman and B R Madhusudhan Raosaid that the conduct of the parties clearly indicates that there is no intention on either side to lead a marital life. It is apt to note that when the petition was filed, the appellant was 33 years old and the respondent was 27 years old. At present, they are 49 years old and 42 years old, respectively. They have been living separately for approximately 16 years. The appellant has categorically stated that he is not willing to resume cohabitation or take her back into his society, the September 18 order reads. The bench further noted that the couple had been living separately for around 16 years, neither had made a genuine effort to resume living together, and the husband had clearly stated that he was unwilling to take the wife back. The court held that continuation of the marriage would serve no meaningful purpose and would cause mental cruelty to both parties. Husband sought divorce over cruelty The petitioner-husband has filed a plea challenging the 2017 order of the family court which dismissed his petition seeking divorce on grounds of cruelty. The couple got married in 2007. The husband sought divorce, claiming that after three to four months of marriage, the wife started harassing and torturing him, and insisted that he should become a puppet husband. He stated that she stopped performing her matrimonial obligations. The petitioner alleged that when he refused to accede to her demands, she physically assaulted him. He further alleged that her parents assured him that they would counsel her and took her away for around 10 days, but when she returned, she resumed abusing and harassing him. According to the husband, the two started living separately in the same house in separate rooms from 2008. He claimed that in 2009, she left the matrimonial home and started residing at her parental home. The wife denied the allegations and, in turn, accused the husband and his family of harassment, physical abuse, and interference in their marital life. She alleged that her mother-in-law and other family members subjected her to harassment and that the husband had also physically assaulted her. The matrimonial dispute escalated in 2010 after the wife and her father approached the womens protection cell, following which a criminal complaint was lodged against the husband and his family for cruelty and under the provisions of the Dowry Prohibition Act. The husband then filed the divorce petition in 2010, alleging cruelty. The family court initially dismissed the husbands divorce petition, holding that he had failed to establish cruelty through clear evidence. He challenged that decision before the high court. On the other hand, the criminal case against the husband and his family ended in acquittal in 2020, and the acquittal was upheld in 2025 following a plea. Wifes dowry claims unsupported Order The high court observed that cruelty is not defined by statute and whether a particular act amounts to cruelty depends on the facts and circumstances of each case. It said the court must consider the parties background, social and economic circumstances, values and the overall conduct between them. The ruling stressed that the cumulative effect of the parties conduct has to be considered rather than examining individual incidents in isolation. Persistent quarrels, humiliating treatment, mental harassment, abusive language, disrespectful behaviour, unilateral desertion and false accusations may constitute cruelty, while ordinary disagreements or petty quarrels would not. The bench also noted that the wifes allegations of dowry harassment and possession of her jewellery were vague or unsupported. The dowry allegation was raised for the first time during cross-examination, without details of any specific demand, while her claim regarding jewellery was found inconsistent with her own statement about having the keys to her almirah. The court held that the criminal complaint lodged by the wife against the husband and his family, which ended in acquittal and was also upheld in appeal, could be considered as subsequent evidence of cruelty. It is a well-settled legal position that when a criminal case ends in acquittal, it can be considered as a ground for cruelty, it concluded. The court clarified that subsequent events and the conduct of parties can be considered while examining a claim of cruelty. In this case, although the husbands own testimony was alone not enough to establish cruelty, the later acquittal in the criminal case, coupled with the wifes contradictory statements, supported his case.

articleTitle: ‘Cristiano Ronaldo should decide how he wants to end his time with national team’, says Portugal coach Jesus
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ronaldo left Portugal's training camp after being an unused substitute in a win over Norway and learning he would not start against Denmark. (AP Photo)
description: Jorge Jesus said that he had told Cristiano Ronaldo that he needed him, regardless of whether he was playing or not, when he had his first conversation with him after taking charge.
body_raw: Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus has said that it is upto Cristiano Ronaldo to decide if he wants to return to the national team or not. Jesus said that he had told Ronaldo that he needed him, regardless of whether he was playing or not, when he had his first conversation with him after taking charge. If he wants to, hell return to the national team. We can talk before the next call-up, but Cris is the one whos going to decide, Jesus told reporters after Portugals 2-1 Nations League win over Norway on Sunday. Ronaldo left Portugals training camp after being an unused substitute in a win over Norway and learning he would not start against Denmark. He subsequently said on social media that he would explain his reasons for leaving the national team in due course. The incident caused shockwaves around the world of football, with Jesus in particular receiving significant backlash in Portugal for leaving Ronaldo out of the squad. Hes the one who should decide how he wants to end his time with the national team. In my first call-up, I said, I need you, I need you to be close to me, playing or not playing, I need you. And now Im saying the same thing, said Jesus. Portuguese Football Federation President Pedro Proenca also said Ronaldo remained part of the teams plans, describing the episode as a misunderstanding that should be resolved internally. He is in the national team on sporting merit, and that must be unquestionable, Proenca told RTP. We have to pay tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo. In the days after Ronaldo announced his departure, speculation was rife that the 41-year-old may end his illustrious international career. Ronaldo had earlier said that he had briefly considered retiring after the 2026 World Cup. Yes, I thought about it, Ronaldo had told reporters. I always think about my decisions, about the future and also about the present. I am someone who thinks a lot. You have to think. That is why you see me here now. It means I will continue. I think I can give the national team my support, not only through goals but also outside football, he said. My goal is to be able to play, score goals and help the team win matches.

articleTitle: From TMC to BJP: Koel Mallick joins saffron party, eyes Rajya Sabha return
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Koel Mallick joins BJP, Koel Mallick BJP, Koel Mallick Rajya Sabha, Koel Mallick TMC, West Bengal Rajya Sabha bypoll, Koel Mallick BJP candidate, Rukmini Mallick, Koel Mallick political career, October 16 Rajya Sabha election, Bengal BJP, former TMC MP Koel Mallick, Indian Express, BJP news, Bengal news
description: Koel Mallick will submit her Rajya Sabha nomination later in the day in the presence of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari.
body_raw: Former Trinamool Congress MP and actor Koel Mullick formally joined the BJP Monday, a day after the ruling party named her as its nominee for the October 16 bypoll for Rajya Sabha in West Bengal. A popular face in the Bengali film industry, Mullick was elected as a TMC Rajya Sabha MP in April this year. However, she resigned from the Upper House in July after the Mamata Banerjee-led partys electoral setback in the West Bengal Assembly elections. She joined the ruling party in the presence of Sashi Agnihotri, state BJP general secretary. Mullick is scheduled to submit her nomination later in the day inthe presence of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Proud to be in such a party While speaking to reporters shortly after joining the BJP, shethanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari forgivingme this opportunity. In the last few months after BJP came to power in Bengal, there has been significant development in the state. It is inspiring. I am proud to be in such a party, Mullick said. People of Bengal want development and jobs. We have seen that after finishing their education, people leave Bengal for jobs outside because there is a dearth of jobs here. One should create more jobs here so these people can return, said Mullick. I am privileged. But many are not as privileged as I am. I will like to work for them. Since childhood, my family taught me to help people who are not as privileged as I am. During summer vacation, we used to go to the Missionaries of Charity. Even if I can contribute in a small way in helping people, I will be happy, she added. When asked about the TMC, Mullick said, Different parties work in their own ways. Each political party has its own way of working and trying to do good for people. I have never spoken against anyone, not during my film career or otherwise. BJP must also clarify the dilemma Koel is the fourth TMC Rajya Sabha MP to join the Bharatiya Janata Party after Sushmita Dev, Sukhendu Sekhar Ray, and Prakash Chik Baraik joined the BJP on July 9, 2026, after resigning from the TMC and the Upper House. They were also elected to the Rajya Sabha on BJP tickets. While West Bengal BJP leaders said they welcomed these leaders as untainted members to strengthen the party, the TMC labelled the moves as acts of betrayal. Our leaders Mamata Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee have already stated that our evaluation of some people was wrong. Our trust in some people was a mistake, Krishanu Mitra, TMC Mamata Banerjee spokesperson, said. The BJP must also clarify the dilemma within the party. First, they said no TMC men or women will be taken in the BJP. Then they said they picked good TMC leaders. They should evaluate who are their own party members and who are outsiders, Mitra added. Koel Mallick is the daughter of veteran Bengali film actor Ranjit Mallick and Deepa Mallick. She married film producer Nispal Singh in 2013. She has won several awards for her performances in movies, including a Filmfare Awards Bangla, two Bengali Film Journalists Association awards, and an Anandalok Puraskar. In 2023, the Bengal Government, under the TMC, honoured her with the Mahanayak Samman.

articleTitle: Employer can’t recover erroneous overpayment from retiree: Karnataka High Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka High Court salary recovery after retirement
description: The Karnataka High Court rules that an excess amount is recoverable only if it was paid on account of any misrepresentation or fraud by the employee.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court has held that an excess amount paid to an employee while in service cannot be recovered upon retirement if the payment resulted from the employers error. Justice M Nagaprasanna issued this ruling while directing Bangalore Electricity Supply Company Limited Bescom to refund a retired assistant lineman Rs 2,81,887. This amount had been recovered from his pension due to an erroneous increment granted 15 years ago. If the excess amount was not paid on account of any misrepresentation or fraud on the part of the employee, such excess payments of emoluments or allowances are not recoverable, the judge said in his order on September 25. The petitioner, Manjunath N, retired on April 30, 2025. His counsel, Devaraj N, argued that he did not receive the excess pay through fraud or misrepresentation but because of an alleged error by Bescom. Employer admits it cant recover the amount Bescom also admitted that money cannot be recovered from a retired employee unless fraud or misrepresentation on his part is involved. The court referred to a Supreme Court judgment in the case of Jogeswar Sahoo vs District Judge, Cuttack 2025. The judgment held that if the excess amount was not paid due to misrepresentation or fraud by the employee, or if the excess payment resulted from the employer applying a wrong principle for calculating payallowance or based on an interpretation of a ruleorder that was later found to be erroneous, such excess payments of emoluments or allowances are not recoverable. Holding that Manjunath was accused of neither fraud nor misrepresentation regarding the excess amount, the high court directed Bescom to refund it along with interest within eight weeks.

articleTitle: ‘Completely illegal knocking out of citizen’: Former top court judge Rohinton Nariman on Bengal SIR
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Justice Rohinton Nariman Election Commission
description: The former Supreme Court judge referred to the petition challenging the 2023 law on the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and said the sooner it is decided, the better
body_raw: Former Supreme Court judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman has called for the Supreme Courts intervention in issues related to Special Intensive Revision SIR, saying, We cannot have an Election Commission that malfunctions. The senior jurist referred to The Indian Express investigation about the Election Commission and said the right to vote, which is at the heart of our democracy, is in great peril. The Express investigation, dated September 23, showed that the question of who makes it to the voters list and who is left out was being raised within the Commission itself. The former Supreme Court judge, who has also served as Solicitor General of India, spoke at the Late CA MJ Rindani Centenary Memorial Oration at Rajkot last Sunday September 27 on the subject, Constitution and the Common Man. Referring to the SIR in West Bengal ahead of the Assembly polls earlier this year, Justice Nariman said, All of you have seen that in the West Bengal election, 90 lakh voters - its an astounding figure - were disenfranchised. Now 90 lakh voters getting disenfranchised didnt somehow move the Supreme Court enough to stay this, so that these 90 lakh voters were out when the Bengal election took place. Out of those who were disenfranchised, some 22 lakh voters actually filed appeals the others have all seemed to have accepted - they must be poor people, they must be people who dont have the wherewithal or the access to justice that the others had. And of these 22 lakh voters, some one lakh voter appeals were decided, 93 per cent in favour of the voter. So can you imagine, this was a completely illegal knocking out of the common man, of the citizen of India, in order that a government obtains what it wants, and the result, as you saw in West Bengal, was something that upset the government of the day and brought in the government of the state, he said. Saying that very, very disturbing things are happening in our country today, the jurist said, Equally disturbing is the fact that we discover now, thanks to The Indian Express, that the two gentlemen on either side of the Chief Election Commissioner voiced objections to whatever was going on 14 times, and somehow or the other they didnt press their right under the new Act, Section 18, to say that look, between the three of us, its the majority vote that counts. So the two of us prevail over you, Chief Election Commissioner. They didnt do that. They were also appointees of the present government. So what do we have today? And as of right, as of today itself, todays newspaper tells us that there is some patch-up between these three gentlemen, to the nations great detriment, where they have come out with some common statement saying, yes, some of the objections you people took seem to be correct, we revert to the old Form 6, and so on and so forth, Justice Nariman said. So the first issue I wish to flag today is that the common man today under our Constitution, and at, if I may say so, the heart of our Constitution, the heart of our democracy, which is the right to vote, is at great peril. And I hope that the apex court, an institution to which I once belonged, steps in immediately and rectifies these things. You cannot have an Election Commission which functions or malfunctions like this. Its something amazing, he said. On appointment of Chief Election Commissioner The senior jurist referred to the petition challenging the 2023 law on the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner. A two-judge bench recently gave a split verdict on the petition and said that it should be referred to a five-judge Constitution bench. And the sooner the Constitution Bench decides that you have to have somebody like a Prime Minister, Leader of Opposition, coupled with the Chief Justice or his nominee, who then picks up the best name in order to see that votes actually translate into what theyre supposed to translate into happens, the sooner that happens, the better, he said. The panel that appoints the Chief Election Commissioner now has the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and a Union Cabinet minister appointed by the Prime Minister. The main opposition Congress has opposed this, saying the current system gives undue advantage to the government. The Election Commission, Justice Nariman said, originally consisted only of the Chief Election Commissioner. He was to be appointed by the government of the day, subject to a law made by Parliament. This is very important. And later, laws added two more commissioners, so that we have three commissioners as of date. This Chief Election Commissioner had a fixed tenure of 5 years, could not be removed save by impeachment in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge, which meant that you required a two-thirds majority in both houses, present and voting, in order to get rid of him. So it becomes difficult to get rid of, but the difficulty is, if the appointment is in the hands of the government of the day, then this removal procedure doesnt add very much to independence or impartiality. This is the first conundrum that we face, he said. Second, the two commissioners who are with him are also appointed by the government of the day, and they can only be removed with his concurrence, with the Chief Election Commissioners concurrence, he said. Recently, we had in Anoop Baranwals case in 2023, the Supreme Court looking into the fact that so many years have passed since the Constitution came into force and Parliament making no law whatsoever under Article 324 for appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners. So the court suggested, why dont we take a leaf out of Section 4A of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, which appoints the Director of the CBI, and for that Director you require to have a collegium consisting of the Prime Minister of India, Leader of the Opposition, and the Chief Justice of India? So the court suggested that pro tem, until Parliament makes a law, we will have these three people who will select somebody who is independent and impartial. Now what does Parliament do? Its amazing. Parliament immediately enacts in 2023 itself, an Act for the appointment of all these people, and instead of these three functionaries, the Prime Minister has his own minister as number two, and then as Leader of the Opposition, so that again you are back to square one, he said. Now the unfortunate part is that all this came before the court very recently. Two learned judges differ, and the ultimate thing is now that its gone before a bench probably of five judges in order to find out whether this is good law, not good law. But meanwhile, these appointments continue only in the hands of the government of the day, the jurist said.

articleTitle: Why India’s clock towers still matter in the age of smartphones and smartwatches
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mumbai's Rajabai Clock Tower
description: Clock towers may have little relevance now but they are markers of a city, its people and history
body_raw: Flanked by automobile spare parts shops and art framers, a narrow lane leads up to Sabzi Mandi Ghanta Ghar, near Kamala Nagar, in Delhi. Time moves at a different pace as we inch up to the centre of what was once the wholesale vegetable market. Workers who spent languorous hours beneath the tower dont hear the hands of time ticking away. But this clock is keeping time. At 50 ft, with its repetitive jaali pattern on its four sides, there is a plaque that calls it the Ram Roop Tower, named after the industrialist of the 1940s, who has also built a temple and schools in the area. It used to be a landmark when my father sold fruits in the market and later opened RK Dry Fruits, this shop, in 1980, says Rakesh Kumar of the recently refurbished tower. It stands testimony to time, industry and education in the area. As have many such towers over centuries. Recently, the Allahabad High Court questioned the building of one such tower in Firozabad market in Uttar Pradesh, when it asked What is the point of building one when people can check the time on their phones and wristwatches? While philosophers have contended about the illusion of time, there have been many attempts to map its transience. Gurugram-based horologist Debasish Das, author of Clock Towers of India Sentinels of Time Niyogi, 2026, has been chronicling the journey of clock towers for over six years. What began as an essay on documenting sun dials in mosques in Delhi grew to become a book that has taken him to different parts of the country, including Kochi, Mumbai, Lucknow and of course, Delhi. What fascinates me is the constant effort to measure, regulate and publicly communicate something as intangible as time. A clock tower is not merely a machine it gives time a visible and audible presence in the life of a community, says Das, who is an engineer with Nokia. He recalls his visit to the clock tower in Delhis old and well-known institutes, Shri Vishwanath Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya. Everyone spoke only in Sanskrit on the campus. They allowed me go all the way to the top of the clock tower. Its got balconies and a marble canopy, and has to be manually wound every seven days, he says. In his book, he writes, the Indian clock tower was never a single architectural type. Some of them evolved from older gateways, temple structures or civic buildings, others were purpose-built monumental towers, while in princely states they often became expressions of royal patronage and modernity. Their locations were equally varied as well, from markets and railway stations to palace precincts, municipal squares, ports and major intersections. So, although we use the common expression ghanta ghar, the structures themselves represent very different histories and purposes, says Das. While he has documented nearly 150 clock towers across the country, many with the help of friends, he sees how royal and industrial patronage, family ties and the aspirational intent of a city shaped the existence of these towers. For instance, Jodhpurs ghanta ghar was built during the reign of Maharaja Sardar Singh, while Sangramsinhji High School Gothic clock tower in Gondal was modelled on the English public schools such as Eton and Harrow. Nestled in many of these towers are stories of their origin. Mumbais famous Rajabai Clock Tower brings together Western technology and a personal story. Das writes, Its Victorian Gothic architecture and European clock mechanism were commissioned with the wealth of Indian merchant Premchand Roychand, who named it after his mother, Rajabai. She followed Jain traditions and would eat only before sunset. Its chimes helped her keep time. Though this is an oft-repeated story, it also points to the citys philanthropic and cosmopolitan character. Das takes us further back in time to the origin of the word itself. He says, The expression ghanta ghar has its roots in the sophisticated water clocks or ghatika yantras. This was a device, a hemispherical bowl made of a thin sheet of copper, with a fine hole at the centre of its base. When the bowl was placed within a large basin of water, the bowl would slowly sink as water entered through the hole. It was then lifted, emptied and placed back on the water. The bowl sank once every 24 minutes. Since the Sanskrit word for a vessel or pot is ghata, the interval of 24 minutes measured by it came to be called a ghati. Over time, ghati evolved into the familiar ghari, which is now associated with a clock or a watch. What has been fascinating is that these towers have not worked on the same mechanism. From the water clocks to weight-driven mechanical clocks and later pendulum-regulated mechanisms, depending on the period and technology, they have moved with time itself. Replacing an original mechanical movement with a cheap quartz mechanism may make the clock functional but it can also turn a living timepiece into a mere facade. When the gears stop turning and the bells fall silent, the tower may still stand but its heartbeat is gone, says Das. Many of these towers have clip-clocked through centuries, sometimes without ever stopping. Like Mumbai-based architect Brinda Somaya found out when her firm, Somaya Sampat, with a team of conservation experts, worked on the Rajabai Clock Tower. The project demanded research, patience and respect for craftsmanship. Even during the restoration process at a height of 280 feet, the clock continued to function. It reinforced a fundamental principle of conservation understand the building first, intervene sensitively, and allow it to continue its life without losing its authenticity, says Brinda. Das affirms, Strictly speaking, we no longer need clock towers to tell the time. Our smartwatches have made the clock tower redundant. But we still need them to remind us where we have come from and to give our cities a sense of place and memory.

articleTitle: Thane gangrape: 7 farmhouses, 17 properties — Absconding constable’s assets under scanner
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ex MLA pawar and constable patil thane gangrape
description: Thane gangrape case: Police are now verifying addresses of 10 more farmhouses that are owned by constable Patil and his wife, bringing the total number of properties being examined to 17
body_raw: The Thane rural police, investigating the alleged gangrape of a 22-year-old woman, have found that absconding former police constable Shailesh Patil owns sevenfarmhouses in his and his wifes names. The farmhousewhere the alleged assault took place is also registered in Patils name. The police are now verifying the addresses of 10 morefarmhouses that, according to a close aide of Patil, are owned by him and his wife, bringing the total number of properties being examined to 17. Patil and former BJP MLA Narendra Pawar are both absconding in connection with the Thane gangrape case. An officer investigating the case said, We were informed by his close aide that there were 17 farmhouses in the couples names in the MMR region. We have found evidence linking him to seven. Given his background, it seems unlikely that he purchased thefarmhouseson his own, and we suspect somebody may be using his name as a front. The immediate priority is to trace Patil and Pawar in the Thane gangrape case. Patils mother alleges assault Soon after their names were mentioned in the FIR, Patils mother, Sulochana, held a press conference in which she alleged that her son had assaulted her as well and demanded the death penalty for him. She alleged that Patil was trying to protect an IPS officer. According to police sources, Patil was jailed and suspended after his arrest in 2013 for allegedly accepting a bribe on behalf of others. He was reinstated in 2019. Two days later, he applied for voluntary retirement and quit the force, an officer said. An FIR was registered against Pawar and Patil on September 17 based on the statement of a 22-year-old woman, who alleged that the two had gang-raped her at Patils farmhousein Padhga. Pawar and Patil have been absconding since the allegations surfaced. A few days later, CCTV cameras and the digital video recorder DVR at thefarmhousewere found missing. Thefarmhouseis located in a secluded area along National Highway 3 between Bhiwandi and Kalyan. Pawar has resigned from all party positions after the FIR was registered. In his resignation letter, he denied the allegations and called the FIR a conspiracy to defame him. He said he was resigning as the case could adversely affect the partys image.
