articleTitle: Jorge Jesus won’t bend, and Cristiano Ronaldo cannot be bent
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Perhaps both Ronaldo and Jesus could look into the mirror and see each other. (AP Photo)
description: Portugal's coach Jorge Jesus picks his team by his own system, even when it means leaving out the country's greatest footballer
body_raw: Some time next week, or next month, Cristiano Ronaldo will reveal his side of the story. Of his latest, dramatic falling out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus. The coach has offered glimpses of his version in a press conference that the countrys greatest footballer didnt suit the tactical demands of the game. Rumours and speculation have swirled like a juicy whodunit. Spanish journalist and Ronaldos close friend Edu Aguirre claims the footballer felt betrayed. There supposedly was a closed-door meeting between the Portuguese football federation, Ronaldo and the coach, in which Jesus apologised to Ronaldo and said he would offer a public apology. Instead, he emphatically defended his decision to not play him against Norway in a press conference, only moments later.   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Cristiano Ronaldo cristiano Numerous inside stories, half-truth and half-fiction, will spill out, dividing a country and the footballing universe. But the falling out was imminent, considering the collision of two headstrong, egoistic personalities the coach who considers himself a supreme force and a footballer who believes he is gods gift to the sport. Only no one expected the relationship to unravel so fast. There were hints, when you revisit Jesuss first press conference, where he said, I wouldnt stand up to anyone. The coachs methods and his unflinching devotion to his ideals made a clash likely. Jesus, 72 and with flowing silvering locks, might not be the most fabled tactician of his times. He was a modest footballer, a midfielder whose career had more stops than a shuttle train 13 clubs in 17 years, largely in the lower rungs of the Portuguese league. He was an uncelebrated manager, whose best years were spent with Benfica 2009 to 2015, with stops in Brazil, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, in a career that began when Ronaldo was five. But most players he has managed either love or loathe him. To some, including Pablo Aimar, Fabio Coentrao and David Luiz, he is the greatest coach they have played under. To others, he is an autocrat. On his first day at Benfica, he made the players train for four hours without a break, without letting them have a swig of water. He made them train twice a day, would shout and berate, but at the end of the day, former Portugal international Fernando Mendes said, we knew we had a great friend in him. To the players who rebelled, he would say Inside the club, only one person gives me the orders. The president. No one else. Those who revolted against his exhaustive regimen, he ruthlessly relegated to the bench. He was so secretive in his tactics that he revealed them to his assistants only on the morning of the game. The rigorous methods reaped rewards. Benfica won the league the first year he joined them. In the next six years, the club won two more, in what was their most successful era this century. His tactics shape-shifted, but were always thrilling and intense. He claims he doesnt follow prototypes. Some only copy what others do. I dont. God gave me the opportunity to be a creator, Jesus once told ESPN Brazil, after guiding Flamengo to five titles in a year. He has no dogmatic guiding philosophy and swears by no idol, even though he spends hours studying the patterns and principles of all accomplished coaches. But there are core principles, as seen in Portugals demolition of Denmark. They hounded the Danes with fluid aggression and heavy counter-pressing, and defended in a compact mid-block. He used three different formations in four games, but they were less tactical decisions than structural ones. Portugal played with a sense of identity that it had seldom shown before. It was evident why he ignored Ronaldo, and why he could again in the coming matches. He needs pace upfront, he wants his number nine to press aggressively, he demands heavy work off the ball. Ronaldo, at 41, is still a prolific scorer, but he failed to fulfil his off-the-ball shifts in the 67 minutes he played against Wales. Jesus has not shut the door in Ronaldos face. After beating Norway on Sunday he said There are no bad feelings with Cristiano. For the next call-up, if Cristiano is playing and wants to be with the national team, then why not? There are shades of the Ronaldo-Erik ten Hag skirmish, but with a more brazen edge. Perhaps both of them could look into the mirror and see each other. A coach who believes in ultimate supremacy, built on smouldering ego. Its his burnishing hubris that made Ronaldo, Jose Mourinho would say. Its the flaming ego that made Jesus too. It reflected in the words that explained Ronaldos benching I told him I would take him to the bench and that, if I needed him for 30 minutes, he would play. But I saw the game differently, so he didnt come on. It wont be Cristiano, or any other player, who changes my ideas as a coach. Never. Neither him nor anyone else. Not even a president. Never. Zero. Perhaps Ronaldos endgame was written the day the federation chose Jesus to succeed Roberto Martinez, who indulged Ronaldo with disastrous results.

articleTitle: OpenAI’s Sam Altman says AI benefits warrant accepting some risks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sam Altman said that OpenAI has signed a deal with the US government to deploy AI models in the Department of War's classified networks.
description: Altman said there remained a fundamental difference in worldview between OpenAI and rival Anthropic on AI ⁠regulation.
body_raw: OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman said the benefits of artificial intelligence justify accepting some risks and argued the technology should remain broadly accessible to the public We believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency, Altman said in an interview with Politicos technology-focused newsletter Decoded. Altman said there remained a fundamental difference in worldview between OpenAI and rival Anthropic on AI regulation, adding I think theres a lot of daylight. I disagree, but I understand the perspective of people who are like, This technology is going to get so powerful, and its so dangerous, that a single lab in San Francisco should have it and make sure nothing bad happens, and kind of figure out how to dole out the benefits, Altman said. He called that a completely unacceptable trade-off that runs counter to the lighter-touch regulatory stance backed by OpenAI. I wouldnt take a trade of saying, Well make sure theres no major hacks, theres no misuse of this technology, theres zero scams, theres zero all the other bad things that will happen, Altman said. Because I think people will do tremendously - orders of magnitude more - good stuff than bad stuff. Altmans remarks come amid a growing debate within the AI industry over the pace of development and the risks posed by increasingly capable systems. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei in September published an essay calling on the industry to slow down to pace the frontier, a stance that Altman publicly endorsed. Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned in September, saying the people building AI believe it could kill us all by the end of the decade. Reuters reported in September that Anthropic warned that, despite AIs potential benefits, the technology can sometimes act in ways that run counter to its makers intentions and penetrate other companies systems. The company said advanced models could exhibit self-preserving behaviors, including attempts to resist shutdown, conceal or manipulate information, or generate outputs that could be interpreted as coercive, deceptive, or manipulative. However, US President Donald Trump has largely dismissed calls for new restrictions, arguing they would make it harder for American companies to compete with Chinese rivals. He has repeatedly said existing law enforcement agencies, including the Justice Department, provide sufficient safeguards and that no new rules are needed.

articleTitle: Two books to read: A family shaped by Partition, a girl who disappeared
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Book covers of No One Gets Out Of Here Alive by Ranbir Sidhu and The Fourth Girl by Arefa Tehsin
description: Ranbir Sidhu's Partition memoir No One Gets Out Of Here Alive and Arefa Tehsin's feminist thriller The Fourth Girl both earn a hit this fortnight
body_raw: Welcome to Quick Verdict, a fortnightly column where every book gets a hit or miss. This week How Ranbir Sidhus No One Gets Out Of Here Alive uses his parents deaths to ask who they might have been without Partition, and how Arefa Tehsins The Fourth Girl turns a decades-old disappearance into a feminist mystery spanning India and Sri Lanka. Ranbir Sidhus No One Gets Out Of Here Alive Verdict HIT Ranbir Sidhus No One Gets Out Of Here Alive is a Partition memoir that discusses the death and grief that followed it. The book opens with the death of Sidhus father, and then goes back in time to nine months earlier, when his mother died. In their deaths, he looks back at their lives and tries to understand who they were beyond being his parents, and who they might have been had Partition not happened. Blending elements of essay, travelogue and history, Sidhu traces the geographical space of Punjab, where his parents were born and died, against its history of violence and its demand for a masculinity that deformed the lives of both women and men. In capturing beautifully the subtle nuances of the parent-child relationship, Sidhu makes the memoir an engrossing and poignant read for anyone interested in decoding the complexities of intergenerational relationships and everything that affects them. Reviewed by Anusree K C Arefa Tehsins The Fourth Girl Verdict HIT Arefa Tehsins The Fourth Girl is a feminist mystery thriller telling the story of three women with varied backgrounds Bhairavi, a Dalit who converted to Christianity Qailah, a Muslim and Rajvi, a Rajput. The fourth girl joins their yearly trip to the fictional Sumer forest unexpectedly, and then disappears. The incident changes the course of their lives. Twenty years later, the three meet at the funeral of a famous journalist in Sri Lanka, with another journalist digging up the death. Tehsin, who has published over 20 novels, grew up in Udaipur, the novels base setting. She now shuttles between India and Sri Lanka, introducing the other setting of the novel Colombo. The author doesnt shy away from depicting the ingrained patriarchy, the systemic colourism, casteism and classism of Indian society, but it is her writing that makes the third-person narrative feel like a first-person one. Every time you think you know something, a new question pops up in your head, and you cant help but turn the page. The Fourth Girl is definitely a relevant read in this day and age. Reviewed by Reva Thakkar

articleTitle: IIT Delhi scholar dies of injuries after suicide attempt, FIR filed
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The police were subsequently informed and Anand was rushed to the AIIMS Trauma Centre, where he remained under treatment. (File Photo)
description: Police said that prima facie, the scholar, identified as Manish Anand who lived in Kishangarh’s Munirka village, attempted to die by suicide.
body_raw: Delhi Police has registered a case of abetment to suicide after an IIT-Delhi PhD scholar, who was allegedly found in an injured and unconscious state inside his rented room in South East Delhi on August 18, died during treatment on Saturday, an officer said on Sunday. Police said that prima facie, the scholar, identified as Manish Anand who lived in Kishangarhs Munirka village, attempted to die by suicide. According to the police, the door of his room was locked from the inside. They said his neighbours had to break the door open. The police were subsequently informed and Anand was rushed to the AIIMS Trauma Centre, where he remained under treatment. Anand died on Saturday while undergoing treatment. An FIR was registered at Kishangarh police station under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS on Sunday, a police officer said. The FIR was registered based on directions from the Supreme Court-led National Task Force NTF, constituted in March last year to address mental health concerns and prevent suicides in higher educational institutions, police said. The task force was formed after students and family members of deceased students filed a petition in the Supreme Court seeking inquiries into incidents of suspicious deaths. The case has been registered on the basis of a complaint and the courts directions. An investigation is underway, the officer said. Police said that neither Anands family nor anyone else had, during the course of the initial inquiry, raised suspicion or levelled any allegation against anyone in connection with the incident. Police said they also examined CCTV footage from cameras installed outside the rented accommodation Anand lived in. The footage did not indicate the presence of any suspicious person entering or leaving the premises around the time of the incident, they said. The police are yet to ascertain how Anand sustained the injuries.

articleTitle: FSSAI declares ‘low-fat dairy whitener’ unsafe at top Delhi hotel — note the risks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Is your dairy whitener adulterated?
description: A dairy whitener is not milk. It is a processed food designed to look and feel like milk, and the real health question is what it adds to the diet when it is used several times a day
body_raw: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India recently issued a non-compliance notice and banned the sale of Nestles Low Fat Dairy Whitener after a sample taken from a Delhi hotel was declared unsafe and substandard. Taking to X, the regulatory body shared A sample of Nestle Low Fat Dairy Whitener collected from Ms Bharat Hotels Ltd. The Lalit, New Delhi, has been declared unsafe and substandard by Food Analyst reports under the FSS Act, 2006. A sample of Nestl Low Fat Dairy Whitener collected from Ms Bharat Hotels Ltd. The Lalit, New Delhi, has been declared UNSAFE amp SUBSTANDARD by Food Analyst reports under the FSS Act 2006. Directives have been issued to immediately prohibit the sale of product FSSAINotice  - FSSAI fssaiindia October 3, 2026 What exactly makes it risky? We reached out to Kanikka Malhotra, clinical nutritionist and diabetes educator, who shares that whatever the adjudication decides, this story should make us look at the cup, not just the lab report. A dairy whitener is not milk. It is a processed food designed to look and feel like milk, and the real health question is what it adds to the diet when it is used several times a day, she tells indianexpress.com, adding that phosphorus is the key point to understand. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. It is a nutrient our bodies need, and it occurs naturally in milk, pulses and nuts. But the phosphorus in food and the phosphorus in additives behave differently in the body, she says, further stressing that naturally occurring phosphorus is bound in protein and phytate, so we absorb only about half of it. Phosphate additives, used as stabilisers and emulsifiers, are absorbed almost completely. Therefore, a cup of tea with a whitener sachet is a small dose, but three or four cups a day, every day, are not. Who is at risk? Malhotra says this matters most for people whose kidneys are already under strain. Diabetes is a leading cause of chronic kidney disease in India, and when kidney function falls, the body struggles to clear surplus phosphate. High phosphate levels are linked to vascular calcification and heart risk in people with kidney disease, she elaborated. In the general population, the evidence for harm from phosphate additives is largely observational, so Malhotra says she would not overstate it. But for diabetic and kidney-risk clients, it is reason enough to be cautious, she adds in warning. As for the brand in focus, Malhotra adds Nestle has said that its product is compliant and that the labs reading reflects total phosphorus, which includes the natural contribution of milk. That is a technical question for the regulator and the company to settle, and consumers should wait for the outcome. How can you make sure your dairy whitener is safe? Malhotra shares some practical advice to tackle this problem Use fresh milk or plain curd-based options whenever you can. Read the ingredient list for phosphate or INS numbers such as 338 to 343 and 450 to 452. If you have diabetes, kidney disease or high blood pressure, ask your doctor how much additive phosphate is appropriate for you. Good health is rarely lost in one dramatic exposure. It is shaped by small things repeated every day, and the humble cup of tea is one of them, she concludes. articleTitle: Sanjay Dutt says his ‘can’t feel peace in India’ remark a ‘scripted conversation’, Shekhar Suman comments
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sanjay Dutt offers a clarification for his India remarks on Shekhar Tonite.
description: Sanjay Dutt offered an explanation for his remarks on Shekhar Tonite, where he confessed that he "doesn't feel peace in India anymore". The actor claimed it was part of a scripted conversation in the form of a satire.
body_raw: Actor Sanjay Dutt ended up inviting the ire of the internet and certain sections of society after his remarks this past weekend on Shekhar Sumans satire show Shekhar Tonite on YouTube. The actor, after confessing he doesnt feel peace in India anymore, went on to deliver a monologue commenting on Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump in his signature style of iconic character Munna Bhai from Rajkumar Hiranis seminal social comedy franchise. However, Dutt has now offered an explanation. Dutt lives with his family, wife Maanyata Dutt and two children, in Dubai. Sanjay Dutt offers clarification on India remark I want to clarify that it has never been my intention to hurt the feelings of any individual, community, or institution, to insult them, or to disrespect them, wrote Dutt on his X handle on Sunday. He claimed he made those remarks in context of a scripted conversation intended to engage in lighthearted and humorous dialogue. He further explained that his tone was akin to the humour and satire used in the Munna Bhai franchise, particularly the second part, Lage Raho Munna Bhai 2006, which used Gandhigiri, a modern take on Mahatma Gandhi to comment on the current state of society. He claimed that the intention was to convey a message of love, unity, and goodwill. He reiterated that unfortunately, his words were interpreted out of that context. He wrote on X, I would like to clarify that it was never my intention to hurt, offend, or disrespect the sentiments of any individual, community, or institution. My remarks were made in the context of a scripted conversation intended to be light-hearted and humorous. The spirit behind them was similar to the humour and satire seen in films like Munna Bhai, particularly the concept of Gandhigiri, which was intended to convey a message of love, warmth, togetherness, and goodwill. Unfortunately, my words were interpreted outside of that intended context Shekhar Suman defends Sanjay Dutt Hours after Sanjay Dutts clarification, the shows host Shekhar Suman also came out in his defence. Sanjay Dutt has huge respect for our country and fellow countrymen, and what he said was completely innocuous and in a very positive way. He should not be penalised and maligned for what he never said or meant. I know him for years he is a good man who loves his country and has utmost regard for it, Shekhar told NDTV in an interview. What did Sanjay Dutt say on Shekhar Tonite? Before he was asked to deliver a monologue as Indias Prime Minister in the final segment of Shekhar Tonite, Dutt confessed he doesnt feel peace in the country anymore. The people of this country are so lovely. There should be peace here. I cant feel that peace in our country anymore. We Indians are large-hearted people and we are hospitable. We have given so much, and we should always remain that way. I pray to Shiva ji that those days come back soon, he said. Later, he delivered a monologue as Indias PM in the Munna Bhai style. During that performance, he underlined the criticism towards PM Modi that he takes too many foreign trips instead of spending more time with his countrymen. Aap log ekdum tension nahi lene ka. Apun is khushi ko celebrate karne videsh nahi jaane wala hai. Apun idharich rahega, aap sab logon ke beech. Nahi to PM aur janta mein connection kaise banega You people dont have to worry at all. I am not going abroad to celebrate this happiness. I will stay right here, among all of you. Otherwise, how will there be a connection between the PM and the people?, he said. He also indirectly claimed that PM Modi focuses too much on optics and getting his pictures clicked everywhere. Apun ko desh ke liye bahut kuch karne ka mauka mila hai PM banke, toh apun ek aur kaam karega. Jahaan jahaan uska photo laga hai na, apun usko ekdum kam kar dega. Desh ko desh ka photo dikhna chahiye. I have got the opportunity to do a lot for the country as a PM, so I will do one more thing. Wherever the PMs photograph has been put up, I will cut that down. The country should see a picture of the country, added Dutt. He also proposed replacing PM Modis pictures with those of Gandhi, since the Father of Indias non-violent philosophy is what every contemporary leader should be subscribing to in order to make the world a better place. He didnt spare Trump either, referring to him as mamu and offered him a jadoo ki jhappi. Dekho Trump mamu, zyada tante nahi paalne ka. Duniya mein missile waise hi bahut ho gaya hai. Ab thoda pyaar bhi export karne ka. Kahin missile bhejne ka mann kare to pehle guldasta bhejne ka. Kisi ko dhamki dene ka mann kare na to use phone karke ghar bulane ka aur chai peete-peete baat suljhane ka. Trump, dont create so much trouble. There are already enough missiles in the world. Now export a little love too. If you feel like sending a missile somewhere, send a bouquet first. If you feel like threatening someone, call them home and resolve the matter over a cup of tea, said the actor. Lage Raho Munna Bhai revolved around Dutts gangster character who reads up excessively on Gandhi, in order to impress his love interest and radio jockey Vidya Balan, that he ends up hallucinating Gandhi everywhere. That leads to him treading on the non-violence path of Gandhi, offering bouquets instead of threats to his friend-turned-nemesis Lucky Boman Irani. Its the sequel to Hiranis 2003 gangster comedy Munna Bhai MBBS, and also stars Arshad Warsi, Dia Mirza, Saurabh Shukla, Kulbhushan Kharbanda, and Jimmy Shergill among others.

articleTitle: Janhvi Kapoor calls her Chuttamalle AI video with NTR ‘assault’: ‘Reality of being a woman’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Janhvi Kapoor opens up on AI edits of her Devara song "Chuttamalle".
description: Jr NTR and Janhvi Kapoor were featured in deepfake video of the Chuttamalle song. The actress has finally reacted to the ongoing controversy.
body_raw: Actor Janhvi Kapoor has called out the misuse of AI to objectify women as an AI-generated inappropriate video featuring her with Devara co-star Jr NTR from the track Chuttamalle emerged on social media. She compared the explicit video to assault as many leading voices from the South film industries supported her. The morphed clip showed Janhvi in a sexually explicit scene, that was never a part of the original song. After the video went viral on the internet, NTR criticised such distasteful videos, threatening legal action against them. Chiranjeevi, Khushbu Sundar, Vijay Deverakonda, and others also extended their support to Janhvi. Taking to her Instagram handle, Janhvi Kapoor slammed the criminal misuse of technology. The criminal misuse of technology to objectify women and circulate fictionalised content without consent is deeply violating, bordering on sexual assault. Almost every woman in my industry has faced some version of this, and women everywhere are increasingly being subjected to it, she started her long note. ALSO READ  Janhvi Kapoor lauds Telugu film industrys work hours Nap for 20 minutes The actor continued, Consent, choice and respect for a womans body should be among the most basic notions of humanity. Yet somehow, they continue to be treated as complicated. They are not. It is surprising that it still seems too nuanced for some people to understand that even if a woman says yes five days in a row and no on the sixth, that no must be respected. If she happens to wear a miniskirt, it does not give anyone permission to put a camera up her skirt, capture violating angles or visually exploit her body. What a woman is comfortable with, where she draws the line and what she chooses to do with her body are decisions that belong exclusively to her. This is basic. Janhvi mentioned that the issue goes beyond what she has ever experienced in her entire career. It is about the larger reality of being a woman, the gaze, the judgement, the constant negotiation for safety, and the feeling that our boundaries somehow remain open to interpretation. That threat has now expanded into the digital sphere, when we have not even adequately addressed the very real, physical fear that continues to disrupt the lives of women every day. She highlighted that facing such things is a reality of being a woman. To conclude her note, she thanked her co-star NTR, and other actors for their support, including, Chiranjeevi, Vijay Deverakonda and Khushbu Sundar. I am deeply touched by NTR sir for taking such a strong stand and condemning this violation. Thank you, sir. When someone whom millions look up to speaks up about something that may not directly concern him, it makes a difference to every woman who has experienced some degree of this behaviour. Thank you also to Chiranjeevi sir, Vijay and Khushbu maam for amplifying that sentiment and calling for action against this mentality and these immoral practices. Janhvi Kapoor and Jr NTRs film Devara Part 1 released in September 2024. The concerned song Chuttamalle, was composed by Anirudh Ravichander and sung by Shilpa Rao, turning out to be one of the most famous tracks from the film.

articleTitle: ‘I want to feel safe’:  Young women attempt to march towards Jantar Mantar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: jantar mantar protest, gyanesh kumar
description: Meanwhile, many independent journalists and other protesters, who had sat outside the Parliament Street police station till Saturday night demanding accountability, returned on Sunday morning to demand the registration of an FIR into the allegations raised by the three women journalists.
body_raw: As the march from Andhra Bhavan Canteen towards Jantar Mantar reached Ashoka Road on Sunday, Adira 26 stood on the side of the road in silence, clutching her friends hand as she watched the crowd. The final-year law student, originally from Kerala and studying at Delhi University, had initially not planned to join the protest, which has been underway since October 2 demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar. However, Sundays march was not focused solely on alleged irregularities in the Election Commission of India. It also voiced concerns over womens safety, coming a day after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of alleged sexual harassment while covering the stir near Jantar Mantar. Womens safety in the Capital has dominated conversations since the alleged gangrape of a minor girl by three men posing as police officers at a park in Delhi last month. Against this backdrop of rising crimes against women in the Capital, Adira said she felt compelled to join the march. I want to feel safe, she said. I came to Delhi in 2023, and when I was staying in a hostel, there were several restrictions. I wasnt allowed to wear sleeveless tops in our own premises, she said. Her parents were hesitant to send her to the Capital and have grown more worried since the news of the gangrape of the minor at a park in September. They called and told me to discontinue the course and come back, but how can I?, she said. Standing beside Adira was her friend Ayushi 20, also a DU student, from Champawat, Uttarakhand. For Ayushi, the fight has been long and is often unfair. Even in 2026, we have to fight for our basic rights. Crime happens against women but eventually they are the only one that suffers., she said, recalling how classes at DUs Lady Shri Ram College had moved online after the alleged gangrape last month. Already we have very little freedom, dont go here, dont wear such clothes. Even after any crime happens, were the ones that get blamed, she said. Another protester, Saniya Ali 18, said she had lied to her parents, who are based in Bihar, to join the protest in the Capital, telling them she was going to Delhi only for exploring. Today Im here because I think I need to. I stayed here because I have many questions to ask Prime Minister Narendra Modi. I want to ask him, what all is not happening here. Votes are being stolen, women are being raped, what is our country doing? Yesterday I was detained, were here to ask for justice. They are scared that were again seeking resignation. I lied because my parents will be scared if I go out and something happens, but I do not blame them completely, she said. Meanwhile, many independent journalists and other protesters, who had sat outside the Parliament Street police station till Saturday night demanding accountability, returned on Sunday morning to demand the registration of an FIR into the allegations raised by the three women journalists. The Crime Branch has now been tasked with investigating the matter, officers said on Saturday. Rishabh Ranjan, who works with the All India Congress Committee AICC law department and represents one of the women journalists who raised the allegation against the officers, said the police still had not registered an FIR, even though she was taken to RML hospital last night for a Medico-Legal Case MLC. We had gone inside with an expectation that a senior police officer at least of a rank of DCP would speak to us and share what was the reason that they transferred the case to the Crime Branch. We dont know whether they have named the person in the complaint registered or not. We wanted them to register a zero FIR, he said.

articleTitle: Gujarat Hardlook: How do you remake Gandhi’s ashram for Rs 1,200 crore — and keep it simple?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A good part of that pathway is already complete. It is lined with baobabs from Madagascar, black neem from Thailand and exotic flora such as Mayan spinach from Mexico and bird-of-paradise.
description: Visitors can walk through the house where Gandhi and his wife Kasturba once lived — a house that, every year without fail, marks Gandhi Jayanti with an all-faith prayer meeting open to the public.
body_raw: Under the Gandhi Ashram Redevelopment Project, most of the original ashrams buildings have been restored. The project is now deciding how these buildings will tell the Mahatmas story through museums, activities and experiences for visitors within the 55-acre space, write Parimal A Dabhi and Leena Misra. IMAGINE A granite-paved pathway lit by Victorian-style lampposts, with ornate wooden benches along the way, taking visitors on a journey through the life of a barrister who became a Mahatma while fighting to free India from British rule. A good part of that pathway is already complete. It is lined with baobabs from Madagascar, black neem from Thailand and exotic flora such as Mayan spinach from Mexico and bird-of-paradise. The walk through a series of repurposed buildings is designed to culminate in an arboretum called Mohan-to-Mahatma - the plants are colour-coded to mark each phase of Gandhis life. That, though, is all in the extended part of the project. At its heart is a five-acre space that feels frozen in time. The Five Acres Frozen in Time Here, visitors can walk through the house where Gandhi and his wife Kasturba once lived - a house that, every year without fail, marks Gandhi Jayanti with an all-faith prayer meeting open to the public. This year, on October 2, Vijaybhai Joshi arrived at the ceremony dressed in khadi, with a cotton hank around his neck and a walking stick slung over his shoulder. After the prayer meeting at Hriday Kunj - marking Gandhis 157th birth anniversary - he climbed onto the back of a scooter to head home. This country has not seen anyone like Gandhiji. Weve been shaped by his ideology, and because we followed it, here I am before you at 104 years, Joshi says, chuckling. Hard of hearing, Joshi pulls a small contraption from his bag - a funnel attached to a transparent pipe. To speak with him, one must talk into the funnel he listens through the other end, pressed to his ear. Born in Bihar in 1922, Joshi worked for a British firm and was posted in Pakistan. During the partition in 1947, his employer asked if he wanted to stay on. No, he told them, and asked instead to be transferred to his home state of Gujarat. He has lived in Ahmedabad since, where his family sings Gandhis favourite bhajan, Vaishnava Jana To, every evening. Driving the scooter was 84-year-old Jesingbhai Parmar, a former Reserve Bank of India employee who reaches the ashram every Friday - because that is the day Gandhiji died, he says. On his visits, he spins 250 metres of yarn on the charkha at Hriday Kunj for over three hours. This October 2, he sat in the front row of the prayer meeting, spinning alongside children from the ashrams school, which has since relocated outside the complex. One Ashram, Six Trusts Hriday Kunj - the house Gandhi built in 1917 on land he bought along the Sabarmati River a year earlier - was just one structure among several that made up the 120-acre ashram until 1930. Todays redevelopment covers the 55-acre ashram itself, within a wider precinct of roughly 322 acres. After Gandhis death in 1948, the land was divided among six trusts tasked with carrying forward Gandhian thoughts and practices the Harijan Ashram Trust 1939, Gujarat Khadi Gramodyog Mandal 1940, Sabarmati Ashram Preservation and Memorial Trust or SAPMT 1950, Gujarat Harijan Sevak Sangh 1952, Sabarmati Ashram Gaushala Trust 1952 and Khadi Gramodyog Prayog Samiti 1958. The Core Hriday Kunj sits within the five acres known simply as Sabarmati Ashram. On an average day, this stretch alone draws 4,000 visitors, says Kartikeya Sarabhai, chairman of SAPMT - whose first chairman, in 1949, was Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Several luminaries succeeded him, such as Ganesh Mavlankar, the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and Kartikeyas late father Dr Vikram Sarabhai known as the father of Indias space mission, to name a few. SAPMT manages this core area, which includes Gandhis and Kasturbas residence, Vinoba Bhave and Mira Kutir, Nandini Guest House, Magan Nivas, and Sanghralaya - a museum designed by late architect Charles Correa that houses the ashrams exhibition and library. A Vision, Delivered Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Rs 1,200-crore redevelopment project in 2024. It envisions the ashram as one contiguous space across 55 acres its buildings restored to how they stood when Gandhi was alive. The project is being executed by the Union Ministry of Culture and the Gujarat government through the Mahatma Gandhi Sabarmati Ashram Memorial Trust MGSAMT, headed by Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel. Retired Gujarat IAS officer I P Gautam is leading the projects execution as Chairman of the Executive Council. Another retired IAS officer, I K Patel, is also playing a key role in the project as officer on special duty and member secretary of the Governing Council. It was the Prime Ministers wish that we restore the ashram to how Gandhi left it in 1930, with modern facilities, says a source associated with the project. A public road that once split the land in two has now been closed and a large brick-and-concrete gateway has come up to serve as the new main entrance. Beyond the SAPMT-managed core lies the part of the ashram now under restoration - buildings that once housed schools, hostels, teachers quarters, and units producing cloth, paper, leather and dairy products. This stretch, the source says, will take visitors through Gandhis life, from the Champaran Satyagraha, where he became Mahatma, through the freedom movement, and till the British left India. Restoring 28 Buildings, Developing 24 Museums Inside what used to be the ashrams gaushala cowshed, an artisan, Hirenbhai, dips bunches of coir fibre into a paste of Fullers earth, popularly called Multani mitti, and smooths it over a plinth. We will finish it with lippan, he says, referring to traditional mud plaster. A marble plaque at the entrance notes that the structure was built in 1938 for Rs 7,200, funded by a donation from the Ahmedabad American Cotton Exchange Association Ltd, a private company founded in 1932. It is among the first of 28 buildings to be fully restored. In one room, thatched roofs for a set of representational cowsheds - part of an upcoming museum - are in place. It is the only one of 24 planned museums being developed by the National Dairy Development Board NDDB. The rest have been contracted to Paris-based Museum Studio, which is working in consortium with Ecofirst Private Ltd, a subsidiary of Tata Consulting Engineers. Ahmedabad-based urban planner Bimal Patels firm HCP Design Planning  Management Pvt Ltd created the master plan for the project and executed the civil works using traditional methods. Sources say no cement concrete was used in any of the restorations. Of the 28 restored buildings, 24 will house museums. Activities once central to ashram life - papermaking and spinning among them - have been assigned to buildings within the wider precinct. It was Gandhijis idea that these activities should not just survive but also prosper. We will produce more khadi and more paper, so visitors to the ashram can buy them, says a source involved in the project. At the entrance, an interpretation centre will lay out what each space in the new ashram offers, helping visitors plan their visit around the time they have. Keeping the Tranquility SAPMT prepared a concept note meant to guide the MGSAMTs work closely. Kartikeya Sarabhai recalls that Modi, as Gujarats Chief Minister then, had a clear vision for the revamped ashram even back in 2009, when the Trust first approached him. The PM, from the beginning, felt that whatever changes we make should be done in the context of the overall ashram, not as individual ones. He had that vision even then - it got articulated later, Sarabhai says. When Modi became Prime Minister and approached the ashrams trustees about redeveloping the full complex, Our only request was that the ashrams core values - tranquility among them - stay at its heart, Sarabhai says, adding that the government held to that promise. He notes that Hriday Kunj, the Gandhis home from 1917 to 1930, originally stood amid an open maidan. We will keep it in the maidan, he says. The concept note, Sarabhai explains, outlines the need to communicate what the ashram stood for in Gandhis time. It was a site for experiments in truth, non-violence, dignity of labour, respect for all religions and the removal of untouchability. It was to be one of modern Indias most audacious experiments. The uniqueness of this experiment makes this site of immense significance to India and to the world, he says. The new trust has left SAPMTs management of the core area undisturbed. SAPMT has engaged Ahmedabad-based conservation architect Dr Rabindra Vasavda to restore its portion of the buildings. Making Room The Ashramvasis According to sources, 307 claims were made by ashramvasis - long-time residents occupying 256 buildings- who had to vacate the premises. The MGSAMT offered three options compensation by cheque, flats purchased by the trust, or homes in cooperative housing financed by the trust. The trust has spent Rs 190 crore on rehabilitation so far. Of those relocated, 223 families - the largest group - opted for compensation, with payouts of up to Rs 90 lakh per family. We have treated them with respect. They were not encroachers, said a source. Only Krunal Rathod and his family, who occupy a cottage, are yet to evacuate. Their case is under litigation in the Small Causes Court. The Rathods fight concerns three properties which they claim were handed over to their predecessor by the trustee of the relevant Ashram trust around 1930. The PMs Stamp Several personal interventions by Modi shaped the redevelopments final look The pathways colour was changed from red to grey cobblestone Victorian-style wrought-iron lamp posts will be installed throughout red stone benches were replaced with ornate wooden ones. What Visitors Can Expect Original artefacts from SAPMTs collection - a sari Gandhi wove for Kasturba, his cycle, his charkha - may be part of the exhibits, with security details still being worked out parking for 250 cars and 25 buses to serve the higher number of visitors. At present, the Sabarmati Ashram sees nearly 4,000 visitors daily. A food court near the entry gate that will serve sattvik cuisine. A souvenir shop featuring Gandhis three monkeys, carved from wood sourced from the original ashram. A walkthrough rainforest of medicinal plants and trees. The ashrams original trees - peepal, jamun, asopalav, piludi, neem, gundo, mango, moringa - still stand in many places. Retired Deputy Conservator of Forest Jayant Solanki is overseeing this effort, assigned to the Heartfulness Institute, a spiritual organisation. Ticketing still undecided - though Kartikeya Sarabhai suggests non-priced tickets to regulate visitor flow. Residential facilities for visiting Gandhian scholars, an idea still under consideration. An artificial lake connected to stormwater drains to harvest rainwater. The lake was naturally tested in July when the city saw excessive rain, and water drained into it, filling it. The Ashram is my best and only creation. And the world will judge me by its results, reads a quote by the Father of the Nation at the entrance of the MGSAMT office, as if summarising the projects objective. By the time the pathway reaches its end, visitors will have walked through more than a restored ashram - they will have retraced, tree by tree and room by room, the journey of a barrister who became one of historys most enduring symbols of non-violent resistance. Iconic Buildings Being Restored Anand Bhavan Constructed around 1920 as the ashrams needs grew. Gandhis secretary and confidant, Mahadev Desai, lived here for a time. Imam Manzil Built in 1919 for Imam Saheb Abdul Kader Bawazeer, a close companion of Gandhis in both South Africa and India. He gave up his business to join the Satyagraha movement and stayed with Gandhi until he died in 1931. Bal Mandir Inaugurated in 1940 by Madame Montessori, this building trained the children of Dalit craftsmen and workers in the crafts practised in their own homes. Junu Rasodu Built in 1918 as a kitchen and dining hall with a storeroom cellar. Meals followed a strict ritual a bell rang thrice, the kitchen doors closed after the second ring, and prayers began at the third, according to an account by the late Narayan Desai, Mahadev Desais son. Somnath Chhatralaya Built in 1922 to house the growing number of ashram residents, this 100-room facility later served as a hostel for female PTC students after 1955. Jamna Kutir Built in 1924 by industrialist Jamnalal Bajaj as a residence for his family during visits to the Satyagraha Ashram, which Gandhi later renamed Harijan Ashram. It later housed two ashram workers. Restoration of this building is pending due to litigation.

articleTitle: CBSE ‘hack’, IIT gig and US recognition: Nisarga Adhikary’s incredible year at 19
articleFeaturedImageAlt: nisarga
description: The cybersecurity researcher, who is now working at IIT Kanpur, was recognised by the US Department of Justice for reporting a vulnerability in one of its systems
body_raw: Tuesday, September 22. It was almost an hour past midnight. Nisarga Adhikary was sitting in the Starbucks caf at IIT Kanpur. An email notification flashed across his screen. It was a message from the US Department of Justice, acknowledging his work in finding and reporting a security flaw within their systems. I was having my second cup of coffee when I received the email, he recalls. Nisarga Adhikary is only 19 years old. On paper, this recognition stood as one of the most prestigious accolades he could have ever imagined. Yet, surprisingly, he remained unfazed, showing no trace of excitement. I love to break stuff, Nisarga says. Hacking things is a part of me trying to understand how things work. The security flaw was not something he had been assigned to find. There was no college project or professional brief behind it. He was simply trying to understand how the system worked. Still, the recognition was the latest turn in a remarkable five months for this 19-year-old. In February, he first drew public attention for identifying alleged security flaws in the Central Board of Secondary Educations digital examination system and has since landed a job at IIT Kanpurs cybersecurity hub. Nisarga is from Siliguri, West Bengal. His parents, both senior government officers, wanted him to take the Joint Entrance Examination JEE and he was preparing through a FIITJEE South Delhi programme. Then, his work began attracting attention. His parents were worried, Nisarga says, before they gradually became more accepting of it. The CBSE controversy Earlier this year, Nisarga began examining publicly accessible parts of CBSEs On-Screen Marking OSM system, the digital platform used to evaluate scanned answer sheets. He claims he found several weaknesses in the system. One, its One-Time Password OTP checks could be bypassed, allowing an unauthorised user to access examiner accounts without receiving an actual code. Two, poorly configured storage on Amazon Web Services AWS allegedly gave him access to about 1.8 million scanned answer sheets. Nisarga also demonstrated the account-takeover risk by accessing the account of a physics teacher on the live CBSE system. Asked about the ethics of accessing a real persons account, he says hed blurred the teachers details and used the access only to demonstrate the vulnerability. He reported his findings to the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team CERT-In, the government agency that coordinates responses to cybersecurity incidents, in February. By May, he had published a detailed account of what he had found. He had also come on television to describe and explain his findings. His revelations quickly attracted attention as students, teachers, and parents were already raising concerns about glitches, evaluation inconsistencies, and operational problems linked to the OSM rollout. The board initially denied that its OSM portal had been compromised, but later acknowledged that cybersecurity issues had been flagged in the public domain. Subsequently, on May 31, CBSE stated that it had been closely monitoring the vulnerabilities in the OnMark portal and that a team of cybersecurity professionals drawn from various arms of the government as well as the IITs had been deployed over the last few days to fortify the system. Nisargas findings soon became part of a wider political debate. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi was among those who publicly praised him for raising questions about the CBSE system. Nisarga also participated in protests organised by the Cockroach Janta Party CJP over the NEET-UG paper leak and posted a photograph with CJP convenor Abhijeet Dipke. He says he was invited to meet Rahul Gandhi alongside Sarthak Sidhant, who had separately flagged alleged irregularities in CBSEs tendering process, but chose not to go. Sarthak, an 18-year-old student from Jharkhand, had known Nisarga before they became publicly associated with the CBSE controversy. He says they met around three years ago on Reddit and credits Nisarga with supporting him during CBSE times. Kshitij Kapoor, a software engineer at AI research lab Nous Research, says he has known Nisarga since he was 14. He met him through Capture The Flag CTF, competitive cybersecurity exercises where players find hidden text strings called flags inside vulnerable systems or programmes. Hes always had a knack for poking holes in systems. The curiosity hasnt changed much but the scale definitely has, Kshitij says. I was happy to see him get recognition. Having known him since so early on, it felt very personal to me in a way. The teen behind the screen Nisarga describes himself as a nerd all his life. He says he spends almost all his waking hours glued to a screen, claiming that he has no non-technical friends. Outside cybersecurity, he reads young-adult fiction, like The Fault in Our Stars. He is also a big fan of Japanese animation such as Tokyo Ghoul. He reads books about activism and says he is interested in activism for the rights of neurodivergent people, queer rights and internet freedom. His views on technology and society are shaped, he says, by what he calls neoliberal technocratic biases. He describes himself as socially very left and economically right. He looks up to the likes of Sam Altman and Mark Zuckerberg, the heads of the artificial intelligence company OpenAI and technology company Meta, respectively, for their drive to build things. From exam-system sleuth to IIT Kanpur Around the same time, Nisargas views on technology and government brought him to the attention of IIT Kanpur Director Manindra Agrawal. When the Centre moved to restrict Telegram before the NEET-UG re-exam, Nisarga criticised the decision, arguing that authorities had failed to prevent paper leaks while trying to restrict a messaging platform that could still be accessed through proxies. IIT Kanpur director Manindra Agrawal responded to his comments, saying he would need to sit Nisarga down and explain. He had already reached out to the teenager earlier, and the interaction eventually led to Nisarga joining C3iHub, IIT Kanpurs cybersecurity-focused technology innovation hub, as an Open-Source Intelligence OSINT and Threat Intelligence Engineer. His job involves identifying and understanding potential security threats. Nisarga, however, remains sceptical of an educational system that measures people through examinations and credentials alone. You can have a PhD and still produce low quality research and do worse than your peers with no degree. It depends on talent and curiosity, he says. For now, he is settling into life at IIT Kanpur. He says the transition has not been difficult, although he describes Kanpur as a bit bad compared with places he has lived before. Eventually, he wants to work across technology, defence and artificial intelligence and may eventually return to formal education, possibly in the US or another country. For someone whose curiosity began with figuring out how computer systems work, the question now is what he will choose to explore next. But when that email from the US Department of Justice arrived, Nisarga did not see it as a defining moment for him. I was unamused. It was like any other normal Hall of Fame mention for me, he says. I think I work a lot and put all my time into research because thats the only coping mechanism I have. Why is he unmoved by this latest recognition? Alex Karp, CEO of Palantir once said that one cannot have a great social life at age 20 and achieve extraordinary career success at the same time, he says. It might sound toxic but hes kind of right, I feel.

articleTitle: Team depth to individual gaps: India’s Asian Games report card for 2028 Olympics
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Indian contingent during the Asian Games closing ceremony in Nagoya, Japan, Sunday. (AP Photo)
description: Talent spotting, investment under lens; officials say performance ‘encouraging’: India finished fourth at the Asian Games with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals, 85 in all. It fell short of the 100-medal target and finished 21 medals behind its record haul in Hangzhou.
body_raw: Between the 2022 Asian Games in Chinas Hangzhou and the latest edition that wound up Sunday in Japans Nagoya, the Government spent Rs 97.84 crore under the Target Olympic Podium Scheme TOPS. Only two per cent of it, approximately, translated to gold medals this time.  Teenager Kumkum Mohod won arguably Indias biggest individual gold despite not being in the flagship scheme Suruchi Singh, the shooter, was added only recently, while her mixed team partner, Kamaljeet Singh, isnt on the list Neeru Dhanda, who won a trap gold in shooting, remains outside the TOPS core group, too.  Thirteen of Indias 21 golds came in team events, some of which arent in the Olympics, while 19 of its 27 silvers came in individual events. These numbers present different stories from Nagoya the first about talent identification, the second on allocation of considerable investment in elite sport, and the third offering encouragement and a warning - there is growing depth in team events but athletes are struggling in individual events to make that final push from silver to gold. India finished fourth at the Asian Games with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals, 85 in all. It fell short of the 100-medal target and finished 21 medals behind its record haul in Hangzhou. We may have lost a few medals compared to Hangzhou but individual performances were satisfying, Adille Sumariwala, the Athletics Federation of India spokesperson, said. Going just on the basis of medals may not be the only way to judge. Improvement in performance is what should be tracked for future preparation for Olympic Games. Though the gold rush of the last two days ensured a heady end to a dwindling campaign, the overall number does not tell the entire story. Start with the gold. More than half of Indias gold medals came from events where several athletes contributed to one result -cricket, kabaddi, hockey, archery, athletics relays and shooting. The individual events produced a different pattern. Those 19 silvers came from athletes who had already negotiated the difficult part of reaching an Asian Games final but could not make that push to gold. That makes the gold medals of Kumkum, Suruchi-Kamaljeet and Neeru significant. Kumkum was not part of TOPS when she became Indias first individual Asian Games champion in womens recurve. Suruchi was added to the programme only recently before winning shooting mixed team gold along with Kamaljeet Singh, who, too, isnt part of TOPS. Neeru remains in the developmental group despite becoming Indias first womens trap champion at the Asian Games. Collectively, these three medals translate to Rs 3.5 lakh of TOPS funding - three gold medallists, three Olympic hopefuls who were either outside or only recently inside the established priorities of the countrys elite funding system. According to the Sports Ministry, Rs 97.84 crore was spent under TOPS during the Asian Games cycle. The money goes towards customised training programmes, foreign exposure, specialised coaches, support staff and equipment. Of this, it turned out, Rs 2.05 crore was spent on athletes who ultimately won gold. Under the Annual Calendar for Training and Competitions programme, which funds camps, tournaments, coaches salaries and other competition expenses, the Government spent another Rs 702.86 crore between 2023 and 2026. Only 12.5 per cent of that spending was associated with gold medals in Nagoya. A senior official of a federation governing an Olympic sport in the country said The pattern was seen during the Paris Olympics too, and raises a question over whether the system is identifying the athletes who will eventually deliver at the biggest events early enough for that investment to follow them. When contacted, a Sports Ministry official said, The performance of the contingent has been very encouraging and players have performed creditably. Some disciplines have not performed up to their potential but there have been some incredible results. The official said TOPS follows a dynamic and continuous evaluation process. The TOPS team closely monitors emerging and established elite athletes, with regular assessments to ensure that deserving athletes are inducted into the Development and Core Groups based on their performance, potential and medal prospects, the official said. Nagoya also confronted some of Indias traditional strongholds with reality checks.  In badminton, India failed to win an individual medal for the first time in 12 years. The sport had already returned empty-handed from the Paris Olympics, its first medal-less Olympic campaign since 2012.  In weightlifting, Mirabai Chanus silver was Indias first Asian Games medal in the sport since 1998. At 32, she remains the countrys most established name, but the only one doing the heavy lifting, with no obvious successor.  Athletics and shooting, which won 51 medals combined in Hangzhou, contributed 39 this time athletics 24, shooting 15. According to the Sports Ministry official, there will now be a review of the performance. Where performance has been below expectations, a thorough assessment will be undertaken to identify gaps, draw lessons and strengthen preparations, with a clear focus on the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games, the official said, adding that the review would have been conducted irrespective of whether performance exceeds expectations or falls short of targets. Archery provided one of the clearest signs of what is possible. Indias womens recurve team ended South Koreas 28-year Asian Games reign before Kumkum won the individual title, evidence that a younger generation is now capable of challenging a programme that has dominated the event for decades. Womens hockey offered another example of how quickly a programme can change. After missing the Paris Olympics, the players went through specialised penalty-corner and goalkeeping clinics with foreign experts, while 11 injured players received rehabilitation support. In Nagoya, they beat China for gold and secured qualification for Los Angeles. Mens wrestling produced Aman Sehrawat and Sujeet Kalkal as gold medallists. Ankush Panghal, Lovlina Borgohain and Parveen Hooda helped return boxing to the top of the Asian Games podium. Womens pistol shooting, where India has considerable depth, continued to produce results. These are the reasons Nagoya can offer encouragement ahead of Los Angeles. The Asian Games are a mid-term examination before the Olympics. India has shown depth in several team events, new names have emerged in individual sports and established athletes remain capable of providing a foundation for the next cycle. The gaps are clear, too.

articleTitle: ‘Way ahead of time’: Bappi Lahiri’s grandson Rego on his disco hits in Dhurandhar, Raja Saab
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rego B, Bappi Lahiri
description: In an exclusive interview with SCREEN, late music maestro Bappi Lahiri’s grandson Rego B opened up about his new song, ‘Chand’, and reflected on his grandfather’s musical legacy.
body_raw: Bappi Lahiris musical legacy continues through his 17-year-old grandson Swastikk Bansall, who performs under the stage name Rego B. Fresh off the release of his new single, Chand, Rego sat down with SCREEN to discuss his grandfathers influence, the resurgence of his disco classics, and how Bappi Lahiris music found a global audience long before the age of social media. Speaking about Bappi Lahiris songs that continue to resonate with people, Rego B said, Granddads songs are universal, but his foot-tapping tunes that continue to resonate with younger audiences are disco songs like Auva Auva Koi Yahan Nache, Ramba Ho Ho and Jimmy Jimmy. Those songs were very different, and granddad was way ahead of his time. He knew what would work even 20 years later, and they are still working today. Shashwat Sachdev remixed Bappi Lahiri and Usha Uthups iconic disco track Ramba Ho for Aditya Dhars film Dhurandhar, headlined by Ranveer Singh. Rego admitted that he was surprised to see the cult song featured in the film. He said, I was so surprised to see his song, Ramba Ho used in Dhurandhar, and how his song Koi Yahan Nache Nache was used in Prabhas The Raja Saab. This shows that his music is still appealing to the mass audience. Its an honour to learn from him and his style of music. I feel so grateful that I have been brought up in this family, and I am lucky to be his grandson. Rego B on Bappi Lahiris international reach and his meeting with Michael Jackson Rego also offered insights into Bappi Lahiris association with international music stars and his influence beyond India. Granddad worked with many superstars, including Snoop Dogg, Lady Gaga, Elton John and Akon. It shows how influential his music was. For an artist from India, especially at that time, to have international musicians approach him and ask him to make songs for them shows just how far his music had reached, shared Rego. Also Read Inside Bappi Lahiris 40-year-old house 1,000 Ganesha idols, a gold chair, Kishore Kumars last photo and rare 100-Year-old instruments He also recalled a story his mother had told him about Bappi Lahiris meeting with Michael Jackson in 1996. Rego said, When Michael Jackson came to Bombay, my grandfather went to meet him. My mother tells me this story. She was also very young at the time and started crying when she saw Michael Jackson because who wouldnt? He is the King of Pop, hes the G.O.A.T. Even he told my granddad, I love your song Jimmy Jimmy. Its a beautiful song. So, Michael Jackson saying that to my granddad in the 90s showed how far his music had reached. Coming from a small village in West Bengal to making a name for himself in Bollywood and then becoming known worldwide shows what he achieved and how far his music travelled. Today, we have social media to showcase our music, but back then there was nothing like that. Despite that, his music travelled overseas, and that shows its reach. Its a huge thing. Rego also shared an interesting anecdote about one of Bappi Lahiris most iconic tracks, Jimmy Jimmy. He said, It was one of the most played songs in Russia. When the President and the Prime Minister come, the marching bands play Jimmy Jimmy, and they still play it. Its such an honour to see that. You are like, Oh my God Its absolutely unreal. Rego B on his new single Chand Talking about his latest release Chand, Rego expressed gratitude for the love coming his way and the opportunity to release his first independent single. I am really grateful that Chand is finally out for everyone to hear. Its really special to me because it was released on my 17th birthday September 21, during the Ganesh Chaturthi festivities. So, it truly means a lot to me as an artiste. I am grateful to my parents and my granddad, who have mentored me and raised me in that safe space of music, and helped me reach a point where I could release my own independent single. When you hear it, it gives you a homely feeling. It has that 90s and 2000s touch to it, with the nuances in the lyrics and the singing style. Watch the song Chand below Sharing his excitement over the response to the song, he said, I can feel the energy around it, and I got to know that Chand has organically made it to New Music Friday Pakistan on Spotify. It has also made it to New Music Hindi. Its really resonating with people. The word Chand is also so universal because you can connect it with anyone your girlfriend, your husband, your wife or your family. Thats one of the reasons we chose the name Chand, because not many songs are named that. Theres a special feeling behind it. Im grateful that people are giving it so much love and are also liking the video, which is very different. My friend Adrija is my co-actor in the video, and she is an impeccable dancer and actor. So, it all has a very homely feeling.

articleTitle: Nirmala Sitharaman writes: Next-Gen GST & India’s next phase of growth
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nirmala sitharaman
description: "Under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision, Next-Gen GST was conceived with two connected purposes: to reduce and rationalise rates, and to make compliance easier," writes Nirmala Sitharaman.
body_raw: INDIAS AMBITION to become a Viksit Bharat requires an economy in which enterprises of every size can grow, wherever they begin. Over the past 12 years, our government has worked to create those conditions. GSTs introduction in 2017 established a common national framework for indirect taxation. Next-Gen GST carries that effort forward, drawing on nine years of implementation and the experience of taxpayers and states. Under Prime Minister Narendra Modis vision, Next-Gen GST was conceived with two connected purposes to reduce and rationalise rates, and to make compliance easier. The rate changes took effect on September 22, 2025. The next phase of process reforms will come before the GST Council shortly. Together, these efforts seek to give households relief, businesses greater certainty and taxpayers a system in which they can fulfil their obligations without avoidable difficulty. The states have been partners throughout. They brought their priorities and experience to the Council, helped shape the decisions and undertook their implementation. I thank them for that commitment. GSTs progress rests on this willingness to pursue a shared national purpose while respecting each governments responsibilities. The results provide grounds for confidence. Between October 2025 and July 2026, the value of reported taxable supplies grew by 25.8 over the corresponding period a year earlier. A lighter rate structure has been accompanied by a substantial expansion in reported economic activity. This is an encouraging foundation for a reform intended to support both enterprise and public finances. That resilience is visible in the latest revenue figures. Gross GST collections reached Rs 12.46 lakh crore during April-September 2026, up 11.6 over the corresponding period last year. Every month from June through September recorded double-digit annual growth together, collections for these four months accelerated by nearly 15. Net collections, after refunds, also grew by 10.4 over the half-year. Taxpayer relief has coexisted with growth in the resources available for development. The breadth of the expansion matters as much as its scale. Reported taxable supplies grew across all 11 sector groups and all major states. In an economy as diverse as Indias, this spread is significant. Growth across sectors and regions creates opportunities for more businesses to participate in expanding markets, and for more communities to benefit from the demand, investment and employment that follow. Reported sales to consumers B2C also rose by 26.7 in the post-reform comparison. When tax relief is reflected in prices, families have more room to meet other needs or save. Consumer relief and enterprise growth are closely connected the purchasing power of households sustains demand for the goods and services that businesses provide. The benefits can extend from the household to the retailer, the supplier and the producer. For small and medium enterprises, a national market is valuable when it opens a practical route to customers beyond their immediate surroundings. Businesses in Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns should be able to build those relationships while continuing to invest and employ people locally. Enterprises expanding into these towns, in turn, can create opportunities for local suppliers and distributors. GSTs common framework supports these connections simpler administration must make them easier to sustain. Participation in that framework is substantial. GST registrations across central and state jurisdictions stood at approximately 1.71 crore at the end of August, up nearly 15 from a year ago. For the April-July 2026 tax periods, GSTR-3B returns filed by their due dates were 12.6 higher than for the same periods last year. These improvements place a corresponding responsibility on the administration regular compliance must be supported by reliable service, clear guidance and timely resolution of difficulties. The functioning of input tax credit is another important part of this experience. The post-reform figures show that the share of tax liability discharged through credits rose, while accumulated credit declined relative to taxable supplies. This is encouraging for businesses that depend on the effective use of eligible credit. For a smaller firm, working capital determines how readily it can purchase inputs, fulfil an order and take on the next one. Refunds are equally relevant. Approximately Rs 1.80 lakh crore was refunded during April-September. Returning amounts due to businesses is part of a well-functioning tax system. Greater predictability in this process would help enterprises plan purchases and production with more confidence. The taxpayers experience of receiving an eligible refund is an important measure of administrative performance. The states also have a stronger revenue position. Their aggregate SGST receipts, including their share of IGST settlements, grew by about 16 during April-September this year. These resources support investment in infrastructure and public services, which improve the conditions in which families and enterprises pursue their aspirations. The gains can therefore reinforce one another household relief supports demand, enterprise strengthens economic activity, and public revenues help sustain development. The experience also points to the work ahead. A growing system must remain attentive to the costs it imposes on smaller participants. Their time and resources are limited. Each improvement in filing, credit or refunds should allow more of those resources to be devoted to running and expanding a business. The proposals before the Council on 7 October have been developed through sustained work with the states. They address registration, returns, refunds, disputes and improved flow of input tax credit, with the aim of reducing the time and cost of compliance. Taxpayer experience must continue to guide implementation. GSTs growing maturity gives us a stronger foundation for the next stage of reform. The same commitment to clarity, certainty and respect for the taxpayer guides our work on direct taxes. A dependable tax system enables enterprises to plan beyond their immediate obligations and invest in opportunities that take time to mature. Giving them that confidence, wherever they operate, helps build the economic strength of a Viksit Bharat as envisioned by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Nirmala Sitharaman is the Union Minister of Finance and Corporate Affairs

articleTitle: Can gut bacteria quietly raise Alzheimer’s risk? New study has clues
articleFeaturedImageAlt: alzheimers
description: New research shows that higher levels of this bacterial product may be associated with changes in the brain linked to Alzheimer’s disease
body_raw: What happens in the gut may have consequences far beyond digestion. Scientists are increasingly discovering that the trillions of microorganisms living in our intestines produce chemicals that can enter the bloodstream and influence metabolism, inflammation and the immune system. Now, researchers are investigating whether one of these microbial chemicals could also affect the ageing brain. The molecule attracting attention is imidazole propionate, or ImP, which is produced by some gut bacteria. What is imidazole propionate? ImP is a small molecule made when certain bacteria break down an amino acid found in proteins. New research shows that higher levels of this bacterial product may be associated with changes in the brain linked to Alzheimers disease. The findings, highlighted in a University of WisconsinMadison research announcement on October 3, came from research involving both humans and mice. What did the researchers find? The researchers studied 1,196 adults who did not have cognitive impairment. People who had higher concentrations of ImP in their blood tended to perform less well on certain cognitive tests. They also had more biological markers associated with Alzheimers disease. The researchers additionally found associations between some ImP-producing gut bacteria and Alzheimers-related markers. But there is an important distinction here an association is not proof of cause and effect. Having a higher level of ImP does not mean that a person will develop Alzheimers disease. To explore whether there might be a biological mechanism behind the association, the researchers turned to mice. Could a gut chemical affect the brain? In experiments, mice exposed to ImP over prolonged periods developed changes resembling some features of Alzheimers disease. These included alterations involving beta-amyloid and tau, two proteins closely associated with Alzheimers. In Alzheimers disease, beta-amyloid can accumulate as plaques, while abnormal tau can form tangles inside brain cells. The researchers also found evidence that ImP can affect the blood-brain barrier. The blood-brain barrier is a protective system formed largely by specialised cells lining blood vessels in the brain. It helps regulate which substances in the bloodstream can enter brain tissue. If this protective barrier becomes impaired, it may contribute to processes involved in brain ageing and neurological disease. Taken together, the findings suggest a possible pathway Certain gut bacteria produce ImP. This enters the bloodstream, may affect the blood-brain barrier and brain cells, triggering changes associated with Alzheimers disease. Does this mean probiotics could prevent Alzheimers? No-not based on this study. The research did not test whether probiotic supplements can lower ImP levels or reduce the risk of Alzheimers disease. Probiotics contain different strains of bacteria, and one probiotic product cannot be assumed to have the same effects as another. In addition, the gut microbiome is extremely complex. Simply adding bacteria to the gut does not necessarily mean that the overall microbial environment will change in a predictable way. The study also did not identify a particular food or diet that can reliably eliminate ImP. Alzheimers disease has many risk factors It is also important not to view Alzheimers disease as the result of a single molecule-or even a single biological pathway. Age is the strongest known risk factor, while genetics, cardiovascular health and other factors can also influence risk. Blood pressure, cholesterol, diabetes, physical activity, smoking, sleep and overall health are among the factors researchers continue to study. The gut microbiome may eventually turn out to be one piece of this much larger puzzle. Why is the finding important? Looking at the chemicals produced by those bacteria may provide a more precise way of studying the gutbrain connection. Researchers can now ask questions such as Which gut bacteria produce ImP? What causes those bacteria to make more or less of it? How much ImP enters the bloodstream? Can lowering ImP levels alter Alzheimers-related changes? Could targeting ImP or the bacteria that produce it be safe and effective in people? These are the questions that future studies will need to answer. If future research in humans shows that lowering ImP can reduce Alzheimers-related changes or help preserve cognitive function, this early finding could eventually become the basis for a new therapeutic strategy.

articleTitle: Omani pilot may have shut off flydubai plane’s engines after Tel Aviv crash plan failed, says report
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai Dubai-Tel Aviv Flight News
description: The Omani co-pilot may have shut off the engines of a flydubai Boeing 737 after his plan to crash it in Tel Aviv failed.
body_raw: The Omani co-pilot accused of attacking his captain on a flydubai flight may have shut off the engines of the Boeing 737 after his main plan went wrong, according to the Italian newspaper Corriere della Sera. The paper says investigators are checking whether he moved the two engine fuel switches from Run to Cutoff. The paper says the co-pilot, Hammam al-Hammami, first planned to kill Captain Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, fly the plane to Tel Aviv and crash it into a tall building, citing Israeli intelligence. When that failed, it says, he tried to crash the jet in the desert. The plane lost 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before passengers and two off-duty pilots took control and landed it at Tabuk in Saudi Arabia. A social media account believed to be linked to Hamam al-Hammami repeatedly mentions stomping on women. Photo LinkedIn The flight was carrying 174 passengers, most of them Israeli, NBC News said. Officials say the investigation is at an early stage. US officials and a former Israeli security official told NBC News that early signs point to a lone attacker, not a group or a government. Authorities have not released the suspects name. NBC News identified him from sources. How the attack began Corriere della Sera built its account from the flight crews reports to safety authorities, people familiar with the incident, airport staff, air traffic controllers and data from flight-tracking platforms. It says al-Hammami pretended to pray in the cockpit, took out the crash axe, came up behind the captain and attacked him. Machchhar first thought a broken part of the aircraft had hit him. He understood he was under attack when the blows kept coming. His head was badly bruised and his arm was almost cut off. He tried to open the cockpit door, the co-pilot shut it, and he opened it again. A woman whose daughter was in the toilet heard thudding from the cockpit. She told other passengers and two off-duty pilots on board. Several passengers ran into the cockpit and found the captain in a pool of blood. The evidence on the engines The paper points to videos filmed during the struggle that show the cabin emergency lights on at high altitude. On a Boeing 737 these lights come on when the main electrical power is lost, which happens if the generators are off or both engines have shut down. Corriere della Sera says al-Hammami saw his plan could not work and switched off the autopilot and pushed the control stick forward. In about 30 seconds the plane lost 16,000 feet. Its speed passed 970 kilometres an hour, which damaged the tail rudder. The paper says he also tried to damage the controls before passengers overpowered him. Yaniv Hayoun, a plumber, pulled the control stick back and stopped the plane from dropping further. At one point the plane lost height again, probably because the engines were giving no thrust, the paper said. It says the two off-duty pilots then returned the plane to level flight, and the flight data fit with the engines being restarted. These points come from one newspapers account. The findings of the official investigation have not been released. I knew I couldnt let all of them die Saudi air traffic controllers told the crew to turn back and then to make an emergency landing at Tabuk. The pilots landed the plane safely. Machchhar was taken to hospital, and the co-pilot was handed to Saudi authorities, Corriere della Sera said.
