articleTitle: To Trinath Mishra, with respect and wistfulness
articleFeaturedImageAlt: To Trinath Mishra, with respect and wistfulness
description: Mishra's career is proof that one can pay the price, keep one's dignity, and go on serving the institution that failed to protect you for doing the right thing.
body_raw: A life in khaki is not for everyone. Even amongst those given the privilege to wear the uniform, a few stand out as the embodiment of virtues that make an ideal police officer. Trinath Mishra, a member of the 1965 batch of the Indian Police Service, who passed away on October 1, belonged to that rare category. For a generation of policemen, his name was spoken with a mixture of respect and wistfulness Respect for what he did, wistfulness because the system he served with impeccable integrity and dedication seldom makes room for officers of his calibre. I first met him not as an officer but as a young school boy. The introduction came through Kanhaiya Lal Gupta, his batchmate in the UP cadre, and my uncle by marriage, who passed away last year. In the company of these two men, I encountered, for the first time, policing as an idea rather than a job. They disagreed about almost everything except the one thing that mattered Khaki is a trust, not a privilege. Mishras story began, in a sense, at Netarhat. He was among the first batch of a remarkable residential school there, an institution founded on the conviction that a holistic education need not be the monopoly of metropolitan elites. It instilled in him his love for austerity and a quiet sense of self-belief. As a young SP, he served in some of the most challenging districts of UP and was an integral part of the team of officers who wiped out the scourge of dacoity in the state. In the early 1990s, he served as the director of the Special Protection Group. He was then selected to officiate as director of the CBI, and subsequently headed the Central Reserve Police Force CRPF, holding concurrent charge of the CISF as well. Few officers of any generation have commanded so many of the institutions that hold the Indian state together. But what matters is what a man does when the coveted seat he occupies is on the line. That test came in October 1998. As CBI director, he authorised searches on the premises of the countrys most powerful corporate house. Within weeks, he was out. Not for any impropriety, but, by every account of the time, for not having kept the political executive in the loop. There was then no fixed tenure for the CBI chief. He took this transfer as a badge of honour and moved on. What struck me then, and strikes me more now, is that he did not nurse a grievance in public. He went on to lead the CRPF, and did that job with the same unfussy competence. Years later, as courts and governments argued over tenure protection for the CBI director, his removal was cited as Exhibit A for why it was needed. He had become, without ever seeking it, a case study in the vulnerability of honest institutions. What did I learn from men like Trinath Mishra and Kanhaiya Lal Gupta? From Mishra, I learnt that the hardest decisions in policing are between the right thing and the safe thing, and the safe thing almost always comes with the better posting. From Gupta, I learnt that such choices must be made without self-righteousness, and their consequences borne without bitterness. Together, they taught me that institutional loyalty and personal integrity are not opposites, though many well-wishers will often try to persuade you otherwise. The Indian police has not always been generous to its best and brightest. It rewards compliance and penalises professional integrity more often than it cares to admit. Mishras career is proof that one can pay the price, keep ones dignity, and go on serving the institution that failed to protect you for doing the right thing. He belonged to a generation who built many of the institutions we inherited, and always warned us how easily they could be hollowed out from within. Arguably, we have honoured the first half of their legacy far more faithfully than the second. To his family, my deepest condolences. To the young officers who never knew him, I offer a small assignment Read about the events of October 1998, and then, ask yourself honestly what you would have done in his place. That question is his parting gift to all of us who attempt to wear the uniform with pride and honour. The writer is a serving IPS officer. Views are personal

articleTitle: An old friendship renews itself through an ambitious pact
articleFeaturedImageAlt: An old friendship renews itself through an ambitious pact
description: What TEPA has delivered is not just a headline but something more durable: Tariff lines that have actually moved, and firms making decisions on the strength of it
body_raw: The last time I wrote for this newspaper was in February, when I arrived in Delhi for the AI Impact Summit. Eight months and one G7 meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi later, I am back in Delhi. This time, I am here to mark a significant anniversary The first anniversary of the entry into force of the Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement TEPA between the EFTA states and India. I am returning as a guest of the Republic of India on a state visit, demonstrating how what began as a trade negotiation has evolved into a partnership between two economies and a friendship between two democracies. Anniversaries invite summaries. I would rather treat this one as a checkpoint. What TEPA has delivered is not just a headline but something more durable Tariff lines that have actually moved, and firms making decisions on the strength of it. Switzerland is bringing precision machinery, pharmaceuticals, MedTech and specialty chemicals to this agreement - the kind of intermediate goods and technical capability that will feed into Indian manufacturing rather than compete with it. It is too early to declare results after a year, but the direction is clear. Tariff schedules and procedures do not change behaviour by themselves they only do so when companies decide that the change is substantial enough to plan around. From our conversations with Swiss businesses, we can see that they are in the early stages of making this calculation. The figure that will matter more than any other over the next decade and a half is the 100 billion investment and job-creation goal tied to TEPA - the first time an Indian trade agreement has linked market access to a concrete investment goal rather than tariff schedules alone. Beyond this is a broader ambition To deepen economic ties, encourage long-term investment, create opportunities for employment and strengthen cooperation between companies, institutions and people. The essential work of building institutions is well underway. A dedicated Desk has been set up to support EFTA companies with a smooth, informed, and confident investment experience. This is a partnership in which both sides gain. India gains capital, technology, and easier access to a market for high-value goods. Switzerland gains something we need just as much A large, fast-growing trading partner at a moment when global trade is more fragile and unpredictable than it was even a year ago. Diversification is a strategic priority. One more point deserves emphasis because it distinguishes TEPA from an older generation of trade deals. The TEPA carries meaningful provisions on labour standards, environmental protection and responsible business conduct. They reflect commitments that India and the EFTA states made together, and they show what a modern trade agreement can achieve. Alongside the trade and economic relations between our countries, there is a broader relationship Scientific and research cooperation that go back decades, a steady flow of Indian students and professionals through Swiss universities and technical institutes, growing numbers of Indian visitors to the Alps, and Swiss tourists drawn to India. There is also a substantial diplomatic relationship that has produced a dense web of bilateral agreements on science and technology, aviation, taxation, and education over the decades. None of this is reflected in the trade balance, yet it arguably makes the trade balance possible, a level of familiarity and trust between our two societies that has been quietly built up over many years, visit by visit and exchange by exchange, long before anyone thought to call it a partnership. In 2028, Switzerland and India will mark 80 years since signing their Treaty of Friendship, a document that promised perpetual peace and unalterable friendship. Those are large words for any two nations to live up to. But I think we have. Each era renewed it in the terms available to it. Scientific exchange in one decade, student visas in another, now a trade agreement with a 100-billion ambition attached to it. The TEPA, but also the Migration and Mobility Partnership and the Young Professional Agreement to be signed are simply todays answer to a promise made almost 80 years ago A practical framework that can deepen our friendship through mutual support and a shared interest in sustainable growth, prosperity, and long-term success. The writer is president, Switzerland

articleTitle: A late surge at Nagoya and a long way to Los Angeles
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A late surge at Nagoya & a long way to Los Angeles
description: India must aspire to increase the gold medal count. China’s is 169, more than double the number won by Asian Games host Japan
body_raw: A shadow of despair hung over the early phase of Indias Asian Games campaign with the gold haul stuck at four for what seemed like ages. But within a week, thanks to a late surge and a few spectacular medals, the national anthem was played 21 times. The total gold count fell from 28 in Hangzhou, and so did the total medal tally, from 107 to 85. However, India finished fourth, the same position as the previous Asiad. The standout performance came from the archery contingent, which humbled the mighty Koreans enroute to multiple gold medals. While compound archery was expected to make a mark, the mixed team winning gold and booking a quota for the LA Olympics was a shot in the arm. A truly world-class performance came from Kumkum Mohod, just 17, who ended the Korean dominance by winning gold in individual recurve - the first-ever Indian male or female to do so at the Asian Games. The womens hockey team won the title after 44 years by beating China in the final. This after reports of infighting and a string of poor results had brought down the team morale. The turnaround after coach Sjoerd Marijne returned to the helm was commendable. The boxers with three gold medals and wrestlers with a haul of two, too, contributed to Indias late climb after athletes from both sports failed to finish atop the podium in the last edition. The comeback story from boxing belonged to Parveen Hooda - stripped of her 2023 bronze medal for an anti-doping whereabouts failure, she bounced back to win gold. On the penultimate day, golfer Pranavi Urs, little known outside the ranks of those who regularly follow the sport, added a surprise continental title. But while India has defied the catastrophic forecasts, there is still a long way to go to catch up with the global superpowers. India must aspire to increase the gold medal count. Chinas is 169, more than double the number won by host Japan. Some of the performances by Indian athletes give them little or no chance at the Olympics two years from now. India didnt win a single gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics despite the government pumping in money for training. A repeat show two years from now at Los Angeles will be disappointing.

articleTitle: Ronit Roy, 60, stuns fans with six-pack abs and a high-intensity chest workout

body_raw: Actor Ronit Roy has long been a familiar face in Indian cinema and television, but his current fitness levels are prompting a fresh wave of attention. At 60, an age when many people begin to scale back physically, he is doing the opposite lean, strong, and visibly muscular, with a physique that challenges long-held assumptions about ageing. His journey reflects not just discipline but a deliberate approach to strength training and overall health. In an Instagram video posted in September last year, Roy shared a behind-the-scenes look at a high-intensity chest workout. The clip captures him performing dumbbell bench presses with 40-pound 18 kg weights, maintaining controlled form under the supervision of a spotter. He is also seen pushing his limits, lifting heavy weights while attempting to perform squats at the squat rack in the gym. These arent casual or occasional exercises - they are structured, high-resistance training aimed at building and preserving muscle mass over time. Even more striking is his physical condition. The video highlights a level of leanness and core definition, including a clearly visible six-pack, that is rarely associated with men in their sixties. So, for someone in their 50s or 60s, how can heavy resistance training like the kind shown in Ronit Roys workout be incorporated safely? Sadhna Singh, senior fitness and lifestyle consultant at HereNow Official, tells indianexpress.com, A structured and progressive approach is critical. Individuals in this age group should prioritise mobility, joint stability, and proper movement mechanics before introducing heavy loads. Starting with moderate resistance and gradually increasing intensity allows the musculoskeletal system to adapt without undue strain. Equally important is listening to the body and allowing adequate rest between sessions, as recovery capacity naturally declines with age. Role of recovery time, protein intake, and metabolic conditioning in maintaining muscle mass Singh states that recovery becomes a central pillar of fitness as one ages, since muscle repair and hormonal responses are slower compared to younger years. Adequate protein intake supports muscle protein synthesis and helps counter age-related muscle loss. Metabolic conditioning, including a mix of strength training and cardiovascular work, improves insulin sensitivity and fat metabolism. Together, these elements create a sustainable framework for preserving lean muscle while maintaining overall metabolic health, notes Singh. Realistic fitness benchmarks older adults should aim for The focus should shift from aesthetics to functional strength and resilience. Benchmarks such as maintaining muscle mass, improving grip strength, sustaining balance, and preserving bone density are far more meaningful indicators of health. Consistent strength training, weight-bearing exercises, and activities that challenge coordination have been shown to support not only physical independence but also cognitive function. The goal is to remain strong, mobile, and metabolically healthy rather than chasing visual outcomes alone, concludes Singh. articleTitle: Global capital is no longer cheap, that’s the challenge
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Global capital is no longer cheap, that’s the challenge
description: Simply put, investors are demanding higher returns from governments on the tradable debt instruments issued by them that, being backed by the sovereign’s power to tax and print currency, are ostensibly default risk-free
body_raw: Ten-year US and French government bond yields hit 5.34 and 4.99 per cent respectively last week, their highest since 2002, while crossing 3.1 per cent for Japan, the first time after 1996. The increase in borrowing costs for the governments of these countries over the past one year works out to 1.2-1.4 percentage points. Thats roughly twice the 0.7 percentage points rise in the 10-year Indian government security yield, which closed the week at 7.21 per cent. Simply put, investors are demanding higher returns from governments on the tradable debt instruments issued by them that, being backed by the sovereigns power to tax and print currency, are ostensibly default risk-free. And unlike before, they arent differentiating much between the governments of advanced and emerging economies the bonds of the former are the ones that have surged to multi-decade peaks. There are three reasons for this. The first is the persistent deficits run by developed country governments, due to aging populations, expanded social welfare commitments alongside military build-up, and voter resistance to tax increases or entitlement cuts. The USs outstanding public debt has surpassed 40 trillion. Its defence budget for 2026 reached a record 1 trillion, with the Donald Trump administration proposing 1.5 trillion of spending for the coming fiscal year. The Washington-based Institute of International Finance has estimated that advanced economies paid over 3.3 trillion in interest on globally traded government bonds last year. The perception of mounting fiscal risk also explains Chinese holdings of US Treasuries falling to an 18-year-low of 618 billion in July 2016, from the peak 1.32 trillion of November 2013. The second reason is commodity inflation from war and weather-induced supply shocks, driving central banks to raise interest rates as well as signal further increases ahead. The third has to do with the global race for building AI infrastructure. The combined capital expenditure of the four large hyperscalers alone - Meta, Microsoft, Amazon and Google - was 410 billion in 2025, while projected at 725 billion in 2026 and 1.1 trillion-plus in 2027. A significant part of this is being funded through debt. As tech companies have turned to the bond markets, it has forced governments to compete ever harder for investor money, driving up yields on even safe haven long-term US Treasuries. For India, the implications are two-fold. Policymakers and corporates, for one, must reconcile themselves to global capital being no longer available cheap. Secondly, the importance of fiscal discipline, and the government not crowding out private sector borrowings, applies no less at home.

articleTitle: He swore and hung up. Hours later, 3 kidnapped Gujaratis were free
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Held in Ethiopia on ‘dunki’ route to US, cousins freed as police reach out to ‘kidnapper’
description: Three cousins from Mehsana allegedly on the illegal ‘dunki’ route to the US were captured by ‘Baba Khan’, who wanted more than Rs 1 crore ransom. But Gujarat Police and the family bargained, and the Ethiopian authorities rescued the cousins in Addis Ababa.
body_raw: When cousins Mamta 30, Rutvik 23, and Mayuri 27 reached Langhnaj in Gujarats Mehsana district on October 1, their first stop, even before they went home, was the local police station. This was a procedural requirement-but the cousins also wanted to meet the officers whose remarkable negotiating skills over phone had extricated them from the clutches of a gang of abductors in Ethiopia. The cousins, all between the ages of 23 and 30 from a farming family in Vadasma village in North Gujarat, had hoped to travel to the United States. However, given the severe restrictions on migration by the Trump administration, they had allegedly chosen to take an illegal, circuitous dunki route. They never made it. The cousins were allegedly waylaid in Ethiopia, in eastern Africa, not far from the theatre of hostilities between the US and Iran, abducted, and held hostage for a week, sources in the Mehsana Police said. When they were finally able to board Ethiopian Airlines Flight ET 640 to Mumbai from Addis Ababa on September 30 evening, all that the cousins had with them were their passports-everything else had allegedly been kept by their abductors. The cousins told the police that the abductors had, however, booked the tickets for the flight back and released them without extracting a ransom. For this unexpected turn of events, the cousins have Inspector A M Gehlot to thank-and his long negotiations with the suspected leader of the kidnappers, a man who police sources said spoke in Hindi and identified himself as Baba Khan. This, in essence, is the story of an alleged attempt at illegal entry into the US by two women and a man, their abduction and, ultimately, their extraordinary escape back to India, according to Mehsana Police and Inspector Gehlot. Mehsana Superintendent of Police Himanshu Solanki and Collector S K Prajapati were not available for comment. Sources in the Ministry of External Affairs MEA told The Indian Express that three Indian nationals had been kidnapped in Ethiopia, and rescued by the local authorities there. They were rescued by Ethiopian authorities in Addis Ababa. Our Embassy in Addis Ababa was constantly in touch with the local authorities on this matter. Indian law enforcement authorities also contributed to the efforts. The three Indian nationals returned home on October 1, MEA sources said. Mehsana district is known for its residents desire to migrate to the United States, with locked homes across several villages in this region bearing testimony to this trend. Vadasma lies about halfway between Gandhinagar and Mehsana cities, and about 4.5 km from Langhnaj, which is on the main road. On September 29, members of the cousins family filed a missing persons report at Langhnaj police station, saying they had not heard from the three since their last call on September 22. The cousins had allegedly told their relatives that they were in Canada. They told their families that they would now contact them from the US. But then they went incommunicado, Inspector Gehlot said. In fact, the cousins were allegedly already in the custody of Baba Khan at the time, and had been coerced to lie to their families and not disclose that they had been abducted and were in Ethiopia. According to police sources, the three had left India on different flights from Jaipur and Delhi on September 21, and reached the Bole International Airport in Addis Ababa via the Middle East. Thereafter, investigations revealed, the agent who had booked their tickets abducted them, stole their belongings, and demanded a ransom of Rs 1 crore USD 1,05,000 for their release. The cousins extended family and police were alerted about the abduction by a youth from Kadi town in Mehsana, identified as Vansh, police sources said. This youth had returned home after being kidnapped in Ethiopia, and after having allegedly paid a ransom of Rs 40 lakh, the sources said. Officers from the Langhnaj police station immediately persuaded the families of the three cousins to file missing persons complaints. By then, Baba Khan too had reached out to a contact in Dangarva village, whom police sources identified as Aditya Panchal. This person directed the cousins family to an agent from Vadodara, identified as Bhargav Patel. But police found that Patel had already gone underground. Information on the case was shared with the Local Intelligence Branch LIB of Mehsana Police, the Gujarat Police headquarters at Gandhinagar, and the MEA in New Delhi, the sources said. They said that Langhnaj police decided to take Aditya Panchal into confidence, and get him to engage with the alleged abductor in their presence. Panchal, a member of the cousins family, and two police personnel spoke to Baba Khan continuously over several calls. They tried to convince Baba Khan that the middle-class family was engaged in farming, and couldnt afford to pay the huge ransom, especially as they had already paid Rs 60 lakh to the network-at Rs 20 lakh per person-to ferry them to the US, Inspector Gehlot said. Following the negotiations, the kidnappers brought their demand down to Rs 15 lakh. They said this was the lowest they were willing to go, at Rs 5 lakh per person, Gehlot said. By then, investigators had begun to suspect that Baba Khan was only an alias. The man on the other end would speak on WhatsApp voice calls, and would never agree to come on video, which might offer police clues as to his identity, sources said. At one point, on September 30, the family representative told Baba Khan that they could not afford to pay him even Rs 5 lakh, let alone the Rs 15 lakh that he was demanding, Gehlot said. This was followed by some tense moments. The abductor seemed very angry, and he swore and hung up, police sources said. But later that day, the family got a video call from an unknown number. When they answered, they saw Mamta, Rutvik, and Mayuri on the screen. The cousins told them they had borrowed someones phone to make the call. They said that the abductors had dropped them 2 km from the airport and had booked their tickets back to India, the sources said. The three landed in Mumbai around 2 am on October 1, and headed to Gujarat. The cousins told police that in Addis Ababa, they were taken to an isolated residence, tied and blindfolded. Rutvik was beaten but there was no mistreatment with the two women, Gehlot said. The three also told police that they did not know Vansh, the youth whose tip-off allegedly helped police get on their trail. According to sources, the family had decided to send the cousins via the dunki route after the US government rejected Mamtas visa application. Since they were sending Mamta, they thought that the two younger cousins could also start new lives in the US, and decided to send all the three together, Inspector Gehlot said. Police are now trying to trace Bhargav Patel, the alleged travel agent who is suspected to be part of Baba Khans network.

articleTitle: Supreme Court to hear today two pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s functioning, SIR
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court to hear today two pleas against CEC’s functioning, SIR
description: A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will hear the matter.
body_raw: The Supreme Court will hear on Monday two petitions questioning the functioning of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, calling for an SIT probe against him and others and seeking to declare the nationwide SIR of electoral rolls illegal. A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will hear the matter. The petitions were filed days after The Indian Express reported that ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR of electoral rolls. The two commissioners said some of the decisions were issued without their knowledge or recommendation. The two ECs separately wrote to the countrys top bureaucrat, Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan, flagging concerns over the integrity of voter software. The ECI said the letters sent by Sandhu and Joshi to the Cabinet Secretary concerned an officer on deputation and were not related to policy or IT division matters. One of the petitions by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh referred to the alleged differences between CEC Kumar and Sandhu and Joshi and the objections raised by them. Article 3241 of the Constitution does not vest the superintendence, direction and control of elections in an individual Chief Election Commissioner. It vests those powers in a Commission, said the plea. Singh pointed out that Article 3242 provides that the ECI comprises the CEC and such number of other ECs as the President may determine from time to time. Article 3243 further stipulates that, when other ECs are appointed, the CEC shall serve as the Commissions chairperson. The constitutional text therefore deliberately separates membership of the Commission from the chairmanship of the Commission, and separates the chairmanship of the Commission from the Commissions power. Singh said his grievance is not that Kumar exercised the CECs powers improperly, but that he has. held out as entitled to exercise a power, the collective decision-making authority of the Commission under Article 324 and Section 18 of the 2023 Act Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, to which Article 3243 gives him no individual title, he being Chairman of the Commission and not the Commission itself. The petitioner urged the court to declare SIR, and all actions, decisions, directions, and measures taken under it, invalid from the very beginning and without legal authority. The petitioner argued that the SIR was undertaken without the necessary statutory or constitutional authority and without following the procedure required by law. The other petition by Delhi-based lawyer Shailendra Mani Tripathi has sought a probe by an independent, high-powered judicial inquiry commission or an SIT headed by a retired judge of the top court. The petition refers to unprecedented constitutional fractures and illegalities committed within the ECI under the CEC as exposed by documentary records published on September 23, 2026. The plea said the alleged act of. CEC Kumar. falls squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constitutes distinct, personal criminal liability.

articleTitle: Newborn found dead inside Madhya Pradesh hospital. Then, doctors noticed marks around her neck
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Newborn found dead inside MP hospital. Then, doctors noticed marks around her neck
description: What initially appeared to be a sudden deterioration in the newborn’s condition became a suspected murder case after doctors noticed marks around her neck and blood coming from her mouth.
body_raw: A newborn girl was allegedly strangled to death, within 16 hours of her birth, at a hospital in Madhya Pradeshs Ashoknagar district, with police now probing the family members. The baby, born to a couple from the Chanderi area, was admitted to the hospital shortly after birth and was being kept under medical observation. By Saturday afternoon, she was dead. What initially appeared to be a sudden deterioration in the newborns condition became a suspected murder after doctors noticed marks around her neck and blood coming from her mouth. An initial medical investigation showed that there were some marks on the infants neck. Furthermore, blood was also spotted on her face. We are questioning the infants family members, said a police officer. Police said the examination subsequently found ligature or compression marks around the babys neck, indicating that she could have been strangled, the officer said. The finding prompted investigators to reconstruct the few hours between her admission and her death, including who had handled the baby, who had entered the ward and when she was last seen alive. The baby was born late on Friday night, around 11.50 pm, and was admitted to the Special Newborn Care Unit SNCU soon after. She was found dead between about 3 pm and 4 pm on Saturday, less than 16 hours after her birth. A health official from the district said hospital staff immediately took the newborn to the SNCU after she was found unresponsive. Doctors examined the child and found that she had already died. The baby had blood coming from her mouth and marks resembling pressure around her neck. Given these circumstances, the hospital treated the death as suspicious and informed the police, following which the body was sent for post-mortem examination, the official said. The newborn was the second daughter of her parents. Investigators are, therefore, examining whether the babys gender and the familys circumstances could have played a role in her killing. The possibility of a family member being responsible for the death has emerged also because access to the child was restricted. Besides, the absence of CCTV cameras inside the SNCU has also made it difficult to immediately ascertain how she was killed.

articleTitle: Ujjain is preparing for 40 crore pilgrims. What will the ancient city lose?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hotels, roads and the race against time: Inside Ujjain’s Simhastha 2028 makeover
description: With the state government approving 128 projects worth Rs 13,851 crore, Ujjain is being transformed at a pace rarely seen in the temple town’s modern history as it races to prepare for the 2028 Simhastha — from new highways, bridges and ghats to five-star hotels.
body_raw: Ujjain has always resisted the march of time, clinging to its ancient city of temples, ghats, bazaars and British-era offices. Now, as Ujjain prepares for Simhastha 2028, its maps are being redrawn, hurtling the sleepy temple town towards a new modernity - carved through its old streets with bulldozers, widened roads and concrete. On September 27, a crowd gathered outside the Shahi Masjid, where the administration was preparing to remove the portion of the mosque within the proposed road alignment, as protests raged over road-widening projects in Ujjain ahead of the 2028 Simhastha. Hours later, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav took an axe to his grandfathers ancestral home in Abdalpura. The demolitions came as the administration raced against time for the Simhastha Mela 2028, for which the government has approved 128 projects worth about Rs 13,851 crore across 10 departments. For Yadav, Simhastha has become his governments defining project, with the administration effectively mobilised around a single task transforming the ancient temple town before pilgrims arrive. On the ground, the transformation is unfolding on a scale rarely seen in Ujjains modern history. Highways are being carved into the citys approaches, railway lines and bypasses are being built, roads and bridges widened, kilometres of new ghats taking shape along the Shipra, and water and sewerage networks being laid underground. What is taking shape is not simply a city preparing for a festival, but a centuries-old temple town being physically remade into a modern pilgrimage city. Simhastha Mela Authority director Jagdish Aggarwals office in Kothi Road, a leafy neighbourhood, is less a conventional government chamber these days than a control room for one of Madhya Pradeshs biggest infrastructure exercises. Project officers come in with updates, meetings are held with swamis and other stakeholders, and meetings with the chief minister are woven into a schedule dominated by Simhastha. Every Thursday, Aggarwal sits with the collector and deputy collector for a review devoted to the same question how to get Ujjain ready for 2028? We are preparing keeping in mind the possibility of around 40 crore people coming to Ujjain, Aggarwal said, explaining why projects that would otherwise appear excessive for Ujjain are being taken up simultaneously. But theres also a human cost involved the eroding trust among residents. Yasin Khan, a local, welcomed the road-widening project but frowned upon the speed at which the administration proceeded. When the houses were marked in my neighbourhood, both Hindu and Muslim families came out and demolished portions of the houses ourselves. But the administration barely took us into confidence. Its better to demolish on your own than wait for the administration to come with a bulldozer. Changing Ujjain The most visible changes are on Ujjains roads. The Ujjain-Indore six-laning project, estimated at Rs 1,692 crore, is under construction, while a separate Indore-Ujjain greenfield four-lane corridor, estimated at Rs 2,935 crore, is also being developed, SMA officials said. A 98.73-km Ujjain-Jaora greenfield four-lane corridor, costing about Rs 5,017 crore, received its foundation stone in July. Planned with seven flyovers, three railway overbridges, eight major bridges, 22 medium bridges, 36 underpasses and 430 culverts, it is targeted for completion by December 2027. It is intended to provide an east-west connection towards Jaora and the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway while taking long-distance traffic away from the city, SMA officials said. More than 80 percent of road and connectivity works had reached the ground, with the road component around 70 percent complete. Around 15 bridges are under construction, and we expect five or six to be ready for inauguration by December, Aggarwal said. More than 10 five-star hotels are either coming up or planned in Ujjain, Aggarwal said, alongside smaller hotels and guest houses. Along the Shipra, the government is building approximately 29.2 km of new ghats and associated works, stretching from the Shani temple area towards the Nagda bypass. The Rs 778-crore project is intended to spread bathing and pilgrim movement over a longer stretch of the river, officials said. At Gaughat, Akram Khan, a project supervisor for a private company, said they would meet the deadline for the restored ghat by December. The restoration is taking place against an old British water works department office, built in the 1930s. Only the old English chimney remains as the Madhya Pradesh government races ahead with the modern ghat. We began work in May and employed over 100 workers per day, paying them at least Rs 800 per day to finish this work. The reason we can race through the project is that the governments fully focused on this. From making roads to providing us with electricity and water connections, they raced through all that to help our project, Akram said. The second major riverfront project is the Rs 919.94-crore Kanh closed-duct diversion scheme, intended to prevent polluted water carried by the Kanh River from entering the Shipra. The scheme involves a 30.15-km diversion system, including an 18.15-km cut-and-cover section and a 12-km tunnel. Inside Ujjain, the road programme is being executed through municipal packages, with roads widened around the old city and Mahakal area. One of the most contentious stretches is the road from Khajurwali Masjid towards Ganesh Chowk, where widening work has now moved to the ground and brought the Shahi Masjid within the road alignment. Protests - and race against time Across Ujjains old neighbourhoods, the transformation is not happening only behind construction-site barricades. It is happening at peoples front doors. Hindu and Muslim families alike have been taking hammers and pickaxes to portions of homes, shops and religious structures marked for demolition under the new road alignments. Lokendra Nigam, a cloth merchant from Chattri Chowk, lamented the removal of a small portion of his shop. We are doing it for the Simhastha. Of course, we understand the devotees need space to move. But we should be adequately compensated. We feel the authorities dont listen to us. At the Simhastha division of the Madhya Pradesh Public Works Department, Executive Engineer Praful Jain studies the map of Ujjain on his computer, tracking projects for Simhastha 2028. The PWDs Simhastha division has 20 works underway, Jain said, including an underpass, a bridge and road and connectivity projects. Among the most significant is the 629-metre Hari Phatak underpass, intended to provide an alternative route towards Mahakal Lok. More than 100 structures, on average, have been identified for impact across the underpass and elevated-corridor projects, Jain said. The focus, he said, is on resource and manpower planning, machinery planning and resolving issues on multiple fronts simultaneously, so that construction can begin at the appropriate time rather than waiting for one project to finish before another starts. Jain said the department is increasingly relying on precast technology to compress timelines. Beams, columns and girders can be prepared in advance and brought to sites for assembly. The road network is also intended to create capacity beyond the festival. Four-lane and six-lane interconnected roads are being developed at different locations, Jain said. The Simhastha works, in that sense, are being designed as infrastructure that can continue to serve the city after the festival. We want to develop international-level infrastructure across the world, like the Temple Mount in Israel or Mecca in Saudi Arabia.

articleTitle: This building in Bastar used to house a security camp. Now, it is home to 150 students
articleFeaturedImageAlt: This building in Bastar used to house a security camp. Now, it is home to 150 students
description: The campus in Bhatpal houses two hostels for Scheduled Tribe boys studying in pre-matric and post-matric levels. Another hostel will come up for girls in Abujhmad in a few days.
body_raw: Until recently, this building in Chhattisgarhs Bastar region used to house a security camp, aiding the forces fight against Maoists. Since August, instead of paramilitary personnel, it has been home to students from nearby Maoism-hit areas, including Abujhmad that has seen over a 100 Maoists, including top leaders, being killed in the last two years. Hundreds of others have surrendered. The Bhatpal campus currently houses two hostels for Scheduled Tribe boys studying in pre-matric and post-matric levels. The objective was to address one of the key challenges faced by children from distant and difficult-to-access areas - access to safe accommodation close to school. Previously, this particular area Bhatpal had no post-matric boys hostel, making it difficult for tribal students to pursue higher education, said Narayanpur collector Namrata Jain. With the establishment of a post-matric hostel for tribal youths for the first time, students from remote areas can now continue their education with access to safe accommodation and better educational opportunities, said Jain, who recently visited the Bhatpal hostel kitchen and reviewed the quality of food. The security camp was established here 15 years ago. The pre-matric hostel caters to students from Classes 6 to 10 and is currently accommodating 114 students. The post-matric hostel, for students of Classes 11 and 12, with a sanctioned capacity of 50 students, is currently accommodating 39 students. Going by the response to the boys hostels-the pre-matric one is running beyond its sanctioned capacity of 100 students-the authorities are planning to set up more such accommodations. The next one is coming up in Kurushnar, at the entrance of Abujhmad or Maad, as it is locally known from the Narayanpur end. In 2011, a residential school was built here after permission from Maoists who demanded the school be made without a concrete ceiling or a high boundary wall to ensure forces do not start camping there. With the Maoists now gone, the security camp established less than a decade ago is being turned into a girls hostel, which is expected to be ready in a few days. Though Bhatpal hostel is away from Maad, it houses students from villages in and around the area. These include Kohkameta, Madamnaar, Orrcha, Nelwad, Chote Donger, Korenda, Chimdi, Remavand and Benoor. One such student is Komendra from Rajbeda-located around 22 kilometres away. For the Class 12 student, the opening of the post-matric hostel has provided significant relief and taken off the burden of additional expenditure on accommodation. Earlier this year, a budget of Rs 100 crore was allocated towards turning Maad and Jagargunda in the Bastar region, which were known as hotbeds of Maoism, into modern education cities.

articleTitle: J&K collected Rs 114 crore from job aspirants in 3 years, Assembly told
articleFeaturedImageAlt: J&K collected Rs 114 crore from job aspirants in 3 years, but vacancies dipped
description: According to the figures shared by the government in the Assembly, the number of posts advertised by the Public Service Commission in the UT has declined from 2,586 in 2023-24 to 1,400 in 2024-25 and just 357 in the last financial year.
body_raw: Jammu and Kashmirs two government recruitment agencies have collected Rs 114 crore as application fee from aspirants of different examinations over the last three years. The information was shared by the government in the JK Assembly during the ongoing autumn session. The figures shared by the government also reveal a sharp decline in the number of posts advertised by the two recruitment agencies since the Omar Abdullah regime took power in October 2024. The number of posts advertised by the Public Service Commission declined from 2,586 in 2023-24 to 1,400 in 2024-25 and just 357 in the last financial year. The posts advertised by the SSB have also shown a sharp decline. In 2023-24, the agency had advertised 4,228 posts, which rose to 5,044 posts in 2024-25. However, the number has come down to just 1,731 in 2025-26. Responding to a question, the government said that over the last three years - 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 - the Jammu and Kashmir Public Service Commission JKPSC and the Jammu and Kashmir Service Selection Board JKSSB have collected Rs 114 crore from the candidates applying for various jobs. The Public Service Commission recruits candidates for the gazetted posts while the Service Selection Board does it for non-gazetted posts. The government informed the House that the Service Selection Board has collected around Rs 89.50 crore from aspiring candidates as application fee for 11,003 non-gazetted posts advertised by the recruitment agency. It further said that the Public Service Commission has advertised 4,961 posts over the last three years and collected Rs 24.43 crore from the aspiring candidates. Agencies have become money-minting machines Government examination agencies have become money-minting machines, extracting money from unemployed youth instead of helping them, said Peoples Democratic Party PDP legislator Waheed Para, who had asked the question in the House. Papers are sold, exams are withheld and nearly 90 of recruitment has remained stalled for two years. The irony is that the recruitment agency itself doesnt even have a permanent chief, he said. While the two recruitment agencies withdrew many posts, the Public Service Commission is yet to refund its candidates. The SSB, on the other hand, has refunded an amount of Rs 1.36 crore to the applicants. JKPSC, with the assistance of NIC National Informatics Centre, is devising an online mechanism for refund of fees on account of withdrawal of posts or multiple payments, the government has said. The mechanism is likely to be operational shortly, it added. Giving the details, the government has said that the SSB has advertised 4,961 posts - 2,586 in 2023-24, 1,400 in 2024-25, and 357 in 2025-26. While the recruitment agency has received 2,76,065 applications for these posts, only 1,85,808 candidates appeared in the exams. Similarly, the SSB has advertised 11,003 non-gazetted posts over the last three years - 4,228 in 2023-24, 5,044 in 2024-25, and 1,731 in 2025-26. The recruitment agency has received 18,36,056 applications for over 11,000 posts. Only half of the candidates - 9,38,777 - appeared in the recruitment exams.

articleTitle: Manipur: Kuki man found dead day after abduction
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Manipur: Kuki man found dead a day after abduction
description: The incident comes against the backdrop of renewed Kuki-Naga tensions in Manipur, particularly in parts of Kangpokpi district and neighbouring areas.
body_raw: A DAY after he was allegedly abducted from his field in Kangpokpi district of Manipur, a 71-year-old Kuki man was on Sunday found dead-with his hands tied behind his back-in a nearby forest, sources said. The man was identified as Hemjang Haokip of Khunkho Kuki village near Leimakhong. He was reported missing after his field hut was set ablaze on Saturday. Haokips farm trousers, shirt and sweater were recovered during a search on Sunday, following which security forces deployed sniffer dogs and intensified the operation to trace him. His body was subsequently found in a nearby forest. The circumstances surrounding Haokips death and the identity of those responsible were not immediately known. According to initial reports, heavy rainfall on Saturday had kept many villagers away from their fields, and the incident came to light only in the evening. Haokip was known to frequently spend the night at his field hut. After learning that the hut had been burnt and Haokip was missing, villagers launched a search that continued until dark but failed to locate him. The Kuki Youth Organisation KYO, Leimakhong block, had earlier demanded Haokips immediate and safe return and urged the authorities and security agencies to intensify the search and take action against those responsible. The Khunkho Kuki Village Authority had also condemned the abduction and issued a 24-hour ultimatum for Haokips safe and unconditional release, warning of widespread democratic protests if he was not released. The Committee on Tribal Unity, Sadar Hills, had separately appealed for Haokips safe release. Meanwhile, the Ariang Khunkhu Naga Village Authority, in a clarification issued on Sunday, expressed solidarity with Haokips family and said neither the village nor its residents had any involvement in his disappearance. The Naga village authority appealed against unverified allegations and speculation, warning that such claims could create unnecessary distrust and tension between the two villages, which it said had maintained peaceful and cordial relations for decades. The incident comes against the backdrop of renewed Kuki-Naga tensions in Manipur, particularly in parts of Kangpokpi district and neighbouring areas.

articleTitle: Mad Sandhu murder: Punjabi influencer was set to enter Bigg Boss, says father
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjabi influencer Mad Sandhu was set to enter Bigg Boss, says father
description: Two gangsters claim they ordered the hit: 'was ruining new generation'.
body_raw: Punjabi LGBTQI social media influencer and makeup artist Mad Sandhu, who was murdered Saturday, was set to enter reality television show Bigg Boss as a wildcard contestant later this month, his friends and family said. The 30-year-old, whose real name was Madhusudan Sandhu, had built a following through his outspoken social media presence and was preparing for a major break in his career. He was to enter the Bigg Boss house on October 29, had completed the necessary paperwork, but had not made the information public, according to his father Bhupinder Singh. He was due to leave for Mumbai to take part in show on on October 20, Bhupinder Singh, said. On Sunday, the family cremated Sandhu. Sandhu died of gunshot wounds after two motorcycle borne assailants opened fire at him in Amritsar outside a car wash. The killing sent shockwaves through Amritsar, with Sandhus family saying he had previously received online abuse and threats over his outspoken social media presence and his association with the LGBTQ community. He had also approached the police several times seeking protection, his father said. The murder took another turn after two gangsters separately claimed responsibility for the killing in social media posts. Gangster Goldy Dhillon was the first to claim responsibility, alleging that Sandhu was ruining the new generation and warning others who, according to him, promoted similar content on social media platforms. Spain-based alleged gangster Lucky Johal subsequently disputed Dhillons claim and said he was responsible for the killing. Johal allegedly said the murder was not motivated by money or personal gain but by what he described as an attempt to protect Punjabs culture and environment. He also threatened another influencer, Arupreet, whose content he claimed was similar to Sandhus. Police have not established the veracity of either claim. Amritsar Police Commissioner Harmanbir Singh Gill said, police has obtained significant leads regarding the shooters and expressed confidence that arrests would follow. Sabndhu was eldest of three siblings. His father is a retired Punjab police sub-inspector, while his mother is a homemaker. The family originally lived on Sultanwind Road before moving to the Manawala area along the Amritsar-Jalandhar road. Recalling his sons childhood, Bhupinder Singh said Sandhu had expressed his individuality and gender identity from an early age. From early childhood, he was different. We initially tried to change him, but later we understood that this is how God has made him, he told The Indian Express. The family later became supportive of Sandhus choices, his father said. We never restricted him from living his life on his own terms. After completing Class 12, Sandhu trained as a makeup artist at a private institute and later established his own salon and makeup business in Amritsar. His work took him into the Punjabi entertainment industry, where he worked with actors and attended events in Mumbai. His reported selection for Bigg Boss marked another milestone in his career. He was supposed to go to Bigg Boss as a wildcard entry, his father said. Sandhus public profile, however, had also made him a controversial figure at times. In April 2025, he publicly supported the cancellation of a Pride parade in Amritsar and appealed to members of the LGBTQ community not to turn the issue into a confrontation with wider society. If society does not want to accept these things right now, or if it isnt ready for them yet, then we shouldnt force it, he had said. He had also urged members of the community to take cultural and religious sentiments into consideration. According to his family, Sandhu had faced hostility and threats from several people, including some Nihang factions. His father said Sandhu had informed police about the threats and submitted applications seeking protection, including one several months before his death. He would just go to work, work to home, home to work, his father said, describing the cautious routine Sandhu had adopted. The family said they had received no ransom demand. Police are now investigating the circumstances of the shooting, including the identity of the assailants and the competing social-media claims of responsibility.

articleTitle: CBI arrests DGCA official, firm director in bribery case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: CBI arrests DGCA official, firm director in bribery case
description: The agency has alleged that Garg demanded and accepted a bribe of Rs 2.5 lakh for extending undue favours in the airworthiness certification of the aircraft operated by the private firm.
body_raw: THE CBI has arrested Directorate General of Civil Aviation DGCA Deputy Director Airworthiness Sushil Kumar Garg, posted in Chennai, and Director of Ekvi Air Training Organisation Pvt Ltd Sushil Kumar Garg in connection with an alleged bribery case. The agency has alleged that Garg demanded and accepted a bribe of Rs 2.5 lakh for extending undue favours in the airworthiness certification of the aircraft operated by the private firm. According to sources, the payment was linked to regulatory clearances concerning the airworthiness of aircraft operated by Ekvi Air Training Organisation Pvt. Ltd. Airworthiness certification is a key regulatory process intended to ensure that aircraft meet prescribed safety and operational standards. Besides Garg and Bhane, the CBI has also named the company and other unknown persons in the case, officials said. Further investigation is underway to ascertain the role of other individuals in the case and to examine whether the purported exchange of money was part of a wider arrangement involving aviation-related approvals, the agency said. The CBI had received inputs about the alleged bribe demand, following which an FIR was registered and a raid was conducted, sources said. According to officials, Garg accepted the Rs 2.5 lakh bribe, after which he and Bhane were arrested. The agency will move court seeking transit remand of the accused officer to bring him to the national capital for questioning, they said.

articleTitle: Rs 2,400 crore Mokama rail bridge opens: 2 new lines boost Delhi-Howrah train capacity
articleFeaturedImageAlt: New Mokama rail bridge over the Ganga in Bihar. (Image: East Central Railway)
description: Mokama’s new rail bridge over the Ganga is now open for train operations, adding two railway lines and strengthening North-South Bihar connectivity.
body_raw: Indian Railways has commissioned Mokamas new rail bridge over River Ganga in Bihar. Built at a cost of around Rs 2,400 crore, the new bridge will further strengthen rail connectivity between North and South Bihar. This will also provide an additional route for passenger and freight train operations. The new bridge has been constructed parallel to the existing Rajendra Pul and has a double railway line. It was opened for train operations after receiving the required safety approval from the Commissioner of Railway Safety CRS, Eastern Circle. The CRS conducted the safety inspection of the new bridge and the associated doubled and electrified railway line on October 3 and 4, 2026.Following the safety clearance, train operations have started on the new bridge. Speaking to Indianexpress.com, Saraswati Chandra, Chief Public Relations Officer CPRO, East Central Railway, said the new Mokama rail bridge has been commissioned and train operations began around midnight. He added that train number 15483 Mahananda Express was the first train to cross the newly commissioned bridge. Location of new Mokama rail bridge The new Mokama rail bridge has been constructed about 50 metres towards the Patna side of the existing Rajendra Pul, which has been in service since 1959. The project spans around 15.5 km, including a 1.9-km main bridge over the Ganga connecting Mokama and Barauni. The main bridge comprises 17 steel spans, while the project also includes around 3.6 km of rail viaducts. Besides the main bridge, the project includes eight minor bridges, two road overbridges and three rail-over-rail structures. According to the CPRO, the new bridge has been planned in a way that requires minimum changes to the approaches of the existing bridge. It connects to the existing railway stations on both sides of the Ganga. Existing Rajendra Pul to continue carrying trains The railway official said that the new bridge will not replace the existing Rajendra Pul. Thus, the train operations will continue on the old bridge as well. He added that with the new double-line bridge alongside the existing bridge, the route will now have three railway lines, increasing capacity for train movement. It will significantly boost capacity on the busy Delhi-Howrah rail corridor. Better train connectivity between North and South Bihar The new bridge will provide an additional rail route between North and South Bihar, while also strengthening connectivity towards the northeastern parts of the country. According to the official, railway traffic in the corridor is expected to increase by around 2.5 times. The higher capacity is also expected to make freight movement smoother and reduce transportation time and costs. This could benefit the movement of essential goods as well as trade and commercial activity in the region, he stated. However, for passengers, the two new lines will help Railways manage train operations more efficiently on this important route.

articleTitle: This is what happens to heart health when you stop GLP-1 medicines
articleFeaturedImageAlt: medicines
description: Stopping GLP-1 medicines does not automatically trigger a heart attack, but some of the health benefits may gradually fade. Here’s what to know.
body_raw: GLP-1 medicines are increasingly used to manage type 2 diabetes and obesity, with some drugs in this class also shown to reduce cardiovascular risk in certain groups. But what happens to the heart when a person stops taking them? According to Dr Parin Sangoi, Consultant Interventional Cardiologist, Wockhardt Hospitals, Mumbai Central, stopping a GLP-1 medicine does not mean a person will immediately have a heart attack. The immediate effects of GLP-1 medicines on blood sugar, appetite, body weight and several cardiovascular risk factors disappear gradually when the medication is stopped, said Dr Sangoi. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. The concern is what happens to the risk factors The issue is not that abruptly stopping the medicine will cause a heart attack, but that the factors it had been helping to control may come back, Dr Sangoi explained. He adds that weight regain, rising blood sugar, rising blood pressure, and deteriorating metabolic health can contribute to higher cardiovascular risk over time. This is particularly relevant for people taking GLP-1 medicines to manage diabetes or obesity, as well as those who already have cardiovascular disease. Do the heart benefits remain after stopping? Studies involving drugs such as semaglutide have demonstrated a decrease in major cardiovascular events while patients were on the treatment, said Dr Sangoi. He explains that the cardiovascular benefits should not be considered to last after the medication is stopped. Studies involving drugs such as semaglutide have demonstrated a decrease in major cardiovascular events while patients were on the treatment. Moreover, evidence suggests that stopping weight-management medications can lead to considerable weight regain and reversal of some cardiometabolic improvements. The degree to which cardiovascular protection continues after stopping differs from person to person, and there is a lack of long-term data that look at protection following discontinuation. In clinical practice, attention should be paid to sustaining the improvements in weight, blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol which reduce cardiovascular risk, Dr Sangoi explains. Should you stop GLP-1 medicines on your own? Dr Sangoi advised against stopping these medicines without discussing it with the prescribing doctor. Stopping a GLP-1 drug should not be something that is done on ones own initiative but rather a decision that is carefully planned, he said. For someone with diabetes, blood sugar may rise again after discontinuation, while people taking the medication for obesity may experience weight regain. For those with existing cardiovascular disease, it is also important to consider why the medicine was prescribed and whether another treatment is needed to manage their risk factors. What if you need to stop because of side effects or cost? Wherever the decision to stop the treatment is based on side effects, cost, plans for pregnancy or some other medical reason, the doctor in charge can determine if the dose should be modified, if another medication should be started, or if more frequent monitoring is needed, Dr Sangoi said. After stopping treatment, regular monitoring of weight, blood pressure, blood sugar and other cardiovascular risk factors can help identify changes early, he adds. articleTitle: AISA chief Neha Bora among 120 detained on Day 3 of protest against CEC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: neha bora
description: The protest came a day after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment while covering the stir near Jantar Mantar.
body_raw: Around 120 protesters, including All India Students Association AISA president Neha Bora, Yogendra Yadav, were detained for several hours on Sunday as the protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision SIR of voter rolls entered its third consecutive day. The protest came a day after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment while covering the stir near Jantar Mantar. On Sunday, while some protested against CEC Kumar, others attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar to demand accountability and a probe into the journalists allegations of sexual assault. Bora was detained while leading a march from Andhra Bhavan Canteen towards Jantar Mantar. The march saw participation from civil society activists such as Yadav, student protesters and political parties like the Indian Youth Congress IYC and the AAP. This has just started and many organisations are now joining this, we wont stop. Even though the Jantar Mantar is closed, were on the streets, even women are here to reclaim them. This is the power of common people. Jab tak Gyanesh Kumar ki chhutti nahi hoti, hum chhutti nahi karnege Until Gyanesh Kumar takes a leave, we will not take a leave, Yadav said while marching towards Jantar Mantar. Flags waved and slogans of Gyanesh has to go pierced the air as the crowd split into groups and moved towards Ashoka Road. With the protest entering its third day, Lutyens Delhi was heavily fortified, with elaborate security arrangements in place since morning. A large fleet of buses and riot action vehicles had been deployed on multiple lanes, and movement on several roads leading to Jantar Mantar and the Parliament Street police station was restricted. The Delhi Police also closed the stretch between Ashoka Road and Parliament Street near Jantar Mantar, while prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS were already put across the New Delhi district. At around 4 pm, as the march progressed towards Jantar Mantar, barricades were put up. When a few protesters tried to cross them, the police began detaining them. Bora was detained in a car by officers, but the vehicle remained stuck for over 20 minutes as protesters stood around it to prevent it from moving. Ashoka Road remained shut and traffic was halted until 6.30 pm as the protests continued. Amid the chaos, police kept detaining protesters, including AISA activists and members of other left-wing parties. As one police bus filled with detainees pulled away, the next quickly took its place in line. Teams of four to five officers lifted and carried protesters to the buses, while some tried to break the bus windows to get out. Even as detentions continued, people kept protesting. Traffic resumed briefly on the roundabout, but police carried on detaining protesters as their numbers grew. According to police sources, around 120 people, including AISA, AAP and IYC workers and Yadav, were detained. Bora was taken to Narela police station, police said, adding that all of the protesters were later released. According to police, around half a dozen of their personnel including women staff were also injured while handling the protesters. The injured officers were given first aid at a hospital as well, police said.

articleTitle: US demands up to $20,000 visa bond from 50 countries; India left out
articleFeaturedImageAlt: us visa, us visa news, us visa bond
description: US visa bond programme requires eligible B1/B2 applicants from 50 countries to post financial guarantees of up to $20,000.
body_raw: The US Department of State introduced a visa-bond programme that designated nationals from 50 countries as requiring financial guarantees up to 20,000 in order to receive tourist and business visas. The mandate has encompassed South Asian nations like Bhutan, Nepal, and Bangladesh. How the US visa bond programme works Pursuant to the Immigration and Nationality Act INA Section 221g3, under which the visa bond programme has been established, a consular officer may require posting of a visa bond before visa issuance. The final rule, issued on August 3 by the State Department, states that any citizen or national travelling on a passport that falls under the list of 50 countries and is eligible for B1 B2 visa is required to post a bond for 10,000, 15,000, or 20,000, adding that the amount is determined at the time of the visa interview. Visa overstay rates determine eligibility As per the INA section, the visa overstay rates are based on the B1 B2 overstay rates from the Department of Homeland Securitys entry exit overstay report, the US State Department stated. Apart from the visa bond requirements, the applicants must also submit a Department of Homeland Security DHS Form I-352. Eligible citizens can pay the required amount through the Department of the Treasurys online payment platform, Pay.gov. US warns applicants about visa bond scams The department has alerted applicants not to post the bond on any website not specifically listed in the instructions received from the consular officer and that the administration would not be held responsible for any money paid outside of its systems. India exempt from US visa-bond requirement In a major respite for Indian nationals, holders of Indian passports have been exempted from the visa-bond obligation. The departments website shows that Nepal and Bangladesh have faced the mandate since January 21, whereas Bhutan was added beginning January 1.
