articleTitle: ‘I was lucky to have him’: Zinedine Zidane on Cristiano Ronaldo
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ronaldo
description: "I will always have great respect for him, as for all players, but even more so for those with whom I shared so much time," Zidane said
body_raw: Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo left the national team training camp ahead of their Nations League campaign against Norway, which has created speculation around his retirement. France will face Belgium next, and Frances head coach, Zinedine Zidane, was asked about Ronaldos poor end to his illustrious career. No, I think he should be congratulated on his great career. What he did is exceptional, Zidane said. I was lucky to have him with me and he made me win incredible things, so I take my hat off to Cristiano. I will always have great respect for him, as for all players, but even more so for those with whom I shared so much time, and in particular Cristiano, who made us win so much, said Zidane who coached Ronaldo during his time at Real Madrid. Perhaps the difference is that at a club it never stops it is day to day, it is very all-consuming. I loved doing that, and now I have another side to it and I will try to do it this way, which will be a little different. But in any case, the desire to work well around my team is the same, he added. In a press conference on Wednesday, Portugal Head coach George Jesus said that he was not planning to start Ronaldo in Portugals game against Denmark in the Nations League on Thursday, adding that there is no feud between the pair. After the said press conference, Ronaldo put out a post on Instagram saying that he would be leaving the Portugal camp which was preparing for the upcoming Nations League matches. After the national team press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp. In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave the national team, to which I always devoted myself. Now is the time to wish Portugal and all my teammates good luck, without exception, Ronaldo posted on Instagram.

articleTitle: Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 winner: Avinash Mishra takes home trophy and Rs 20 lakhs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 winner Avinash Mishra
description: Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 winner: Along with the Khatron Ke Khiladi Season 15 trophy, Avinash Mishra won prize money of Rs 20 lakh, a trip to Europe and a car.
body_raw: Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 winner Rohit Shetty-hosted stunt-based reality show Khatron Ke Khiladi returned with Season 15 in August this year after a one-year break. With the theme Darr Ka Naya Daur, the season brought together former contestants and new participants to compete against each other. After weeks of taking on challenging stunts, television actor Avinash Mishra has emerged as the winner of Khatron Ke Khiladi 15. Avinash Mishra wins Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 Avinash Mishra defeated fellow top 3 finalists Rithvik Dhanjani and Orry to lift the Khatron Ke Khiladi 15 trophy. Along with the title, Avinash won prize money of Rs 20 lakh, a trip to Europe and a car. The top 3 finalists were also given a bike. Talking about his win, Avinash said in a statement, Winning Khatron Ke Khiladi feels special because I thought I signed up for the show with a point to prove, but along the way, the person I ended up proving it to, was myself. I have spent years being associated with television and, yes, with being the good-looking guy on screen. I enjoyed that journey, but I also knew there was so much more I wanted people to see in me. This show gave me the chance to put everything else aside and literally let my actions speak. He continued, Most of this journey was actually about the mind. You can prepare yourself physically, but when you are standing at the edge of something terrifying, there is no performance left-it is just you, your fear and the decision you make in that moment. I had to learn to tune out the noise, trust myself, and keep going. There were days when I surprised myself, and those are the moments I will cherish. And to win the show after everything I have discovered about myself here is the kind of ending I could only have hoped for. I came to Khatron Ke Khiladi wanting to test myself I am leaving with a belief in myself that I didnt have before. That, for me, is the biggest victory. Right from the beginning, Avinash Mishra emerged as one of the strongest performers on the show. In fact, he did not abort a single task throughout the season and also won the Swift Immunity Jacket, which gave him the power to either save a contestant from elimination or opt out of performing a task. Despite his consistent performance in the stunts, Avinash faced stiff competition from Farrhana Bhatt and Orry from the new batch, as well as returning contestants Karan Wahi and Rithvik Dhanjani. Also Read Bigg Boss 18 finalist Avinash Mishra on his negative image I have no regrets About Avinash Mishra Avinash Mishra has been working in television for nearly a decade. Before becoming an actor, he worked as a DJ. Avinash made his acting debut in 2016 with Sethji and later appeared in Ishqbaaz in 2017. In 2018, his performance in Mariam Khan Reporting Live brought him wider recognition. A turning point in his career came with the 2022 show Nath. Avinash followed up its success with a stint on Bigg Boss 18 in 2024, where he emerged as one of the strongest contenders and finished fourth. While he was still inside the Bigg Boss 18 house, Avinash was finalised as a contestant for Khatron Ke Khiladi 15.

articleTitle: ‘Jude Bellingham can become one of the greatest players of all time’: Roy Keane
articleFeaturedImageAlt: England's Jude Bellingham in action during Nations League match against Croatia. (AP)
description: Former Manchester United captain hails England star's complete performance in 7-0 rout of Croatia, says his work off the ball inspires the entire team
body_raw: Former England footballer Roy Keane believes Jude Bellingham has it in him to become one of the finest players the game has ever seen, describing the England midfielders display in the 7-0 demolition of Croatia as a complete performance. Bellingham was at the heart of Englands biggest-ever win over Croatia, scoring once and setting up three more in Rijeka as Thomas Tuchels side ran riot in the Nations League. The 23-year-old has become the focal point of this England team, registering 13 goal involvements in his last 11 matches since the start of the World Cup. Speaking on ITV after the match, Keane was effusive in his praise for the Real Madrid star, insisting there is still more to come. Theres a lot more to come from Bellingham. He can go on to become one of the greatest players of all time, Keane was quoted as saying by Sky Sports. England thrashed Croatia in a game where skipper Harry Kane and Bukayo Saka scored braces, Anthony Gordon and Morgan Rogers also registered their names on the scoresheet apart from Bellinghams goal. The former Manchester United captain, who was famously exacting in his assessment of players during his own career, singled out Bellinghams work rate as the quality that sets him apart. I have been praising him for being fantastic in possession, but what he is doing out of possession lifts all these players, Keane said. If you have a player who is that good in your team, who is amazing in possession and is playing for Real Madrid and doing brilliant things, but his work rate off the ball, that will inspire all the other players. Croatia, a Gibraltar-type of team Keane also had a sharp assessment of Croatias performance, suggesting England made the worlds 14th-ranked side look like minnows on the night. Keane said England made Croatia, who are ranked 14th in the world, look like a Gibraltar-type of team. Englands victory was as comprehensive as the scoreline suggests, and Keane summed up the display in typically succinct fashion. Everything you would want. A complete performance, he said.

articleTitle: Inside Shahid Kapoor and Mira Rajput’s luxe home with a dramatic black staircase, majestic carpets and more
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shahid Kapoor
description: Take a look inside Shahid Kapoor and Mira Rajput’s 10,000-sq-ft Mumbai home, with a dramatic staircase, art, sculptural furniture and earthy interiors.
body_raw: alk into Shahid Kapoor and Mira Rajputs Mumbai home, and there is plenty to catch your eye. A dramatic black geometric staircase cuts through the interiors, large artworks fill the walls, sculptural furniture adds unexpected shapes, warm light adds drama, and plants bring greenery into almost every space. Yet, for a home spread across approximately 10,000 square feet, it doesnt feel like it is trying too hard to look luxurious. Instead, the four-bedroom duplex feels warm, personal and lived in - a mix of art, architecture and everyday comfort that reflects both Shahid and Miras personalities. While he likes to be a lot more experimental and creative, I only think about how practical things are and if it is easy to clean. So, it was about finding the right balance between form and function and allowing both our personalities to shine, Mira said while welcoming Architectural Digest India into their home. That balance becomes apparent as you move through the house. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. The dramatic staircase that steals the show The first thing you may notice is the staircase, which is also the Kapoors favourite. Finished in black and made up of bold geometric forms, it is far from purely functional. It acts almost like a piece of sculpture, becoming a visual anchor around which the homes spaces are arranged. The geometric black staircases in this house are used as architectural statements rather than as vertical circulation infrastructure, Manoj Goyal, Director, Forteasia Realty Pvt. Ltd tells indianexpress.com. And this is part of a larger shift in luxury home design. According to Goyal, staircases in large Indian homes and duplexes are increasingly being treated as sculptural elements, with designers experimenting with geometry, materials, lighting and finishes. Raghunandan Saraf, founder and CEO, Saraf Furniture, agrees. Geometric Black Staircase is a striking example of how architecture can transform a merely functional element into a defining design element of an interior. In Shahid and Miras home, the staircase does exactly that it gives the otherwise soft interiors a strong architectural edge. A calm palette, with plenty happening The rest of the house takes a gentler approach. Whites, creams, warm wood, black and earthy neutrals form the base, while natural light and greenery keep the spaces from feeling stark. Textured upholstery, rugs and wooden elements add warmth without disrupting the clean lines. Goyal describes the palette as a warm contemporary one, created through a mix of blacks, whites, neutrals, wood and greenery. It is also a clever backdrop for the homes most expressive elements - particularly its art. The art gives the home personality Miras love for art is evident throughout the residence. Among the pieces are a striking Yuvan Bothysathuvar work, a sculpture by Radhakrishnan and a commissioned work by Subodh Kerkar. The formal dining area, for instance, gets a strong focal point from the Yuvan Bothysathuvar painting. But the artworks dont feel as though they have simply been added to fill empty walls. Art has the power to influence the mood of a space. It helps to create a unique sense of a space and makes the space feel complete and collected, rather than decorated, Goyal says. Saraf puts it more succinctly Art adds an emotional layer to a home. Furnishings define how you use a given space. Meanwhile, art defines how the space is felt. That distinction is important here. The house feels collected rather than coordinated, as though the objects belong to the family rather than having been selected from one catalogue. Even the furniture gets to be playful The couple has not played it entirely safe with furniture either. One particularly eye-catching sofa features a paw-like base, while other pieces bring in unusual silhouettes and sculptural forms. They add little moments of surprise to an otherwise restrained interior. When a chair or sofa has an unusual silhouette, sculptural base or unexpected detail, it can function almost like an art object, Saraf says. But there is a catch statement furniture works best when the rest of the room knows when to step back. Balance is good. If you have a relatively simple palette in your architecture, you can add a few playful, unusual, unexpected pieces of furniture without overwhelming a space, Goyal explains. A design rule seems to run through the house keep the larger picture calm and let a few pieces do the talking. Look down, and youll notice a different world altogether Another, quieter design layer lies underfoot. The rugs around the seating areas rely more on texture and tonal variation than loud patterns, helping define the spaces while adding softness to the homes stone, wood and glass surfaces. Anupriya Choudhary, Director, Saraswati Rugs, was particularly drawn to the rug near the sofa. I liked how the tonal variation and texture add depth and visual interest without becoming overpowering, she tells indianexpress.com. That restraint is particularly useful in a home already filled with artwork and sculptural elements. A hand-crafted rug can bring together furniture, art and architecture through colour, scale and texture, Choudhary says. In luxury homes, she adds, rugs are increasingly being viewed as more than floor coverings. It is no longer simply a floor covering it is an important design and collectable element within the home. But this isnt just a house to look at Beyond the carefully curated living spaces, the home has plenty of room for actual living. The upper level includes a glam room, guest suite, home theatre and lounge, Shahids DJ setup, an open-air gym, a small pantry and an office. The expansive balcony has also been treated as an extension of the living room, with seating and greenery rather than being left as a purely decorative outdoor space. The family designed the home entirely online over 14 months during the Covid pandemic, making it particularly meaningful to them. This house is where the four of us Mira, Shahid and their two kids have found ourselves all together our first one for all of us, Mira said. Her idea of home also has roots in her childhood. Growing up, my mom loved entertaining. She really is the perfect hostess, and there were always people at our house. Thats the kind of home I wanted to create, full of fresh flowers and enough food on the table. Thats something I wanted to recreate, that feeling of an inviting home. And that perhaps explains why the house doesnt feel overly precious. There is art, but also comfortable seating. There are statement pieces, but also greenery and open spaces. A dramatic staircase, but plenty of warmth around it. The new idea of luxury Perhaps the most interesting thing about Shahid and Miras home isnt its size or even its collection of expensive-looking pieces. It is how selectively those pieces have been used. Goyal believes luxury housing is moving toward what he calls the curated lifestyle house-a home that reflects the person living in it rather than simply signalling how much they spent. Saraf sees the same evolution. I dont see the future in the luxury of personal homes becoming centred in the overfill of rooms with expensive objects. Rather, I see those homes becoming selective in the quality of pieces and how those pieces become instrumental in developing the houses character. And perhaps that is what makes this home memorable. It doesnt just look luxurious. It looks like someone actually lives there - someone with an eye for art, a weakness for beautiful objects and, judging by Miras description, a very strong preference for a home where there is always something good to eat. articleTitle: Kumkum, Sujeet named inaugural recipients of Jaspal Rana & Raja Randhir Singh awards
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Archer Kumkum Mohor and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal with their medals at Asian Games 2026. (AP)
description: IOA honours the two standout performers of India's Asian Games campaign in Aichi-Nagoya
body_raw: Archer Kumkum Anil Mohod and wrestler Sujeet Kalkal have been named the first-ever recipients of the Jaspal Rana Award and the Raja Randhir Singh Award respectively by the Indian Olympic Association, in recognition of their performances at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. The awards have been instituted by the IOA to honour the best female and male sportspersons of the Games, and to commemorate the legacy of two stalwarts of Indian sport who passed away earlier this year. Kumkum, 17, making her Asian Games debut, claimed three medals, including two gold, and was central to ending South Koreas long-standing dominance in womens recurve archery. Alongside Ankita Bhakat and Kirti, she won the womens recurve team gold, snapping South Koreas run of seven consecutive Asian Games titles dating back to the 1998 Bangkok Games. ALSO READ  Surfeit of silver paints a picture of what could have been for India at Asiad Kumkum then followed it up with gold in the individual event, ensuring South Koreas women failed to win a recurve gold at the Asian Games for the first time in the disciplines history. Her individual gold also secured a quota place for India at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Sujeet, 23, was named the inaugural recipient of the Raja Randhir Singh Award after winning gold in the mens 65kg freestyle wrestling category. He produced one of the most dramatic performances of the Games, defeating reigning Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka of Japan in the semifinal before staging a remarkable comeback in the gold-medal bout against Abdulmazhid Kudiyev, trailing 2-9 with time running out before fighting back to secure a 10-9 victory. ALSO READ  How Kumkum Mohod beat best in world to win historic archery gold in Asiad Sujeet also continued Indias strong tradition in the 65kg category, following Olympic medallists Yogeshwar Dutt and Bajrang Punia, who won gold in the same weight class at the 2014 and 2018 Asian Games respectively. The IOA will felicitate Kumkum and Sujeet at a ceremony in the coming days. India finished fourth in the Asian Games medal standings with 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze medals. With PTI inputs

articleTitle: Are all medals equally significant? The top five out of the 85
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Medals
description: A look at the podium finishes which broke new ground for India and raised hopes for even bigger honours in the future
body_raw: Asian Games 2026 Indias breakthrough medals Not all medals are equal, some carry more importance than others due to the tougher competition in the event or the historical significance of the achievement. Here are five such feats by Indians at Aichi-Nagoya Womens Hockey Gold India finished on the top of the podium when the event made its debut at the 1982 Asian Games. It took 44 years for an encore as the side led by Salima Tete and guided by Dutch coach Sjoerd Marijne put it across 2024 Paris Olympic silver medallists China in the final. What makes the achievement all the more special is that it comes with a direct berth at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games. India had missed out on Paris after finishing narrowly outside the medals at the previous edition in Tokyo. Now, the players, coaches and administrators can put all their focus on doing their best at the Olympics and even vying for a medal. Wrestling Aman Sehrawat Mens 57 kg category gold By beating reigning world champion Han Chong Song of North Korea in the final, Aman has added another feather in his cap after his bronze at the 2024 Paris Olympics. It is Indias first-ever gold medal in the 57 kg category, one of the most competitive in the world. Another wrestling medal of note is Nitesh Siwachs silver in the mens 97 kg Greco-Roman category, the first for India in 64 years. Archery Kumkum Mohod Womens recurve individual gold Archery has been there in the Asian Games since 1978 but no Indian woman recurve archer had made the individual final despite the likes of Dola Banerjee and Deepika Kumari featuring in the category. It took 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod to break the jinx. She didnt just enter the final but also defeated Korean shooter Oh Je-yin to win the gold medal, also taking the Olympic quota. The womens team gold meant India ended the 28-year-old Korean stranglehold in the event, raising Indian hopes two years before the Los Angeles Games. Shooting Neeru Dhanda Womens Trap gold Rifle and pistol are disciplines in shooting that usually contribute the bulk of Indian medals at the Asian Games, but for the first time in history, it was the shotgun section that won more gold medals than the other two. The main protagonist was 26-year-old Neeru Dhanda from Haryana. The shooter is having an impressive year with a World Cup gold and now two gold at Aichi-Nagoya. Her trap individual gold was first for India in the discipline since Randhir Singh climbed the top of the podium at the 1978 edition. Athletics Sawan Barwal Mens marathon silver India had never won an Asian Games marathon medal outside the country. National record holder Sawan Barwal clocked 21137 to win the silver in the event, ending a 44-year-old medal drought. In the process, he improved upon his own national mark, doing so at a big stage. Indias previous three medals came in the event had come in 1982 Bronze and 1951 Gold and Bronze, both those editions staged in Delhi. Barwals achievement is all the more praiseworthy as 10 runners on the start list had better personal best timings than him, but yet the Indian managed to better his own and the countrys mark. That too in rainy conditions.

articleTitle: Disenfranchising millions arbitrary, no whataboutery can justify it: SC judge
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan warns wholesale disenfranchisement under Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls violates Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution
description: “From the persona of an Indian citizen, the right to vote or right to be included in the voters' list cannot be detached. It will be like taking out the soul from the body,” Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said
body_raw: Amid the row over the SIR of electoral rolls against which petitions have been filed in the Supreme Court, Justice Ujjal Bhuyan, a judge of the top court, said Sunday that any process that leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of the Constitution. No amount of whataboutery can justify it, he said. Justice Bhuyan said detaching an Indian citizen from the right to vote would be akin to taking out the soul from the body. Speaking at the valedictory ceremony of Justice Bodh Raj Sawhney Memorial Moot Court competition at Nalsar University of Law, Hyderabad, he said, If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second-class citizens in their own country, in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary. No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of the Constitution and I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order, which we have adopted under the Constitution of India, he said. Speaking on the significance of universal adult suffrage, especially in the context of India, Justice Bhuyan said, From the persona of an Indian citizen, the right to vote or right to be included in the voters list cannot be detached. It will be like taking out the soul from the body. He said the earliest articulation of adult franchise in India can be traced to the Constitution of India Bill, 1895, also known as the Swaraj Bill. Speaking about the debate in the Constituent Assembly on universal adult suffrage, he said, In the draft Constitution, which was debated by the Constituent Assembly, there were two articles of relevance, though included subsequently. These were Articles 289A and 289B. Draft Article 289A became Article 325 and draft Article 289B became Article 326 of the Constitution of India. Article 326 gives meaning and content to the equality principle enshrined in Article 14. Article 325 of the Constitution of India declares that there shall be one general electoral roll for every territorial constituency for election to the Lok Sabha or to the Legislature of a State no person shall be ineligible for inclusion in any such roll or claim to be included in any electoral roll for any such constituency on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or any of them. As per Article 326 of the Constitution, election to the Lok Sabha and to the Legislative Assembly of every State shall be on the basis of adult suffrage. In other words, every person who is a citizen of India and who is not less than 18 years of age prior to March 28, 1989, it was 21 years and who is not disqualified under the Constitution of India or by any law made by the appropriate legislature on the ground of non-residence, unsoundness of mind, crime or corrupt or illegal practice, shall be entitled to be registered as a voter at any such election, he said. Quoting Dr B R Ambedkar, Justice Bhuyan said, Justifying universal adult suffrage, Dr Ambedkar said since we have taken a very important decision, which practically nullifies the past, it is better that the Constitution should, in express terms, state it is the basis for insertion of Articles 289A and 289B in the draft Constitution, which are now Articles 325 and 326. Dr Ambedkars closing speech warned that the right to vote and the Indian citizens entitlement to adult suffrage should be written into the Constitution of India, instead of being left to the whims of parliamentary legislation, he said. Justice Bhuyan said, Adoption of universal adult franchise reflects the determined opinion of the Constituent Assembly that years of freedom struggle and the revolt against foreign rule made the adoption of universal adult franchise a natural choice and an essential ingredient of democracy, which we have adopted as the form of governance. Therefore, it was an act of faith for our founding fathers in the common man of India and in his pragmatism and wisdom. It was the first step taken to achieve equality in India. One may be a billionaire, and one may be a rickshaw-puller. Yet both will have their votes, and the value of their votes would be equal. Likewise, a socially high-placed temple priest on the one hand and a person belonging to the lowest strata of the society compelled to work as a manual scavenger have an equal vote with equal value. This is the transformational vision of the Indian Constitution, he said. In his concluding remarks, he congratulated Nalsar students for being what students, especially law students, should be.

articleTitle: Surfeit of silver paints a picture of ‘what could have been’ for India at Asiad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: (Clockwise) India's Tajinderpal Singh Toor, Esha Singh, Elavenil Valarivan, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Ancy Sojan with their silver medals at 2026 Asian Games. (PTI & AP)
description: Aichi-Nagoya showed that competition has got tougher in the continent, and even personal best performances may not always be enough to challenge the cream
body_raw: Day 1 A 10.4 and 10.1 from Elavenil Valarivan on her last two shots of the 10m air rifle erased the Indians handy 1.5 lead, to see the first gold missed by India at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. What gets lost in the lament over the 27 silvers is acknowledgement that Japans Hinata Taichi shot 10.6 and 10.2 to snatch that gold - coming out of the blue, given Japan didnt have a single medal in this event since 1994. India finished tied on gold with Uzbekistan at 21, and only a last-day scramble helped push it up, with two extra silvers giving it fourth place. But all those silvers were gold medals lost. Accepting that even Indias best-ever showing in womens air rifle, Elavenils silver, might not be good enough for gold is central to understanding why the country was stuck at just four the first week, reaching double digits 10 only on the 11th day of the Games. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage The ultimate tally of 21 was seven off the 2023 Asiad with 28 gold, while total medal haul was 21 less than the 106 at Hangzhou. The drop has come in several sports Shooting 22 to 15 4 golds less, Athletics 29 to 24 5 gold less, Tennis 2 to 0 1 gold less, Badminton 3 to 1 1 gold less Rowing 6 to 1 Equestrian 2 to 0 1 gold less. While archery made fantastic gains in recurve, its total count stayed constant at nine from 2023, with five gold medals, the same as last time. Squash retained its five medals, but with a significant drop of two gold. Wrestling has maintained its count of six. While men added two gold to the nil last time, and won five of the six Indian medals, womens wrestling dropped from three last time to the one silver upgrade of Antim Panghal. Sujeet Kalkal and Aman Sehrawat will be expected to carry the momentum to Los Angeles. ALSO READ  As the Asian Games close, with a last-minute gold rush, India finish fourth Boxing made real gains, going up from five to six medals-and significantly three gold from none last time. The golf gold for Pranavi Urs is an uptick, as is the womens team silver. However, a few medal drops are worrying. In badminton, Lakshya Sen could not defend HS Prannoy bronze while Ayush Shetty had a poor Games. Asiad medals are toughest in badminton, and Satwik-Chirag gold was missing in the 2026 tally. Shooting sent a star-studded womens air pistol troika, but a medal was nowhere in sight after poor qualifications. While Suruchi Phogat salvaged matters with a strong comeback for the Mixed Team gold and Esha Singh fought four shoot-offs to take sports pistol silver, individual golds were out of reach till Neeru Dhanda won in trap. India had regressed in 50m 3 position since the Paris Olympics, with two silvers in the event, while they had won two gold in Hangzhou, among other medals. Hits and misses Parul Chaudhary recorded her Personal Best PB in 5,000m to take a second bronze. Steeplechaser Avinash Sable, defending a gold medal, did his seasons best but missed a medal by four seconds to finish fourth. The next rung in steeplechase isnt on the horizon. Other freakish circumstances struck. Murali Sreesankar, looking to upgrade his silver, slipped on the takeoff on his fourth attempt and was in no position to contend for gold. Two Chinese did their best in their fifth attempt to leapfrog Ancy Sojan in the long jump. The Indian could not summon a 6.60 jump, though her best this season is a national record. Hurdler Jyothi Yarraji, triple jumper Praveen Chitravel and decathlete Thowfeeq Noushad couldnt register a mark to be in contention in their events. While AFI president Adille Sumariwala had stressed that the athletes would peak at the Asiad, the periodisation seemed to have gone awry as the push for the Commonwealth Games disrupted fitness for Asiad, including taking Neeraj Chopra out of contention. The two big events within two months of each other also saw some athletes bomb at both places. The rowing federation switched up combinations two days before the race, after crews had trained together for four years. They got an Australian expert to convey the news, and he didnt explain why his plan for gold didnt come through, or why the rowers were not kept in the loop. No gold fetched up either it was chaos injected into an erstwhile well-oiled unit. Equestrian was blighted by contested selections. A gold and bronze from Hangzhou got casually tossed out, finishing at zero. Some losses are nuanced - could Gulveer Singh have focused on one event and gone all out for gold, instead of four races in five days, finishing with two silver and one bronze? Are double-starters in shooting those who are fielded in two events costing India gold? Track and field athletes scored 11 personal bests, nine silvers and three seasons bests. But the net result was one gold. It proves both that the competition has levelled up and Indians, even at their best, are only playing catch-up.

articleTitle: ‘Turn that music off’: Vijay Deverakonda’s blunt first words to Rashmika Mandanna on set
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rashmika Mandanna, Vijay Deverakonda
description: In a recent interview, Vijay Deverakonda recalled how he once dismissed love as merely a marketing term. Rashmika Mandanna, meanwhile, opened up about the importance of expressing affection and making small gestures in a relationship.
body_raw: Actors Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna recently opened up about their relationship, their journey from co-stars to life partners and how their understanding of love has evolved over the years. The couple also spoke about the little efforts that keep a relationship going. When Prakhar Gupta asked Vijay if he knew instantly that Rashmika was the one when they first met, the actor dismissed the idea of love at first sight. The Liger actor said, No. Can you ever know instantly? I dont believe in love at first sight. I need to go through a journey for love. You can know instantly that she is beautiful. But can you know instantly that she is the one? No. I knew nothing about her. I did think that she was a very beautiful girl but when I met her, I guess it was my third or fourth film. So, its more about the excitement of being on set, nervous of being on day 1 with a new team, and the aspiration of doing something successful. First day on any set is nerve-racking. Youre not comfortable enough to think about love and such. It has been eight years since we first met. Rashmika, however, corrected him about the timeline of their first meeting, saying, No, its been 9 years since we met but 8 years since our film released. Vijay jokingly responded, So, that film is my marker for how long I have known her. Vijay Deverakonda also spoke about how his perception of love was very different when he was younger. He admitted that he once considered love a marketing term and questioned the idea of falling in love more than once. The actor said, First of all, at that age, I was somebody who didnt believe in love, I was around 28-29. If you look at my interviews from then, youll see that I talk very disrespectfully about love, from a distance, and that comes from a place of young energy. I thought love is a marketing term. Weve all fallen in love multiple times in life. So, what does love mean? If I can fall in love with somebody and then I can fall in love with somebody else, then this is bullshit. So, I used to talk like this a lot. He added, You feel your mothers love, dont you? There is love where people think about you more than themselves. It took growing up and maturity to understand that. Dont disrespect the love in your life. Dont say love is a marketing term. Respect it, appreciate it, nurture it. So, for that journey, it took me many years. When I got an understanding about these things, then I started looking at love and relationships differently. Also Read Digital equivalent of sexual assault Vijay Deverakonda on Janhvi Kapoors AI deepfake video Vijay revealed that he only felt ready for marriage when he was 36, admitting that maturity played an important role in his decision. Rashmika Mandanna playfully interrupted him, telling him, Baby, you were late. Vijay said, When I was 36, I finally felt, I feel like getting married. I felt that I was ready and mature to understand this, to love it, I felt ready. Rashmika Mandanna says love is about making small efforts, Vijay Deverakonda calls her the more mature one Talking about what keeps a relationship strong, Rashmika Mandanna stressed that people often make efforts for those around them but tend to take their partners for granted. The Cocktail 2 actor said, We human beings always have to keep making efforts for the people that we love. Because most often we make a lot of efforts for people around than the people at your own house. I keep thinking that after getting married, you stop telling each other some very basic things. Something like Good morning, Are you doing well? or How was your day? It becomes, My partner already knows, so whats the point of saying it? And then, at some point, it could become, Why havent I heard this in such a long time? Meanwhile, life keeps pulling us in different directions. She further emphasised that these efforts should continue even after marriage and having children. Efforts, no matter how much into the relationship or marriage you are or even if you have kids together, I still feel like those little efforts should be made for each other, and that is love. It should be effortless but also you need to do these things because you want to do these things. Thats something that I believe in love. Vijay Deverakonda agreed with Rashmika Mandanna and called her the more mature one when it came to relationships. Vijay said, Rashmika is more mature when it comes to relationships. Look at how shes talking. She makes sure she tells me I love you at least 10-15 times a day, and she tells me that its important for me to express it too. I constantly feel it, but I shouldnt think, Okay, she knows it, so I dont need to say it. She reminds me of that, which makes me more aware because we are so caught up in life that sometimes we can forget these smaller, simpler but important things. He also opened up about being a control freak and how it took him time to trust the relationship and allow things to fall into place naturally. The Liger actor said, So, she is the one who actually made me. I was worried for the longest time whether I will be able to drive this because I am a control freak, and I was wondering if I left the steering, will it work automatically? My 4-5 years went in that laughs. She knew that the car was working, and would say, You relax. By nature, thats probably your upbringing, childhood. You are who you are because of everything that you dont even remember. Everything shapes you into the kind of person that you are. Vijay became emotional while talking about Rashmika and how she ensured that their relationship stood the test of time. He said, Shes somebody who always made sure that this relationship got through every obstacle and lasted. Rashmika Mandanna recalls Vijay Deverakonda calling her music shitty on Geetha Govindam sets Recalling her first meeting with Vijay Deverakonda on the sets of Geetha Govindam, Rashmika Mandanna revealed that she initially addressed him as sir because he was more experienced in the industry. She also remembered an incident from the first day of the shoot when Vijay asked her to turn off the music she was playing, leaving her upset. She said, I remember when I first met him on set, I used to call him sir because I was new into the industry and he had done 3-4 films by that time. On Day 1, I was playing this random music on the set, and he goes like, Turn that music off. Vijay interrupted and said, I am a blunt person, and I assume everyone to understand the intention. I feel like, we should be able to talk freely, openly but sometimes when you dont know each other fully, it was stupid of me to assume, shell get it. I just casually said, What is this shitty music that youre playing? I shouted because we had to share a locked caravan in between but because we were not big stars, so half caravan was for her, and half was for me and my team. I screamed, What is this shitty music that you are playing? Rashmika pointed out that it was hardly the ideal thing to hear from a co-actor, especially when she was new to the industry. She said, That is the first thing your co-actor is telling you, right? Vijay responded, What should I say? Rashmika added, Youre absolutely right. Now that I think about it, I wonder what that was all about. Vijay then revealed that the incident had deeply affected Rashmika, although she did not tell him about it at the time. He said, She had tears in her eyes because she thought that he doesnt like me. Rashmika explained, Because it is a new place, new industry. Vijay recalled, She thought it is going to be a torture like this. She told me this much later. Rashmika admitted, Yes, for a long time, I hadnt said it. When Vijay asked why she had not spoken about it earlier, Rashmika explained that she was extremely sensitive at the time and would get emotional over even the smallest things. However, as they began working together, their equation gradually changed. Rashmika said, I was extremely sensitive and everything would tear me up. Going to the set and there were these situations when we started working in the film, he would help me with the dialogues, and everytime I used to call him sir, he used to be like, Stop calling me that. I have a name, call me that then of course, it became Vijay, and then we became friends. She revealed that working on two consecutive films together gave them the opportunity to spend a lot of time with each other, eventually turning them into close friends. Rashmika added, Because we did two back-to-back films with each other, we sort of spent so much time with each other, we were pretty much talking to each other the whole day, you are shooting and prepping for the same film. Hence, it became like. he was my best friend back then, and then much later on, I was like, Okay, I am feeling something, and this is not. Rashmika Mandanna says God had a hand in her relationship with Vijay Deverakonda Rashmika also spoke about how her feelings for Vijay developed over time and said that she believes a higher power guided their relationship. What began as a friendship eventually turned into love, with the couple finding their way to each other. The Animal actor said, I just feel that God has his hand in our relationship, in our love. There is some sort of supreme power who has guided us into this. Hence, the wedding happened and here we are. Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna are currently gearing up for the release of their period drama Ranabaali, which marks another on-screen reunion for the actors. Directed by Rahul Sankrityan and produced by Naveen Yerneni and Y Ravi Shankar under the banner of Mythri Movie Makers, the period action drama is scheduled to release in theatres worldwide on October 16, 2026.

articleTitle: Domestic capacity, reforms key amid global uncertainty: Shaktikanta Das
articleFeaturedImageAlt: On the external front, Das said India's financial sector and prudent management had also emerged as strong pillars of economic growth. (Image: Ministry of Finance)
description: India is within striking distance of 8% growth, said Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister at the Kautilya Economic Conclave
body_raw: Amid sustained shocks and global uncertainties, India seeks to emphasise on sustained structural reforms, building domestic capacity and competence in areas where there is large import dependence, and continuously focusing on fiscal, monetary, macroeconomic and macrofinancial stability, Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, said on Sunday. Das further said that the country stands at a pivotal moment in its development journey and a leap to Viksit Bharat 2047 is in the realm of realisation, adding that India is within a striking distance of 8 growth. There can never be a moment where you can say that, whatever I have done is sufficient. There is always something more to do but in the current context. The emphasis has been to build our domestic capacity, competence in areas where we are largely import dependent. So, whether it is energy or fertiliser and so many other areas, the government is now focusing on such areas. the focus of the government is also to take measures and to develop long-term capacity in areas where again we are dependent on imports, Das said while answering a question on day two of the three-day Kautilya Economic Conclave organised by the Ministry of Finance and the Institute of Economic Growth. Calling for strategic self-reliance, Das said self-reliance or Atmanirbharta should not mean isolation. Rather, it stands for building stronger domestic capabilities while remaining integrated with global markets and concluding more free trade agreements, he said. Das underlined that Indias real GDP grew by an impressive 7.8 in Q1 of 2026-27, adding that if the period from July-September 2025-26 to April-June 2026-27 is taken into account, real GDP growth in India just exceeds 8. This resonates with my statement to Financial Times London a few months ago that India is within a striking distance of 8 growth, he said. Reforms undertaken over the past decade were not one-off measures but were designed to build buffers that would help the economy absorb disruptions and recover rapidly, he said. Indias resilience is not accidental. It is the outcome of broad and mutually reinforcing reforms, he said. The former Reserve Bank of India governor cited flexible inflation targeting, the introduction of the goods and services tax, fiscal prudence, the push for digital payments and banking sector reforms among such measures. On the external front, Das said Indias financial sector and prudent management had also emerged as strong pillars of economic growth. External sector indicators have remained broadly resilient, supported by export diversification, free trade agreements, a sustained surplus in services trade and steady inward remittances, he said. Going ahead, Das said India must harness the artificial intelligence AI revolution to sustain high growth. Indias AI strategy rests on two complementary pillars. First, sovereign AI capability through investments in indigenous foundation models, high-performance computing infrastructure, semiconductor developments and robust innovation ecosystem, he said. He also called for deepening the financial sector to support Indias expanding economic weight. While Indias financial sector has evolved significantly, the next phase of growth will require strengthening of long-term finance and patient capital, Das said. This would require further deepening of the corporate bond market, pension and insurance funds, municipal finance and innovative infrastructure financing, he added.

articleTitle: Safari season is back: What to know before visiting India’s national parks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: First-time safari-goers should look beyond tiger sightings and observe the wider forest ecosystem in National Parks.
description: As India’s national parks reopen after the monsoon, experts share what first-time safari-goers should know before heading into the forest.
body_raw: Monsoon is when our forests breathe without disturbance. However, after being closed or operating with restrictions during the rainy months, several national parks and wildlife sanctuaries are now reopening for visitors. From Ranthambore and Sariska Tiger Reserves in Rajasthan to Jim Corbett National Park in Uttarakhand and other wildlife destinations, the reopening marks the return of the safari season in several parts of the country. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Talking about Jim Corbett, Ajay Kareer, general manager, Corbett Hideaway, Jim Corbett - IHCL SeleQtions says, Every reopening of Corbett after the monsoon brings a renewed sense of anticipation for wildlife enthusiasts. The forest is dense and green, the Kosi is flowing at its fullest, and there is movement everywhere, from birds and butterflies to elephants and deer emerging into the open. Know these before heading for your first safari For those heading out on their first safari, the anticipation of a tiger sighting is naturally a major part of the excitement. However, experts say that visitors should approach a safari with a broader understanding of the forest and the inhabitants. Renuka Natu, Founder of Africa with Renuka, and Kareer share certain things travellers should keep in mind Tread carefully as you re-enter wild spaces. Take a moment to soak in all that the backdrop has to offer the birds, the bees, the butterflies the wasps the bears the antelope the elephants and the tigers. Visitors should look beyond just the tiger and notice the many signs of a thriving ecosystem. An alarm call, a herd moving through the grass or a fresh pugmark can turn an ordinary stretch of forest into a moment of discovery. Take note of the necessary guidelines and respect animals space, rather than expecting every safari to deliver a particular sighting. The most memorable safaris are often those where you slow down, observe and allow the forest to reveal itself in all its song and glory. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to.

articleTitle: Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi going to be in India’s ODI mix a lot: Shubman Gill
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gill
description: Stating that there is "not much time to experiment" before the 2027 World Cup, India captain Shubman Gill admitted the team must find a way to get its star players back on the field by the next ODI series in New Zealand
body_raw: In a series where the batting mainstays bought themselves a truckload of runs, India were still pushed for a hard reset and review by the time West Indies seized a record 352-run chase in the final ODI in New Chandigarh on Saturday. In as many games that Shubman Gill, Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul piled on five centuries, the bowling department has looked depleted, both in wicket-taking ability and combinations. Within six days, India fiddled with six seam-bowling options, sharing eight wickets between them. The attack often lacked a proven figurehead across phases in the absence of Jasprit Bumrah, Indias only sure-shot bowling pick in a full-strength XI. However, a spate of injuries and overlapping assignments have meant that Indias first-choice players have rarely convened in Gills first year in charge of the ODI side. Now a year left to the World Cup, Gill admitted the team must find a way to get its star players back on the field by the next ODI series in New Zealand, starting next month. I think there is not much time to experiment. The combination that we want to play, hopefully, we get all the players that are available from the next series, and we would like to start playing with the combination that we want in the World Cup, Gill told reporters after Indias five-wicket defeat. Besides Bumrah, India are missing Hardik Pandya, the cornerstone of all combinations the team adopts in the format. In their sustained absence, India have rotated with untested new-ball bowling options with an emphasis on seamers who can contribute with the bat at number eight. The team management rushed domestic First-Class performers Auqib Nabi and Anshul Kamboj for ODI debuts this week despite their limited white-ball records. Touted for the Test cap after a record-breaking Ranji Trophy season, Nabi opened the bowling on debut and leaked 84 runs in 8.4 overs on a batting paradise in Guwahati. Kamboj had seemed far from a national return after his listless Test debut in Manchester last year. Batting number 8, he struck two sixes in nine deliveries. Opening the attack, Kamboj struggled for rhythm against the West Indies top order. In a chase led by captain Shai Hopes unbeaten 162, the Haryana pacer eventually conceded 82 runs in nine overs. Notwithstanding their tough initiations, Gill backed Nabi and Kamboj to feature in the plans moving forward, offering a peek into the emphasis on seamers who can contribute with the bat. Anshul and Auqib are the kind of players who are going to be in the mix a lot. Anshul can bat at number 8. And that number is very crucial for us. We dont know who will be fit at the World Cup. And if we want someone who can bowl and can bat a bit at number 8, Anshul and even Auqib can do the job, the skipper said. They would have liked to have done a much better job. But its a little bit harsh on them. Its not easy to come and be able to deliver straight away. In international cricket, sometimes you require a bit of time. I hope that they learn from their mistakes, from the opportunities that they get, Gill added.

articleTitle: Flare-up at SRFTI as Hindu outfit protesters hurl bricks, bottles at students
articleFeaturedImageAlt: srfti
description: Students had earlier expressed concerns to I&B Ministry over protest march, and asked Kolkata Police not to give permission for rally
body_raw: A week after clashes at Kolkatas SRFTI over an RSS-linked outfits event on the campus, tension flared up at the film institute again on Sunday evening as members of a Hindu outfit hurled bricks and bottles at the students from outside. Members of the Bangiyo Hindu Jagaran Manch BHJM, who held a protest march, alleging insults to Swami Vivekananda and Bharat Mata by SRFTI students, also scuffled with the police as they tried to enter the SRFTI campus, leaving some of the policemen injured. According to students, they wrote to Kolkata Police and the West Bengal government on Saturday, asking them not to allow Bangiyo Hindu Jagaran Manch to hold the march, and to deploy adequate police personnel for their safety and security. A similar letter was sent to Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw by students of FTII Pune, SRFTI Kolkata, and FTII Itanagar, expressing serious concerns over the security of students at the institutes Kolkata campus in the aftermath of the September 27 clash on the campus. On Sunday, members of the Bangiyo Hindu Jagaran Manch reached the gates of the SRTFI on the EM Bypass and tried to enter the campus. They shouted slogans against the institute, calling the students of SRTFI Naxalites. They must be thrown out. They have insulted Bharat Maa. We will not tolerate this. They either have to love India or have to leave India, shouted a protester. Inside the campus, the students and teachers were seen deflecting the bottles and bricks thrown at them by protesters and chanting slogans like Go Back, No entry to fascists. A student of the SRFTI alleged that the protesters tore down the pictures of Dr BR Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi and instead put pictures of Bharat Maa on the gates of the institute. In a letter to the Minister of Information and Broadcasting, the students wrote, We have been informed that a rally organised by the Hindu Jagran Manch is proposed to take place on October 4 at 4 pm, approximately 800 metres from the main gate of the SRFTI. This comes barely a week after the violent confrontation on the SRFTI campus, in which several students and members of the institute community were injured. In the present circumstances, the proposed rally in such close proximity to the institute has understandably caused serious concern among the students. The SRFTI students are presently engaging with the concerned authorities to seek that the rally not be permitted within the periphery of the institute. Last Sunday, a group of students objected to an event of Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat, an RSS-linked outfit, on the campus, leading to clashes. The students union of the SRFTI said that members of ABGP assaulted students and teachers and called them anti-nationals, urban naxals and terrorists. A day later, three FIRs were registered on Monday-two against unknown students and one against unknown persons. Taking suo motu cognizance of the incident, the Kolkata Police filed an FIR against unknown students. Another FIR, registered on a complaint filed by Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat ABGP, the RSS-linked outfit, also named unknown students. Only the FIR, based on a complaint lodged by SRFTI Dean Film Sukanta Majumder, was filed against unknown persons. All three FIRs more or less include BNS sections of wrongful restraint, assault on public servants, voluntarily causing harm, and criminal intimidation. It was alleged that ABGP members wrongfully restrained students and two faculty members of the institute, voluntarily caused hurt, insulted women students modesty, and also threatened them. Two days later, the BJP government in the state formed a six-member Special Investigation Team to probe the September 27 violence on the campus.

articleTitle: Appointing the Election Commission: An Expert Explains what Constituent Assembly said
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Election Commission
description: The controversy is really about whether the appointment process produces the appearance of independence. The system should be such that selection of Election Commissioners should not only be impartial but also appear to be so.
body_raw: On June 15, 1949, a little-remembered member of the Constituent Assembly named Shibban Lal Saxena rose to object to a deceptively simple clause. The draft Constitution said the President would appoint Indias Election Commissioners. In a parliamentary system, Saxena pointed out, that meant the government of the day would effectively be choosing the referee for its own contests. It is quite possible that some party in power who wants to win the next election may appoint a staunch party-man as the chief Election Commissioner, he warned. Saxena was careful to say he wasnt accusing anyone in the room. He even called the sitting Prime Minister lucky to have the independence and impartiality he did. But that, he said, was exactly the problem with resting a constitutional safeguard on the character of one man. We are making a Constitution for ever, and not only for today, he said. Saxena proposed that appointing an Election Commissioner should require a two-thirds majority in Parliament not to make the Commission answerable to Parliament, but to make it impossible for one party to install its own nominee. The Assembly voted his proposal down. But the warning stayed on the record. The next day, H N Kunzru pushed further. Provincial governments had been kept out of election administration because they might be politically biased. Fair enough, he said - but why assume the Central Government would be any less capable of bias? Is there no danger that the political prejudice of the Central Government may prevail where otherwise the prejudices of the provincial Government might have prevailed? Kunzru wanted safeguards strong enough that Commissioners could act fearlessly, and then delivered a stark warning Worked by people whose integrity cannot be depended upon, democracy will be poisoned at the source. How the Chief Election Commissioner is appointed Even B R Ambedkar didnt dismiss the concern. He called it one of the Drafting Committees greatest headaches. He considered borrowing the American model, where the Senate confirms presidential appointments, but worried it would import its own political games. The eventual compromise the Constitution would establish the Election Commission and shield the Chief Election Commissioner from easy removal, but leave Parliament to legislate the actual appointment mechanism. That became Article 324 - a foundation with the front door deliberately left unlocked. For 74 years, Parliament never walked through that door. No law was passed. Then, in 2023, the Supreme Court did what Parliament hadnt in Anoop Baranwal v. Union of India, it ruled that until Parliament acted, appointments should be recommended by a committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition, and the Chief Justice of India CJI, a structure built to keep any one side from controlling the outcome. Parliament did act and excluded the CJI from the selection committee. The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, replaced the CJI on the selection panel with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. The committee today is the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition, and a minister the Prime Minister himself picks. Two of three seats effectively answer to the same person. The perception of impartiality None of this proves an Election Commissioner appointed under the new law will act improperly, or that the Commission has turned partisan. But it does raise a legitimate constitutional question, and its almost exactly the one Saxena and Kunzru asked in 1949 does this appointment mechanism give the government enough distance from the body that referees elections involving the government itself? Simply put In an election, the government is one of the contestants. The Election Commission is the referee. The question was never whether the referee will actually favour one side. Actually, most of the time, individual Commissioners will do their jobs honestly. The question is whether a system that lets one contestant hold disproportionate sway over who gets to referee should be designed. This is precisely why Saxena refused to let the Constitutions safeguards depend on who happened to be Prime Minister at the time. His argument was structural, not personal. Its a design principle, not a character judgment, and it holds regardless of who sits in which chair today. The system should be such that the selection of the referee should not only be impartial but also appear to be so. Which is also why this controversy isnt really about any individual Commissioners competence or integrity. Its about whether the architecture of appointment produces both the right incentives and the right perception - because in institutions of this kind, the appearance of independence often matters as much as the fact of it. A referee no one fully trusts is, for practical purposes, no referee at all. Seventy-seven years after Kunzrus warning against a flawed electoral machinery, the argument has looped back to that exact source who chooses the people who run the machinery? The Constituent Assembly saw the danger clearly, debated it seriously, and then - perhaps wisely, perhaps not - left the final answer to a Parliament that would one day have to decide for itself. Whether Parliament decided well is the debate we are having today, but whats striking is how little the terms of that debate have changed. Sometimes, the sharpest commentary on the present isnt written by todays columnists at all. It was spoken, on the floor of the Constituent Assembly, by those who could not have known exactly how the future would test their words, only that it eventually would. The author is a former IAS officer and economist. He was CEO of Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana AB-PMJAY and the National Health Authority.

articleTitle: 54 years, five languages, zero repetitions: Singeetham Srinivasa Rao was one of a kind
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao
description: In a career spanning 54 years and five languages, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao attempted things no other Indian filmmaker dared to try: A dialogue-free comedy, a time-travel science fiction, a high-fantasy adventure rooted in folklore. And at 94, a musical fantasy.
body_raw: The easiest way to understand what Singeetham Srinivasa Rao meant to Indian cinema is to list what he did and then try to find another filmmaker who did the same. He made a film without dialogue. He made a film with a time machine. He made a film set on a mythical island ruled by a sorcerer. He made a film about a classical dancer who lost her leg and returned to the stage. He made a film where the comedy was entirely physical, entirely visual, entirely dependent on the audiences ability to follow a story through images alone. And then, at 94, he made one more film because he was not done. Find another Indian filmmaker who did all of this. Not one of these. All of these. Across five languages. Across six decades. Without a single repetition. You will not find one. Because there is no one else. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, who died at Kauvery Hospital in Chennai on Saturday night at the age of 94, was not merely an experimental filmmaker. He was the filmmaker against whom every other attempt at innovation in Indian cinema must be measured, and one who, measured against anyone else, invariably comes out ahead. Also Read Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao dies at 94 The experiment nobody believed in The story of Pushpaka Vimanam is the story of Singeetham Srinivasa Rao in miniature. A filmmaker walks into a room and says I want to make a film with no dialogue. Not a silent film. A film with sound, music, ambient noise, everything except spoken words. The story will be told entirely through images. In 1987, this was not a pitch that anyone wanted to hear. Indian cinema, in every language, was built on dialogue. Take away dialogue, and you take away the scaffolding that the entire commercial film industry stood on. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao could not find a producer. Nobody wanted to fund a film that could not be marketed with a single quotable line. So he produced it himself, partnering with Shringar Nagaraj, a Kannada producer who was willing to take the risk. The idea for the film came to Singeetham while he was in the shower. He wrote the screenplay in two weeks. Also Read Made for Rs 15 lakh, Kamal Haasan, Singeethams pathbreaking film earned 6.6x its budget The result was a black comedy starring Kamal Haasan, Amala and Tinnu Anand that told a complex, funny and emotionally engaging story without a single word being spoken on screen. Because there was no dialogue, the film did not need dubbing. It was released simultaneously across all Indian languages under different titles Pushpaka Vimana in Kannada, Pushpaka Vimanam in Telugu, Pushpak in Hindi. Same film. Same audio track. Every audience understood it. The film won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. The time machine nobody expected Four years later, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao did it again. This time, the experiment was science fiction. Aditya 369, starring Nandamuri Balakrishna and Mohini, was the first Telugu film to feature a time machine. The concept was inspired by H.G. Wells The Time Machine, which Singeetham had read during his college years at the University of Madras. The film sent its characters back in time to the court of Sri Krishnadevaraya in the Vijayanagara Empire, mixing historical drama with futuristic technology in a way that nobody in Telugu cinema had attempted before. The film was presented by S.P. Balasubrahmanyam, the legendary playback singer who was also Singeetham Srinivasa Raos frequent collaborator. The combination of talents was extraordinary, but the concept was the real risk. In 1991, Telugu cinema was defined by family dramas, action films and romantic comedies. Science fiction was not a genre anyone believed the audience would accept. However, they accepted it. The film that proved the audience was willing to go wherever the filmmaker took them, as long as the maker knew where he was going. Singeetham always knew. Thirty-five years later, time travel is a common device in Telugu cinema. The lineage traces back to Aditya 369 and, by extension, to a filmmaker who read HG Wells in a Madras university library and decided that Telugu cinema deserved a time machine. The fantasy world nobody had built Bhairava Dweepam was the third experiment in three consecutive decades, each in a different genre, each doing something Indian cinema had not done before. Also Read Sing Geetham movie review At 94, Singeetam Srinivasa Rao delivers a musical fable The film, starring Balakrishna, was a high-fantasy adventure set on a mystical island ruled by a malevolent sorcerer seeking immortality. It drew from Indian folklore, mythology and adventure storytelling to create a world that was entirely self-contained its own geography, its own rules, its own visual language. The screenplay was co-written with Raavi Kondala Rao, one of Telugu literatures most respected writers, and produced under the Chandamama Vijaya Pictures banner. In 1994, Indian cinema did not make high-fantasy films. The genre was considered too expensive, too risky and too unfamiliar for audiences raised on realism-adjacent commercial cinema. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao ignored all of that. He built the island. He populated it with wizards, warriors and magical creatures. He created set pieces that were elaborate by any standard, let alone the standards of a mid-budget Telugu film in the early 1990s. Bhairava Dweepam completed a 100-day theatrical run in 28 centres. It proved a full two decades, before Baahubali made high fantasy commercially viable on a massive scale, that Telugu audiences were ready for mythology, magic and world-building. They just needed a filmmaker who was willing to try. The biography that changed lives Before the dialogue-free comedy, before the time machine, before the fantasy island, there was Mayuri. The film that made Singeetham Srinivasa Raos name and, in the process, changed a young womans life. Mayuri was inspired by the true story of Mumbai-based Bharatanatyam dancer Sudha Chandran, whose right leg had to be amputated after she was injured in a road accident in Tamil Nadu in 1981. Doctors fitted her with a Jaipur foot prosthetic, and Chandran returned to the stage, performing classical dance with an artificial limb. Singeetham saw the story and knew it was a film. Sudha, who had never acted, played herself. The film was a critical and commercial triumph. It was remade in Hindi as Naache Mayuri with the same cast. It launched Sudha Chandrans career as a film and television actress, a career that continues to this day. And it demonstrated that Singeetham could take a real-life story, handle it with sensitivity and turn it into a mainstream film without compromising either the storys truth or the audiences entertainment. The Tamil connection Singeetham Srinivasa Raos versatility extended beyond genres to languages. While Telugu was his primary language, his Tamil filmography includes some of the most significant films in that industrys history. Also Read Why Singeetham Srinivasa Rao banned Sing Geetham crew from referencing his masterpieces Anand, a romantic comedy starring Kamal Haasan and Revathi, was a commercial hit that was later remade in multiple languages. His collaboration with Kamal on Pushpaka Vimanam remains one of the most critically acclaimed actor-director partnerships in South Indian cinema. Magalir Mattum was a Tamil film that addressed womens issues. He also worked in Kannada, Malayalam and Hindi, making him one of the very few Indian filmmakers to direct films in five languages. The question that lingers after reviewing Singeetham Srinivasa Raos filmography is why did nobody else attempt what he did? The answer is not that other filmmakers lacked talent. It is that they lacked the specific combination of traits that Singeetham Srinivasa Rao possessed technical knowledge deep enough to execute his ideas, creative ambition wild enough to conceive them, and a stubborn indifference to whether the market was ready for them. Most filmmakers work within genres. They find what works and refine it. They make action films, or comedies, or romances, and they get better at making those specific things over time. Singeetham never did this. Each one of his films was a fresh start. Each one required learning a new visual language, a new set of production challenges and a new way of engaging with the audience. The commercial film industry does not reward this behaviour. It rewards consistency, predictability and brand identity. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao offered none of these. He offered surprise. And surprise, while thrilling for the audience, is terrifying for the people who invest money in films. The fact that he continued to find producers willing to back his experiments, decade after decade, is itself a testament to the power of his track record. The last experiment In February 2026, at the age of 94, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao announced his return to directing with Sing Geetham, a musical fantasy that marked his first film in over a decade. The project was produced by Nag Ashwin, the director of Kalki 2898 AD. Sing Geetham was completed. It was released. And it was the work of a man who, at an age when most people have forgotten what ambition feels like, walked onto a set and made one more film. Because he had one more story to tell. Because cinema was not something he did, it was something he was. Also Read Singeetham Srinivasa Rao 1931-2026 Kamal Haasan pays last respects to filmmaker Chiranjeevi, Jr NTR mourn demise The measure of the man Singeetham Srinivasa Raos career cannot be reduced to awards, it can only be understood as a body of work that is unlike any other in Indian cinema. Not because every film was a masterpiece, but every film was an attempt to do something that had not been done before. Indian cinema has produced filmmakers who are more commercially successful. It has produced filmmakers who are more critically acclaimed. It has produced filmmakers who are more consistently brilliant. But it has not produced another filmmaker who spent 54 years refusing to make the same film twice, who treated every project as a first film, who looked at the boundaries of what Indian cinema could do and, every single time, decided to step past them. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao did not push boundaries. He made the films he wanted to make, in the way he wanted to make them, for 54 years. And then, at 94, he made one more. Because one more was still not enough. That is not experimentation, that is devotion. And Indian cinema will not see its like again.

articleFeaturedImageAlt: BERMUDA plane missing, boston plane crash

According to the Federal Aviation Administration FAA, the Coast Guard was notified about the plane around 2 am local time on Saturday that the Gulfstream G100 jet, tail number CGRJP, had lost contact with air traffic controllers, reports stated. Gulfstream jet lost contact after leaving Bermuda The plane was being used as an air ambulance and had two passengers and four crew members on board when it left for an overnight flight to Massachusetts. I am aware of reports of a Canadian-registered air ambulance aircraft that went missing while travelling from Bermuda to Boston. Four Canadians are among the six people on board. We are closely monitoring the situation and are working with the relevant authorities as search and rescue efforts continue. I want to thank all first responders involved for their ongoing efforts. - Steven MacKinnon stevenmackinnon October 3, 2026 Four Canadians, two Bermudians were on board In a statement, the Coast Guard revealed the nationalities of those on board and said four Canadians and two Bermudians were aboard, and their next of kin were notified as the search continued. Following the discovery of a debris field that belongs to the missing plane, the armed forces added that the search operation for the six people aboard along the coast of Nantucket continues. Coast Guard search crews located a debris field that has been confirmed to be associated with the missing aircraft.
