articleTitle: Israel had names before flydubai FZ1073 took off, failed to flag Omani co-pilot: Report
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Netanyahu
description: Israeli officials had the Flydubai crew list before the Tel Aviv flight, says Haaretz, but the Omani co-pilot was not flagged. The Transport Ministry will not say whether it checked the names.
body_raw: Before Flydubai flight FZ1073 left Dubai for Tel Aviv on Wednesday, Israeli officials already had the names of everyone on board. The list of crew and passengers had been sent to them in advance, according to Israeli newspaper Haaretz. Yet the Omani co-pilot, who is now accused of attacking Indian Captain Smit Machchhar and trying to crash the plane, was not flagged. Here are the key facts and figures 174 people were on the Boeing 737 Max, most of them Israelis. 705 am The flight left Dubai on Wednesday, 30 September, and climbed to 34,000ft, according to Flightradar24. Just over two hours later the plane began to descend and fell more than 17,000ft in about two minutes. 15,000ft the height at which the plane levelled out, after passengers and crew overpowered the co-pilot. Code 7500 The transponder was set to this code, which signals unlawful interference. 2 reserve pilots on board took the controls and landed the jet at Tabuk, in northwest Saudi Arabia, at 945 am local time. 1 captain, Smit Machchhar, an Indian national, was hurt in the cockpit and is now in hospital in Abu Dhabi. Now the questions are about who knew what before take-off, and why a man who had reportedly been barred from flying in his own country was in the cockpit at all. Haaretz, quoting security sources, reported that Israels Transport Ministry and the Mossad were meant to check the crew list. The Israel Tax Authority confirmed it received the list. The Transport Ministry would not say whether it went through it. What did Israel know before the flight? According to Haaretz, Israeli government officials received the crew and passenger list ahead of the flight. Here is what is known and what is not What is confirmed Israeli officials received the list of crew and passengers before the flight. The Israel Tax Authority confirmed to Haaretz that the list reached it. Security sources told the paper that the Transport Ministry and the Mossad were supposed to check the crew names. The Omani co-pilot was not flagged before the flight. What has not been confirmed Whether the Transport Ministry went through the list. It declined to say. Whether the Mossad checked the crew names. The part of the Haaretz article seen here does not say. Whether any Israeli body raised a concern about the co-pilot before take-off. None has said so publicly. Whether Oman told Israel or any airline about its reported concerns over the co-pilot. Al Jazeera reported that it is unclear. Who is the co-pilot, and what is known about his past? Three people with knowledge of the matter, including a Gulf diplomat and a Western diplomat, told the AP news agency that the co-pilot is Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national. They spoke without giving their names. The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed sources, said Omani authorities had barred him from flying in Oman over concerns about alleged extremist views. It is not clear what those views were, or whether Oman told other countries or airlines. CNN, citing a source and an Israeli official, said he was born in the UAE to a Syrian mother and spent several years there. CNN also quoted a regional diplomatic source who said he had been removed from flight training over similar concerns and moved to another role. A LinkedIn profile with his name, seen by CNN, says he spent seven years at Oman Air and left in February 2025. It says he joined Royal Air Maroc in June 2025 and left in January 2026. Buckinghamshire New University has confirmed he finished a distance-learning course in aviation management there, and says he did no pilot training with it. A Gulf diplomat told AP that investigators are trying to learn whether he acted as a lone wolf or had links to extremist groups. What happened on flight FZ1073? According to Flightradar24, the plane left Dubai at 705 am on Wednesday and climbed to 34,000ft. A little over two hours later, it began to descend, and the data showed it fell more than 17,000ft in about two minutes before it climbed and dropped again. Inside the cockpit, the co-pilot had attacked Indian pilot Machchhar. The UAE says he used the emergency crash axe, a tool kept in cockpits to cut through the aircraft in an emergency. Machchhar later told Prime Minister Narendra Modi, from a hospital in Abu Dhabi, that he was on the floor and could feel the plane dropping. He said he knew it was the last chance to do something. He told PM Modi he reached the door and opened it, and people came in. Passengers and crew overpowered the co-pilot. The plane levelled out at about 15,000ft, and its transponder was set to code 7500, which signals unlawful interference. Two reserve pilots on board took the controls and landed the jet at Tabuk at 945 am local time. Saudi authorities said Captain Machchhar was taken to a hospital and then airlifted to Abu Dhabi after medical clearance. What is the UAE saying, and what happens next? UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif al-Shamsi said on Saturday that investigators found the co-pilot had begun what he called a terrorist act. He said the co-pilot attacked the captain with the crash axe and tried to take control of the aircraft. On Thursday, he had ordered investigators to check whether the incident was tied to terrorist activity or intent, or to planning or direction by others. Abu Dhabi is leading the case because the plane is registered in the UAE and flies under its flag. Al-Shamsi said UAE law covers crimes on board even outside the country. Investigators are looking at the motive, any links to others, and physical and digital evidence. The UAE has not said what the motive was, or whether it thinks al-Hammami acted alone. UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said on X that the attack shows the regions fight against extremism is not over. Flydubai flights to Israel remain suspended while the investigation is ongoing. Did Netanyahu miss a warning before 7 October as well? The questions about the Flydubai crew list come at a bad time for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces a close election on 27 October. He is also dealing with a second security question, this one about the Hamas-led attacks of 7 October 2023. On Sunday, the Wall Street Journal published a report saying Netanyahu had been warned of that attack by Egypts intelligence chief, Abbas Kamel. According to the report, Kamel phoned the prime minister a few days before the attack. It adds to earlier claims that Kamel flew to Israel in September 2023 to tell security officials in person that Hamas was planning an attack. Netanyahu is alleged to have received warnings before 7 October, and the claim has followed him since.

articleTitle: We are in talks with both Russia and Ukraine: Jaishankar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: JAISHANKAR
description: ‘Gone beyond advocacy, a little more involved in efforts to end conflict’
body_raw: Disclosing that India has gone beyond advocacy to be a little more involved in the efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war raging since February 2022, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said Sunday that Delhi has been in conversations with both Moscow and Kyiv, trying to be helpful on the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, grain and energy exports and on non-attack possibilities. His remarks, at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, came days after Ukraines Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said India had put forward a comprehensive and broad proposal to end the war for the first time. Jaishankar said, We are seeing today an unfortunate conflict. Our position on that conflict has been very clear, which is that we would like to see an end to this conflict, and we believe that this will require dialogue and diplomacy. There has to be negotiations in this regard. We have been advocating it for many years, and in recent months, we have got a little bit more involved beyond advocacy. So we have conversations with both Russia and Ukraine in this regard. We are trying to be helpful, starting with the Black Sea safety of shipping issue, but going beyond that to cover some immediate concerns which both of them have on grain exports, on energy exports, on non-attack possibilities. So those are ongoing conversations right now. He said India and Russia have historically had very good relations, particularly since the 1950s, and that history is not forgotten. For us, Russia and the Soviet Union before that was a country that stood by us in many ways when our security, when our territorial integrity was under threat. And at a time when, you know, much of the world preferred backing a military regime next to us, Russia was a country with which our relations were very good, and. we are obviously shaped in many ways by that legacy. Today, the relationship has widened beyond that. You know, it is again, the world has changed. We have changed. Our own relationships are not what they were in the 70s and 80s. Neither is the case with Russias, he said. So, like any relationship, it is refreshed. It undergoes a change. New issues come. Old issues sometimes get rebalanced. So it is very much more today an economic relationship as well. So there is a military component. Theres a nuclear component. There are space issues, but there is a significant amount of trade and investment between the two countries, and of course, energy and resources as well. So, any country would, when you view another country, you judge it from our experiences. I cant expect Europe, for example, to look at the world and say, okay, what does India think? And my view should be based on Indias experience. Europe will base its judgement on Europes experience. India will base its judgment on Indias experience. So Indias experience has been, frankly, quite positive and consistently positive, he said. On October 1, Russian President Vladimir Putin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi constantly raises the question about putting an end to the conflict and has very good ideas. Later that day, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, Ukraines Foreign Minister Sybiha said, We have four proposals. The most comprehensive is Indias proposal. For the first time, India has signalled its willingness to play a role. He said Ukraine is prepared to agree to an energy and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, and is also considering an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact. Besides India, Ukraine has received proposals for a possible ceasefire from Turkey, Egypt and the United States. According to Sybiha, Ukraine will agree to a ceasefire on the condition that it covers not only combat operations, but also an end to attacks on energy and port infrastructure, as well as the situation in the Black Sea.

articleTitle: Born in Bihar, made in Bengal: Mukesh Kumar and Akash Deep behind RoI’s Irani Cup triumph
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mukesh
description: The two seamers ran through Ranji champions Jammu and Kashmir in the Irani Cup final, making a strong case for a India recall ahead of the Tests against New Zealand
body_raw: Mukesh Kumar and Akash Deep are rarely at a loss for words. Alongside seam movement and pace, humour comes naturally to them, and never more so than when they are paired together. Yet asked when they first met, both had to rummage through their memories. They have been bowling together for so long that the answer simply would not come. Laced with wit, a riposte arrives from Mukesh. Pehli baar kab mile hataiye usko. Bas jab bhi mile hai, gale mile hai Forget when we first met. Just that whenever we did, we hugged one another. It has been nearly seven years since the pair first shared the ball in a senior domestic match - on the Christmas Day of 2019. Bowling in tandem, they took five wickets against Andhra. In the cold of Kolkata, Bengal had to settle for a draw. They would reach the final for the first time in 13 years, carried by the 67 wickets the two shared between them, but the silverware remained elusive. In the cold of Srinagar, here at the Sher-I-Kashmir stadium, the silverware is theirs. Mukeshs 633 and Akashs 325 steered Rest of India to the Irani Cup, their first since 2024, with a 167-run defeat of the defending Ranji Trophy champions, Jammu  Kashmir. This was the first time we played together for Rest of India. Whenever we bowl together, it is so much fun. When something happens off the pitch from my end, I communicate it to him, and when the ball does something from his end, he comes and tells me Bhaiya, aisa kar sakte hai brother, we can do this. Saamne waale to pata chal jaata hai ki hum jab saath bowling karte hai, runs banana kitna mushkil hai the batter knows how difficult it is to score when we bowl together, says Mukesh. Akash, three years his junior, offers the quintessential younger brothers nod of agreement. Our strength has been that weve played together for quite a while against great teams and top batters. We talk through things, which makes it simple whenever theres any confusion about what to do. Sometimes conditions favour the batters, and discussing things between us makes handling those situations much easier, he adds. Their journeys run along parallel tracks. Akash, hailing from Bihars Sasaram, arrived in West Bengal in 2010 to live with his uncle. Mukesh, also from Bihar, relocated from Gopalganj a couple of years later, to help his father in his taxi business. Neither set of parents approved of their cricketing ambitions, yet both made the Bengal side, and then India. Our backstories are the same, says Mukesh. He would have continued, if not for the interjection from Akash. Our story is such that things for both of us seem to happen in parallel. Whatever happens, happens together. Dont know if this is a stroke of destiny. Hum do alag jism hai, par ek hi kismat hai we share separate bodies, but the same fortune. It is hard to explain. Even we dont understand why everything turns out so similar for us, he says. For both men, the match carried a weight beyond a single trophy. For Mukesh, who has not played for India since July 2024, it was the opportunity to raise a case against his exile. For Akash, the challenge was to prove himself fit before the selectors - two of whom monitored him closely from the sidelines - pick the team for the New Zealand series. It was his first match in nearly eight months, having recently recovered from a lower-back stress fracture. What I felt during those six months was that my body needed a break. God perhaps gave that to me in the form of an injury, and I utilized that time really well. When I went into training and understood how my body was reacting, I made full use of that period. Diet, sleep, training, skill work-I did everything systematically. The outcome of that is showing now its not like I am exerting extra strain right now just to hit 145 kmph. It is the cumulative result of what I did over those six to seven months. Its not just about what Im doing in this match today or the speed on the radar, says Akash. Mukesh arrived in rich form, having led the wicket-takers charts in the Duleep Trophy with 12 scalps. Im enjoying my bowling immensely because even in the Duleep Trophy, I was bowling with great rhythm. Things went well in the semi-final and final as well. Winning the trophy boosted morale, and in between, I took no time off. I played another fixture in the English County Championship, bowled overs, and practiced in between. That momentum carried over here because the rhythm was never disrupted. Going forward, our goal is the upcoming Ranji Trophy. We will prepare for it, train for it, and do our best to help our team win. For Rest of India, the wait for a title was a mere two years.The task ahead is much steeper. Bengal have not won the Ranji Trophy since 1990. Should the pair keep bowling as they did in the valley on Sunday, though, they are entitled to dream.

articleTitle: China or Japan, who was the biggest winner of the 2026 Asian Games
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Japan may have finished second behind China in their home Asiad, but they have cause to celebrate having increased their gold medal haul by 31 compared to last edition. (AP)
description: China finished top of the medal podium for the 12th consecutive Asiad in Aichi-Nagoya, but fell 42 medals short of what they managed in the previous edition of Hangzhou as hosts Japan gained significantly to finish in the second spot increasing their gold haul by 31
body_raw: China conquered the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, claiming a whopping 341 medals, 169 of them gold. China mined so much gold in Aichi-Nagoya, that even if Japan, South Korea, India and Uzbekistan - the next four nations on the medals tally - were to pile up their gold medals together, China would still have five more golds. China did finish on top of the medals tally for the 12th consecutive edition of Asian Games since 1982. However, Chinas total production of medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Games is still a whopping 42 medals short 341 in Nagoya compared to 383 in Hangzhou 2023 of their total haul from their home Asian Games in Hangzhou. The continental giants also fell 32 gold medals short 169 in Nagoya compared to 201 of their last Asian Games benchmark. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage Meanwhile, Japan may have finished second in their home Asiad, but they have cause to celebrate having increased their gold medal haul by 31 83 in Aichi-Nagoya while 52 in Hangzhou and their total medal tally by 81 269 in Nagoya compared to 188 in Hangzhou. Chinas medals came in 57 different disciplines in Hangzhou but fell to 47 sports in Nagoya. In comparison, Japan claimed medals across 56 disciplines in 2026 compared to 48 in Hangzhou. So where did China miss out compared to the previous Asian Games? And what sports did Japans gains come in? Story behind Chinas tally The single biggest contributor to the 32 gold medals China was short of their Hangzhou tally was the exclusion of disciplines like dragon boat racing five golds, xiangqi three and chess three from the recently concluded Asiad. The boxers also came back four golds shorter than in Hangzhou while sailors returned with three less golds. Then there were many disciplines like athletics, badminton, rowing where they could not reclaim two golds, while there were other events like artistic gymnastics, basketball where they fell short by one gold. ALSO READ  As the Asian Games close, with a last-minute gold rush, India finish fourth Five sports - swimming, athletics, shooting, diving and wushu - contributed half of Chinas gold medal haul with wushu being the one sport where Chinas 12 medals were all gold. At the Nagoya Asian Games, one sport where China made visible gains was archery, particularly compound archery. China had three medals at Hangzhou, all in recurve. Of the six archery medals China won at Nagoya, three were in compound archery, a discipline where they had none in Hangzhou. This is understandable, since compound archery will be a medalled sport at the Olympics in LA 2028. The 19-year-old swimmer Zhang Zhanshuo was Chinas athlete of the Asian Games, winning seven golds in freestyle distances ranging from the 100m relay to the 1500m solo. Swimmers Yu Yiting and Li Bingjie contributed to five golds each. In fact, if there were to be an individual medals table for medal-winning athletes, among the top 20 athletes ranked by number of medals won, 19 would be Chinese. Most of them were swimmers and shooters, and almost all of them were in the age group of 18 to 24. At this Asian Games, we have achieved our goals of testing our team, discovering new talent, identifying problems and conducting comprehensive training, further strengthening our confidence in achieving outstanding results at the Los Angeles Olympics, Zhang Xin, secretary-general of the Chinese delegation, said in a statement. China sent a 815-athlete contingent to Nagoya - which had 36 Olympic gold medalists - who broke five world records, 11 Asian records and 22 Games records, But of these athletes 548 about two-thirds were competing at their first Asian Games. Where did Japan gain? At their home Asian Games, Japans biggest gain came in athletics, where they turned their two gold medal return from Hangzhou to 10 golds. At least four of these golds were upgraded medals from Hangzhou Misaki Morota turned her womens pole vault silver from Hangzhou to gold while Yuma Maruyama converted his bronze in mens decathlon from three years back to gold. Japan actually lost five golds from the 10 it had won in track cycling in Hangzhou. But sports like judo nine golds in 2026 compared to five in 2023, fencing six golds in 2026 compared to two, wrestling seven compared to five, swimming seven compared to five helped make up for it. The total medals from fencing for Japan was not too different, but the colour changed. Japanese fencers earned 10 medals at Hangzhou, only two were gold while half of those 10 were bronze. This time in Nagoya, the fencers earned six golds in an overall haul of 12 medals on the piste. The Nagoya Games also served as a reminder of Japans inclination towards combat sports, with 19 of their gold medals and 44 total medals coming from 8 disciplines judo nine golds and 14 overall, wrestling seven gold, 15 overall, boxing one gold, four total, karate two gold, four overall, kurash two bronze, taekwondo two bronze, wushu two bronze and MMA one bronze. Japan had three golds and a silver in the triathlon in Hangzhou. At Nagoya, China took away two golds and two silvers while Japan had three medals, one of each colour. Japan had eight medals in soft tennis at Nagoya, four of them gold. China, in contrast, had no athlete representing it in the discipline, understandable since its not an Olympic sport or a discipline with any history with China. articleTitle: Is it safe to reheat rice more than once?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Reheating leftover rice more than once may increase food-safety risks if the rice has not been cooled and stored properly.
description: Is reheating rice more than once safe? A dietitian explains the risk of Bacillus cereus, how to store leftover rice and the safest way to reheat it.
body_raw: Consuming leftover rice is common in many households, whether it is eaten at the next meal or turned into another dish. But reheating rice more than once raises an important food-safety question should you? It is equally important to consider how the rice is cooled, stored and handled between meals. Lets find out. Is it safe to reheat rice more than once? Deepa Mishra, dietitian, Narayana RN Tagore Hospital, Mukundapur, Kolkata, says, Reheating rice more than once is generally discouraged, especially if it has not been stored properly between meals. While reheating rice is not inherently dangerous, improper storage and repeated exposure to room temperature can increase the risk of food poisoning. One of the main concerns, she says, is Bacillus cereus, a bacterium commonly found in raw rice. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. It can produce heat-resistant spores that may survive cooking. When cooked rice is left in the temperature danger zone, between 4C and 60C, for an extended period, these spores can multiply and produce toxins. Some of these toxins are heat-stable, meaning that reheating the rice may not destroy them. Therefore, simply reheating improperly stored rice does not necessarily make it safe to eat, she adds. Additionally, repeated reheating can affect quality and texture and cause moisture loss, which may change the starch structure, making the rice dry, mushy, hard, or unpleasantly chewy. But thats not all. Repeated heating may also contribute to some nutrient loss. More importantly, if the rice is not heated evenly, some portions may remain at temperatures that allow bacterial growth, increasing the risk of spoilage, Mishra tells indianexpress.com. What is the best practice? The best practice is to take out only the portion you plan to eat and keep the remaining rice refrigerated. Mishra advises, Cooked rice should be cooled and refrigerated promptly rather than being left at room temperature for long periods. When you want to eat it again, reheat only the required portion thoroughly and avoid repeatedly reheating the same batch. Safe cooling, prompt refrigeration, proper storage, and thorough reheating are key to reducing the risk of food poisoning. articleTitle: 4 days on road for 2 seats: Why Vijay stakes prestige for bypolls after Tamil Nadu win
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay during an election campaign for party candidate Sathyabama ahead of the upcoming Dharapuram Assembly constituency by-poll
description: In multi-cornered fights for Madurantakam and Dharapuram, TVK aims to shore up its tally and get voters to ratify its candidates who had switched to the party after winning the seats on AIADMK tickets
body_raw: Chief ministers do not ordinarily spend four days campaigning for two Assembly by-elections in Tamil Nadu. However, C Joseph Vijay has done it. With Madurantakam and Dharapuram voting on October 6, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam TVK chief has spent two days addressing public rallies and another two on roadshows, including a 45-km journey through more than 30 villages in Madurantakam. The intensity is striking for another reason during the April Assembly election that brought him to power, Vijays own campaign appearances were comparatively limited, with several scheduled rallies cancelled and much of TVKs constituency-level campaigning left to candidates and other leaders. Inside the TVK, expectations have risen with the CMs effort. With this much campaigning by Vijay himself, we should get 50 of the votes, a senior TVK leader said. That number explains why these two bypolls have become considerably larger than two seats. The TVK is the ruling party. Both constituencies were vacated by AIADMK legislators who resigned within weeks of being elected and crossed over to Vijay. The same two leaders-Maragatham Kumaravel in Madurantakam and P Sathyabama in Dharapuram-are now contesting as TVK candidates. What is at stake? A victory would suggest that not merely politicians but at least enough of their voters have travelled with them. A defeat in even one seat would complicate the story that the TVK has been telling since it came to power in May that the centre of Tamil Nadu politics has shifted decisively towards Vijay. More immediately, senior TVK leaders acknowledge that losing a seat could slow the movement of AIADMK functionaries towards the ruling party. Since the Assembly elections, the TVK has been drawing former ministers, legislators and local functionaries from the weakened AIADMK. In Dharapuram alone, local-level AIADMK leaders have moved towards it. A victory would make further movement easier. A loss, on the other hand, would remind leaders contemplating a switch that a change of party is far simpler than transferring a constituency. That is why the bypoll is also a test of something difficult to measure until votes are counted on October 9 how much of Vijays April coalition of voters remains personally attached to him after the excitement of the general election has passed. TVK leaders believe women may be particularly important. Their assessment is that male voters could remain more firmly distributed among established party loyalties, while Vijay still has room to increase his support among women. Why Vijay has stepped in? Whether that assessment survives the ballot box is another matter. But it partly explains Vijays decision to campaign at close range rather than leave the election to ministers and local organisers. In Madurantakam, his roadshow included village stops, interactions with residents, a tractor ride and tea at a roadside shop. The Chief Minister who campaigned sparingly while seeking power is campaigning unusually hard after acquiring it. The Opposition understands the symbolism. The AIADMK has turned the circumstances of the bypoll itself into its campaign. Its supporters have repeatedly called Sathyabama a traitor for winning Dharapuram as an AIADMK candidate and then resigning to join the TVK. The argument is simple voters elected an AIADMK MLA in April, why should they be asked five months later to elect the same person for another party? Former CM and DMK chief M K Stalin has made a similar argument from the DMK, describing the elections as resulting from the death of democracy and attacking the TVK for making voters return to polling booths before, as he put it, the indelible ink from the general election had disappeared. The DMK, however, faces a different test. DMKs strength test The DMK enters these by-elections without the broad alliance that accompanied it into the Assembly election. The Congress, VCK, MDMK and IUML have moved into Vijays political orbit, while the CPI and CPIM are contesting separately. That means the DMK does not necessarily have to win to construct a favourable argument from the result. If its candidates substantially increase the partys vote share from April while contesting largely on its own, DMK leaders can argue that the defeat five months ago did not destroy the partys underlying electoral strength. A victory would be much more significant, but even a stronger second-place performance could provide Stalin with evidence that voters who deserted the DMK are beginning to reconsider. Do or die for AIADMK? For the AIADMK, the stakes are more existential. These were its seats. If its former MLAs can resign, join TVK and then defeat AIADMK candidates in the same constituencies, Vijay would have demonstrated something more damaging than attracting prominent defectors that the AIADMK label itself may no longer be necessary for some of its former representatives to win. The campaign has also acquired the familiar complications of Tamil Nadu by-elections. Leader of the Opposition in the Tamil Nadu Assembly Udhayanidhi Stalin has accused the TVK of distributing cash in Dharapuram, alleging that money was being carried in tiffin boxes. CPIM state secretary P Shanmugam has separately said villagers told Left campaigners that several parties were distributing money and that the TVK was paying the most. The TVK has categorically denied the allegations, saying it opposes cash-for-votes politics. Left adds intrigue The Lefts presence adds another peculiarity. The CPI and CPIM have supported Vijays government from outside but are now fighting his candidates. The PMK, meanwhile, has remained neutral amid discussions about a possible future relationship with the TVK. All of which makes October 6 an unusually crowded examination of a government less than five months old. By-elections are poor instruments for measuring an entire state. Local candidates, organisation, turnout and the advantages of incumbency can distort any attempt to turn two constituencies into Tamil Nadu. But these two seats have acquired importance because Vijay himself has made them important. Four days of personal campaigning has raised the price of victory. The TVK is no longer merely trying to retain two defectors. It is asking voters to ratify the political movement that brought those defectors to Vijay in the first place. In April, Vijay had to prove that his crowds could become votes. Then he returned with 108 seats, falling 10 short of the required 118 for an absolute majority in the 234-member House. Five months later, the question is narrower but perhaps more revealing. After government, Assembly debates and the ordinary frictions of power, will those votes still follow him? For the TVK, winning both seats keeps the political traffic moving towards Vijay. Losing even one could, for the first time since April, give some of those travelling in that direction a reason to check the road.

articleTitle: Salman Khan schools Qazi Touqeer over his ‘lollipop’ comment: ‘Should have backed off’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Salman Khan Qazi Touqeer Bigg Boss 20
description: On the latest Weekend Ka Vaar episode of Bigg Boss 20, Salman Khan reprimanded Qazi Touqeer over his comment to Kanika Mann. He also dismissed claims that he was biased towards the singer.
body_raw: Singer Qazi Touqeer has emerged as one of the most talked-about contestants on Bigg Boss Season 20. Over the past three weeks, host Salman Khan has also praised his game. However, during the latest Weekend Ka Vaar episode, Salman reprimanded Qazi over a comment he had made to Kanika Mann the previous week. What happened between Qazi Touqeer and Kanika Mann? During an episode last week, Kanika Mann commented that Qazi Touqeers outfit gave her very professor vibes. Qazi later changed his outfit and joked that he had now become the student, while Kanika was his teacher. Playing along, Kanika asked him which subject he would like to study. Qazi replied that he would like to study biology with her and then joked about the two having a lollipop together. He said, Maam, can we have a lollipop together? The comment offended Kanika, who told Qazi that she did not like what he had said. Qazi defended himself, saying that his intention was not to make a cheap remark. Also Read Everyone was thrashing me Salman Khan recalls how Dus Ka Dum saved him from career downfall   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by JioHotstar Reality jiohotstarreality As the conversation escalated into an argument, Kanika said Qazis comment had made her uncomfortable. Mahhi, Arishfa and several other contestants urged Qazi to apologise to Kanika, but he refused. He later also lost his cool with his friends when they told him that he was in the wrong. Salman Khan schools Qazi Touqeer In the latest episode of Bigg Boss 20, Salman Khan also pulled up Qazi Touqeer for his comment. He said, Qazi, what you said this week didnt go down well with Kanika. In the first three weeks, you played well you were entertaining. This week also, you entertained, but in this matter, you were wrong. Whatever your intention was, if someone found your comment wrong, or they felt discomfort, you should have just backed off. But you kept at it, like a stuck record. You stretched the matter like rubber, and thats where you went wrong. If your intention with the lollipop comment was not wrong, you should have said sorry and moved on. Kanika chimed in, saying, Sir, he has gotten an air about him because for the last three weeks he was praised. Salman asked Kanika, Did he apologise to you? When Qazi said that he said sorry to her while they were joking, Salman added, We didnt see you say sorry, Qazi. You said youd rather take a bullet than say sorry. Thats where you went wrong. Who says sorry in a joke? When you apologise, you should actually feel it. When its in your heart that you went wrong, you just back off.   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by JioHotstar Reality jiohotstarreality Salman Khan also gave the other contestants a wake-up call and addressed the perception inside the house that he was biased towards Qazi. He said, I feel you guys are not showing your personality, thinking that I will come on the Weekend Ka Vaar and give you a hearing. You all are being very calculative on the show. Seems like you guys have modified your personality out of fear of me. Dont worry about me. I am only coming here to give feedback. If you guys are not giving content, what do I come and do here? Tum log mera naam kharab kar rahe ho. This season, there is a narrative spread in this house if you say something to Qazi, I will come and pull you up on the weekend. Is he my brother? Have I taken a loan from him? Or has he gifted me his property? I have met all of you on this show. He had reminded me of meeting earlier. I didnt remember, but then I saw videos on social media and realised that yes, he was there. Its not your fault, Qazi. I work 18-20 hours a day. After seeing all of you for 3 months, I will recognise you all. So far, Qazi has been entertaining, but when he does something wrong, I will explain it to him too. I dont want to use a certain tone anymore, Salman said. Salman Khan also took a playful dig at the makers, joking that even if he merely pretended to shout at a contestant, the Bigg Boss team would turn it into a promo and make it go viral to draw audiences to the show.

articleTitle: NEET PG answer keys out, but candidates call it ‘eyewash’; here’s why
articleFeaturedImageAlt: NEET PG answer keys out, but candidates call it 'eyewash'; here is why
description: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences earlier said it would release the answer keys and candidates' response sheets to comply with a Supreme Court order ensuring transparency.
body_raw: The National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences NBEMS has released the answer keys for NEET PG 2026, the postgraduate medical entrance examination held on August 30 and September 5. Earlier this week, the NBEMS clarified that it issued candidates scorecards along with section-wise question IDs and their corresponding answer keys. Soon after the answer keys were released, candidates who had initially welcomed the move found themselves questioning the boards approach to disclosure. While the document included candidates responses alongside the questions and answers, the release of the answer keys, with only the question IDs and other limited details visible, left many questioning how far the move actually went in ensuring transparency. On social media, several candidates described the exercise as eyewash and merely a formality, arguing that making only the question IDs available did little to clarify the evaluation process and, in some cases, only added to the confusion. Also Read  NEET PG 2026 cut-off falls to 6-year low Why does it change? The NBEMS had earlier announced through the NEET PG 2026 information bulletin that it would release the answer keys and candidates response sheets in compliance with the Supreme Courts April 29, 2025, order that directed the board to make raw scores, answer keys, and normalisation details publicly available to ensure transparency. Speaking to indianexpress.com, a 30-year-old aspirant from Jaipur and a former junior resident at Guru Nanak Eye Centre, New Delhi, said, I was hopeful that when the answer keys are out, if I am not able to make the cut-offs, I will still be able to understand where I lost marks. This would help in preparing for any subsequent rounds. What is visible in NEET PG 2026 answer keys? As announced by the NBEMS and as confirmed by candidates, upon accessing the answer keys in the candidate login, only these fields are shown - Section-wise question IDs in the sequence in which they appeared in the candidates question paper. - Status of each response, including whether the question was answered or not attempted. - Correct answer key ID 1234 for every question. - Response marked by the candidate against each question. - Score awarded for each question as per the examination scheme. Why are these details insufficient for candidates? The aspirant clarifies, In NEET PG, the order in which the questions and their options appear is not the same for all candidates. During the actual exam, the questions are shuffled within the section. Examination authorities often resort to jumbling the order of questions and answer options to protect the tests integrity and, to a large extent, restrict chances of malpractice. According to the aspirant, Since the sequence of questions within a section was shuffled, question IDs and their corresponding correct option ID appeared differently for candidates. We have no way of knowing or recalling which question ID is against what actual question, and what we have answered. Also Read  NMC releases institute and course-wise seat matrix While the NBEMS has released the correct answer key ID, the information remains irrelevant for candidates because the explicit questions and their correct answers have not been disclosed. Without knowing the exact question and its corresponding correct answer, candidates cannot independently verify whether the answer has been marked correctly. Another candidate, a practising junior doctor at a hospital in Madhya Pradesh, told Indianexpress.com that other nationally organised public entrance and qualifying exams issue answer keys where the questions and their answers are visible to candidates. CUET UG and PG, NEET UG, JEE Mains and Advanced - all these exams issue answer keys. Why can we not expect the same rigour for NEET-PG? he said. Can candidates raise objections? Neither of the notices issued by the NBEMS on September 24 and October 1 mentions an objection window or any procedure for candidates to challenge the answers. In its circular issued on September 24, the board said, Each and every question asked in both the question papers of NEET PG 2026 was reviewed by faculty members from the concerned speciality area after the conduct of NEET-PG 2026 to recheck for technical correctness of the questions as well as answer keys. The board announced that none of the questions was found technically incorrect, further eliminating any provision for candidates to challenge the question paper. IMA official challenges answer key in Supreme Court Meanwhile, Dr Dhruv Chauhan, national spokesperson of the Indian Medical Associations Junior Doctors Network IMA-JDN and founder of the Legal Cell for All India Doctors, has moved the Supreme Court with a public interest litigation PIL challenging the NEET-PG 2026 answer keys. The petition seeks greater transparency in the evaluation process, demanding that the complete question paper be made available along with the corresponding answers and the options actually marked by candidates, rather than merely the serial numbers of the questions and responses. Dr Chauhan told indianexpress.com, The aspirants wanted only one thing, that is transparency in the exam. He added, Our legal team will pursue this in the larger benefit of the medical students, and have also called for a time-bound objection window to address any discrepancies. With the matter now before the Supreme Court, candidates await clarity on whether directions will be issued to make the complete question paper and answer details available, and whether that happens before counselling begins.

articleTitle: Mukesh Kumar and Akash Deep bowl Rest of India to Irani Cup title
articleFeaturedImageAlt: It was the first time since 2024 that the Ranji Trophy winners had failed to complete the double.
description: Set a massive target of 279, the two Bengal seamers run through Ranji champions as RoI win the title they last won in 2024
body_raw: The beauty of red-ball cricket lies in its intrinsic irony. An otherwise long, languid affair, spread across days, and yet, a few hours could be all it takes to deliver the games verdict. Basking in a Sunday sun that had found its full intensity after two subdued days, fans here at Srinagars Sher-I-Kashmir Stadium was offered a slice of that beauty, as Rest of India defeated the reigning Ranji Trophy champions, Jammu  Kashmir, by 167 runs to claim the Irani Cup. What an incredible performance by the boys. Finally, it happened after two years, quipped batting coach Laxmi Ratan Shukla, relief written across his face as he entered the dressing room to join the captain Rishabh Pants birthday celebrations. Three hours earlier, the players in that very room had cut desolate figures. Chasing a target of 279 runs, the hosts had gone off to a flier. Qamran Iqbal and Shubham Khajuria batted as if they had already pencilled in a free Day 5. In accordance, 54 runs came in the first 10 overs. What followed would feel to the JK players like a fever dream. Iqbal, perhaps too eager to reach the finish line, shuffled across to deposit an Akash Deep delivery into the temporary stands past square leg. Instead, the delivery marked his deposit to the dugout, trapped lbw. Drinks were called in the 13th over, and a single conversation during that break shaped the outcome of the match. Mukesh Kumar, the least effective of his sides pacers in the first innings, pleaded with the stand-in captain, Sarfaraz Khan, for just one more over. Kumar was successful in his convincing bid. That, however, was only the first part of the job. The pacer would take two wickets in that over and turn the game on its head. An inswinger trapped Shubham Pundir lbw, and the JK captain, Paras Dogra, was undone by a peach that shaped away from the bat and disturbed the stumps. At 893, however, a semblance of parity still lingered, as it had through the first three days in the valley. Then came an hour of impeccable bowling, which made the contest look like something it never was - a one-sided affair. Shubham Khajuria, man with the most first-Class appearances for JK, would offer a shot in the very first delivery after Lunch that was not in synchronisation with his vast experience. He chased a wide delivery from Akash and could only find the edge. Kanhaiya Wadhawan, apparently untaught by the veterans misfortune, offered a near-identical stroke and was caught by the substitute wicketkeeper Aryan Juyal in the same fashion. The only difference between the two dismissals lay in the bowler - this time it was Mukesh Kumar, collecting his third wicket. He would take three more wickets. Before that, however, Akashs away movement would result in the second duck of the day - all-rounder Sahil Lotra following in the footsteps of his captain. The day belonged to the two seamers from Bengal, yet perhaps the most important dismissal came from the showstopper of the first innings, Mukesh Choudhary. Abdul Samad, who had told this paper of his ambition to score over 1,000 runs in the coming Ranji Trophy season, was a man intent on backing his words. Fresh from a first-innings half-century, he was the picture of poise in the second - batting unperturbed on 20, with the chaos surrounding him not affecting his zen. But in the 28th over, Choudhary lured him into a drive, and got him caught by Shikhar Mohan at second slip. That, effectively, was the game for Rest of India. Kumar would dismiss Abid Mushtaq, Umar Nazir and Sunil Kumar in the span of four deliveries in the next over, recording his 11th five-wicket haul in first-class cricket. It was the first time since 2024 that the Ranji Trophy winners had failed to complete the double. Save for a session of brain fade, though, Dogras men did offer a good account of themselves. They have 7 players in their team who have played for India. Bahut saari teamein sochti bhi nahin ki unko hara paayenge, but hum mein belief tha Many teams would not even have fathomed beating them, but we had belief. We fought till the last moment, Dogra said, his head held high. Outside the stadium, two young fans - Schrodingers optimist and pessimist - were locked in debate. What was the point of hosting this game involving such big players like Rishabh Pant, and then embarrassing ourselves in front of them? asked the pessimist. Rishabh Pant is here because we are the champions of India. Never forget that, replied the optimist. The debate ended in a draw. The trophy ended up in the Rest of Indias locker. Brief scores Rest of India 237  319 Ravichandran Smaran 135 Sunil Kumar 356 defeated Jammu  Kashmir 278  111 Shubham Khajuria 36 Mukesh Kumar 633 by 167 runs.

articleTitle: Market analyst claims Shah Rukh Khan’s Rs 12,500 crore net worth is 4x his contemporaries
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shah Rukh Khan's net worth is more than four times than that of Salman Khan.
description: Popular market analyst JS Khepar aka Jassi Tech claims Shah Rukh Khan's net worth is more than four times than that of his contemporaries Salman Khan, Akshay Kumar, and Aamir Khan.
body_raw: It may not come as a surprise that Shah Rukh Khan is counted among Indias richest actors. What is perhaps less widely known is the scale of the wealth gap between him and his A-list contemporaries, including Salman Khan, Akshay Kumar and Aamir Khan. Popular market analyst JS Khepar, aka Jassi Tech, recently claimed that Shah Rukhs net worth is more than four times that of each of these actors. Shah Rukh, Salman, Aamirs net worth From the data that I could last decipher, Salmans net worth is around Rs 3,000 crore to Rs 3,200 crore, said JS Khepar in a conversation with Siddharth Kannan, adding that Aamirs net worth is between Rs 1,900 to Rs 2,000 crore. Between both is Akshay Kumar, whose net worth lies between Rs 2,700 crore and Rs 2,800 crore, as per Jassi Tech. However, he dropped the biggest bomb when he revealed Shah Rukhs net worth. Hes the king I dont think his net worth is less than Rs 12,000 crore to Rs 12,500 crore. Thats why he the king, said Khepar on Siddharth Kannans podcast. Hes the badshah emperor in not only films, but also business. Look at KKR Wherever he has investments, theyre all zabardast outstanding, added the analyst. Shah Rukh Khans astronomical net worth includes his Indian Premier League cricket team Kolkata Knight Riders, his sea-facing palatial bungalow Mannat on Bandra Bandstand and a 4BHK sea-facing apartment in Shree Amrit Society on Carter Road in Mumbai, properties in London and Dubai, production house Red Chillies Entertainment, a VFX studio, and salaries from film projects and brand endorsements, among others. Aamir a test player, Akshay a T20 batsman JS Khepar also pointed out the differences between the investing and working styles of Salman Khan, Akshay Kumar, and Aamir Khan. Aamir is a test player, and Akshay is a T20 player. The approach is different in both the games. A T20 player is supposed to bat recklessly. A Test player is all about class. Aamir has that class. Whether his films work or not, he should remain Mr. Perfectionist, said Khepar. Hailing Akshay as a khiladi player even in the way he invests, the analyst said the actor has a presence everywhere. If there was a T5 format, he would have aced it too, he said, adding, And Salman is like a one-day cricketer. Kheper also lauded Akshays incredible fitness, which also allows him to pack in around four films within a year. JS Khepar also revealed that Salmans primary investment is in the real estate of Mumbai. Salman has a Midas touch. He turns mud to gold in real estate, and earns a lot of money there. One should learn that from him. The whole world loves him, including real estate. Theres only money and more money in Mumbais real estate. If not here, then where?, he added. Also Read Neem Karoli Baba film Hanuman Ansh refuses to bow to Drishyam 3, crosses Rs 419 crore mark Salman Khan owns multiple properties in the city, including the palatial Galaxy Apartments on Bandra Bandstand, where he resides with his joint family. Besides other properties on Carter Road and in Worli, Salmans net worth also boasts of a massive 150-acre farmhouse in the suburb of Panvel.

articleTitle: Why TVK joins INDIA bloc, hits pause on Vijay as PM face
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay
description: TVK's move to formally join the national Opposition alliance led by its key Tamil Nadu ally Congress pushes DMK further into a corner and with fewer allies
body_raw: For Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay, joining the INDIA bloc was less a dramatic turn than the formal acknowledgement of where Tamil Nadus post-election arithmetic had already taken him. His Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam TVK governs the state with the Congress as an ally. The VCK and IUML are also part of the arrangement that enabled Vijay to form the government after TVK won 108 seats, short of the 118 needed for an absolute majority. A national third front has not taken shape. Remaining outside the BJP-led NDA while simultaneously keeping away from the principal national Opposition grouping was becoming an increasingly narrow political space. On Saturday, TVK stepped out of it. TVK representatives Aadhav Arjuna and Marie Wilson attended an INDIA bloc meeting at the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee headquarters in Chennai, alongside the CPI, CPIM, VCK, MDMK and IUML. Tamil Nadu Congress chief president Manickam Tagore declared that Vijays party had formally joined the alliance, calling it a historic day. More questions than answers The announcement settles one question but opens several others-including where the DMK, until recently the principal Tamil Nadu component of the national Opposition alliance, now fits. The immediate occasion was electoral rolls rather than alliance arithmetic. The parties adopted resolutions against the Special Intensive Revision SIR exercise and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and announced demonstrations across Tamil Nadu on October 13 and 14, followed by a larger Chennai protest on October 15. The TVK is expected to participate. Whether Vijay himself will attend remains unclear. Until recently, even this relationship had remained deliberately undefined. Tagore had maintained that the TVK could not technically be treated as an INDIA bloc constituent because it had no representation in Parliament. The party was not invited to the INDIA blocs national meeting in New Delhi last week. Saturday therefore marked a change not merely in TVKs position but in the Congresss willingness to recognise it formally. For Vijay, the move also provides a national structure for an alliance that already exists at home. The Congress has five MLAs and is part of the TVK-led government. The next Lok Sabha election in 2029 now provides a larger horizon an INDIA bloc arrangement potentially gives TVK a framework for negotiating parliamentary seats without having to construct another national partnership from scratch. Vijay-for-PM plans on hold Inside the TVK, that transition has also required some message control. According to senior party sources, the leadership has instructed functionaries before the by-election campaign not to project Vijay as a future prime ministerial candidate. Resources that had been going towards Instagram reels and social-media material presenting Vijay in that role have also been curtailed, a senior TVK leader told The Indian Express. The intervention is partly practical. The TVK is fighting immediate Assembly by-elections Vijay is barely months into his first term as Chief Minister. The national ambition can wait. Politics occasionally requires social media to observe seniority. DMKs dilemma The more consequential effect of Saturdays decision may instead be on the DMK. After losing power, the party has found itself without the coalition structure that surrounded it before the Assembly election. The CPI and CPIM, now contesting the by-elections independently after distancing themselves from Vijays alliance, might under different circumstances have found a return to the DMK politically natural. The TVKs entry into INDIA complicates that route. The Left parties attended Saturdays meeting alongside the TVK. So did the VCK and MDMK. In other words, the national Opposition platform now contains several parties whose Tamil Nadu relationships are considerably less tidy than their seating arrangement at the Congress office suggested. That distinction, between a national alliance and a state alliance, will matter increasingly. The INDIA bloc gives its members a common national opponent in the BJP without automatically resolving who should fight whom in Tamil Nadu. For the Congress, however, Vijay is already its governing partner. For the TVK, Congress provides both legislative support today and a potential bridge to parliamentary politics in 2029. Slim chances for Third Front For the DMK, the situation is more awkward. Its leaders can continue engaging INDIA parties nationally, but Vijays formal arrival means the coalition can no longer be assumed to be a political space in which the DMK is Tamil Nadus default representative. Recent contacts by DMK deputy general secretary Kanimozhi with non-Congress INDIA leaders had also triggered speculation about whether another Opposition configuration could emerge. But without the Congress, and with several potential partners now sitting at an INDIA table that includes the TVK, the room for a viable third formation appears limited. The irony is that Vijay entered the Assembly election as the leader of a new party arguing against Tamil Nadus established political arrangements. Five months after the result, governing has steadily required arrangements of its own. First came the partners needed for a majority. Now comes a national coalition. Saturdays meeting did not resolve all of those contradictions. It merely gave them a name INDIA bloc.

articleTitle: China This Week | Rumours about Xi Jinping’s health, US jets arrive in Taiwan, and more
articleFeaturedImageAlt: US President Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump with China's President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan at the White House, on September 24. (AP Photo/Alex Brandon)
description: Every week, we recap highlights of the news from China. This edition looks at the nature of rumours around Chinese President Xi Jinping's health in recent weeks, a sale of jets to Taiwan, and activity in the South China Sea.
body_raw: Over the last few days, analysts and longtime China watchers have tried to make sense of the bilateral leaders meeting in Washington, DC, in late September. What stood out was the pageantry surrounding Chinese President Xi Jinpings visit, even as many argued that the trip itself fell short on substantial outcomes. A report from The Wall Street Journal has now claimed that Xis staff requested several breaks during the visit and to cut down the duration of some events, raising questions about the 73-year-olds health. It also follows similar rumours that swirled during Xis trip to India for the BRICS summit in New Delhi earlier in September. Another noteworthy event this week was the delivery of two American F-16V fighter jets to Taiwan. The Chinese Communist Partys CCP tabloid, Global Times, commented on the fact that it came years behind schedule. The jets have also come as a major arms sale from Taiwan to the US hangs in the balance. Finally, we look at a recent Reuters report that used satellite images to find that China is building a full-scale runway at the Antelope Reef in the disputed South China Sea. Military attaches and security analysts say it could be one of Chinas most important offshore bases in the region, the report said. Here is a closer look at these developments. 1. Why Xi Jinpings health is often the centre of rumours The WSJ report cited former US officials involved in planning state visits and analysts, who said that the nature of Chinas requests for Xi was unusual. Chief among the requests was a private room inside the West Wing of the White House for Xi to take a break between events, with only his wife, Peng Liyuan, permitted to join him, the people said. No others from the Chinese delegation were allowed to use the hold room, as it was called, the report said. UPSHOT Such rumours are not exactly new. In fact, back in 2012, months before Xi was elevated as the general secretary of the CCP - the most powerful position in China - he was not seen in public for a while, sparking speculation over his health. Xi is not alone, in that many key public figures in China often draw such scrutiny given the lack of transparency in the countrys political and media systems. Information flows are heavily regulated by the government, which, in turn, heightens curiosity among observers. With a leader like Xi, who has concentrated power at the top and bypassed term limitations, China watchers are particularly interested in observing the tiniest body language shifts and movements to understand his health condition, including Xi reportedly clasping his wifes hand while using the stairs in Washington, SC. This incident may turn out to be about Xi simply requiring rest given his age and the long-duration flight to the US. The rumours of his supposed ill-health in India were also not found to have a strong basis, at least so far, but are indicative of how Chinas political system, in an attempt to project strength and infallibility, can damage those very perceptions. 2. Taiwan gets new jets, with some delays During Donald Trumps first presidential term in 2019, the United States approved an 8 billion sale of Lockheed Martin F-16V fighter jets to Taiwan, but issues such as software problems delayed delivery, Reuters reported. The arrival of the first two of 66 F-16V Block 70s strengthens Taiwans defense capabilities and safeguards our skies. We thank the United States for its longstanding support and continued security cooperation. As President ChingteLai has said, investing in defense is investing in peace. Taiwan remains committed to defending our homeland and to contributing to regional peace and stability. - DPP U.S. Mission TaiwanDPPDC October 2, 2026 The jets were to reach Taiwan between 2023 and 2026, but only two of the 65 F-16V Block 70 jets have been delivered. Commenting on the news, Global Times noted the positive reactions from Taiwans ruling Democratic Progressive Party DPP, calling it political performance. The article spoke of The DPPs alarm over the rising prevalence of abandoning Taiwan and doubting the US sentiments, particularly as China and the US have sought greater strategic stability in their relationship. Under this narrative, the arrival of two F-16Vs in Taiwan has been. cited as proof of continued US support for Taiwan island. UPSHOT The article touches on a subject that has worried some stakeholders in the US of late the countrys longstanding relationship with Taiwan. While the latest jet delivery may have been approved years ago, its delivery comes when Trump has held off on approving a 14 billion arms sale to Taiwan. Once signed, it would be the biggest such package to date. Amid the visit, Lyle Morris, Senior Fellow on Foreign Policy and National Security at the US-based Asia Society Policy Institutes Center for China Analysis, told The Indian Express that Trumps delay could be an attempt to accommodate China. Xi and the Chinese State have criticised such arms sales as part of the broader objection to any conception of Taiwanese independence. But Trumps more recent statements have also diverged from the more assured US support for Taiwan over the past few decades. In that context, it would be understandable why the DPP would see the jets as evidence of US support, and why the CCP would describe it critically. 3. New activity in South China Sea Reuters reported that a completed base at Antelope Reef would be Chinas most significant military expansion in the South China Sea in a decade, extending the reach of Chinese naval ships and military aircraft in a waterway that is an increasingly militarised arena of competition between Beijing and the United States and its allies over Taiwan. It would also help protect the approaches to Hainan Island, where China keeps its nuclear-armed ballistic missile submarines, the report said. UPSHOT In the last decade or so of increasingly assertive Chinese foreign policy, the South China Sea has been a major component. Apart from the regions vast oil and gas resources, it has also become a source of territorial contestation, with claims upto various points made by countries such as Vietnam and the Philippines. For the US, it could also emerge as a region where China incrementally increases its presence through the deployment of smaller vessels and forces, creating a strategic threat. In July, the US government issued a joint statement with countries including Japan, Australia and the Philippines on the tenth anniversary of the Philippines-China South China Sea Arbitral Tribunal Award. That award had criticised Chinas claims to the region, while China has said the tribunal was not eligible to adjudicate on the subject. We reaffirm that the Award rendered ten years ago by the Arbitral Tribunal is a significant milestone and is final, legally binding, and definitive between China and the Philippines. We reaffirm the Arbitral Tribunals decision that there is no legal basis for Chinas expansive maritime claims in the South China Sea, including those based on historic rights, it said. With continued Chinese activity even a decade after the ruling, however, there is little to suggest that tribunals and other means of adjudication will influence China to slow down its work there.

articleTitle: Akmal slams Ayub’s celebration after Sooryavanshi’s wicket: ‘Doing things for social media’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sooryavanshi
description: "No matter whether he is 13, 14, or 15, he's playing international cricket. Saim Ayub is not a kid. He should focus on his performances," Akmal said
body_raw: Pakistan off-spinner Saim Ayub took the wicket of Indian teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on Saturday in the gold medal match of the Asian Games 2026, and after the wicket, Ayub immediately made a baby cradle gesture. Sooryavanshi did not react and walked away quietly. However, despite the early breakthrough, Pakistan could not restrict India to a small total, nor could they chase the runs. Former Pakistan cricketer Kamran Akmal slammed Ayubs celebration, saying the performances have not been great, but they continue to do things for social media. These things have been happening for a long time. Our performance hasnt been great, but we are doing things for social media, Akmal said on sports discussion show. The management should think about this. Its international cricket. No matter whether he is 13, 14, or 15, hes playing international cricket. Saim Ayub is not a kid. He should focus on his performances. Top 100 The 15-year-old Sooryavanshi is the only Indian athlete on the coveted list in TIME magazine, which the American publication unveiled last week. The Bihar prodigy is also the youngest person and one of only seven athletes named. This years list-makers are pushing boundaries, creating new possibilities, and advancing their fields and communities around the world, said Time CEO Jessica Sibley. Featuring in the Phenom category, TIME observed that Sooryavanshi is fast becoming one of global sports most electrifying figures. The Sooryavanshi phenomenon has gained rapid strides since 2024, when he first made his professional cricket debut at the senior level in the Ranji Trophy, aged 12. After being one of the youngest ever Indians to play First-Class cricket, Sooryavanshi was swooped up by the Rajasthan Royals for Rs 1 crore ahead of the IPL 2025 season. Sooryavanshi set the stage on fire in the worlds most famous T20 franchise league in his maiden itself, smashing 252 runs in seven innings. It comprised a whirlwind 35-ball century against the Gujarat Titans, making it the then-fastest ton ever struck by an Indian in the IPL. In his second season this year, Sooryavanshi relished a full-fledged batting season with the Royals, plundering 776 runs with a century and five half-centuries to emerge as the highest run-getter. articleTitle: Ambedkar University Delhi revises attendance guidelines for PhD scholars amid students’ protest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ambedkar University Delhi revises attendance guidelines for PhD scholars amid students' protest
description: The university's July 31 notification had introduced attendance requirements for full-time PhD scholars receiving fellowships, which had led to concerns among research scholars over restrictions on their academic and research-related activities.
body_raw: Ambedkar University Delhi has revised its guidelines for full-time PhD scholars receiving fellowships, superseding an office order issued on July 31 that had triggered a protest by students. The universitys July 31 notification had introduced attendance requirements for full-time PhD scholars receiving fellowships, which had led to concerns among research scholars over restrictions on their academic and research-related activities. The Ambedkar University administration has now said that the notification has been superseded by the revised office order issued on September 30, which provides greater flexibility while requiring scholars to attend coursework and seminars and maintain academic engagement and research progress. Attendance records will be maintained by the research supervisor and programme coordinator and verified by the dean of the concerned school. The research supervisor will also be responsible for ensuring satisfactory academic engagement and progress of the scholars research work under the overall guidance of the dean, the administration said. Also Read  DU relaxes 28-credit promotion rule What changes for students The guidelines are purely academic in nature and in line with UGC regulations and practices followed by other central and state universities, it said, adding that the objective was to strengthen the research ecosystem and ensure participation of research scholars in academic and research activities. The clarification comes amid a week-long protest at the university by students associated with AISA on the attendance issue, campus restrictions, access to facilities and other demands. The situation had escalated late Friday night after protesters alleged that security personnel restricted the entry of food and water and that a student who collapsed around 3 am faced delays in medical evacuation. The university, however, said its medical team was continuously monitoring the health of protesting students and providing necessary medical assistance. The All India Students Association AISAhad also alleged that students were subsequently denied access to the campus, affecting those attending classes and examinations. The university said the library, laboratories and certain other blocks had been closed for maintenance and safety purposes and that students had been informed in advance. The administration said the indefinite sit-in was being held without prior permission and that a designated space had been provided for peaceful protests. It also alleged that some protesting students had manhandled security guards, a matter which it said had been brought to the notice of Delhi Police. Also Read  Rs 1,668 Crore investment approved for Ambedkar Universitys futuristic new campus in Dheerpur AISA has demanded removal of the physical barriers, restoration of what it describes as campus democracy, accountability over the alleged obstruction of emergency medical access and unrestricted entry for all registered students. In its latest statement, the university appealed to students and other stakeholders against spreading misinformation and said it remained open to dialogue and clarification. Many students and their guardians have placed their hope, future and career in this University, the administration said, urging all stakeholders to avoid creating panic or tarnishing the institutions image through misleading information.

articleTitle: Unchecked high-rises strain Pune: PIL challenges rules permitting more construction
articleFeaturedImageAlt: pune high rise, construction, indian express
description: A bench of the Bombay High Court has issued notices to the Maharashtra government, Pune civic body, and the central pollution control body after prominent Pune citizens, including former MP Vandana Chavan, filed a petition to halt extra FSI provisions.
body_raw: As Pune witnesses rapid vertical growth driven partly by redevelopment, concerns over liveability and civic infrastructure have prompted a group of prominent citizens to petition the Bombay High Court. The petition challenges rules that permit increased real estate construction and seeks to abolish additional buildable potential to prevent severe urban strain. The matter requires consideration. The court and the petitioners issue notices to the Maharashtra government, Pune Municipal Corporation PMC and the Central Pollution Control Board CPCB, stated a bench of Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi and Justice Advait M Sethna in its order on the petition. Former Rajya Sabha MP and ex-mayor Vandana Chavan filed the petition along with prominent citizens Vijay Paranjpye, Ajit Abhyankar, Vishwambhar Choudhari, and Abhay Chhajed. It challenges the provisions allowing extra real estate construction through additional Floor Space Index FSI under the Unified Development Control and Promotion Regulations, 2020 UDCPR 2020. The petitioners argue that these regulations were introduced without essential prior evaluations-including regional carrying capacity, infrastructure adequacy, environmental impact, and public liveability- rendering them arbitrary, unconstitutional, and environmentally unsustainable. Pointing out that Pune already faces acute deficits in water supply, sewage treatment, waste management, open spaces, and traffic control alongside rising pollution, heatwaves, and flooding, they warned that unscientific densification will aggravate public health and safety risks. Call to revert to 2017 rules pending studies The petition appeals to the High Court to quash the chapters of UDCPR 2020 that allow extra FSI for construction in Pune and order the temporary implementation of the 2017 Development Control Rules instead. The petitioners contend that the PMC should be permitted to implement additional FSI provisions only after conducting comprehensive impact studies. The court should issue direction to restrain the PMC from issuing any development permissions under UDCPR 2020 till detailed studies on the regions carrying capacity are carried out, which should include population density projections, infrastructure and utilities capacity assessment, public utilities and infrastructure capacity study and deficit analysis, traffic and transportation network study, environment and climate impact assessment, urban heat island effect and disaster risk mitigation, socio-economic impact evaluations, geotechnical and structural feasibility study, natural features, biodiversity and sustainability studies, said Chavan. The petition further requests the court to restrain the PMC from granting development permissions for Transit Oriented Development TOD without completing a city-wide impact assessment and finalising local area plans, and to stay UDCPR chapters on FSI increases in the interim. Ecological and structural risks While UDCPR 2020 incentivises the redevelopment of old, dilapidated, or dangerous buildings by offering higher FSI, the petitioners warned that this approach carries hidden structural and environmental costs. They noted that UDCPR-driven growth leads to taller structures requiring deeper foundation excavations for underground parking. This process threatens to cut into crucial underground aquifers while significantly worsening construction and demolition waste disposal across the city.

articleTitle: ‘No filter’: Tamannaah Bhatia’s advice for dealing with bad skin days
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tamannaah Bhatia shares mantra for bad skin days
description: "There are good skin days and then there are not so good skin days...as you can see, no filter. It is so important to love yourself on these days," The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest actor shared.
body_raw: Some days, our skin refuses to behave, and Tamannaah Bhatia believes it is crucial to extend grace and embrace yourself as you are. Taking to Instagram Stories, The Vvaan Force of the Forrest actor shared a candid note to young girls struggling with their skin. There are good skin days, and then there are not so good skin days.as you can see, no filter. It is so important to love yourself on these days. And I have chosen to love myself just the way I am. Because I think, that does not take away from who I am, and how I look, and how I feel, she shared. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Dealing with bad skin days Dr Shareefa Chause, Dermatologist at Dr Shareefa Skin Care Clinic, Mumbai, says it is important to remember that skin naturally changes from day to day. Stress, lack of sleep, weather, diet, hormonal changes, and even small changes in our routine can affect how the skin looks. Having a breakout, dryness, dullness or redness on a particular day does not mean that your skin is unhealthy or that you have done something wrong, she tells indianexpress.com. Dr Chause stresses that people should avoid becoming overly focused on achieving perfect skin. Instead, follow a simple, consistent routine suited to your skin type, including gentle cleansing, moisturising, and daily sunscreen. Avoid repeatedly changing products or trying several treatments at once just because the skin looks different on a particular day, as it can sometimes irritate the skin further, she warns, adding that you should not constantly check your skin in the mirror or compare it with highly edited images on social media. Skin has texture, pores, marks, and occasional imperfections, and these are normal. If a particular skin problem is persistent, painful, worsening, or affecting confidence, it is better to consult a dermatologist rather than self-treating, she suggests. Finally, Dr Chause says making peace with imperfect skin does not mean ignoring skin concerns. It means taking care of your skin without allowing every temporary change in appearance to affect your self-confidence. Healthy skin is about care and comfort, not looking flawless every single day, she concludes. How to take care of bad skin? Dr Rinky Kapoor, Consultant Dermatologist, Cosmetic Dermatologist and Dermato-Surgeonat The Esthetic Clinics, adds that a dermatologist can evaluate and manage simple psychological issues like stress and lifestyle-related problems connected toskindisorders however, some disorders requirepsychological intervention. According to her, problems like dysmorphia, where the patient feels that they have an abnormal-looking skin despite them being completely normal, or skin disorders related to psychiatric medications, have to be evaluated by a mental health expert, as dermatologists alone may not be able to diagnose or solve the root cause of the issue. articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sparsh Shrivastava

body_raw: Dupahiya Season 2, set in the fictional village of Dhadakpur in Bihar, is now streaming on Amazon Prime Video. Ahead of the seasons premiere, Sparsh Shrivastava and Renuka Shahane opened up about the preparation that went into playing Bhugol Jha and Pushpalata Yadav, respectively, in the show. In Dupahiya, Sparsh Shrivastavas character Bhugol Jha is an aspiring actor who makes reels dressed as a girl to attract followers. The actor admitted that mastering the Bihari dialect was challenging for her and said that, as a Maharashtrian, it took her some time to become familiar with it. And finally, now its so in me now that sometimes I speak Hindi like that. Because I find it so interesting that you can say the most hard-hitting things, and say it in a way, succinctly its delightful. So, now I am very comfortable.
