articleTitle: Who can be Kohli’s successor at 3 in ODI’s? Wasim Jaffer says southpaw can do it
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Virat Kohli
description: "When Virat and Rohit leave, Rohit, obviously, is a top-order batter, and Yashasvi Jaiswal is there to replace him, but I feel there will be a left-handed batter in Virat's place," Jaffer observed
body_raw: Since becoming the number three in the Indian ODI batting line-up, Virat Kohli has had no looking back. He has been one of the greatest players of all time, not just in the format but in that position too. He has been a master of chases for India over the years, but the 37-year-old said the 2027 World Cup will be his last, leaving a big void in that position. Former Indian cricketer Wasim Jaffer said Tilak Varma might be the right guy to replace Kohli in that spot for India. It feels great to see his versatility. He previously scored a century at No. 3, and now he has adapted to the No. 5 and No. 6 positions so beautifully. This is an amazing quality, Jaffer said on his YouTube channel. Its about time. When Virat and Rohit leave, Rohit, obviously, is a top-order batter, and Yashasvi Jaiswal is there to replace him, but I feel there will be a left-handed batter in Virats place. He has that game we saw the way he scored runs in the Duleep Trophy. His first-class average is around 55. So, he can fit into all three formats pretty easily, Jaffer said. For me, its the last World Cup Im going to play for India, Kohli told broadcaster JioStar on Saturday. That is my motivation and like, you know, to leave everything out there. And of course, the goal is absolutely to win the World Cup and whatever it takes, Im absolutely ready, he added. The upcoming World Cup will be Kohlis fifth ODI World Cup. The intensity of a 50-over World Cup is greater than anything. Because now, its about 10 games at a Twenty20 level of intensity, he said. Jaffer also spoke about Abhishek Sharma and noted his observations on how the batter has matured in recent times. It seems that Abhishek has matured a bit. He takes a little time, and the assurance is visible now, although this format doesnt give you a lot of time. His earlier approach was to try to hit a six on the first ball. Now, he has understood that it was the wrong approach, Jaffer observed.

articleTitle: Want Rohit Sharma to have more ODI centuries than his age when he retires: Sunil Gavaskar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rohit is 39 years old and has scored 35 centuries thus far in his illustrious ODI career. (PTI/File Photo)
description: Rohit Sharma fell on 92 off 85 balls in the third ODI and had he scored a century, it would've been the 36th of his illustrious career in the format.
body_raw: Rohit Sharma nearly scored a second ODI century in a row during Indias match on Saturday against the West Indies in Mullanpur, falling for 92 in 85 balls. Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar said that he was quite disappointed that Rohit fell eight runs short of his century, for a rather unique reason. The reason I was disappointed with Rohit getting out on 92 is because he didnt get a hundred and he might possibly quit international cricket after the end of the ICC Mens Cricket World Cup 2027. And at that particular point in time, when he decides to call it a day, I personally would like Rohit to have more ODI hundreds than his age, said Gavaskar. Rohit is 39 years old and has scored 35 centuries thus far in his illustrious ODI career. Had he gotten a century in the third ODI, he would have moved closer to achieving that feat with his 36th hundred. For me, its a special thing when a players hundreds outnumber his age at retirement. It shows the kind of career they have had and the standard they have maintained for so many years. That is why I really want Rohit to reach that mark. In my last year of international cricket, I wanted to get as many Test centuries as my age, and I got out in the 90s thrice. If Id got those hundreds, then my centuries would have matched the age of my retirement, which was 38, Gavaskar said on JioStars Haier Cricket Live. Gavaskar, the first player to score more than 10,000 career runs in Test cricket, retired with 34 centuries in the format. India went on to put up a score of 3517 thanks to Rohits 137-run partnership with Ruturaj Gaikwad and KL Rahuls unbeaten 129 in 87 balls. However, they went on to lose the match five wickets with West Indies captain Shai Hope notching up an unbeaten 162 in 143 balls.

articleTitle: ‘Will tear you to shreds’: Rakhi Sawant warns Komal Rani Swarnkar over Govinda controversy
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rakhi Sawant, Govinda, Komal Rani Swarnkar
description: Amid the ongoing controversy involving Govinda, Sunita Ahuja and Komal Rani Swarnkar, Rakhi Sawant warned Komal not to mess with her.
body_raw: Ever since Govinda visited Mumbais Lalbaugcha Raja with his Roopa co-star Komal Rani Swarnkar, their appearance has sparked fresh speculation about their relationship. Sunita Ahujas emotional appeal for support as her home is falling apart further fuelled the controversy, prompting several celebrities to weigh in. Last week, Kashmera Shah shared a cryptic post about homebreakers, while Divya Khossla also reacted to the controversy. On Saturday, Komal addressed the speculation surrounding her and Govindas relationship. Now, Rakhi Sawant has come out in support of Sunita and openly challenged Komal. Komal Rani Swarnkar on speculations around her and Govindas relationship On Saturday, Komal Rani wrote on social media, Recently, I have seen some celebrities openly commenting on Govinda ji and my personal life and our character. Yet I have never seen them come forward so strongly to express their opinion on any serious issue, whether it was terrorism, politics, the death of actors, or even another actors multiple marriages. Why, then, has our personal life suddenly become such a public spectacle that everyone feels entitled to comment on it? Also Read Divya Khossla questions Komal Ranis sindoor at Lalbaugcha Raja Whom are you kidding? Since when did going before Ganpati Bappa alongside my hero and praying for the success of my upcoming film Roopa become a matter of shame, a national issue, or dikhawa for others? We announced our film Roopa, not a romantic affair. We are working together, and we will continue to be seen together. If that bothers anyone, let them burn. Some actresses in the film industry, whose careers have gone cold, whose films are no longer working at the box office, seem to have nothing left except their washed-out brand tags they are trying to stay relevant by sticking their noses into other peoples ongoing controversies and trying desperately to keep themselves in the limelight, added Komal. She concluded, I honestly dont give a damn whether these people think I am a good person or a bad one I feel they are all part of the same group, taking out their frustration over their own failed marriages on someone else. Rakhi Sawant reacts to Komal Rani Swarnkars comment Following Komal Rani Swarnkars strongly worded post, Rakhi Sawant responded to her remarks while speaking to the media in Mumbai. She said, I have been very angry. Govindaji, first of all, return my Rs 65,999. I have seen all his films since childhood he was my favorite hero, but now I want all the ticket money to be refunded. Whatever he is doing with Sunitaji is very wrong. I am really upset. He even spoke about me,, saying that those who are divorced shouldnt comment on the matter. My story is very painful, and I have been through a divorce, but you have left your happily married life, aur keechad mein kamal dekhne chale gaye. This doesnt suit you, Chichi bhaiyya. Rakhi further added, On a serious note, Govindaji, pura desh naaraz hai aapse Govindaji, the whole nation is upset with you. The woman who married you and gave birth to your two kids, who has been with you for 40 years- you left her. And who is this Komal? She is badmouthing me and talking trash about other celebrities too. Chichi Bhaiya is the one who gave her these wings. Listen, Komal, dont mess with me. I am not Sunita I will tear you to shreds. Respectfully, do your film, chudail, pati chor you wrecked somebodys home. You thought you would woo a rich man and become a gold digger, take his money, and make films. Apply the vermilion of his name on your forehead, but if Govinda couldnt be loyal to Sunita, how will he be loyal to you? Rakhi Sawan had earlier spoken about the controversy after sharing with the media a private conversation with Sunita, in which the two discussed claims that Govinda was planning to marry Komal.

articleTitle: Ex-MP Kuldeep Bishnoi’s ‘Sneh Milan’ without BJP flags sets Haryana abuzz
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kuldeep Bishnoi outreach programm
description: While Kuldeep Bishnoi has maintained that he continues to be with the BJP, the events have nevertheless been seen as a show of strength.
body_raw: For the past three months, former MP Kuldeep Bishnoi, younger son of three-time former Haryana chief minister Bhajan Lal, has been on an intensive public outreach across Haryana-but without BJP flags, banners, or other party symbols. Since launching the campaign from Sirsa on July 21, Bishnoi has held gatherings in parts of Panipat, Kurukshetra, Jind, Kaithal, and Dadri districts, drawing political attention and triggering speculation about his next move, particularly after he was not nominated to Rajya Sabha a few months ago. While Bishnoi has maintained that he continues to be with the BJP, the events have nevertheless been seen as a show of strength. Bishnois gatherings have been named Sneh Milan. The manner in which these programmes are being held across districts, with old political associates and supporters seen alongside him, has raised questions about their political significance. There are no party flags on the stage, no formal political rally format, and no indication of any major political announcement. A close associate said he was reaching out to old contacts and supporters separately from the BJPs formal programmes. Old political relationships associated with the Bhajan Lal family, former associates and people from various social groups are being seen at these gatherings. It would not be appropriate at present to view these programmes as a sign of his distance from the BJP, the aide said. Bishnoi himself has given no indication of breaking away from the BJP and has reiterated that he remains with the party. Addressing his supporters in Dadri on Friday, Bishnoi said, Struggle has taught me not to bow down, but to keep moving forward. With your faith and support by my side, my courage is high, and my resolve is strong. Dadri has given this journey new energy today now the caravan will move forward. Expressing gratitude to his supporters for the gathering, Bishnoi said he viewed the honour as a reflection of the peoples continued support and blessings throughout his long political journey, including during difficult times. He said, In politics, I have seen both good times and difficult times. Circumstances changed, paths changed, but I never stopped trying to remain honest to my principles, my colleagues and my relationship with the people. I never let go of the hands of my people, and you too never withdrew your hand of affection from my shoulder. Nothing anti-party about Bishnois programmes BJP However, BJP leaders point out that Bishnoi currently holds no post in the party organisation, while his son and former MLA Bhavya Bishnoi is the partys state vice-president. Haryana BJP media head Bhupeshwar Dayal said, All political programmes being done by Bhavya are held under the banner of the BJP. Kuldeep Bishnoi is a very senior leader who is doing a lot of social activities. There is in no way anything anti-party about it, as social outreach is the right of any political leader. The ongoing outreach comes a few months after Kuldeep Bishnoi expressed anger over remarks made by BJP Rajya Sabha MP Rekha Sharma about Bhajan Lal on April 25. Her remarks drew a sharp reaction from Bishnoi, his supporters and members of the Bishnoi community, who sought an apology. Sharma expressed regret, saying she would withdraw her statement if it had caused pain to Bhajan Lals family and supporters. In an apparent effort to ease tensions, Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini visited Adampur in Hisar district in June to attend Bhajan Lals birth anniversary programme. Four-time MLA and two-time MP Bishnoi has also been a prominent Congress leader, a four-time MLA, and a two-time Lok Sabha MP. He eventually fell out with the Congress leadership after he was not considered for the post of the state party chief and joined the BJP in 2022 after resigning as an MLA. Later that year, his son Bhavya was elected MLA from Adampur on a BJP ticket but, contrary to expectations among their supporters, was not inducted into the Cabinet. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP chose Ranjit Singh Chautala over Kuldeep Bishnoi for the Hisar seat. Later that year, Bhavya lost the Adampur Assembly election.

articleTitle: ‘Had 27 paise in his pocket’: Shabana Azmi recalls Javed Akhtar’s early struggles in Mumbai
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shabana Azmi celebrates 62 years of Javed Akhtar moving to Mumbai.
description: Shabana Azmi marked 62 years since her husband, veteran poet, screenwriter and lyricist Javed Akhtar, first arrived in Mumbai with just 27 paise in his pocket.
body_raw: On this day, 62 years ago, veteran screenwriter, lyricist, and poet Javed Akhtar first stepped foot into Mumbai. He left home in Gwalior, Uttar Pradesh, and took a train to Mumbai, the proverbial city of dreams, getting down at the Mumbai Central station on October 4, 1964. More than six decades later, his wife and veteran actor Shabana Azmi celebrated the occasion with an Instagram post on Sunday. Shabana Azmi recalls Javed Akhtars early Mumbai days 4th Oct 1964. A young lad arrived at Bombay Central Station with 27 naye paise in his pocket but with big dreams in his eyes, wrote Shabana in the Instagram caption, along with the picture of a young Javed Akhtar. Life gave him several hard knocks. He slept on the footpaths, at the railway stations, and in the compound of many a studio. A day came when he had nothing to eat for 3 days and the only clothes he had were the shreds on his body, she added. Recalling how Javed refused to give up despite those hardships, Shabana continued, On the edge of despair, when he could have given up, he said to himself, Main yunhi marne ke liye nahin paida nahin hua tha. Yeh din badlenge I wasnt born to die like just like that. These days will change, as they did. 4th October, 1964 a 19-year-old, almost penniless. 4th October, 2026, decades later a life that has given India some of its most memorable words. This is the story of Javed Akhtar. Shabana Azmi ended the post by turning Javed Akhtars journey into a message of hope for others Some journeys begin with almost nothing. Except a dream. If he can do it, so can you. Never give up. In the comments section of the video, celebrities including Javed Akhtars daughter and filmmaker Zoya Akhtar, actors Hrithik Roshan, Dia Mirza, Divya Dutta, and Amruta Subhash, among others, shared red heart emojis. The boy continues to dream and build fire emoji, commented music composer Ankur Tewari. Javed Akhtar on his early days of struggle In the 2024 Amazon Prime Video India docuseries Angry Young Men, Javed Akhtar also looked back at his early days of struggle in Mumbai. I decided that after my graduation, Id go to Mumbai and work as an assistant director, hopefully with either Guru Dutt or Raj Kapoor. I was sure that after a couple of years of doing this, Id definitely become a director, he recalled. After living with his father and legendary poet Jan Nisar Akhtar, Javed then moved out and slept wherever he found a place, from friends homes to railways stations, parks, studio compounds, corridors, and benches. Some days, Id walk all the way from Dadar to Bandra, because I didnt have money for bus fare. Some days, it would strike me that I hadnt eaten for two days. I would always think to myself that if one day, a biography were to be written about me, this would make for an incredible moment, he added. After Javed Akhtar swore to himself that hed see better days, better days did follow. Eventually, he joined forces with Salim Khan to become arguably Indias most formidable writer duo. Salim-Javed wrote seminal films like Hathi Mere Sathi 1971, Yaadon Ki Baaraat 1973, Seeta Aur Geeta 1973, Zanjeer 1973, Deewaar 1975, Sholay 1975, Don 1978, Trishul 1978, Shaan 1980, and Shakti 1982, among others. However, Javed confessed that the days of hunger left such an indelible impact on his psyche that even after having all the luxuries in the world today, hes unable to believe its true at times. I stay in five-star hotels, in huge suites with large double beds. And I look back on how I came to Mumbai, in a third-class compartment that didnt even have any room to sit. I remember how I was deprived of sleep, and how tired I was. All I needed was a fraction of the room I had now, he said. Also Read - So we dont end up in jail Kapil Sharma on why he watches younger comics The veteran poet also admitted that he still experiences imposter syndrome and sometimes feels as though he is having an out-of-body experience while enjoying the luxuries he has earned after a lifetime of hard work. They bring out so much food, and I always wonder where this food was on the days I had nothing to eat. To this day, I feel like I havent deserved this food. I cant get over that, he added, teary-eyed, in the docuseries.

articleTitle: Rajya Sabha polls: BJP fields Dinesh Arya from Uttarakhand, Koel Mallick from Bengal
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Trinamool leader Koel Mallick has quit her Rajya Sabha MP's post.
description: Ahead of the October 16 Rajya Sabha elections, the BJP finalised candidate names for Uttarakhand and West Bengal.
body_raw: The BJP Sunday announced Dinesh Arya and former Trinamool Congress TMC leader and actor Rukmini alias Koel Mallick as its candidates for the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections from Uttarakhand and West Bengal, respectively. Biennial elections for 11 Rajya Sabha seats, 10 from Uttar Pradesh and one from Uttarakhand, are scheduled for October 16, alongside a bypoll in West Bengal. Mallick will contest the West Bengal bypoll to retain the seat after joining the BJP following the TMCs defeat in the Assembly elections. Arya, an organisational leader with ties to both the RSS and Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, currently serves as vice chairperson of the states Water Resources Management and Regulatory Commission, a position equivalent to a state Cabinet minister. TMC split and Mallicks nomination Mallick, a prominent figure in Bengali cinema, was nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the TMC in April. She subsequently resigned and joined the BJP in July as part of a split within TMC ranks, during which 18 MPs separated, merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India NCPI, and extended support to the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance NDA government. With the October 6 deadline for filing nominations approaching, BJP leaders held discussions at the party headquarters in New Delhi to finalise candidates for the remaining seats, particularly in Uttar Pradesh. Party sources said the BJP is prioritising women candidates and experienced organisational workers as it seeks to expand its current tally of 116 seats in the 245-member House. In Uttar Pradesh, 10 seats are falling vacant, eight of which are currently held by the BJP, while the Samajwadi Party SP and the Bahujan Samaj Party BSP hold one each. The single seat falling vacant in Uttarakhand is held by BJP MP Naresh Bansal. While BJP leaders expressed confidence in retaining all eight seats in Uttar Pradesh, party insiders noted that one seat could be contested. With 256 MLAs in the 403-member UP Assembly, the party falls slightly short of the required first-preference votes 37 per seat to secure all eight seats outright without opposition. Currently, the BJP-led NDA holds 150 seats in the 245-member Rajya Sabha, while non-NDA parties account for just over 100 seats.

articleTitle: Punjab Congress’s September jinx, AAP’s ‘Imaandaar CM’ shift and cash crunch
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjab CM: The aim is to uphold the highest standard of Satkar and reverence for Sri Guru Granth Sahib, it said.
description: Corridors of power: From the Congress changing state presidents months before the 2027 polls to ED raids making bureaucrats switch to disappearing messages, this week's column tracks Punjab's top political and administrative developments.
body_raw: September has not been particularly kind to the Congress in Punjab. In September 2021, barely five months before the Assembly elections, the party removed then chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh and handed the reins to Charanjit Singh Channi. What followed in February 2022 is history. The Congress lost power and the Aam Aadmi Party AAP swept the state. Cut to September 2026. Again, barely five months before the 2027 Assembly election, the Congress has changed its state president, replacing Amarinder Singh Raja Warring with Pargat Singh. The move followed months of differences and consultations within the party. The similarity is hard to miss a major leadership change just months before an election, after prolonged internal uncertainty. Whether the change turns the jinx into a blessing remains to be seen. Officers discover disappearing message After the Enforcement Directorates 50-hour-long questioning of Greater Mohali Area Development Authority GMADA officials and the confiscation of their phones during the searches, Punjabs bureaucracy appears to have discovered a new favourite feature on messaging apps disappearing messages. Bureaucrats who once happily exchanged long messages, documents and political gossip on WhatsApp are suddenly becoming rather conscious of what remains on their phones. Times are unpredictable. We dont know which chat will spell doom, an officer said, summing up the new mood in the corridors of power. The GMADA episode has clearly had a chilling effect. For bureaucrats, a casual message written months ago suddenly acquired significance it never had when it was sent. So messages are now being made to disappear. Whether that will make conversations disappear too is another matter. Decisions still have to be taken, files still have to move and, sooner or later, somebody has to put something in writing. Government vehicles run short of fuel amid cash crunch Punjab governments cash crunch was reflected in an unusual way in September, when official vehicles of several government functionaries were left without fuel for a few days as petrol pumps stopped supplying fuel over non-payment of dues. With the government unable to clear the pending bills, some secretaries were forced to pay for fuel out of pocket to keep their official vehicles running, sources said. The issue was eventually resolved after the Finance Department released the pending payment to the petrol pumps. An official put the amount released at less than Rs 1 crore. The episode has once again highlighted the governments cash-flow problems, with departments facing delays in clearing even relatively small routine payments. The fuel supply to government vehicles resumed after the payment was released. For officials, however, the episode offered a glimpse of how the governments financial constraints are beginning to affect day-to-day functioning. A spokesperson said the fuel issue was not due to a funds crunch but a glitch. Kattar Imaandaar AAP, now an Imaandaar CM Punjabs AAP had built much of its political messaging around the title Kattar Imaandaar. The epithet is meant to describe its claim to maintain a clean image in public life. Now, with the Assembly elections only a few months away, the phrase appears to have taken on a new, more personalised form in Punjab. Billboards describing Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann as an Imaandaar CM have come up across the state over the past few days. The timing has naturally drawn attention, coming months before the 2027 Assembly elections, with the Opposition mocking the self-certification. The message is simple the partys earlier Kattar Imaandaar branding is now being attached directly to the Chief Minister. As elections approach, the AAP is turning to its old-school image plank.

articleTitle: Jharkhand woman still in detention centre despite court order. Now HC asks, ‘under what law?’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: jharkhand woman
description: In 2025, the woman, after allegedly being sexually assaulted multiple times by a constable, escaped from the centre with two other detainees. Though a trial court convicted her in the escape case, she was acquitted of the charge under the Foreigners Act
body_raw: A Jamtara woman, then in her early 20s, was arrested in an alleged child kidnapping case in 2018. Sentenced to two years in prison, she was supposed to walk out free in 2020. Instead, she ended up becoming the first and, for a while, the only detainee at the Foreigners Holding Centre in Hazaribag-over 190 kilometres from her hometown. Police accused her of being a Bangladeshi national and, for the next several years, she remained at the centre inside the Hazaribag prison. In June 2025, the woman, after allegedly being sexually assaulted multiple times by a constable, escaped from the centre with two other detainees. On July 20 this year, an Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court convicted her of escaping from custody but acquitted her of the charge under the Foreigners Act. However, on completion of her sentence, instead of being released from the prison, she was sent back to the detention centre. On October 1, the Jharkhand High Court asked a question that has followed the woman since she completed her first sentence in 2020 under what law is she still being detained? A division bench of Justices Sujit Narayan Prasad and Akhil Kumar questioned under what authority of law the woman was continuing to be kept at the detention centre after the completion of her sentence. Hazaribag SP told the HC that an inquiry would be initiated into the matter. According to social worker and lawyer Apurva Vivek, who filed a habeas corpus petition on the 30-year-olds behalf in the HC, the woman told her that she had been sexually assaulted multiple times by a police constable. The ordeal had caused her severe mental distress and was part of the circumstances behind her decision to escape. Ordeal began in 2018 Married young after her fathers death, the womans life took a turn when she was arrested on February 2, 2018, relating to the alleged kidnapping of a child. The same year, in December, she was convicted under Section 363 of the IPC and sentenced to two years rigorous imprisonment, with the period already spent in custody set off against the sentence. On February 4, 2020, the woman completed the sentence. But instead of being released, she was shifted to the foreigners holding centre at the Lok Nayak Jai Prakash Narayan Central Jail also known as JP Central Jail campus in Hazaribag. It was there that authorities began treating her as a Bangladeshi national. For several years, the woman remained at the holding centre. According to the chronology placed before the HC, she was initially the only detainee there. In November 2024, another woman, Nina Akter alias Khushi, was brought to the centre. On June 10, 2025, the duo along with another detainee escaped. They were apprehended the following day at Dhanbad railway station. A fresh case was registered at Lohsinghna police station in connection with the escape. It is at this point that Vivek noticed something odd. Instead of the womans real name, she was registered in case records as someone from the minority community. Her fathers name was also found to be different that what it is in her original records. The case subsequently came before the Hazaribag court. The prosecution accused the three women of escaping from the foreigners holding camp and invoked Section 14 of the Foreigners Act. On July 20, the trial court stated that the prosecution had proved the charge relating to escape from custody and convicted all three accused under Section 262 read with Section 35 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS. But the Foreigners Act charge did not stand, and the court acquitted the Jamtara woman. The judgment recorded several gaps, including the absence of authenticated cross-border records, original travel documents or validated nationality verification material establishing their foreign status. The investigating officer also admitted that documents including an Aadhaar card and SIM allegedly connected to the woman had not been verified with the issuing authorities. The court, therefore, while convicting her of the escape, acquitted her of the Foreigners Act offence. In its October 1 judgment, the court made a broader observation on personal liberty We are living in the era of Article 21 of the Constitution of India and the inherent liberty conferred upon a human being cannot be taken away without any authority of law. The court directed the Hazaribag District Legal Services Authority DLSA to record the womans statement. It also sought an inquiry by the Hazaribag Superintendent of Police SP into the allegation against the constable and directed the Inspector General of Prisons to participate in the proceedings. The SP told the court that a thorough inquiry into the allegation would be initiated. The Home Secretary of Jharkhand has been directed to appear before the court on October 5. Reports from the DLSA and the SP have also been sought. SP, Hazaribag, could not be contacted for comment despite attempts.

articleTitle: Canadian vlogger’s post prompts footpath repair in Bengaluru’s Indiranagar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru footpath viral video Canadian vlogger
description: While Caleb Friesen's video garnered more than 2.1 million views, the Lokayukta took up a case suo motu and directed its police officers to visit the place.
body_raw: A day after a Canadian vloggers video on the poor condition of a footpath in Bengalurus busy Indiranagar went viral and the Lokayukta took cognisance of it, the civic authorities swung into action to repair the footpath on Sarturday. Vlogger Caleb Friesen posted a video on Friday highlighting that the damaged footpath on 12th Main Road inconvenienced pedestrians. Such footpaths would be totally unacceptable in any other country, he added. On Instagram, he posted, Indiranagar shouldnt be like this. The footpaths should be walkable, safe, pedestrian-friendly, impressive, and a reflection of all the innovation that happens in the city. Instead, theyre a mess. 12th Main in Indiranagar features rubble to rival a conflict zone, holes so big they look extraterrestrial, slabs that seem like they could give way at any moment, and trees that double as dustbins. Why are the footpaths at the centre of Indias tech ecosystem so pathetic? Why doesnt Bengaluru seem to care about its reputation both locally in India and internationally? I dont have answers to these questions. All I know is what I see, and what I experience as a pedestrian any time Im in the city. I think its high time for a footpath upgrade in Bengaluru. Something bigger and more comprehensive than the city has ever seen in all its centuries of existence. Something that Bengaluru can be proud of. Something that sets an example for the rest of the country. I do wonder if the city will rise to this challenge, or continue to be a national and international pedestrian infrastructure embarrassment the way that it is currently. Lets see.  While the video garnered more than 2.1 million views, the Lokayukta took up a case suo motu and directed its police officers to visit the place. The officials found that construction debris had been lying there for three days. Lokayukta warning for engineers Later, the Lokayukta issued directions for the chief engineer of Bengaluru Central City Corporation and other engineers concerned. The officials informed the Lokayukta that they initiated action on Saturday evening, but not against the person who put construction debris on the footpath obstructing the road. The Lokayukta was not satisfied with the response and stated, This clearly shows that, despite this matter being taken very seriously by this authority and the case regarding waste disposal in the city in different zones is being monitored intensively for the last more than 2 years, the concerned officials of the Bengaluru Central City Corporation, are showing such apathy. Therefore, all the engineers are hereby cautioned and instructed to ensure that no such incident occurs or recurs again. This shall be treated as a final warning before initiating any action against them personally for their dereliction and resultant maladministration. The Lokayukta also directed its police team to carry out random inspections of the area under the Bengaluru Central City Corporation and report any such lapses before September 9. Voting not paying taxes not enough Vlogger Caleb Friesen later posted another video on Instagram and said, So glad to see the rapid response from GBA Like so many in the comments, I too wish that the city authorities were more proactive instead of reactive fixing things before anyone needs to complain. That said, I commend their effort and the ongoing work theyre doing to fix up the problematic spots. Also I have said this before and will continue to say it my skin colournationality plays a role insofar as it acts as masala, helping my content to go viral. But anyone can create their own personal masala as a creator Baadal Nanjundaswamy dressed up as an astronaut to highlight moon crater-like potholes. Residents of Cox Town organised a pothole pooja to raise awareness. Anyone can complain creatively to get things done - very few people do though. They believe that if they pay taxes and vote, thats enough. It isnt. If you want positive change to happen, you need to, 1. Make it known that youre not satisfied with the status quo in a respectful, peaceful way, and 2. Do whatever is within your power to make a positive change. Virendra Suryawanshi placed many calls before and while this video went live, and has been working alongside GBA. Arun Pai mobilises volunteers to beautify spaces and discourage further neglect and degradation. Please think about how you the reader of this comment can contribute to positive change. India isnt going to improve on its own.

articleTitle: Tom Cruise’s Digger gets crushed by Ajay Devgn’s Drishyam 3, grosses Rs 1.30 crore in India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Digger box office collection day 2: Tom Cruise's lowest opening in 19 years.
description: Digger box office collection day 2: Alejandro Inarritu's satire is likely to be Tom Cruise's lowest opening weekend in North America since his 2007 war drama Lions for Lambs.
body_raw: Digger box office collection day 2Alejandro Inarritus satire Digger, starring an unrecognisable Tom Cruise as a greedy oil tycoon, has failed to meet expectations at the box office, both in North America and at the Indian box office. Even though it was quite a swing for the A-lister, the film has managed to open at only a minor fraction of the final instalment of his blockbuster spy thriller franchise Mission Impossible from last year. Digger domestic box office collection Digger opened in North America this past Friday at just 3.3 million, including paid preview shows from Thursday, from 3300 screens. Given its current momentum, its likely to score only 8 million during its opening weekend domestically. That figure is far below the range predicted by production house Warner Bros - 12 million to 15 million. This makes Digger Tom Cruises lowest North America opening weekend in 19 years, the last one being Robert Redfords 2007 war drama Lions for Lambs, as per The Hollywood Reporter. That movie, also starring Redford and Meryl Streep, opened at 6.7 million, and went on to earn 64.8 million during its lifetime. However, the budget of that film was far less, at 35 million. On the other hand, Digger has been made and mounted on a massive budget of 125 million. Compared to that, Cruises last release from 2025 - Christopher McQuarries Mission Impossible - The Final Reckoning - was made on a budget of 300 million to 400 million, but it opened at 64 million, and went on to amass 599 million during its lifetime. The reasons behind Tom Cruise registering his lowest opening weekend in almost two decades could be attributed to the polarizing reviews of Digger, as well as Cruise trading his action superstar persona for the role of a potbellied, 65-year-old oil tycoon. The actor will now return to his familiar turf - the second instalment of his popular action franchise, Days of Thunder, slated to release in cinemas in 2028. In fact, Michael Showalters erotic psychological thriller Verity, starring Anne Hathaway and Dakota Johnson, is estimated to emerge as the highest grossing Hollywood film at the North America box office this weekend. It opened at 15.1 million on Friday including Thursday previews, and is likely to score an opening weekend of 33.6 million from 3510 screens, more than four times than that of Digger. Digger India box office collection Even in India, Digger has managed to open at only a small fraction of Mission Impossible - The Final Reckoning. On its first Saturday day 2, the film earned only Rs 45 lakh from 468 screens, an over 30 drop from its opening day collection of Rs 65 lakh from 579 screens. After two days, the Tom Cruise-starrer has managed to earn only Rs 1.30 crore gross and Rs 1.10 crore net at the India box office, as per Sacnilk. This figure pales in comparison to Mission Impossible - The Final Reckoning, which earned Rs 33.50 crore from over 9,000 screens within its first two days at the India box office last year. The low box office opening of Digger at the India box office could also be owing to a major clash with an Indian tentpole release, Abhishek Pathaks crime thriller Drishyam 3. The Ajay Devgn-starrer amassed over 115 crore from over 16,000 screens in the first two days of its domestic box office run. Also Read Neem Karoli Baba film Hanuman Ansh refuses to bow to Drishyam 3, crosses Rs 419 crore mark Digger revolves around the misadventures of a third-generation American oil tycoon, which set off an impending calamity in Europe. That pushes the dictatorial US President and the White House, whove been in bed with the titular character of Digger Rockwell, towards damage control. The movie also stars Riz Ahmed, Sandra Huller, John Goodman, and Jesse Plemons among others.

articleTitle: Actor Vidya Malavade shares Uddiyana Bandha tutorial: How to practise it safely
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vidya Malavade
description: Vidya Malavade shares a detailed tutorial on Uddiyana Bandha or abdominal lock, describing it as a ‘very deep healing science’. A fitness experts explains the science behind it.
body_raw: Chak De actor Vidya Malavade recently shared a detailed tutorial on Uddiyana Bandha, a yoga technique also known as the abdominal lock. The last reel went viral with almost 2000 of you asking for the tutorial, she wrote in the caption. Before getting into the technique, Malavade also highlighted an important precaution MUST BE PRACTISED ONLY ON AN EMPTY STOMACH ONCE THE BLADDER AND BOWELS ARE EMPTIED COMPLETELY  DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. How to practise Uddiyana Bandha In the video, Malavade starts by standing with her feet comfortably apart. She suggests that beginners bend their knees and place their arms on their thighs. She then exhales completely through the mouth, emptying the lungs, before drawing the abdomen inward towards the spine and upward underneath the rib cage to create a vacuum. Do not force this, she says. Malavade then demonstrates Jalandhar Bandha, or the chin lock, by bringing the chin towards the neck and looking down. She also engages the root lock by squeezing the perineum and pelvic floor muscles. She explains that all three locks together are known as Tri Bandhas. The position should be held only for as long as it feels comfortable. To come out of it, the actor releases the chin lock first, followed by the other two locks, then takes a few normal breaths before repeating the practice.   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Vidya S Malavade vidyamalavade What can Uddiyana Bandha do? Ambaji Bodekar, professional athlete and bodybuilding coach, describes Uddiyana Bandha as a traditional yoga technique in which the abdomen is pulled inward and upward after exhalation. Uddiyana Bandha can help you control your breathing. It can strengthen your core. When Uddiyana Bandha is practised correctly it may also aid digestion. Malavades empty-stomach approach also has a practical reason. Bodekar explains that without food in the stomach, the abdominal wall can move more easily, making the retraction more comfortable. For beginners, he recommends taking the practice slowly and avoiding forcing either the abdominal movement or the breath hold. Beginners should not force the stomach in. Beginners should not hold the breath beyond what feels comfortable. Uddiyana Bandha is best learnt with guidance. The idea behind the practice Malavades explanation of Uddiyana Bandha goes beyond the physical movement. In her caption, she describes bandhas as internal energy locks that help control the flow of prana, or vital energy, within the body. She says engaging them can stabilise the core, support the spine, improve posture, enhance breath control and deepen meditation. Uddiyana literally means flying upward, referring to the upward movement of the abdominal wall. Malavade says the abdominal vacuum and release can create movement through the abdominal wall and stimulate the abdominal organs. She also links the practice with digestion and JatharAgni, or digestive fire, along with greater awareness and mobility around the abdominal region. For Malavade, the practice is also about looking inward rather than simply chasing an outward appearance. This is a very deep healing science.. and our Yogis knew that regulating the breath is a sure shot way.. to healing the body and the mind.. She writes that while people often focus on staying youthful externally, internal vitality, stillness and wellbeing are equally important. Bodekar, too, sees practices such as Uddiyana Bandha as a reminder that fitness isnt only about building muscle. Practices such as Uddiyana Bandha remind us that fitness is more than building muscle. It also teaches control. builds awareness. deepens the connection, with your body, the fitness expert concludes. articleTitle: 1965 war postscript: Inside Lahore-Amritsar ceasefire talks and mind games
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Military Digest 1965 India Pakistan War Ceasefire Talks
description: During the post-1965 ceasefire negotiations in Lahore and Amritsar, cross-border military diplomacy saw unexpected moments—from personal reunions at the airfield to a surprising discourse at the Golden Temple.
body_raw: An interesting postscript to the 1965 India-Pakistan war was the series of joint military meetings held in Lahore and Amritsar, where delegations from both nations discussed the fine print of the ceasefire and coordinated the withdrawal of forces. Held under the auspices of the United Nations and in accordance with the Security Council resolution of November 5, 1965, the talks alternated between the two cities and were coordinated by Brigadier-General Tulio Marambio, the UN Secretary-Generals representative. The Indian delegation was led by Lt Gen Harbaksh Singh, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Western Command, accompanied by Lt Col TS Padde GSO-1, Western Command and Captain Amarinder Singh, ADC to the Army Commander. The Pakistani side included Lt Gen Bakhtiar Rana GOC 1 Corps, Lt Col SA Hasan, Lt Col Riaz Azim, and Brigadier Gul Hassan Khan. Initially, the UN representative proposed meeting at a neutral camp midway between Lahore and Amritsar. However, Lt Gen Harbaksh rejected the site as barren and inhospitable, suggesting instead that the Indian team visit Lahore first, followed by the Pakistani delegation visiting Amritsar. When the UN envoy asked whether he had the Indian governments permission to go to Lahore first, Harbaksh replied that he did not need to seek permission and that his decision was final, as he wrote in his book In the Line of Duty-A Soldier Remembers. Diplomatic protocols in Lahore The Indian delegation arrived in Lahore in February 1966 aboard a UN aircraft with General Marambio. Upon arrival, Lt Gen Harbaksh inspected a Pakistan Army guard of honour. At the airfield, a personal connection surfaced the Indian Army Commander recalled seeing his ADC, Captain Amarinder Singh, scion of the Maharaja of Patiala, embracing the young Pakistani Captain commanding the Guard of Honour. Amarinder later explained that the officer was the son of Colonel Majeed, his fathers former Military Secretary, and that the two had played together as children on the Patiala palace grounds. While guiding Lt Gen Harbaksh through Lahore to refresh his pre-partition memories, Pakistani officials attempted psychological one-upmanship. Banners in Urdu were put up across the road advertising rides in a captured Indian vehicle for eight annas. The vehicle was the Jonga jeep of Maj Gen Niranjan Prasad, GOC 15 Infantry Division, which had been captured in a sugarcane field on Lahores outskirts after the officer narrowly escaped an ambush, leaving behind his starred plate, flag, and personal papers. Lt Gen Harbaksh objected to the provocative banners and urged his hosts to turn the car around. When the Pakistani counterpart mentioned making over Rs 10,000 from the rides, Harbaksh denied losing a Jonga jeep and warned that if such trickery continued, he would produce ten Jongas adorned with Pakistani flags for inspection when the Pakistani delegation visited Amritsar. Flowers and spiritual discourses during Amritsar visit When the Pakistani delegation made its reciprocal visit to Amritsar, Lt Gen Harbaksh arranged a tour of the Golden Temple. The visit occurred while Akali leader Sant Fateh Singh was staging a protest inside the shrine premises, preparing for a fast unto death and self-immolation to demand Punjabi Suba a separate Sikh-majority state. Despite the political tension, locals were informed in advance. The reception given to us was tremendous. The shopkeepers of Amritsar were all standing in front of their shops and showered us with flowers. On arrival at Harmandir Sahibs gate, we were received by the whole Prabandhak Committee Shiromani Gurdwara Prabandhak Committee, which had lined up with garlands of flowers, to be presented to every member of the delegation, and the United Nations officers, wrote Lt Gen Harbaksh. Towards the end of the tour, the Pakistani General requested a meeting with Sant Fateh Singh, expecting the leader to make critical remarks about the Indian government. Instead, speaking in Punjabi, Sant Fateh Singh stated that the people of India and Pakistan should not fight each other, offered a discourse on the principles of the Sikh faith, and presented sets of Punjabi religious books to the leaders of the Pakistani and UN delegations.

articleTitle: Aloo vs gobhi vs pyaz paratha: Which is the healthiest breakfast option?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: paratha
description: While people often focus too much on the filling, an expert points to other factors affecting a paratha’s nutritional profile and highlights one nutrient all three options are low in.
body_raw: Whether youre team aloo, gobhi, or pyaz potato, cauliflower, onion, parathas remain one of Indias favourite breakfast foods. But if you had to pick the healthiest one, which should make it to your plate most often? According to Meena Kumari, Chief Dietician, Dietetics, Sarvodaya Hospital, Sector-8, Faridabad, gobhi paratha takes the top spot. If I had to rank them, it would be gobhi paratha first, pyaz paratha second, and aloo paratha third. Why so? Lets find out more below DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Why gobhi paratha comes out on top The dietician explains that she ranked gobhi paratha at the top because cauliflower is naturally rich in fibre and has a good range of vitamins while keeping the meal relatively light. It also offers folate and antioxidants. Pyaz paratha comes next. Kumari explains that onions provide antioxidants and prebiotic fibres that are beneficial for the gut and digestion, although they dont contribute as much bulk as cauliflower. Kumari ranks aloo paratha third-not because its unhealthy, but because potatoes contribute more starch and fewer vegetables per serving. That being said, they are richer in carbohydrates and supply potassium, which is important for muscle and nerve function. Which one is the most nutritious? Kumari further points out that people often focus too much on the filling, while other factors might silently affect the overall nutritional profile of a paratha. The amount of oil or ghee used, the size of the paratha, and what you eat alongside it have a much bigger impact on its nutritional value than whether its filled with potato, cauliflower, or onion. Moreover, the calorie gap between these three parathas isnt as large as many people assume. According to her, the biggest contributor to calories is usually the amount of oil, ghee, or butter used while cooking. Each stuffing has its own nutritional strengths. However, one nutrient all three are relatively low in is protein. Protein is where all three fall short because vegetables dont contribute much. To make breakfast more balanced, Kumari recommends pairing your paratha with curd, paneer, or even a bowl of dal instead of eating it on its own. Which paratha keeps you full for longer? Among the three, gobhi paratha is likely to keep you fuller because its higher fibre content slows digestion. However, as Kumari clarifies, fullness depends on the entire meal, not just the stuffing. Since all three are relatively low in protein, hunger can return quickly. Adding plain curd, homemade raita, or paneer alongside the paratha can make a noticeable difference because protein helps keep you full for longer. She also recommends eating mindfully, avoiding excessive butter or fried accompaniments, and keeping portions sensible. A simple, balanced breakfast with one or two parathas, curd, and perhaps a seasonal fruit is far more satisfying than relying on carbohydrates alone. Easy ways to make any paratha healthier You dont have to stop eating parathas to make your breakfast healthier. Kumari recommends using whole wheat flour and, whenever possible, mixing in millet flour or besan to increase fibre and nutrients. Adding more vegetables to the stuffing, cooking with just enough oil or ghee, and serving the paratha with curd, raita, or paneer can also make the meal more balanced. Instead of topping your paratha with butter or pairing it with pickle, try homemade chutneys or plain yoghurt for extra flavour without overloading the meal with fat. articleTitle: Fujifilm Instax Mini 13 review: Is this the ultimate Gen Z snapshot camera?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Fujifilm Instax Mini 13 Review
description: With simple controls, a playful design and a new self-timer, the Mini 13 puts the fun back into photography.
body_raw: Instant cameras have never really been about image quality, advanced controls, or getting the perfect shot. They are about taking a photo, hearing the motor whirr, and watching the image slowly roll out. The Fujifilm Instax Mini 13 understands that better than most. At Rs 8,499, the Mini 13 does not reinvent the instant-camera experience. Most of it will feel familiar if you have used the Instax Mini 12, but Fujifilm has made a few small changes, including a mechanical self-timer, while keeping the camera simple enough for almost anyone to use. The result is an instant camera that prioritises the experience over technical precision. Design The Instax Mini 13 has a rounded, almost pillowy design that makes it clear this is not aimed at serious photographers. It is designed for parties, travel, casual snapshots and selfies, and the design fits that purpose well. It comes in five colours, Dreamy Purple, Frost Blue, Candy Pink, Lagoon Green, and Clay White. The metallic Instax logo adds a little polish, although the overall look remains playful. Despite accommodating instant film, the Mini 13 weighs around 306 grams and is reasonably comfortable to hold. It is still bulkier than a smartphone, but the rounded body makes it easy enough to carry around. The control layout remains familiar. There is a lens barrel at the front, a shutter button in the centre, a selfie mirror beside it and a flash above the lens. Twisting the lens barrel turns the camera on and extends the lens. The biggest new addition is the mechanical self-timer around the shutter button. A quick flick activates a two-second timer, while twisting and holding it for two seconds activates a 10-second countdown. An orange LED indicates the selected mode. The rear houses the viewfinder, film compartment, confirmation window and film counter. The bottom is completely flat, with no tripod mount, which limits how useful the 10-second timer can be for properly staged group photographs. Performance Getting started with the Mini 13 is straightforward. It runs on two AA batteries, so there is no charging cable or proprietary battery to worry about. Load a Fujifilm Instax Mini film pack into the rear compartment, check the film counter, and twist the lens barrel to switch the camera on. There is no menu system or manual setup to deal with. The camera handles exposure and flash automatically, with shutter speeds ranging from 12 to 1250 of a second depending on the lighting. For close-up photographs, twisting the lens ring activates Close-Up mode, which also brings in parallax correction to help with framing nearby subjects. After taking a picture, the print physically comes out from the front of the camera and takes roughly 90 seconds to develop. This remains a big part of the Instax experience. There is no app, editing interface or instant preview you simply take the photograph and wait for the physical print. The Mini 13 uses a 60mm f lens and Instax Mini film rated at ISO 800. The relatively sensitive film helps in indoor and lower-light environments, where the built-in flash also plays an important role. Image quality This is where expectations need to be realistic. The Mini 13 is not designed to compete with a smartphone or a dedicated camera, and its images have the soft, slightly retro character that has become synonymous with Instax. Photos are generally pleasing indoors, particularly at parties, bars and evening gatherings. The flash helps illuminate subjects in darker environments and gives the photographs a consistent look. Bright sunlight is less predictable. Since the flash fires with every photograph and there are no manual exposure controls, some images can look slightly overexposed. This lack of control can be limiting if you want to deliberately adjust the look of your photographs. For most users, however, the appeal is less about technical perfection and more about the character of the finished print. The occasional imperfect exposure is part of the experience, rather than something the Mini 13 is trying to eliminate. Verdict The Fujifilm Instax Mini 13 costs Rs 8,499 and delivers a straightforward instant-camera experience without unnecessary complexity. The self-timer is a useful addition, the rounded design is comfortable to hold, and the automatic shooting system makes the camera particularly accessible to beginners. At the same time, the fixed flash, lack of a tripod mount, and basic imaging system mean it is best viewed as a fun snapshot camera rather than a serious photography tool. If you already own an Instax Mini 12, the changes are modest enough that there is little reason to rush into an upgrade. For someone buying their first instant camera, though, the Mini 13 captures what makes the format appealing simple operation, imperfect photographs and, most importantly, a physical print that you can hold in your hand. The Mini 13 is not trying to make instant photography technically better. It is trying to make it enjoyable and for the most part, it succeeds.

articleTitle: ‘Was doing my duty’: BLO who stopped bulk submission of pre-printed SIR Form 7s in Hyderabad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The first instance of bulk Form 7s in Hyderabad surfaced on October 1, 2026, in Musheerabad constituency.
description: The video of this BLO rejecting the Form 7s went viral when Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee raised the matter on Saturday. “If some are targeting people by filing bulk Form 7s, we will take strict action,” the CEO’s office said.
body_raw: His voice may have gained unlikely attention, with Telangana Congress sharing a now-viral video of him rejecting a bunch of Form 7s allegedly filed by a BJP booth-level agent BLA, but this BLO from Hyderabad chooses not to make much of it, simply saying, I was just doing my duty. He was posted at Booth 173 in the Goshamahal constituency of Telangana Capital when the said Form 7s of the Special Intensive Revision SIR were filed by a BLA in September-end. Its not possible to accept these Form 7s, he is heard saying. Speaking to The Indian Express, the BLO, who works as a Junior Assistant at Osmania Medical College, said, The forms had printed EPIC numbers. There were no names on them. I had no instructions to receive such forms from my superior officers. Hence, I decided not to accept these. The video of this BLO rejecting the Form 7s went viral three days later, when Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee TPCC on Saturday released the video of pre-printed Form 7s of SIR surfacing in Hyderabad. I dont know how that video went viral. I was only stating my point of view, the BLO said. When asked whether he was scared to reject the forms, he said, No, I was not. I was doing my duty. He, however, did not want to be identified as he did not want publicity for an act which was done as part of the BLO duty. TPCC released the video two days after they complained to the Chief Electoral Officer CEO about apprehensions of a larger conspiracy to bulk delete voters as part of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls 2026. The forms, which the TPCC had accessed, had no names. They were in the last stages of being filed by the BJP BLA, a Congress source alleged. In a press conference on Sunday, BJP state president N Ramchander Rao said his partys BLAs have not submitted bulk Form 7s. The Congress is spreading malicious propaganda against constitutional institutions like the Election Commission, he added. Form 7s are used by electors if they want to delete their own name or to object to any other elector in their constituency. Similar instances The first instance of bulk Form 7s in Hyderabad surfaced on October 1, 2026, in Musheerabad constituency. Pre-printed applications were allegedly filed by a BLA of the Bharatiya Janata Party BJP, seeking deletion of a total 31 electors, who included a Congress BLA and his family members. In another case, a pre-printed Form 7 surfaced in Bahadurpura constituency. This, too, was flagged by the TPCC. In the Goshamahal case, the BLO refused to accept the bulk pre-printed forms, a TPCC leader told The Indian Express. When asked about the complaints, Chief Electoral Officer Sudarshan Reddys office told The Indian Express that an inquiry into the matter is on. If some are targeting people by filing bulk Form 7s, we will take strict action, the CEOs office said. According to TPCC, as per the original plan of BJP BLAs, the forms were to be submitted only after October 1, to inundate the election authorities who are already under the weight of lakhs of pending hearings from the notice phase. The period for filing claims and objections comes to an end on October 7. A TPCC source said, If the CEO does not take action, we will approach the police. This is a matter of protecting peoples right to vote. Telangana BJPs chief spokesperson NV Subhash told The Indian Express that bulk Form 7s are being submitted against Rohingyas who are not citizens of the country. He said, Political parties, including the AIMIM, the Congress and the BRS are supporting enrolment of Rohingyas. There is nothing wrong in filing Form 7s to deny them voting rights. He said AIMIMs Asaduddin Owaisi should personally ensure that the Rohingyas dont get voting rights in India. If he is a true Indian, he should see to it, Subhash said. Earlier in the day, Owaisi, the MP from Hyderabad, said, If false Form 7s are being filed, we appeal to the Election Commission to take action against those responsible for it. If this drama does not stop, remember protests bigger than those at Delhis Jantar Mantar will take place on the roads and streets of Hyderabad.

articleTitle: UPSC Ethics Simplified | Civic Virtue on Indian roads: What does it say about us?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UPSC Ethics Simplified | Civic Virtue on Indian roads: What does it say about us?
description: Roads are not merely physical infrastructure. They are also spaces where citizens practise, or fail to practise, values such as self-restraint, justice, responsibility and respect for others. Our ethicist, Nanditesh Nilay, explores what our conduct on the road tells us about civic virtue.
body_raw: UPSC Ethics Simplified, a special series under UPSC Essentials by The Indian Express, explores ethical concepts relevant to the Civil Services Examination. In todays article, we examine what our conduct on the road reveals about civic virtue and ask a larger question What happens when citizens fail to exercise self-restraint, responsibility and respect for others in public spaces? Our ethicist examines the issue through the lenses of civic virtue, good citizenship, self-restraint and moral duty. What happens when a person is involved in an accident on the road? If someone is hit, intentionally or unintentionally, an immediate ethical response should be to stop, check on the person and take responsibility for ones actions. The recent Gurugram case involving a woman biker raises questions about these basic civic responsibilities. The Indian Express reported that a woman biker was allegedly chased and rammed by a car on Golf Course Road. Video footage showed the car following the biker before colliding with her motorcycle. The police later added sections relating to attempt to murder, stalking and insulting the modesty of a woman to the FIR. The incident is therefore not only about road safety. It also provides an opportunity to examine a larger ethical question What do our everyday actions on public roads tell us about our civic virtues? What are civic virtues? A virtue is a set of traits, habits and qualities that enable individuals to fulfil their responsibilities effectively. Civic virtues are qualities that help individuals act as responsible members of a political community. They include concern for the common good, participation in public life, respect for institutions, opposition to corruption and responsibility towards fellow citizens. The importance and formation of civic virtues have been central questions in political philosophy from ancient times. Roads provide a simple but powerful setting in which these virtues are tested. Patience, self-restraint, respect, responsibility and concern for another persons safety are not abstract ethical concepts when we are behind the wheel. They directly influence the safety and dignity of other citizens. Aristotle Good person and good citizen Aristotle drew a subtle distinction between a good person and a good citizen. The virtues of a good person are universal or absolute in character, while the virtues of a good citizen are also related to the constitution and the responsibilities of living in a political community. Aristotle further connected the two through virtue of character. Qualities such as courage, temperance, justice and practical wisdom are cultivated through habituation in a well-ordered community and expressed through civic engagement. This idea of habituation is particularly relevant to civic life. Ethical conduct is not developed merely by knowing what is right. It is strengthened by repeatedly practising the right behaviour. For instance, stopping after an accident, helping an injured person, controlling anger during a traffic dispute or respecting another persons right of way may appear to be small acts. But repeated acts of self-restraint and responsibility help build civic character. Thus, the question is not merely whether a person knows the rules. It is whether the person has developed the character to follow them, especially when emotions run high. W.D. Ross Duties that guide moral action British moral philosopher W.D. Ross rejected the idea that all moral decisions can be reduced to one supreme principle. He proposed the idea of prima facie duties. These are genuine moral duties that normally carry weight, although in a particular situation one duty may have to take precedence over another. Ross identified duties such as fidelity, reparation, gratitude, justice, beneficence, self-improvement and non-maleficence. The idea is important because real-life ethical situations often involve competing considerations. Determining which duty should take precedence requires moral judgement and practical wisdom. It cannot always be reduced to a mechanical formula or an algorithm. Self-restraint and self-improvement Rosss idea of self-improvement also has a direct connection with civic virtue. Self-improvement is not limited to acquiring knowledge or professional skills. It includes cultivating ones virtues, character and capacity for self-control. A person must understand ones own intentions and limitations well enough to fulfil promises, avoid causing harm and prevent personal desires from overriding ones duties. This is where self-restraint becomes important. On a road, anger, impatience, ego or the desire to assert ones power can quickly affect another persons safety. A mature ethical response requires an individual to recognise these emotions and exercise control over them. The principle of non-maleficence, or the duty to avoid causing harm, becomes particularly relevant. If an action can seriously harm another citizen, the individuals responsibility cannot end with saying that the harm was unintended. Ethical conduct also requires us to consider the foreseeable consequences of our actions and our responsibility towards others. When civic virtue is missing The Gurugram incident brings these questions into sharp focus. The woman biker questioned why the driver did not stop to help her if the collision had been unintentional. The police investigation later examined video footage and escalated the charges. The ethical lesson goes beyond one individual or one incident. When self-restraint, justice, responsibility and concern for others are absent from civic conduct, public spaces can become places where power, aggression or privilege determine who feels safe. This is why civic virtue matters in both personal and professional life. A society cannot depend only on laws and punishment. Laws provide an external framework for behaviour, but civic virtues help create the internal willingness to act responsibly even when no one is watching. Development is more than roads and highways India often views roads, highways and other infrastructure as visible symbols of development. They are important indicators of economic progress and connectivity. But development cannot be measured only by the quality or length of our highways. A developed society also requires citizens who can share public spaces with discipline, empathy, responsibility and respect for others. If physical infrastructure advances while civic virtues remain weak, development remains incomplete. The road, therefore, becomes more than a means of transportation. It becomes a test of citizenship. The fundamental question is not only How good are our roads? It is also How good are we as citizens while using them? Compassion and civic life The Dalai Lamas emphasis on cultivating a compassionate mindset provides another dimension to this discussion. When our thoughts are dominated by excessive preoccupation with the self, emotions such as fear, anger, jealousy and mistrust can become stronger. Concern for the well-being of others, on the other hand, can make our minds clearer and our conduct more peaceful. This idea has relevance for civic life. A road is shared by strangers. We may never know the person driving beside us, walking across the road or riding a motorcycle ahead of us. Yet our actions can directly affect their safety. Civic virtue begins with recognising that the stranger on the road is also a citizen with equal dignity and rights. What should an ethics aspirant remember? The Gurugram case can be used to connect several concepts in UPSC Ethics GS Paper IV Civic virtue Responsibility towards the common good and fellow citizens. Self-restraint Controlling anger, ego and impulses. Non-maleficence Avoiding actions that cause harm to others. Justice Respecting the equal rights and dignity of other citizens. Self-improvement Cultivating ethical character and emotional control. Compassion Recognising and responding to the vulnerability of others. For a future civil servant, these values matter not only in extraordinary situations but also in everyday public life. Roads can testify to a countrys physical development. But the way citizens behave on those roads can testify to its civic character. Post-Read Questions 1. A good citizen is not merely one who obeys the law, but one who possesses civic virtues. Discuss with reference to Aristotle and contemporary public life. 2. How can self-restraint, non-maleficence and compassion contribute to safer and more ethical public spaces? The writer is the author of Being Good, Aaiye, Insaan Banaen, Kyon and Ethikos Stories Searching Happiness. He teaches courses on and offers training in ethics, values and behaviour. He has been the expertconsultant to SAARC countries, UPSC, Central Bureau of Investigation CBI,National Judicial Academy, ATI, RAKNPA, Haryana Institute of Public Administration, ISA MountAbu, National Centre for Good Governance,Competition Commission of India CCI, etc. He has PhD in two disciplines and has been a Doctoral Fellow in Gandhian Studies from ICSSR. His second PhD is from IIT Delhi on Ethical Decision Making among Indian Bureaucrats. He writes for the UPSC Ethics Simplified concepts and caselets weekly.
