articleTitle: UP quacks get life imprisonment 9 years after woman died following C-section
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UP quacks sentenced, woman dies after C-section,
description: The Amroha woman’s son, who survived the incident, is now nine years old.
body_raw: Nine years after a 22-year-old woman died following a C-section performed by an unqualified practitioner at an unauthorised medical centre in Uttar Pradeshs Amroha district, a court on Saturday sentenced two quacks to life imprisonment. The court convicted Wilson and Ghulam Mustafa, both in their 30s, on September 29 on charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, cheating and violation of provisions of the Indian Medical Act. The two men, who had been out on bail, were taken into custody following their conviction and sent to jail. According to the prosecution, the case dates back to October 3, 2017, when farmer Nem Singh took his pregnant wife Ruby to a medical centre after she developed labour pains. Wilson, an unqualified medical practitioner running the centre, and his wife admitted Ruby to the facility, assuring the family that she could have a normal delivery, according to the prosecution. Wilson administered medicines to her and put her on a drip. When her condition subsequently deteriorated, the family informed Wilson. Wilson subsequently told the family that Ruby required an operation and, according to the prosecution, called Mustafa, an unqualified medical practitioner from Naya Gaon village, to the medical centre. At around midnight, Wilson and Mustafa performed the operation on Ruby without obtaining her familys consent, the prosecution said. Ruby died shortly after the procedure. The district administration subsequently sealed the facility, and an FIR was registered against Wilson, his wife, and Mustafa. The police arrested Wilson and Mustafa and sent them to jail, although both were later released on bail during the trial. No evidence against quacks wife During the investigation, the police found no evidence warranting prosecution of Wilsons wife and gave her a clean chit. A chargesheet was subsequently filed against Wilson and Mustafa. Rubys son, who survived the incident, is now nine years old. During the trial, the court examined 12 prosecution witnesses, of whom six, including the complainant, turned hostile. However, we cross-examined the hostile witnesses and were able to establish the prosecution case before the court, said Sanjeev Chaudhary, Additional District Government Counsel, Amroha. The court has directed that notices be issued to the then district magistrate and chief medical officer of Amroha, who were serving in the district in October 2017, seeking their response on the alleged non-compliance with the directions of the Supreme Court and High Court, Chaudhary said.

articleTitle: World Teachers’ Day 2026: Why October 5 is observed, UNESCO’s 44 million teacher shortage warning
articleFeaturedImageAlt: World Teachers' Day 2026: Why is it observed
description: For 2026, UNESCO has announced the theme “Standing with teachers: 60 years of protecting the profession, advancing its status and shaping our futures.” The focus is on the status of the teaching profession and the challenges teachers face today.
body_raw: World Teachers Day is observed every year on October 5 to recognise the role of teachers in education and draw attention to the professional conditions that shape their work. In 2026, the day marks 60 years of the 1966 ILO-UNESCO recommendation concerning the status of teachers. The date has a specific reason behind it. October 5 commemorates the adoption of the recommendation in 1966 at a special intergovernmental conference convened by UNESCO in cooperation with the International Labour Organisation ILO. The recommendation laid down international standards covering teachers rights and responsibilities, initial preparation and further education, recruitment, employment, and teaching and learning conditions. World Teachers Day has been celebrated since 1994. World Teachers Day 2026 This years UNESCO theme For 2026, UNESCO has announced the theme, Standing with teachers 60 years of protecting the profession, advancing its status and shaping our futures. The focus is not only on recognising teachers but on examining whether education systems are giving them the professional and material support needed to do their work. This is also the year in which the 1966 recommendation is being revised. UNESCO says the teaching profession is facing newer pressures linked to digital technologies, climate change, inclusion, migration and displacement. It has also pointed to concerns around teachers autonomy, participation in policy-making, salaries, workloads and working environments. The review is intended to consider how the international framework should respond to these changes. Also Read  How this Kargil teacher turned abandoned war bunkers into Social Science labs The issue is particularly relevant amid a global teacher shortage. UNESCO says 44 million additional teachers will be needed by 2030 to achieve universal primary and secondary education. The figure covers the scale of the global recruitment challenge and places teacher supply alongside questions of retention and working conditions. The global 2026 World Teachers Day celebration will be held at UNESCO headquarters in Paris on October 5. Teachers, ministers and other education stakeholders are expected to participate in discussions on protecting and advancing the status of the profession. Also Read  He once saw education as his only way to a job. Now, hes a national award-winning teacher The programme will also include the award ceremony for the ninth UNESCO-Hamdan Prize for Teacher Development. World Teachers Day, therefore, is both a recognition of teachers and a day centred on the standards, rights and conditions that underpin the teaching profession.

articleTitle: Thackerays demand Gyanesh Kumar’s scalp; Raj calls for ballot paper polls
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uddhav Thackeray protest, Raj Thackeray protest,
description: At an Opposition protest, Uddhav Thackeray questions the centralisation of SIR voter verification, while Raj Thackeray alleges ‘vote chori’ since 2017-18.
body_raw: Shiv Sena UBT chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray led a joint protest march in Mumbai on Sunday against Chief Election Commissioner CEC Gyanesh Kumar, demanding his resignation and the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision SIR of voter lists in Maharashtra. At the concluding meeting of the Virat Garjana Morcha, Raj also demanded that electronic voting machines EVMs be replaced with ballot papers in elections. The march began from Metro Cinema and proceeded towards the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation headquarters. State leaders of the Congress and the Sharad Pawar-led NCP SP also participated. Organisers had asked participants to carry only the tricolour and not party flags. Referring to a letter by former Union Home Secretary R K Singh, Raj said, According to former Union Home Secretary R K Singh, special revision can be done in exceptional circumstances by recording the reasons in writing and for a specific constituency. It is illegal to conduct SIR across India. There is no provision in the law in this regard, he said. Raj said such circumstances could include a major natural disaster, migration, large-scale duplication of names or complaints regarding the voter list. Therefore, the case that is going on now is illegal, he said. Voters were to be increased during the Assembly elections and now two crore people have been taken out in SIR. Are these our voters? Who are they? Raj said, asking all political parties to demand that the exercise be cancelled. Raj also called for an end to voting through EVMs. The voting machines in this country should be shut down and voters should vote on ballot papers. If these two things happen, it will be clear who is right and who is wrong. It doesnt matter who comes to power tomorrow, he said. Raising vote chori since 2017-18 Raj Thackeray Raj said he had spoken about vote theft with Congress leader Sonia Gandhi, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, and NCP leaders long back. Today, we are here for vote chori. I have been saying since 2017-18 that vote chori is happening, he said. He claimed that he had told Opposition leaders at the time to boycott elections so that the alleged irregularities would come to light. Raj also questioned the increase in voter numbers between the 2024 Lok Sabha and Assembly elections, citing the difference to allege manipulation. The Election Commission, however, has maintained that the increase in Maharashtras electorate was within the normal range and has said the 2.07 crore enumeration forms that could not be collected during SIR should not be treated as final deletions. The draft roll contained about 7.72 crore electors against 9.79 crore before the exercise. Raj also asked the Election Commission to spell out how many of the people left out of the draft rolls had been identified as illegal Bangladeshi immigrants. Are those two crore people Bangladeshis? How many Bangladeshis have you found? Give us their details, we ourselves will find them and throw them out of the country, he said. Manufacturing a dictator under Make in India Uddhav questioned the centralisation of decisions relating to voter verification. Referring to a communication from Maharashtra Chief Electoral Officer S Chockalingam to the Election Commission, he said local election officials should have greater powers. Our states Chief Election Officer has written to the Election Commission asking to give rights to local officers after he realised that the right to decide voting rights is not with the local BLOs but has been centralised. It is with Gyanesh Kumar. Who is he to decide this? Uddhav said. Gyanesh Kumar is their weapon. Using him, they are taking away the right to vote also. You can control institutions, but the streets belong to us. The SIR must be scrapped, he said. Uddhav also questioned Kumars appointment as the CEC, alleging bias in the selection process. He criticised the change in the composition of the selection committee for election commissioners and alleged that Kumar was appointed despite Opposition objections. Targeting the government, Uddhav said, If, under Make in India, you are also going to manufacture a dictator in our country, then we have gathered here today to bury that dictatorship and put an end to it. He also alleged that the exclusion of around 13 crore names from draft rolls across the country during the wider SIR exercise amounted to disenfranchisement. The march was held amid a wider Opposition campaign against the Election Commission over SIR and the functioning of the poll panel. In Maharashtra, the Election Commission has extended the deadline for filing claims and objections on the draft voter list to October 12, with the process of issuing and deciding notices extended to November 10.

articleTitle: GNWL vs RLWL vs PQWL vs TQWL: Which railway waitlist has the best chance of confirmation?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: GNWL 20 vs RLWL 20 vs PQWL 20: Why the same number doesn't mean the same thing (Image generated using AI)
description: Railway Waitlist Explained: GNWL, RLWL, PQWL and TQWL are different railway waitlist categories. Know which waitlist generally has the best chance of confirmation and why the same WL number can have different outcomes.
body_raw: Two passengers can have the same waiting-list number on a railway ticket, but their chances of getting a confirmed berth may not be the same. The reason is the waitlist category - whether the ticket is under GNWL, RLWL, PQWL or TQWL. These codes represent different types of railway waiting lists and are linked to different quota arrangements. So, a GNWL 20 ticket cannot automatically be considered equal to an RLWL 20 or TQWL 20 ticket. So, which railway waitlist has the best chance of confirmation? Here is what GNWL, RLWL, PQWL and TQWL mean, how they differ and what passengers should know before relying on their waitlist number alone. GNWL vs RLWL vs PQWL vs TQWL Which waitlist has the best chance? The train ticket confirmation depends on several factors. Speaking to Indianexpress.com, a senior railway official said the actual movement of a waiting list depends on factors such as cancellations and the release of unutilised quota. Indian Railways reservation rules shows that these are not merely different names for the same waiting list. They represent different reservation quotas and different pools of accommodation. Consequently, their movement towards confirmation can also be very different, the official said. GNWL Usually the strongest position GNWL stands for General Waiting List and is associated with the general quota. Among the commonly seen waitlist categories, it generally offers the strongest position for confirmation.The official said that GNWL generally has an advantage because it draws from the main pool of accommodation and benefits from cancellations and release of certain unused quotas. Railway reservation material specifically states that RLWL and PQWL are confirmed after the General Waiting List, giving GNWL an important structural advantage over these smaller quota-based waiting lists, the official noted. The official, however, added that this does not mean GNWL 100 is automatically better than RLWL 2. The actual waiting-list number, train, class, journey sector, day of travel and expected cancellations still matter. But when comparable waiting-list numbers are being considered, GNWL is generally the more favourable category to hold, the official told Indianexpress.com. RLWL stands for Remote Location Waiting List When a passenger books a train from an important intermediate station rather than the originating station, the ticket may be placed under the RLWL quota. Indian Railways keeps a separate quota for certain remote or important stations on a route. The key difference is that RLWL has a smaller, separate pool of seats. Its confirmation therefore depends largely on cancellations or the availability of accommodation in that particular quota. Railway reservation rules also place RLWL behind the General Waiting List in the confirmation order. Railway reservation instructions make the hierarchy clearer RLWL is cleared after the General Waiting List. This explains why an apparently small RLWL number should not automatically be treated as equivalent to the same GNWL number, the official explained. PQWL stands for Pooled Quota Waiting List This quota is meant for passengers travelling between certain intermediate stations on a route. The available seats are shared among these station combinations.Because the number of seats in this pool is limited, PQWL may move more slowly than the General Waiting List. Its confirmation depends on cancellations and the availability of seats in the pooled quota. Railway reservation rules also place PQWL after the General Waiting List for confirmation. Thus, a passenger comparing two otherwise similar booking options should not assume that WL 10 means exactly the same thing under GNWL and PQWL, the official said. TQWL means Tatkal Quota Waiting List Tatkal Waitlist applies when the seats available under the Tatkal quota have already been booked and further Tatkal bookings are placed on the waiting list. It is a separate quota meant mainly for passengers making last-minute travel plans. This means TQWL follows a different confirmation pattern from the General Waiting List. The chances of a TQWL ticket getting confirmed depend on factors such as cancellations and the availability of berths under the Tatkal quota. For passengers, the practical lesson is straightforward TQWL should not be treated as having the same confirmation dynamics as GNWL merely because its numerical waiting-list position is smaller, the official added. Indian Railways waiting ticket confirmation prediction When asked about the actual confirmation percentages, the official said Indian Railways has previously informed Parliament that confirmation and cancellation trends vary depending on factors such as peak and lean travel periods, the type of train, journey details and passenger demand. A GNWL 25 on one train may therefore clear comfortably while GNWL 10 on another heavily booked service during a festival rush may remain uncertain. Other variables include the class of travel, day of the week, boarding and destination stations, cancellations by confirmed passengers, quota releases, additional coaches and the time remaining before departure, the official replied. The railway official also explained that GNWL generally has the strongest position for confirmation. RLWL and PQWL depend on smaller quota pools and are cleared after the General Waiting List, while TQWL follows the Tatkal quota and depends on available berths and cancellations. However, the waitlist number also matters.A GNWL 120 cannot automatically be described as safer than RLWL 2 simply because GNWL has higher priority. There is no mathematically valid comparison without looking at that trains historical and current booking pattern, the official said. Indian Railways waitlist prediction AI Indian Railways RailOne application provides an AI-based prediction of whether a wait-listed ticket is likely to be confirmed or not. According to the national transporter, the accuracy of its waitlist confirmation prediction has increased from 53 per cent earlier to 94 per cent now. The concept itself is not entirely new. Indian Railways introduced a machine-learning-based confirmation prediction facility years ago, using historical PNR data to identify booking and cancellation patterns. The prediction remains an estimate rather than a guarantee. Indian Railways own PNR enquiry system warns passengers that prediction is indicative and based on current and past trends, and that the actual status can differ, the official said.

articleTitle: Manushi Chhillar’s morning ritual includes methylene blue; expert says, ‘not a health supplement’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Manushi Chhillar starts her mornings with methylene blue
description: Taking the wrong dose or using products that are not meant for medical use can also be harmful, so beware.
body_raw: Manushi Chhillar believes performance starts long before the workout and, in a recent Instagram video, shared a ritual that has become part of her morning routine lately. The model-turned-actor revealed that the secret behind her energy and improved focus is methylene blue. In the caption, she also mentioned that the Methylene blue shown here is prescribed and supervised by my physician. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Dr Pooja Pillai, Consultant - Internal Medicine, Aster CMI Hospital, Bangalore, says methylene blue is a prescription medicine used to treat certain medical conditions, including a rare blood disorder called methemoglobinemia, and it is also used in some diagnostic procedures and surgeries. Recently, it has gained attention on social media because some celebrities and wellness influencers have shared that they use it as part of their daily routine, claiming that it improves energy, mental focus, memory, and overall well-being, she shares.   View this post on Instagram   A post shared by Manushi Chhillar manushichhillar Are these claims true? Dr Pillai says that these claims are based on the idea that methylene blue may help the mitochondria, which are the parts of our cells that produce energy, work more efficiently, and it may also have antioxidant properties that protect cells from damage. However, while early scientific research has explored these possibilities, there is not enough strong clinical evidence to prove that methylene blue provides these benefits in healthy individuals or that it should be used as a daily wellness supplement, she clarifies. What to note Just like Chhillar echoed in her video, Dr Pillai reiterates that methylene blue is a medicine, not a health supplement, and it should only be taken under the guidance of a qualified doctor. It can interact with several commonly used medicines, especially certain antidepressants, and may increase the risk of serious side effects, she tells indianexpress.com. She also warns that it is not suitable for everyone, including people with specific enzyme deficiencies, certain kidney or liver conditions, and pregnant or breastfeeding women. Taking the wrong dose or using products that are not meant for medical use can also be harmful, she adds. For most healthy people, Dr Pillai says that there is no need to add methylene blue to their morning routine simply because it is popular on social media or used by a celebrity. She believes a healthy diet, regular exercise, good-quality sleep, stress management, and staying hydrated remain the safest and most effective ways to improve energy, brain health, and overall wellness. But if someone is considering methylene blue for any health reason, they should first speak to a doctor to understand whether it is appropriate for their individual health needs and to avoid unnecessary risks, she warns in conclusion. articleTitle: Knowledge Nugget | India’s UNESCO Tentative List gets new sites: What you must know for UPSC Exam
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Knowledge Nugget | India’s UNESCO Tentative List gets new sites: What you must know for UPSC Exam
description: What are the newly added sites? What is a Tentative List? How does a site get UNESCO World Heritage status? What is India’s latest addition to World Heritage List? Here's what you need to know. Also, go “Beyond the Nugget” to know about the World Heritage in Danger list.
body_raw: Take a look at the essential events, concepts, terms, quotes, or phenomena every day and brush up your knowledge. Heres your UPSC Current Affairs knowledge nugget for today on new heritage sites added to Indias UNESCO Tentative List. Knowledge Nugget New heritage sites added to Indias UNESCO Tentative List Subject Art and Culture Why in the news? Recently, five new sites and transnational proposals have been included in Indias UNESCO Tentative List and it increases Indias count to 78. In this context, it becomes essential to know about the newly added sites and understand what Tentative List of UNESCOs World Heritage Sites is all about. Key Takeaways 1. According to the World Heritage Conventions operational guidelines, a tentative list is an inventory of properties a country believes deserves to be a World Heritage Site. 2. After the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation UNESCO includes a property in the Tentative List, that country has to prepare a nomination document that will be considered by the UNESCO World Heritage Committee. 3. In India, the Indian National Commission for Co-operation with UNESCO INCCU, and the Archaeological Survey of India ASI are the bodies which play a key role in this regard What are the new heritage sites added to Indias UNESCO Tentative List? 4. The newly added sites include the Buddhist murals of Bagh Cave Paintings, Group of Temples of the Chambal Valley, the Gupta-era Udaigiri Caves, the tribal legacy of Ginnorgarh, and Sites of Satyagrah. 5. Group of Temples of the Chambal Valley It is unique cluster of early medieval temples built between the 8th and 11th centuries CE, representing an important phase in the evolution of regional Nagara-style temple architecture. 6. Udaigiri Caves It is a rock-cut sacred ensemble developed under Gupta patronage in the 4th and 5th centuries CE. The site includes 20 caves, sculptures and inscriptions, including the Varaha form of Vishnu in Cave 5 and Anantasayana Vishnu in Cave 13. 7. The Sites of Satyagraha It is a serial transnational proposal connecting India and South Africa. It includes nine properties across South Africa and India, including Sabarmati Ashram, Mani Bhavan Complex, Harijan Sevak Sangh Complex, Sevagram Ashram, Aga Khan Palace and Gandhi Smriti Residence in India, along with Pietermaritzburg Railway Station and Phoenix Settlement in South Africa. 8. Ginnorgarh Fort It was a major political and administrative centre of the Gond kingdom from the early 16th to early 18th century. The fort includes palace buildings, stepwells, reservoirs, wall paintings and an ingenious water management system. 9. Bagh Cave Paintings It is a group of nine rock-cut Buddhist caves, mainly in use from the 4th to 6th century CE. Their murals, particularly those in Cave 4, are significant examples of post-Ajanta Buddhist cave paintings. What is a UNESCO World Heritage Site? 10. UNESCO plays a vital role in safeguarding cultural and natural heritage across the globe. Its primary objective is to identify, protect, and preserve sites that hold outstanding value for humanity. 11. It is guided by the Convention Concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage, an international treaty adopted by UNESCO in 1972. As of 2024, 196 States Parties have ratified the World Heritage Convention. 12. The World Heritage Site is a location recognised for its outstanding universal value. This signifies cultural andor natural significance which is so exceptional as to transcend national boundaries and to be of common importance for present and future generations of all humanity. 13. The World Heritage Site falls into three categories cultural heritage, natural heritage, and mixed heritage cultural as well as natural. 14. Cultural heritage entails an Outstanding Universal Value from the point of view of history, art or science, and includes monuments, groups of buildings, and sites which are the combined work of nature and human agency. Examples include the Taj Mahal, the Statue of Liberty, and the Sydney Opera House. 15. The Sites under natural heritage are those having an Outstanding Universal Value from the point of view of science, conservation or natural beauty, such as the Sundarbans Natural Park or the Victoria Falls. 16. Notably, the concept of World Heritage is universally applicable. According to UNESCOs website, World Heritage sites belong to all the peoples of the world, irrespective of the territory on which they are located. What is Indias latest addition to the World Heritage List? 17. In the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee which was held in Busan South Korea, 25 new properties were inscribed in the World Heritage list, out of which 19 are cultural, 5 are natural, and 1 is mixed. 18. Sarnath has been inscribed on UNESCOs World Heritage List in the 48th session of the World Heritage Committee. 19. With the inscription on UNESCOs World Heritage List, Sarnath becomes Indias 45th and Uttar Pradeshs fourth World Heritage Site. Sarnath is the sacred land where Lord Buddha, after attaining enlightenment, delivered his first sermon to humanity and set in motion the Dharmachakra Pravartan. Counted among the holy pilgrimage sites of Buddhism, Sarnath is described in ancient Buddhist scriptures such as Rishipattan. 20. Notably, Sarnath was included in UNESCOs tentative list on July 3, 1998. Twenty-eight years on, it has been officially designated a World Heritage Site. Until now, the UPs three World Heritage Sites were the Taj Mahal, Agra Fort and Fatehpur Sikri - all in the Agra region. BEYOND THE NUGGET What is the List of World Heritage in Danger? 1. The List of World Heritage in Danger is designed to inform the international community of conditions which threaten the very characteristics for which a property was inscribed on the World Heritage List, and to encourage corrective action. 2. Dangers can be ascertained, referring to specific and proven imminent threats, or potential, when a property is faced with threats which could have negative effects on its World Heritage values. 3. At its 43rd session Baku, 2019, the World Heritage Committee recalled that the inscription of a property on the List of World Heritage in Danger, aims to marshal international support to help the State Party effectively address the challenges faced by the property by engaging with the World Heritage Centre and the Advisory Bodies to develop a programme of corrective measures to achieve the Desired state of conservation for the property. 4. Armed conflict and war, earthquakes and other natural disasters, pollution, poaching, uncontrolled urbanization and unchecked tourist development pose major problems to World Heritage sites. 5. Some sites inscribed on the List of World Heritage in Danger are Bamiyan Valley in Afghanistan, the Historic Town of Zabid in Yemen, the Iranian city of Bam, etc. Post Read Question Consider the following statements regarding UNESCOs Tentative List of World Heritage Sites 1. It is an inventory of properties that a country considers to have potential Outstanding Universal Value. 2.Inclusion in the Tentative List automatically grants a property UNESCO World Heritage Site status. 3. Indias UNESCO Tentative List has total 78 sites. Which of the statements given above isare correct? a 1 and 2 only b 2 and 3 only c 1 and 3 only d 1, 2 and 3 Answer Key c Sources whc.unesco.org, UPSC Issue at a Glance  Indias UNESCO World Heritage Sites - criteria, categories, and recent additions, Sarnath joins UNESCO World Heritage List How it was rediscovered and other facts Click here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for September 2026. articleTitle: In Maharashtra, the story of a drought foretold
articleFeaturedImageAlt: drought
description: What took three failed monsoons to produce in 1972 has taken just one bad season today — a measure of Maharashtra’s deepening fiscal and agricultural vulnerabilities
body_raw: Its easy to spot a few familiar patterns - and some surprises - here. As Maharashtra confronts a water shortage after a weak monsoon, many are comparing the situation with 1972, when the state experienced its toughest drought on record. Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis has expressed concerns that this years drought could be worse than 1972. But theres a bit more to it. Back in 1972, three successive years of poor monsoons led to a real crisis. Things are different this time Last year brought plenty of early rain, topping up all the dams and reservoirs. In 1972, it took three years of failed rains to spark trouble more than half a century later, just one bad season has left the state in a spot of bother. This neatly sums up how things have shifted in a state once celebrated for its farming progress. The 1972 drought brought out the best in politicians who truly cared about ordinary people. Troubled by the harsh conditions, Vitthal Sakharam Page, then chairman of the state Legislative Council, asked his wife how much cash she had at home. Mrs Page found just about Rs 700. He then asked how many labourers that might support, and she replied, Around 10 for two weeks. A dedicated Gandhian, Page quickly raised the matter with the then chief minister, Vasantrao Naik, calling for Rs 100 crore to help the states poor. Naik invited Krishnarao Dhulap of the Peasants and Workers Party PWP, the Leader of the Opposition, to discuss raising the sum. In a rare and heartening move, Dhulap and the entire Opposition proposed a tax raise, which the treasury backed. The Assembly unanimously agreed to add a 15 paise surcharge per passenger on state transport bus tickets. This fund created the Employment Guarantee Scheme EGS, recently renamed VB-G RAM G Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission. Its pretty rare to see the opposition calling for a tax rise. Cut to 2026. Even before the formal conclusion of the monsoon, the state - already constrained by a debt of Rs 11 lakh crore - is securing additional borrowing to fund a Rs 45,000 crore drought relief programme. Although the central government has set a borrowing ceiling of Rs 1.20 lakh crore for the current financial year, the state has already consumed Rs 50,000 crore in loans over five months - much before the drought was officially declared. At the time of the budget presentation in March, a revenue deficit of Rs 40,552 crore and a fiscal deficit of Rs 1.5 lakh crore were projected. This year, the state has allocated a substantial Rs 70,000 crore solely for interest servicing on its borrowings - a figure expected to rise as further debt is incurred. Against this backdrop, Fadnavis, who also holds the finance portfolio, presented supplementary demands totalling Rs 97,000 crore during the first quarter of the current financial year. This is no less than a habitual profligate begging for funds the day after payday. Welcome to todays Maharashtra, which is safe to characterise as fiscally imprudent and entrapped in self-imposed challenges. Money matters arent the only hurdle the state faces. The state is missing figures like V S Page, who could dream up clever ideas for everyones benefit, and opposition leaders such as Krishnarao Dhulap, who showed real generosity by suggesting a tax to help tackle the drought. A discernible shortage of competent personnel and leaders demonstrating public accountability is evident, as Fadnavis is compelled to address every issue personally. He has few ministers on whom he can depend. The three-party coalition presents significant challenges for the administration. Representatives from the governing parties are predominantly occupied with securing drought-affected status for their constituencies. The power-sharing arrangement has fostered a competitive environment concerning the number of regions obtaining this designation. Every prominent leader is endeavouring to ensure their constituency is included. A formal declaration of drought triggers automatic financial, administrative and social support from the state. This enables them to shower political largesse on the electorate at public expense, regardless of whether all areas are genuinely affected. This, in a state which, despite having the largest number of dams of any state in the country, has just about 17 per cent to 18 per cent of the total cropped area under irrigation. It leaves the vast majority of the farming community reliant on delayed or insufficient rainfall. From 2012, Maharashtra has recorded a negative agriculture growth for quite a few years. Even this years Economic Survey projects moderate growth of just around 3.4 per cent compared to the high of 9.1 per cent recorded in the previous fiscal year. Its worth mentioning that Maharashtra received over 100 per cent rains in the year gone by. So far this year, the state has announced drought in 265 out of 358 talukas. Its quite likely the government will soon label the whole state - apart from Mumbai and its nearby suburbs for obvious reasons - as drought-hit. In contrast to 1972, the current expectation is for increased state intervention, given that the administration is aligned with the central governing party. When electoral appeal becomes the overriding imperative for political survival and victory the exclusive objective, it is scarcely feasible for the authorities to remain indifferent. Where the double-engine government has struggled to demonstrate tangible development, its commitments will be rigorously tested during drought conditions. The writer is editor, Loksatta

articleTitle: Abhishek Banerjee objects to rebel TMC MP’s parliamentary panel chair post
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Abhishek Banerjee
description: Questioning the legal basis of Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar's appointment, Abhishek Banerjee urged Speaker Om Birla to restore the panel chairmanship to Trinamool Congress's official nominee.
body_raw: Trinamool Congress MP and national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla Saturday, objecting to the appointment of MP Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar as chairperson of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Chemicals and Fertilisers. Banerjee highlighted that Dastidar is among 20 Lok Sabha members of the Trinamool rebel faction facing pending disqualification petitions before the Speaker under the Tenth Schedule. In my letters dated September 23, I expressly requested that these Members be kept out of consideration for DRSC Department-Related Standing Committees appointments until the petitions were decided, Banerjee wrote in his letter to the Speaker. Banerjee reiterated that in his earlier communication, the party had formally requested to retain the chairmanship of one Standing Committee in the Lok Sabha and submitted its nomination for the existing chairperson to continue. He stated that the recent appointment disregards both the partys explicit objections and its official nomination. Highlighting procedural anomalies, Banerjee noted, The Digital Sansad website continues to show 28 Lok Sabha Members belonging to AITC All India Trinamool Congress. The member appointed, however, claims affiliation with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India NCPI through a purported merger disputed in the pending disqualification proceedings. He further questioned the party affiliation under which the chairmanship was allotted. If it has been allotted to AITC, on what basis has the partys nominee been replaced against its express wishes? If it has been allotted to NCPI, under what order has that affiliation been recognised, and on what basis has NCPI been given the chairmanship? he wrote. Disputed affiliation Banerjee asserted that NCPIs reported association with the National Democratic Alliance NDA cannot resolve the Tenth Schedule affiliation issue while proceedings remain pending before the Speaker. Appointing a member to a chairmanship while leaving the members disputed affiliation undecided is, in our submission, contrary to parliamentary propriety. This appointment cannot be treated as a chairmanship allotted to AITC, Banerjee submitted. Banerjee urged the Speaker to withdraw Dastidars appointment, restore the committee chairmanship to Trinamools duly nominated member, and deliver an early decision on the pending disqualification petitions.

articleTitle: ‘Lacklustre, sleepy, sluggish…’: Brazilian media on 4-0 win over India
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vinicius played in the first half of the match between India and Brazil. (Express Photo by Partha Paul)
description: Brazilian media didn't seem to be too impressed with the national team's 4-0 win over India at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata.
body_raw: Brazil beat India 4-0 in the first-ever senior mens football friendly between the two sides at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata. While that scoreline normally points out to a thrashing, in this case, it was a respectable scoreline for India. Ranked 138th in the world, India have never even come close to qualifying for the World Cup since they qualified by default for the 1950 edition before withdrawing. Brazil, on the other hand, are famously the most succesfull team in the history of the competiton and ranked sixth in the world. This reality seems to have not escaped the Brazilian media either, in which a majority of the opinions expressed after the match seemed to be criticising the Selecao. UOL, an outlet owned by the Folha group which is among Brazils media conglomerates, said Once again failing to impress, the Brazilian national team thrashed the weak India team - ranked 138th in the FIFA rankings - 4-0 in a routine manner in Kolkata. Even against a weak opponent, the Brazilian team started the match in a sleepy, sluggish, and uninspired manner. Vini Jr. had plenty of space on the left, but couldnt take advantage of it and made mistakes in his playmaking. Translated from Portuguese. Terra news said that Brazil left a lot to be desired in their win over one of the weakest rivals the Canarinhos have ever faced. Leading daily O Globo says that the match looked like a training session and that Brazil lacked offensive impetus. Despite their superiority and the scoreline, the Brazilian team failed to translate their control of the match into offensive numbers, creating few chances throughout the game, said the report. Former Former Brazil midfielder Felipe Melo was critical of how they played in this game and the two friendlies they played in Australia before that. Brazil only managed to draw the first of the two matches 1-1, which was their first game after their stunning 2-1 defeat to Norway in the World Cup round of 16. They won the second match 4-2. Brazil has been taking steps backward. The first game against Australia was below what they showed in the World Cup, the second, even though they improved, was also below par. And this third game, despite four goals, was also below par. Im hopeful that Brazil will improve, but in practice, theyve regressed compared to their last World Cup game against Norway, said Melo on Sportv. Melo accepted the fact that the Brazilians may not be used to playing in the kind of humidity that they had to deal with in Kolkata. However, the former Inter Milan midfielder felt that the players didnt seem to have the right attitude. A guy can play badly, but he needs to have the right attitude. Martinelli came on and showed attitude, as did others. Samuel Lino had a bit more attitude and scored two goals. If he had more time, he would have scored more, Melo concluded. Trivela, the Brazilian football news outlet, questioned the sense behind the match for the Brazilian Football Confederation CBF, considering the empty seats that could be seen at the stadium. A lackluster 4-0 victory for the Brazilian team marked the friendly against India this Saturday. It will be a friendly match remembered for failing to achieve even the main objective of the Brazilian Football Confederation CBF, wrote Trivelas report Carlos Vinicius Amorim in the piece. The stadium not being very full raises questions about the CBFs choice. The friendly match in India is justifiable, something long awaited by the population, but only if it were affordable for fans. The report goes on to state that a number of regions in Brazil has not hosted the national teams matches for decades. Instead of playing twice in Australia and once in India with inaccessible tickets, they could serve the population of some of these states. Furthermore, the president of the CBF Brazilian Football Confederation, Samir Xaud, promised to get closer to the Brazilian people after the World Cup. For now, its just talk, the piece concluded.

articleTitle: Why Odisha vs Chhattisgarh over Mahanadi row is back in spotlight
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mohan Charan Majhi
description: After Amit Shah-chaired meeting, Odisha CM Majhi says framework for resolution would be released “very soon”; BJD questions these talks, seeks clarity on water-sharing
body_raw: The Mahanadi water dispute between Odisha and Chhattisgarh is back in the spotlight, with the Odisha government signalling that the two BJP-ruled states are moving closer to an amicable solution, even as the Opposition BJD has called this bid an eyewash. Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, who attended a meeting chaired by Union Home Minister Amit Shah in New Delhi on Thursday along with Chhattisgarh CM Vishnu Deo Sai and Union Jal Shakti Minister C R Patil, said a framework for resolving the dispute would be released very soon. We are gradually moving closer to a resolution. Alongside the legal process, administrative and political resolution pathways have also been expanded. A path to a resolution will be found keeping the interests of both states in mind. This resolution will serve as a model dispute resolution mechanism for other states too, Majhi said. The BJP, which had favoured an amicable settlement while in Opposition in Odisha, has accelerated such efforts since coming to power in the state in June 2024, even as the dispute remains pending before the Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal. The latest round of talks began in July-August 2025, with several meetings between officials of the two states, including at the level of the chief secretaries and water resources secretaries, to discuss technical aspects of the dispute. A meeting between the two CMs was also held in July under the chairmanship of the Union Jal Shakti Minister. At the meeting, the states agreed to share data and information on their respective water requirements with the Central Water Commission. It was provisionally decided in that meeting to find a path to a resolution within three months. Two months have passed in the meantime and there has been satisfactory progress, Majhi said. Sai also indicated that the two states were looking at a cooperative approach. It is our life-giving river, intrinsically linked to the daily lives, agriculture, and culture of the people of both Chhattisgarh and Odisha. Our collective effort is to strengthen irrigation systems in both states through improved water management and to open the doors for new projects, he posted on X. Lifeline of Odisha For Odisha, the Mahanadi is more than a water-sharing dispute. The river is central to irrigation, drinking water, flood management, hydropower and the states broader negotiations with Chhattisgarh and the Centre. At Thursdays meeting, Majhi stressed that the Mahanadi was the lifeline of Odisha and said the states demand was that it receive an adequate share of the rivers water. Issues including irrigation, flood control, hydropower generation, drinking water and environmental concerns were discussed, he added. The Mahanadi river originates near Pharsiya village in Chhattisgarhs Raipur district and flows for about 851 km before merging with the Bay of Bengal. Of this, around 357 km lies in Chhattisgarh and 494 km in Odisha. The river flows through several districts in Odisha, while its wider basin covers 14 districts in the state. The prospect of an early settlement of the Mahanadi dispute has political significance for the BJP, with panchayat and urban local body elections in Odisha scheduled for early next year. The BJP is seeking to contrast its approach with that of the Naveen Patnaik-led BJD, which governed Odisha when the dispute entered the legal process in 2016. Bargarh BJP MP Pradeep Purohit accused the previous BJD government of deliberately keeping the dispute alive for political reasons. The BJD government didnt want the dispute to be settled. They wanted to continue the dispute with Chhattisgarh and make it a political issue. Thats the reason they opted for the tribunal route even as the NDA government at the Centre initiated the process to resolve the matter amicably, Purohit said. Referring to the BJPs governments in Odisha, Chhattisgarh and at the Centre, he said the triple engine dispensation would help resolve the dispute and secure Odishas due share. The BJD, however, has questioned the substance of the latest talks and demanded that the decisions taken at Thursdays meeting be made public. Senior BJD leader and former minister Arun Kumar Sahoo said the meeting should not be reduced to an exercise aimed at the upcoming local body elections. Since there is a triple-engine government, the possibility of resolving the Mahanadi water dispute had increased. However, no urgency was seen towards resolving the issue. There has been no clarity as to whether the dispute will be resolved through a tribunal or through mutual discussions, Sahoo said. The BJD has also sought clarity on whether Odisha would receive the water it requires during the non-monsoon period, and on the status of the barrages built by Chhattisgarh, which the party has described as illegal. Odisha Congress president Bhakta Charan Das also criticised the BJP governments, saying the state was yet to receive its due share of Mahanadi water. What is the dispute? The dispute dates back to 2016, when Odisha objected to Chhattisgarhs construction of a series of barrages and other structures on the Mahanadi and its tributaries. Odisha argued that the projects would reduce downstream flows, particularly during the non-monsoon period. Chhattisgarh has maintained that, given the rivers catchment area in the state, it is within its rights to use Mahanadi water for its requirements. The Centre initiated efforts at an amicable settlement in 2016, but the then Naveen Patnaik government pursued a legal route and approached the Supreme Court seeking constitution of a tribunal. Chhattisgarh favoured the creation of a joint control board. Following the Supreme Courts intervention, the Centre constituted the Mahanadi Water Disputes Tribunal in March 2018. Its tenure has since been extended, with the latest extension running until January 13, 2027. The Majhi government has now initiated a parallel effort towards a negotiated settlement and has informed the Tribunal about the process.

articleTitle: 10 am to 5 pm: Karnataka High Court fixes parole window for murder convicts’ wedding
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka High Court murder convicts parole wedding
description: Observing that moral objections cannot override legal entitlements, the Karnataka High Court granted a seven-hour parole window to two life convicts who murdered the woman's husband so they can marry.
body_raw: The Karnataka High Court last week granted a limited one-day parole to two life convicts, a man and a woman convicted of conspiring and murdering the womans husband, allowing them to solemnise their marriage. The court observed that moral objections cannot override a legal entitlement when no statutory prohibition exists. Justice MG S Kamal at the Dharwad bench passed the order on September 28 on a writ petition filed by Shridhar Arjun Talawar and Siddavva alias Priyanka Jagamutti, both aged 23 and residents of Bhairanatti in Mudalagi taluk, Belagavi district. Currently lodged in the Belagavi central jail, the duo sought directions for their release or, alternatively, 90 days of general parole to conduct their marriage and related ceremonies. Siddavva was married to Shankar Siddappa Jagamutti, 25, but developed a relationship with Sridhar Talawar. Considering Shankar an obstacle to their relationship, the duo conspired to eliminate him. On July 17, 2023, shortly after Shankars birthday, Shridhar stabbed Shankar to death at a temple with Siddavvas assistance before fleeing. Following their arrest, a local court in Belagavi district convicted both of murder on July 30, 2024, sentencing them to life imprisonment alongside a fine of Rs 3 lakh. Moral question and legal rights Addressing the unique circumstances, the High Court noted that the petitioners decision to marry aligns with the prosecutions original conspiracy theory regarding their motive. The petitioners have now decided to get married, which was indeed the conspiracy theory proposed by the prosecution. This poses a moral question as to whether they are entitled to parole to get married when the accusation against them was that they had conspired to eliminate the husband of petitioner No.2 Siddavva. However, legally, there is no such prohibition. Moral consciousness cannot overtake the legal entitlement to get married, the order stated. The court further noted that the right to marry serves a recognised social function and cannot be denied purely on moral considerations in the absence of explicit statutory bars. While the state government argued that the prison manual contains no provisions for granting parole on marriage grounds, it also confirmed upon the courts query that jail regulations do not permit solemnising marriages within prison premises. The court directed prison authorities to grant parole between 10 am and 5 pm on a date chosen by the petitioners, subject to administrative convenience. An adequate number of police personnel, to be deputed by the jailer, shall accompany the petitioners and remain present during the ceremony. The petitioners must be returned to jail by 5 pm on that day, the court directed.

articleTitle: 5 gadgets I recommended to help my friends build the perfect WFH setup
articleFeaturedImageAlt: WFH gear
description: From the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i and Samsung Galaxy S26 FE to the Logitech MK250 keyboard, here are five gadgets to give your work-from-home setup a makeover.
body_raw: A month ago, two of my friends told me they were off to South Goa and Pabbar Valley. I assumed it was a short trip to recharge after their hectic work schedules. But then they told me they had recently switched to freelancing gigs with a US-based company and wanted to temporarily move away from the city, working remotely from offbeat locations instead. More and more people in my circle are either becoming independent contributors or choosing freelancing over full-time work. Maybe thats what the future of work looks like in the AI era. In fact, during a recent group video call, my friends, who are all writers and editors but arent tech nerds like me, asked about the essential tech they would need to set up a work-from-home WFH space and give their workspaces a makeover. As someone who travels frequently for work and occasionally works from home, I know what its like to work remotely. Based on my own experience of working from home on a regular basis, I have found that you need the right gear and other essentials to stay productive and comfortable. I recommended five gadgets, including essential peripherals, to my friends to help them set up their home offices-and tested them over several weeks. The list includes the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i, Samsung Galaxy S26 FE, Logitech MK250 keyboard and mouse combo, Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 5 earbuds, and Xiaomi Power Bank 20000 165W. Together, I feel these devices helped them build a mobile office that allows them to work productively from virtually anywhere Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i 15-inch, Intel Ultra 5 322 processor  Rs 1,17,791 A computer is the bare minimum for setting up a mobile office at home, whether you are a developer, coder, or writer. Since my friends are writers, I recommended the Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3i, which I tested for several weeks. This is a mid-tier Windows laptop and has its share of flaws but my overall experience has been pretty impressive. Perhaps one of the most impressive things about the IdeaPad Slim 3i is its keyboard. I have spent the past week typing on it, including most of this review, and at no point have I felt that the keyboard was underwhelming. For writers, the keyboard is where their hands live, so it had to be good. The trackpad is good, although its missing haptic feedback. The chip is an Intel Core Ultra 5 322 processor, one of Intels newer processors. In everyday use, its plenty fast. Browsing, writing, email, SlackWhatsApp, video calls, light photo editing, dozens of browser tabs, a music app - all running together-were handled without complaint. The 16GB RAM is the one that most likely matter to most people, since companies these days are shipping laptops with 8GB RAM due to memory crisis. The 15.3-inch display isnt colour-graded for creative work, nor does it have an OLED panel, but its sharp, bright, and pleasant to use. To my surprise, the battery lasted 12 hours, which is enough to get through a full workday on a single charge with the brightness at a usable level and meaningful workloads running. Where I do have a few complaints about the IdeaPad Slim 3i is its build quality, which lacks a premium feel. The chassis isnt as refined as the MacBook Air, which is a letdown considering the notebooks asking price of over a lakh. At 1.5kg, the notebook is reasonably portable. It can easily be slipped into a backpack and carried while travelling. However, when it comes to design, it reminds me of notebooks from the pre-Covid era. The IdeaPad Slim 3i isnt a cheap laptop, and its asking price may seem high. But honestly, if you are in the market for a new laptop, almost every notebook can feel overpriced these days. I will leave the final decision to my readers. That being said, I do think the IdeaPad Slim 3i is a laptop for normal people. It delivers on the things that matter without making unnecessary compromises. For most people, the IdeaPad Slim 3i could be the answer. Samsung Galaxy S26 FERs 72,999 onwards When my friends asked me which smartphone they should buy, two options immediately came to mind. However, this time around, they wanted to stick to their budget while also looking for a phone that would last for several years and still have a premium feel. Its a shame about the recent price increase, but even at the new price, my top pick remains the Samsung Galaxy S26 FE for a reason. The S26 FE has the looks that matches the latest flagship S26 devices, meaning the phone has the same glass back and the triple-camera island on the back at the top left. I liked the design and build of the device. It has aluminum sides and an all- flat screen and a an IP68 rating that can survive a dunk in water. The phone has a 6.7-inch OLED display, which is impressive, and supports a smooth 120Hz refresh rate. I wish it came with an LTPO panel, as that would allow the refresh rate to automatically adjust from 1Hz to 120Hz, helping to conserve battery life. The peak brightness is also good, at around 1,900 nits. Inside, theres an Exynos 2500, Samsungs own processor, which I found to deliver better performance and efficiency than the S25 FEs Exynos 2400. For everyday tasks such as browsing, gaming, and photography, I found the performance to be reasonably good. The S26 FEs 256GB of storage and 8GB of RAM may feel limiting for some users, especially those who take a lot of photos or play demanding games. Unfortunately, this is the only configuration available in India. I wish Samsung had offered a 12GB RAM variant, even at a higher price. At least then, consumers would have had the option to choose. The 4,900-mAh battery can easily last a day on a single charge. The phone supports 45-watt wired charging or 15-watt wireless charging. And while its is Qi2-compatible, there are no magnets for easy docking. Samsungs One UI 9 is clean, highly customisable, and comes with a number of AI features. I particularly liked Now Brief, which creates a personalised feed combining weather, health updates, videos, and calendar events throughout the day. The S26 FE retains the same camera setup as last year, with a 50MP main camera, 12MP ultrawide, 8MP telephoto, and 12MP selfie camera. Dont expect it to beat the S26 Ultra or iPhone 18 Pro Max- it simply isnt in the same league. However, I liked the picture quality I got in broad daylight, with plenty of detail, sharpness, and a good dynamic range. I also noticed improvements to the night mode, as well as the phones video-recording capabilities. The telephoto camera, which supports 3x optical zoom, is another useful addition, particularly for capturing subjects from a distance without sacrificing too much detail. The S26 FE is a really good phone if youre an Android user. Its not a flagship-grade device, but its a solid choice for the average user looking for a semi-premium smartphone. Keep an eye out for deals and discounts on the S26 FE in the coming days, and you may be able to get the device for even less. Logitech MK250 Rs 2195 One of my friends had been working from home for five years when he started experiencing neck pain. He was advised to raise his laptop to eye level and use a standalone keyboard and mouse. I have tried a variety of keyboards over the years, and a few days ago, the new Logitech MK250 caught my eye. This is a wireless keyboard and mouse combo that costs just Rs 2,195. The best part is that I dont have to worry about USB dongles anymore. Both the keyboard and mouse connect via Bluetooth, so neither device takes up a USB port. The MK250s Bluetooth connectivity is especially useful on modern laptops with limited ports. It keeps both USB-C ports free for charging and other accessories, while allowing me to easily switch the keyboard and mouse between a laptop, tablet, and desktop without having to search for or carry a USB receiver. The keyboard features a full-size layout with a dedicated number pad. If you work with spreadsheets or frequently enter numerical values, having a dedicated number pad makes data entry much faster. The keys are spacious and quiet to type on, making the keyboard suitable for both home-office and open-office environments. The mouse is ergonomically shaped to fit either hand. It uses optical tracking for smooth movement across various surfaces, including desks, tables, and mouse pads. It has three buttons, which should be enough for most people, while the scroll wheel provides smooth and precise scrolling without requiring you to click through every line. Both devices are battery-powered, but the battery life should be long enough that you will forget they even need batteries. Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 5 Rs 29,990 While finalising the list, I came across a pair of old-school headphones with a built-in microphone that I initially wanted to recommend to my friends. But after hearing about their typical day and their love for music, I thought the Sennheiser Momentum True Wireless 5 might be the perfect fit for them, which I also happen to test them for weeks. The Momentum True Wireless 5 are expensive pair of wireless earbuds, but they provide the best audio quality of any true wireless earbuds I have tried recently and a reasonably better noise cancellation. The Momentum 5s have a sleeker, more rounded design that makes them comfortable to wear for hours. They arent designed for intense workouts, but they are well suited to everyday activities such as walking. I tested the Copper colourway and liked its distinctive look, which stands out from Apples AirPods Pro and Sonys wireless earbuds. The earbuds have an IP54 rating for dust and water resistance, so they should be fine in most everyday conditions. The outer shell of the earbuds features capacitive touch controls that work extremely well. The controls can be customised for single, double, and triple taps, as well as tap-and-hold gestures. Where I think they really shine is in audio quality. They feature 7mm TrueResponse dynamic transducers. While the specifications may look similar to those of their predecessor, I found that software and processing improvements have helped improve the overall sound quality. In my testing, the Momentum 5s performed particularly well with pop and dance music. Madonnas Danceteria and Mikas Relax, Take It Easy sounded excellent, with well-balanced vocals. The bass is deep, while the highs are crisp and clear. The Sennheiser Smart Control Plus app offers basic EQ settings, which I found adequate but nothing exceptional. The earbuds also support aptX codecs and offer Hi-Res and Lossless audio modes for better sound quality. However, these settings can cause connection dropouts, especially in crowded or busy areas. They can last up to 40 hours on a single charge with the included charging case. The Momentum TW 5 also delivers improved noise cancellation, providing stronger noise isolation without relying as much on a tight seal. That being said, Apple and Bose are still ahead of Sennheiser when it comes to delivering superior noise cancellation. Overall, I felt the Momentum True Wireless 5 offer the best of both worlds, delivering impressive sound quality and effective noise cancellation. They are a premium pair of wireless earbuds that offer luxe features such as Dolby Atmos for a more immersive listening experience, as well as a replaceable battery that helps extend their lifespan. Xiaomi Power Bank 20000 165W Rs 5499 Once, I was working remotely from the hills, and I vividly remember it was dusk. There was no power, and the deadline for submitting my story was fast approaching. That day, what saved me was the portable laptop charger I had with me, something I never thought I would need it. Since then, I have always kept a long-lasting power bank with me, and I recommend one to my friends who work remotely or from home. The latest addition to my mobile workflow is the Xiaomi Power Bank 20000 165W, which was recently launched in India for Rs 5,499. I have it and been testing it for a week or so. With a boxy form factor, the power bank is technically pocketable, but I would recommend keeping it in a sling bag or backpack. The design is quite nice- it feels premium and solid, while the glass front with the built-in display adds to its appeal. The screen is operated using a button that is large, indented, and easy to find without looking. One press turns on the display, allowing you to scroll through battery information. The power bank comes with a compact USB-C cable capable of supporting charging speeds of up to 120W. The second USB-C port on the side can deliver up to 45W to another device. Performance from the Xiaomi 20,000mAh Power Bank has been solid. The 20,000mAh capacity is enough to charge two smartphones alongside a MacBook Air and AirPods and a smartwatch. The power bank supports up to 165W charging and a range of standards, including PD 3.0 with PPS and QC 2.0, 3.0, and 3.5. For me, though, the screen on the power bank is the real star of the show. Sure, it isnt necessary for a power bank, but its the easiest way I have seen to check how much battery remains or how long the power bank will take to recharge. Another good thing is that I can fly with the power bank, though it depends on the rules set by each airline.

articleTitle: ‘Organised and difficult’: Carlo Ancelotti on India after Brazil’s 4-0 victory
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vinicius Junior in action against India at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan on Saturday. (Express photo by Partha Paul)
description: Brazil are currently the world’s 6th ranked team while India are languishing in 138th spot. Despite that, Brazil only opened the scoring in the 28th minute
body_raw: The Indian football teams friendly against five-time world champions Brazil ended with a 4-0 scoreline in favour of the visitors at the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan on Saturday, but Selecao boss Carlo Ancelotti praised the Indian team for being organised and making it difficult for them to score their opening goal. Brazil are currently the worlds 6th ranked team while India are languishing in 138th spot. Despite that, Brazil only opened the scoring in the 28th minute, through a goal from Estevao. Then, the floodgates opened. A goal from Pedro ensured the teams went to the half-time break with Brazil leading 2-0. Samuel Lino scored a second half brace to complete the rout. India played their part well. They tried to play their game they defended, they were organised, they tried to play counter-attack. I think that they played a good game. We had difficulty opening the score, but the moment we opened the score with Estevao, we had more opportunities to control the game better, Ancelotti said at the post-match press conference. We feel good. It was a good experience. I think it was a good game, entertaining, with good intensity, and India did their part. Talking about his own team, Ancelotti said I think we defended well. We could have defended better if we had a couple of chances in the counter-attack, but I think for us its important not to concede a goal. Obviously we have to improve some mechanisms in defence, but we had a new defence that never played together, so maybe not everything was perfect. Again, the message is that we are happy to be here. We tried to do our best we tried to show our best quality to all the people who love Brazil and love football, and I hope they enjoyed the night.

articleTitle: After ‘black day’ over women’s safety, Ahmedabad’s Nirma university steps up security
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nirma University students hold Black day protest, Nirma University Black day protest, Nirma Black day protest, Ahmedabad news, Gujarat news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Students observed a “black day” alleging inaction by Nirma University over their complaint about a construction worker’s objectionable behaviour towards women on campus.
body_raw: Ahmedabads Nirma University has imposed stricter control over construction workers movement on campus following a massive protest against alleged inaction after a worker engaged in objectionable behaviour towards women students. On Thursday, students observed a black day in protest against the private universitys administration over a complaint they had filed over the incident reported on September 29. A video of the incident was shared on social media, raising concerns about women students safety on campus. In the first official statement issued since the incident, the universitys executive registrar stated that the police registered an FIR after the university immediately informed them and that all investigations and action regarding the incident are being carried out appropriately. However, women residents of the hostel said that when they reported the incident to the female security staff, they were told not to wear shorts inside the hostel. They also alleged that the university administration ignored their complaint. Net cloth around girls hostel One of the students said that instead of taking action against the worker, the authorities installed a green net cloth around the girls hostel. The university has further strengthened its security arrangements and imposed stricter control over the movement of workers at the construction site, the statement added. According to the university statement, the worker was on the ninth floor of the construction site of the new H5 hostel building, which is approximately 100 feet away from the H4 girls hostel. Investigation into incident involving professor This is the second incident at the university where students have raised concerns about their safety. H K Patel, a professor associated with the electronics and instrumentation course, allegedly grabbed a student by the collar and threatened him during an event on September 19. The statement added that the university has constituted a three-member inquiry committee in connection with the incident and that the investigation is in progress. It is also noteworthy that both parties had apologised to each other on 21 September 2026 and no complaint had been submitted to the university, the statement said.

articleTitle: ‘He’s a sweet killer’: Kumar Taurani reveals three most expensive albums had one name in common
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Tips Music's most expensive albums yet -- Taal, Pardes, and Yaadein.
description: Tips Music’s Kumar Taurani and Ramesh Taurani revealed that their most expensive album acquisitions were for Subhash Ghai’s films Pardes (1997), Taal (1999) and Yaadein (2001).
body_raw: Tips Music, co-founded by brothers Kumar Taurani and Ramesh Taurani, went from a small music shop in 1975 to one of Indias biggest music labels by the 1980s. The two brothers, who have also entered film production, recently revealed their three most expensive acquisitions over the years. And all three albums have one name in common - veteran filmmaker Subhash Ghai. Tips Musics most expensive albums Talking about Tips Musics most expensive albums on the Game Changers podcast, Kumar shared, Back in the time, it was Yaadein, Taal, and probably Pardes. Pardes 1997, starring Shah Rukh Khan and Mahima Chaudhry, had music by Nadeem-Shravan and lyrics by Anand Bakshi. It included memorable songs like Kumar Sanus Do Dil Mil Rahe Hain, Sanu and Alka Yagniks Meri Mehbooba, Sonu Nigams Yeh Dil Deewana, and Kavitha Krishnamurthy and Hariharans I Love My India. Two years later came Taal, starring Aishwarya Rai, Akshaye Khanna, and Anil Kapoor. Composed by AR Rahman, the album boasts of evergreen tracks like Yagnik and Udit Narayans title track Taal Se Taal, Anuradha Sriram and Nigams Ishq Bina, Hariharans Nahin Saamne Tu, Asha Bhosles Kahin Aag Lage Lag Jaaye, and Sukhwinder Singh and Yagniks Ramta Jogi, among others. Besides Subhash Ghai, legendary lyricist Anand Bakshi is another common link between the three albums, having written the lyrics for Yaadein as well. The 2001 romantic drama, starring Hrithik Roshan and Kareena Kapoor, didnt work at the box office, but Anu Maliks compositions like Jab Dil Mile, Eli Re Eli, and the title track Yaadein Yaad Aati Hai stood the test of time. Films success and albums success go hand in hand Reflecting on Tips Musics long-standing association with Subhash Ghai, Kumar Taurani said their successful collaborations were rooted in mutual respect and continuity. Subhash Ghai would respect us a lot. We were happy with him. Hes a sweet killer. But Ive observed over the years that with whichever director or producer our kundali matches, those films work as well as their music. There should be continuity. And whenever that continuity has broken, those films havent worked. Responding to the observation that Yaadein didnt work at the box office, Kumar said, There can be exceptions in life, but generally speaking, the banners which continued to work with us succeeded. Our record is that 80 to 90 of films that we acquired got a good opening because of our promotional strategy. Also Read Neem Karoli Baba film Hanuman Ansh refuses to bow to Drishyam 3, crosses Rs 419 crore mark He then quoted the instance of late filmmaker Kuku Kohli, with whom they collaborated on three to four films, right from his directorial debut, 1991 action romance Phool Aur Kaante, which marked the debut of Ajay Devgn. But there was one film which we didnt like the look of, and he was also asking for a lot of money, that didnt work at the box office. There are a lot of films like that. I think there should be a taalmel between the label and the producer, added Kumar Taurani.

articleTitle: ‘I thought I was going to die’: Flydubai flight FZ1073 pilot Smit Machchhar tells Netanyahu what he did next
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai pilot attack:
description: In a call with Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu, Flydubai captain Smit Machchhar says he thought he was going to die, then opened the cockpit door a second time and let passengers in.
body_raw: When Smit Machchhar lay on the floor of his cockpit on September 30, hurt, unable to see well and with the plane dropping, he had one task left get to the door. In a video call with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday, the Indian captain of Flydubai flight FZ1073 said he thought he was going to die and used what strength he had to open it. The Boeing 737 Max was flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv with 174 people on board, most of them Israelis. Machchhar, who has flown for 17 years, says he opened the door twice. The first time, the co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, shut it and he fell to the floor. The second time, people were waiting outside. They came in, overpowered al-Hammami and helped bring the cockpit back under control. The plane landed in Tabuk, in north-west Saudi Arabia. VIDEO  Jerusalem Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu invites PM Modi and Indian pilot Smit Machchhar to light celebratory flame on Israels next independence day. Source Israel PMO X account Full video available on PTI Videos -  httpst.conG6m5y1Stx- Press Trust of India PTINews October 4, 2026 What did he feel when the first blow came? Machchhar said the plane was flying normally when the co-pilot stood up to pray. He did not think it unusual and, out of respect, chose not to look behind him. After about four to five minutes, he felt a hard blow to the back of his head. It was so sudden that he thought the aircraft itself had been hit. When a second blow came, he understood the attack was from the person behind him. The co-pilots initial blows had completely blurred my vision, he told Netanyahu. He could feel the plane going sharply down. I thought I was going to die what made him try the door again? Machchhar said he reached the door and opened it once. Al-Hammami closed it, and he fell to the floor. He knew then that he had one more chance. I thought Im going to die, and thats when I pushed against everything, he said. When the door opened again, he saw people waiting outside. They rushed in, and the fight ended. VIDEO  Jerusalem Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu calls Indian FlyDubai pilot Smit Machchhar a hero of the entire world. Source Israel PMO X account Full video available on PTI Videos -  httpst.coLVJdyNq6ci- Press Trust of India PTINews October 4, 2026 In an earlier call, on 2 October, he told Prime Minister Narendra Modi that he was fighting for his own life, but was not going to let others die. He also said he recited the Hanuman Chalisa during the attack. How does the cockpit door work? Netanyahu asked about pulling the pin on the door. Machchhar said there is no pin. Inside the cockpit, the door opens with a twist of a knob. People outside need a code. His colleagues were trying the code, but al-Hammami was keeping the door shut. The hard part was reaching the knob. Once his hand was on it, one short, quick twist was enough. Hero of Israel, India and the world Netanyahu used those words for Machchhar and invited him and PM Modi to Israel for the countrys Independence Day. He also said the co-pilot had gone through Islamist radical indoctrination. Machchhar has been moved from Saudi Arabia to the UAE, where he is recovering. Authorities in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Israel are looking into the facts, the motive and whether the attack was planned or linked to terrorism.
